data.summary: SAMA circular (Arabic) clarifying three points in the Updated Consumer Finance Rules: the consumer's right to terminate or withdraw from the finance agreement (Article 10-1), the initial disclosure requirement (Article 11-2), and the method for calculating the Annual Percentage Rate. It states that the withdrawal/termination right ends within ten days of contract signature where the consumer has already benefited from the financing — for example by drawing any part of the cash finance amount, having shares deposited in the consumer's portfolio, or taking ownership or use of the financed asset — and requires use of SAMA's published initial-disclosure form and APR guidance manual. Addressed to banks operating in the Kingdom.

An annex disclosure template for reporting total remuneration paid to board of directors and board committee members, broken down by member name, membership type (executive, non-executive, independent), fixed amounts, attendance allowances, in-kind benefits, profit share, granted shares, chairman/managing director/secretary remuneration, and other items, all in thousands of riyals. It is a reporting format supporting governance and remuneration transparency obligations rather than a substantive rule.

SAMA circular (November 2014) to all banks issuing a revised package of Amended Liquidity Coverage Ratio regulations and guidance, following a comprehensive review of SAMA's Basel III rules against BCBS standards to close identified gaps. The package comprises general guidance, specific guidance, a prudential return, FAQs and national discretions, and states that banks are expected to benchmark liquidity practices against the BCBS 2008 principles for sound liquidity risk management. It supersedes/updates the earlier 2013 Amended LCR circular.

SAMA circular (2013) transmitting the Amended LCR package — guidance documents, prudential returns, FAQ responses and national discretions — and setting reporting mechanics for banks. It requires monthly LCR prudential returns from month-end 30 June 2013 within 30 days of each month end (with a one-off extension to 30 September 2013 for the first submission), excludes foreign bank branches from that requirement, and confirms NSFR reporting continues unchanged under the February 2012 circular pending BCBS alignment.

SAMA standards (1436H) setting out the criteria for designating payment systems as systemically important in the Kingdom, on the basis that SAMA is the owner, operator and sole regulator of such systems and is responsible for their safety and soundness. A system is systemically important if it handles interbank or customer payments posing financial-stability risk, is the principal system by daily volume and value, is used to settle another systemically important financial market infrastructure, or is a central payments infrastructure with no substitutes. It designates SARIE, the Saudi Payments Network (SPAN) and SADAD as systemically important.

SAMA circular confirming, pursuant to a Royal Order and earlier SAMA instructions, that the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSRelief) is the sole entity authorised to receive relief, humanitarian and charitable donations — whether from government or private sources — for delivery abroad. Supervised institutions must verify that such donations and outbound transfers are channelled through KSRelief, review donation transactions made via foreign platforms using bank and credit cards, and continue awareness, service-delivery controls and monitoring. Binds all financial institutions supervised by the Saudi Central Bank.
lookup_terms: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre

data.summary: SAMA circular transmitting the updated Debt Collection Regulations (controls and procedures) for individual customers, replacing/supplementing the earlier collection rules. It defines key terms (customer, guarantor, third party, default, involuntary vs. voluntary change in customer circumstances, total disability, documented contact, complaint) and sets minimum standards for contacting customers and guarantors, rescheduling instalments for distressed borrowers, write-off/exemption on death or total disability, limits on phone contact, and deduction of due instalments from customer accounts (including joint/solidary borrowers per their agreed liability share). It binds banks and finance companies supervised by SAMA and any third party carrying out collection on their behalf.

Duplicate instance of the SAMA circular issuing the updated Debt Collection Regulations for individual customers; content is identical to the companion node. It covers definitions, communication controls with customers and guarantors, collection procedures, collection-unit governance, and final provisions. It binds SAMA-supervised banks and finance companies and third parties conducting collection for them.

SAMA circular amending the seasoning condition for the Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company (SRC) to purchase residential real estate finance portfolios from real estate financiers, shortening the previously required three-month period to one month from grant of the finance or from receipt of the beneficiary's first instalment, whichever is later, while retaining recourse to the originator for six months from the grant date. It binds banks, finance companies operating in the Kingdom and SRC.

SAMA circular issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation requiring finance companies listed on the Saudi Exchange to notify SAMA before publishing periodic financial statements on Tadawul's website, and to provide SAMA with the draft financial-results announcement in Arabic and English five business days before publication. It is without prejudice to other applicable laws and instructions, and binds only listed finance companies.

SAMA circular requiring supervised financial institutions to apply the new Commercial Register Law and Trade Names Law, including rectifying their own commercial registers within the transitional grace period, urging customers to do the same, and verifying that customers' CR entries remain valid. It directs that a suspended commercial register be treated the same as an expired one, and reiterates the money-changing rules requirement that a party wishing to conduct activities other than exchange business establish a company rather than a sole proprietorship (or liquidate the other activities). It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision.

SAMA circular on the Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB), issued under the Central Bank Law and the Banking Control Law, setting the buffer requirement applicable to banks' relevant credit exposures in the Kingdom. It is a macroprudential capital add-on instrument; the source text is heavily degraded, so the effective rate and implementation date should be read from the original document. It binds banks operating in Saudi Arabia.
lookup_terms: رأس المال التحوطي المعاكس للتقلبات الدورية

data.summary: A SAMA circular (superseding an earlier circular on the same subject) clarifying that technical connectivity and support services for e-commerce payment transactions are ancillary/technical services falling outside the definition of related payment services under the Payment Services Implementing Regulation, and therefore do not currently require a SAMA licence. Such providers must obtain the necessary technical approvals from Saudi Payments and must not contract directly with merchants, onboard them, perform KYC/merchant verification, AML/CTF or anti-fraud checks, or complete settlement and deposit of funds into merchant accounts. It binds banks and licensed payment service providers, which may only deal with licensed PSPs for payment services, must notify SAMA of unlicensed activity, and must apply outsourcing rules and mada operational, technical and fee requirements when contracting technical support firms.

A SAMA circular activating GCC-NET point-of-sale acceptance between Saudi Arabia and the Sultanate of Oman from a specified date, supplementing earlier circulars on the GCC payment network POS service and its tariff. It obliges banks to make the technical and operational arrangements to accept and process GCC-NET POS transactions, apply approved pricing with cardholders and merchants, notify and educate GCC-network cardholders that Omani purchases route via Oman's national network linked to GCC-NET, and accept GCC-network branded cards on their POS terminals.

A SAMA circular reinforcing the protected-funds safeguarding obligation in Article 93 of the Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services, addressed to all payment service providers. It requires that any non-objection request be accompanied by policies and controls for managing and operating the protected funds safeguarding account, including defined authorities and authorised persons, with multiple-control principles based on risk assessment, involvement of internal control functions, and limitation of account authorities to designated senior positions. It also requires documented reconciliation between aggregate e-wallet balances or executed payment transaction values and the safeguarding account balance.

A SAMA circular introducing the eSAMA eServices portal, which digitises SAMA services (e.g. non-objection requests for senior appointments and for launching products and services) for individuals, business and government users, with access via the national single sign-on. It designates the chief executive officer (or equivalent) of each supervised financial institution as the portal's main user, authorised to delegate submission rights, with identity data drawn automatically from the Ministry of Commerce linkage. It binds SAMA-supervised financial institutions, which must comply as written submissions are progressively phased out.

SAMA's Internal Audit Principles setting out the definition, independence, mandate and reporting of the internal audit function, and the duties of the board, audit committee and executive management toward it. They apply to finance companies and real estate refinance companies licensed by SAMA, and serve as guidance for finance support companies and finance lease contract registration companies, which SAMA may require to apply all or part of the Principles. Best local and international internal audit standards may be followed only where not inconsistent with these Principles and SAMA instructions.

SAMA's Compliance Principles establishing the compliance function/unit, its officer and staff, and its duties — including monitoring the full body of applicable laws and SAMA instructions (AML/CTF, terrorism financing, BNPL rules, anti-fraud, consumer protection, debt collection, governance and conduct), training, compliance-risk measurement and maintaining an instructions database. The Unit reports directly to the Audit Committee and must escalate irregularities and violations to both SAMA and the Committee, and periodically review the customer care department and debt collection function or outsourced collector (excluding real estate refinance companies). They bind finance and real estate refinance companies and guide finance support and finance lease contract registration companies.

SAMA's Credit Card Issuance and Operation Rules, issued under the SAMA Law and circulated to banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom, replacing the earlier Credit and Charge Card Regulations. It sets the full lifecycle framework for credit cards: definitions (Issuer, Customer, Credit Limit, Amount Due, Minimum Payment, Due Date, APR, Grace Period, Term Cost, Late Payment Fee, Initial Disclosure), issuance conditions, the cardholder agreement, repayment, statements, transactions, liability for unauthorised use, and fees and charges, plus disclosure form annexes. It binds all SAMA-supervised entities licensed to issue and finance credit cards, with a general 90-day compliance window and a longer deferred date for two specified provisions on repayment and on card fees/costs.
lookup_terms: credit card issuance and operation rules

data.summary: A duplicate instance of SAMA's Credit Card Issuance and Operation Rules (same covering circular and text as the other issuance under the SAMA Law). It governs credit card definitions, issuance, cardholder agreements, repayment, statements, transactions, unauthorised-use liability, and fees/charges, with disclosure annexes. Binding on banks and finance companies licensed to issue and finance credit cards; treat as the same instrument when citing.

SAMA circular adopting the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements Guide, issued under the SAMA Law and SAMA's supervisory mandate to raise financial-sector maturity against evolving fraud threats. It imposes a staged compliance pathway: a gap self-assessment against the Guide, a board-approved remediation roadmap, submission of both to SAMA by the stated deadline, quarterly compliance status reporting, and full compliance by the stated final date. Addressed to finance companies and payment service providers.
lookup_terms: دليل المتطلبات الأساسية لمكافحة الاحتيال المالي
finance companies and payment service providers fraud

data.summary: The Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements framework itself, structured as numbered control requirements addressed to Member Organizations, covering counter-fraud governance and risk management, fraud prevention, and supporting definitions (including Fraud, External Fraud, Fraud Risk Appetite, Fraud Risk Assessment, Fraud Response Plan, Electronic Money and EMI, and a broad definition of Employee). It sets expectations for a risk-based counter-fraud programme, board accountability, a Counter-Fraud Governance Committee, KRIs/KPIs, intelligence monitoring, enterprise-wide fraud risk assessment, new-product fraud review, oversight of outsourced counter-fraud resources, and independent audit. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations within scope of the adopting circular.

Section 3.1 of the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements, setting the governance and risk-management control expectations for Member Organizations. It requires a proportionate risk-based counter-fraud programme monitored via KPIs, ultimate Board responsibility for the governance structure and tone from the top, a Counter-Fraud Governance Committee meeting at least quarterly to approve and monitor the programme, policy and MI, operational collaboration with cyber security and financial crime functions, defined KRIs against fraud risk appetite, intelligence monitoring, periodic enterprise-wide fraud risk assessment, counter-fraud involvement before new product launch, vetting of third-party counter-fraud providers, and periodic independent audit.

The Fraud Prevention component of the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements, following the governance controls and read together with the framework's definitions section (Fraud, Fraud case, External Fraud, Fraud Landscape, Fraud Response Plan, Fraud Risk Appetite, Fraud Risk Assessment, Employee, Electronic Money, Electronic Money Institution). It frames preventive control expectations for Member Organizations, including e-money issuers and payment service providers, across internal and external fraud exposure. Useful for scoping which actors and fraud typologies fall inside the framework.

SAMA circular designating Founding Day (22 February) for 1447H as an official holiday for supervised financial institutions, fixing the corresponding Sunday date. It also requires banks, exchange centres and payment service providers to keep a number of branches open at airports and border crossings for defined periods during the holiday and to notify SAMA of those branches and their hours, with public announcement. Binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision.

Circular notifying issuance, by Governor's decision, of the Regulation organising close-out netting and related collateral arrangements, together with an annexed list of qualified financial contracts. It is issued under the SAMA Law and interacts with the Bankruptcy Law and its implementing regulation; the qualified-contract list was determined by SAMA and the CMA in agreement with the Ministry of Commerce. Applies to financial institutions supervised by SAMA, with effect from the date stated in the circular.

Circular issued under Article 14(b) of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business requiring exchange centres in Makkah, Madinah, King Abdulaziz International Airport and Hajj City in Jeddah to be fully staffed and operationally ready for the Ramadan and Hajj 1447H seasons. An annex lists minimum operating conditions, including adequate cash and denominations, suitable opening hours, crowd management, staff ID badges, prominent and system-linked exchange-rate displays, receipts for every transaction, customer-rights signage, POS availability, working CCTV, counterfeit-detection equipment, and reporting of unlicensed currency exchange to security authorities and SAMA. Binds the named exchange centres.
lookup_terms: Rules Governing Money Exchange Business Article 14

data.summary: Circular setting Ramadan working hours and Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha holiday periods for 1447H for SAMA-supervised financial institutions. It fixes bank public-dealing hours (10:00–16:00), six flexible hours for bank-affiliated remittance centres and payment service providers, the Eid holiday dates and durations per Umm Al-Qura calendar, continuous operation of branches and seasonal branches at Hajj arrival points and border crossings, and an obligation to open selected branches during Eid and notify SAMA of their names and hours.

Circular fixing the operating hours of the Saudi Arabian Riyal Interbank Express (SARIE) system during Ramadan 1447H (10:00–16:00) and the Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha closure periods, noting that clearing houses operate in line with SARIE hours and days. Issued under the SAMA Law and Article 16 of the Banking Control Law; addressed to banks operating in the Kingdom.

Circular setting, for Ramadan 1447H, the permitted hours for cash transport to branches, cash centres, remittance centres, exchange centres and retail (09:00–22:00) and for ATM cash replenishment and maintenance (24 hours in listed major cities, malls, airports and train stations; 07:00–22:00 elsewhere), subject to security authorities' directions. It reiterates compliance with the security safeguards in the Law on Transport of Cash, Precious Metals and Valuable Documents, its implementing regulation and related SAMA circulars. Binds banks and exchange centres operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular directing supervised financial institutions to establish technical/electronic linkage with Elm in order to use the Ministry of Interior's "Digital Document" service, which allows an electronic copy of the digital ID to be taken and the digital identity, its validity date and an inquiry reference number to be verified (via QR reader or entry of the National ID/Iqama number). It supplements an earlier SAMA circular on accepting the digital identity for existing customers and on finding a mechanism to capture an ID copy electronically where a copy is required. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA, which must coordinate directly with Elm, notify SAMA of implementation difficulties, comply with applicable laws and instructions, and preserve the customer's freedom to choose between presenting the physical or the digital ID.

Short SAMA circular (issued through the Payment Systems and Companies Control Department) prohibiting the use of social media and instant messaging applications to exchange any data or official documents, directly or indirectly. Such exchanges must instead occur through official, secure and approved channels, given the risks to institutions' activities and to individuals' interests. It binds all financial institutions and takes effect from its date.
lookup_terms: exchange of data and official documents

data.summary: SAMA circular announcing an update to the Requirements for Appointments to Senior Positions in SAMA-supervised financial institutions (second edition, previously issued under circular 17/1594), extending their scope to cover "activities supporting finance activity". The updated version is published on SAMA's website and applies from the circular's date. It binds banks, finance and real estate finance companies and finance-support companies, credit information companies, exchange houses, and payment companies/payment systems operating in the Kingdom.

The primary statute governing the licensing, permitted activities and conduct of finance companies in the Kingdom, including core defined terms (Finance Company, Finance, Borrower, Consumer, License) and the requirement that finance activity be Sharia-compliant. It lists the licensable finance activities (real estate, production asset, SME, finance lease, credit card, consumer finance, microfinance and any other activity approved by SAMA) and empowers SAMA to license entities carrying on activities supporting finance activity. It also imposes hard prohibitions on finance companies — non-finance business, trading in currencies/metals/securities/real estate, deposit-taking without SAMA licence, unsecured finance save as the Implementing Regulations allow, and related-party/connected finance restrictions — and binds licensed finance companies, their board members and external auditors.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulations of the Finance Companies Control Law

data.summary: SAMA circular setting minimum standards where a financial institution offers or promotes products under a trademark different from its original corporate identity and trade name, issued under the SAMA Law and aimed at customer protection, disclosure and transparency. Requirements include addressing brand/identity impersonation, cyber and financial fraud risks in the risk management strategy and policy, engaging brand protection service providers to detect impersonation (including on social media and websites), updating related policies such as usage and data privacy policies, registering the new/updated trademark with the competent authorities before use and notifying SAMA, running a promotional campaign clarifying the trade name, using trade name and trademark together in phone contact and in first SMS contact, and stating the trade name, trademark and licence number on websites and whenever referring to SAMA supervision. It binds financial institutions supervised by SAMA from the circular's date.

SAMA circular reaffirming that supervised financial institutions must apply the Law on the Use of Security Surveillance Cameras (Royal Decree M/9), its Implementing Regulation issued by the Ministry of Interior, and the accompanying document of security conditions and requirements for installing surveillance systems and the general technical specifications for camera equipment. It notes that financial institutions are classified among high-sensitivity sites, so camera installation must follow the site-sensitivity classification, and also requires continued compliance with SAMA's Security and Safety Guide for the financial sector. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision.
lookup_terms: Security and Safety Guide for the financial sector

data.summary: Section 7 (Principle 2.0) of SAMA's Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking, setting requirements for identifying, measuring, managing and reporting credit risk arising from Shari'ah compliant financing. It requires defined credit approval/renewal/refinancing criteria aligned to risk appetite and SAMA's responsible lending requirements, plus monitoring of counterparty repayment capacity, exposure classification, documentation completeness, collateral and contract-stage-specific risks. It binds domestic licensed banks conducting Shari'ah compliant banking, whether full-fledged Islamic banks or Islamic Windows.

Section 8 (Principle 3.0) of the same SAMA framework, requiring banks to maintain a market risk management framework, strategy, limits and independent middle-office monitoring covering all assets held, including illiquid or highly volatile ones. It addresses valuation and income recognition policies, stress-tested quantification of net open positions, product-specific risks (Salam, Parallel Salam, Sukuk, Murabahah assets), FX risk on cross-border and foreign-currency balances, and escalation when limits are approached or breached. Binds banks conducting Shari'ah compliant banking in Saudi Arabia.

Concept node on operational risk in Shari'ah compliant banking, drawing on SAMA's Risk Management Framework, where operational risk is defined as loss from failed internal processes, people, systems or external events and expressly encompasses Shari'ah non-compliance and fiduciary failures. It sits within the framework's board and senior management oversight requirements for an independent risk management function, documented policies and accountability lines. Binds licensed domestic banks offering Shari'ah compliant products.

Concept node for liquidity risk under SAMA's Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking, defined as potential loss from inability to meet obligations or fund assets, and requiring banks to maintain and periodically review liquidity risk profiles and liquidity management policies as market conditions change. It is embedded in the framework's board/senior management oversight and general risk identification, measurement, mitigation, monitoring and reporting duties. Applies to banks conducting Shari'ah compliant banking, including Islamic Windows.

Section 11 (Principle 7.0) of SAMA's Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking, requiring strategies, policies and reporting processes for equity investment risk, including Mudarabah and Musharakah profit-sharing investments. Banks must set investment objectives, risk tolerance, expected returns and holding periods, maintain structures for acquiring, holding and exiting such investments, monitor investee performance, and track how risks transform across investment lifecycle and contract stages. The framework took effect 3 March 2024 and binds domestic licensed banks conducting Shari'ah compliant banking.

Defined term and substantive requirement (Section 9) on Shari'ah Non-compliance Risk: the risk arising from failure of a bank's Shari'ah governance mechanism to ensure compliance with Shari'ah rules and principles determined by its Shari'ah Committee. Banks must manage SNCR as part of operational risk, maintain policies to measure, mitigate and monitor it, treat Shari'ah compliance as a higher-priority risk given reputational consequences, ensure contract documentation is Shari'ah compliant, and track income arising from non-compliant sources. Binds full-fledged Islamic banks and Islamic Windows of conventional banks.

Node covering the fraud detection limb of SAMA's Counter-Fraud Framework, sitting within the wider counter-fraud governance and control requirements and supported by the framework's defined terms (Fraud, Fraud case, External Fraud, Fraud Landscape, Electronic Money, Employee). It requires Member Organizations to maintain systems and controls capable of identifying fraud as part of a risk-based Counter-Fraud Programme overseen by the Board and the Counter-Fraud Governance Committee, with performance tracked through indicators. It binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations, including payment service providers and electronic money institutions within scope.

Node covering the fraud response limb of SAMA's Counter-Fraud Framework, anchored on the defined Fraud Response Plan (actions, reporting protocols, team responsibilities and information logging once fraud is suspected or detected). It connects to the governance requirements placing ultimate responsibility on the Board and oversight with the Counter-Fraud Governance Committee, and to expected coordination between counter-fraud, cyber security and financial crime functions. Applies to SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.

Node on the technology and assurance dimension of the Counter-Fraud Programme, which must address people, process and technology proportionate to the size and nature of the business. It ties to requirements for intelligence monitoring, key risk indicators, pre-launch counter-fraud assessment of new products or services, vetting and monitoring of third-party or managed-service counter-fraud resources, and periodic independent audit of control design and operation. Binds SAMA Member Organizations; note the outsourcing/third-party accountability point.

Node for the additional, mandatory control requirements applying to products and services of elevated fraud risk: licensed EMIs, AISPs, and Member Organizations offering digital payment services allowing funds to be sent and received, credit cards, microfinance, BNPL services, or safeguarding customer funds. It requires real-time fraud detection and prevention operating continuously with resourced handling of alerts, rules customised to the entity's products and risks, real-time intervention such as account freezing and transaction blocking on suspected compromise, and intelligence-driven screening or blocking of high-risk accounts, locations, IPs, devices and VPN use. Entities outside the mandatory list must still take a documented risk-based approach to these requirements.

Node defining the Counter-Fraud Governance Committee, a senior-management-owned governance structure responsible for oversight and control of all aspects of the organisational Counter-Fraud Programme. The framework requires each Member Organization to establish and maintain a CFGC meeting at least quarterly, with minimum responsibility for approving, supporting, communicating and monitoring the Counter-Fraud Programme, Counter-Fraud Policy and management information, sitting beneath ultimate Board responsibility. Relevant when assessing governance adequacy and accountability allocation.

Node on the enterprise-wide Fraud Risk Assessment: identifying fraud risks affecting the organization and its customers, calibrating controls to inherent risk by product and service, testing control effectiveness and determining residual risk. It must be refreshed periodically and on material change in the internal or external fraud risk environment (new products, digital platforms, acquisitions, newly identified threats), and links to Fraud Risk Appetite and KRI monitoring. Binds SAMA Member Organizations and underpins the risk-based scaling of counter-fraud controls.

This node marks the superseded SAMA circular No. 42056371 (dated 10-08-1442H) within the updated Trade Repository Reporting and Risk Mitigation Requirements for OTC Derivative Contracts (v4.0, September 2025), which replaces it with effect from 1 February 2026. It is relevant for dating obligations and determining which text governs a transaction before and after the effective date. The superseding instrument binds banks licensed in KSA, including locally incorporated banks, their financial subsidiaries and SPVs, and SAMA-licensed foreign bank branches.

The consolidated SAMA Requirements for OTC derivative contracts, split into Section A (reporting of reportable OTC derivative transactions to the SAMA-authorised Trade Repository Operator) and Section B (risk mitigation for non-centrally cleared OTC derivatives). Scope covers interest rate, FX, equity, credit and commodity derivatives, with reporting allocated to the KSA-side counterparty; centrally cleared transactions (directly or via indirect/client clearing) fall outside the risk mitigation requirements. Binds all banks in KSA with OTC derivative transactions, regardless of notional size or hedging purpose.

Valuation provisions within the risk mitigation section for non-centrally cleared OTC derivatives: banks must be able to value transactions internally, corroborate counterparty or third-party valuations, use mainstream-accepted models (justifying any new methodology), and periodically review and document the agreed valuation process. Banks must also agree and document fallback valuation approaches where inputs fail, procedures for modifying the process, and how valuation disputes are resolved. Binds banks that are contracting parties to non-centrally cleared OTC derivative transactions.

Sets the requirement for banks to agree, document and implement portfolio reconciliation processes with financial and non-financial counterparties for non-centrally cleared OTC derivatives, ensuring material terms are exchanged and valuations (including variation margin) reconciled at regular intervals. Scope and frequency must be calibrated to the counterparty's risk exposure profile, size, volatility and number of outstanding transactions. Binds banks entering non-centrally cleared OTC derivative transactions.

Requires banks to assess, by reference to risk exposure profile, size, volatility and number of outstanding transactions, whether to undertake portfolio compression with counterparties, and to maintain policies and procedures for regular assessment and engagement in compression of non-centrally cleared OTC derivative portfolios, proportionate to activity. Related reporting fields on collateralisation (including collateral portfolio and initial margin posted) appear in the reporting data tables. Binds banks holding non-centrally cleared OTC derivative portfolios.

Requires banks to agree and document with counterparties the mechanism for identifying when discrepancies in material terms or valuations constitute disputes and how such disputes are resolved as soon as practicable, with material disputes escalated to senior management and the Board under clear criteria. Sits within Section B risk mitigation alongside reconciliation, compression and governance provisions. Binds banks that are parties to non-centrally cleared OTC derivative transactions.

A SAMA circular (Arabic) notifying all SAMA-supervised financial institutions that the Central Bank has approved the official holiday schedule and working hours for financial institutions and for the Saudi Real Time Gross Settlement system for the coming four Hijri years (1447–1450H), published on SAMA's website. It binds supervised institutions to observe the published holiday dates and working-hour instructions, to notify SAMA in advance of branches operating during official holidays, and to announce those branches appropriately. Issued under SAMA's Law (Royal Decree M/36).

The consolidated SAMA requirements (version 4.0, September 2025) governing over-the-counter derivative contracts, issued under SAMA's Law and the Banking Control Law. Section A imposes trade reporting to the SAMA-authorised Trade Repository Operator; Section B imposes risk mitigation obligations on banks that are contracting parties to non-centrally cleared OTC derivatives, regardless of notional size or hedging purpose, with centrally and indirectly cleared trades excluded. It binds banks licensed in KSA (including foreign bank branches and, for reporting scope, financial subsidiaries/SPVs), supersedes the 1442H circular, and takes effect 1 February 2026.

A reporting data-field concept within the OTC derivatives requirements covering product and trade identification: product identifier type (ISIN or Unique Product Identifier under ISO 4914), CFI classification, the internally generated unique trade identifier, and the Unique Transaction Identifier. It defines who generates each identifier (generally the reporting counterparty, but potentially a CCP, clearing member or electronic confirmation platform in cross-border or cleared trades) and how identifiers must be structured and communicated in time to meet reporting deadlines. Relevant to reporting banks completing the SAMA Trade Repository templates.

Describes the role of the SAMA-authorised Trade Repository Operator as the mandatory destination for OTC derivative trade reports and the contractual/operational conditions attaching to it. Reporting banks must report directly (no agents or outsourcing to third-party providers), sign a reporting service agreement containing consent for counterparties to report their trade data, complete electronic system linkages and user testing, and use the Trade Repository's prescribed templates. Binds all banks in KSA with reportable OTC derivative transactions.

Section A of the OTC derivatives requirements: the obligation on all banks in KSA with OTC derivative transactions to report reportable transactions to the SAMA-authorised Trade Repository, directly and electronically, at execution and on subsequent life-cycle events. It covers the manner of reporting, the reporting service agreement and consent clause, template completion, and life-cycle event handling such as new trades pending a counterparty-generated trade ID, modifications, novations and terminations (action types N, M, C), including the T+1 submission deadline.

Section B of the OTC derivatives requirements, imposing specified risk mitigation obligations on banks that are contracting parties to non-centrally cleared OTC derivative transactions, applying regardless of outstanding notional amount or whether the trade is for hedging. Centrally cleared trades, whether directly or through indirect client-clearing arrangements, fall outside these obligations. Related reportable data points include confirmation timestamps, master agreement type and version, settlement and early termination dates.

A SAMA circular (1446H) imposing periodic reporting obligations on digital brokerage companies licensed by SAMA: quarterly financial statements with the auditor's report within 20 working days of March, June and September quarter-ends, and audited annual financial statements within 45 working days of calendar year-end. It also sets deadlines and format requirements for quarterly and annual prudential data returns on SAMA's approved templates, submitted in Excel with a signed data certification form (Chief Accountant, CFO and CEO/Managing Director), with annual prudential templates first reviewed by the external auditor. Effective from the second quarter of 2025.

A SAMA-issued FAQ document accompanying the Rules for Issuing and Operating Credit Cards, circulated to banks and finance companies as non-binding guidance. It explains, in question-and-answer form, issuance conditions (documented customer request, notification timelines, re-issued and supplementary cards, minimum age), and fee/cost treatment (annual fees only after activation, late payment fees, international purchase fees, no term-cost increase on default, grace period, treatment of cash advances, transfers and e-wallet top-ups). It is interpretive only and yields to the Rules and other applicable regulations in case of conflict.

The underlying SAMA Rules for Issuing and Operating Credit Cards (notified by earlier SAMA circular), which govern how issuers—banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom—may issue, re-issue and operate credit cards and charge fees. Substantive points reflected here include the need for a documented customer request, notice of acceptance/rejection with reasons and objection route, supplementary cardholder identification and verification, an 18 (Hijri) year minimum age, restrictions on annual fees before activation, a minimum statement grace period, and prohibitions on increasing the agreed term cost due to late payment or default. The FAQ node is guidance on these Rules; the Rules themselves are the binding reference.
lookup_terms: Rules for Issuing and Operating Credit Cards

data.summary: SAMA's Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking, issued under the SAMA Law and the Banking Control Law, setting supervisory expectations for managing risks specific to Shari'ah compliant activities (credit, market, operational, liquidity and equity investment risk). It allocates board/delegated committee and senior management responsibilities, requires an independent risk management function, and mandates processes for identifying, measuring, mitigating, monitoring and reporting such risks, integrated with the bank's overall risk framework. It applies to all domestic banks licensed by SAMA conducting Shari'ah compliant banking, including majority-owned banking subsidiaries and branches, and supersedes the 2021 version.
lookup_terms: Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking
Banking Control Law licensed domestic banks

data.summary: The Shari'ah Governance Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking (SAMA, February 2020), referenced as the companion instrument to be read alongside the Risk Management Framework. It underpins the role of the bank's Shari'ah Committee, the Shari'ah compliance and Shari'ah audit functions, and the requirement that products, contracts and activities comply at all times with approved Shari'ah rules and principles. Relevant here for the allocation of assurance roles over Shari'ah non-compliance risk and the treatment of reputational risk from Shari'ah non-compliance.

The PSIAs Rules (SAMA, September 2022) governing profit sharing investment accounts, cross-referenced by the Risk Management Framework for Shari'ah Compliant Banking. Banks offering PSIAs must monitor that account holders' funds are used in line with agreed terms, comply with the PSIAs Rules' risk management requirements, and adopt a formal policy addressing conflicting roles, fiduciary and agency duties, fair treatment of fund providers, and allocation of assets and profits between the bank and PSIA holders across investment periods. Liquidity policies and reporting must cover current accounts and PSIAs individually and in aggregate.

This is SAMA's Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements (Version 1.0, April 2025), issued under the Saudi Central Bank Law and circulated to finance companies and payment service providers operating in the Kingdom. It sets risk-based control requirements across counter-fraud governance and risk management, prevention, detection, response, counter-fraud technology, and additional controls for products and services of elevated fraud risk, with board-level accountability, a quarterly Counter-Fraud Governance Committee, and coordination between counter-fraud, cyber security and financial crime functions. The covering circular imposes a compliance pathway: gap assessment and board-approved roadmap submitted by end July 2025, quarterly status reporting from Q3 2025, full compliance by early 2026, and an internal audit compliance report by end Q2 2026, backed by SAMA inspection visits.

This node captures the earlier Anti-Fraud Rules for Finance Companies issued by SAMA circular no. 381000103246, which governed fraud prevention and control obligations of licensed finance companies. Per the covering circular to the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements, these rules are replaced by the new framework with effect from 1 April 2026, so they remain the operative standard for finance companies only until that date. Researchers should treat this as a superseded instrument and check the transition date when assessing which obligations applied at a given time.
lookup_terms: قواعد مكافحة الاحتيال في شركات التمويل

data.summary: Concept node for the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA), the statutory regulator established under the Saudi Central Bank Law (Royal Decree M/36), which licenses, supervises and issues binding rules, circulars and frameworks for banks, finance companies, payment service providers, electronic money institutions and other supervised financial institutions. Its powers also derive from sectoral laws such as the Finance Companies Control Law and the Law of Payments and Payment Services and their implementing regulations. SAMA additionally conducts inspections, sets supervisory reporting requirements, and takes enforcement action against non-compliant institutions.
lookup_terms: Saudi Central Bank Law Royal Decree M/36

data.summary: A SAMA circular addressed to finance companies operating in the Kingdom, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law (Royal Decree M/51) and its Implementing Regulation. It reiterates the obligation to exercise due diligence before granting finance, proportionate to the potential risks, including verifying the authenticity of income-supporting documents submitted by the customer and strengthening internal procedures to that effect. It is a supervisory reminder rather than a new rulebook, but it is enforceable against finance companies as part of responsible-lending and affordability obligations.

A SAMA circular launching Phase 1 of the centralised Complaint Management System for all financial institutions under SAMA supervision, issued under the Saudi Central Bank Law and SAMA's consumer-protection mandate. It requires complaints to be handled end-to-end through the system within fixed periods (five business days at level one, three business days for customer-escalated level-two complaints, and two business days to respond to SAMA requests on accepted escalations), and sets quarterly KPIs covering complaint handling quality, escalation rates, timeliness, response quality, repeat complainants and requests for missing documents. Institutions must resource and empower their customer care units, align internal policies, service level agreements and escalation mechanisms; SAMA will monitor compliance and take action against non-compliant institutions from Q4 2025.

A SAMA circular to payment service providers permitting electronic money institutions to contract with CMA-licensed capital market institutions to distribute units of publicly offered investment funds through their e-wallet applications. It sets conditions: public offerings only, prior notification to SAMA with confirmation that internal policies have been updated, compliance with the Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services (including licensing conditions and limits), due diligence on the products, contractual allocation of liability and risk to the CMA-licensed institution, an EMI role limited to distribution and document completion without opening investment accounts, subscription-only functionality with no redemption or cancellation, and completion of subscription only after the capital market institution confirms suitability to the customer. It also stresses segregation between payment activities and investment activities and the EMI's continuing responsibility for legal and technical soundness of its services.
lookup_terms: Law of Payments and Payment Services Implementing Regulation
segregation of payment and investment activities

data.summary: Section B of SAMA's OTC derivatives framework setting risk-mitigation duties for non-centrally cleared OTC derivative contracts: trading relationship documentation must give legal certainty, capture all material rights and obligations (payment, netting, default/termination, transfer, governing law, confirmation/valuation/reconciliation/dispute processes, credit support and margin arrangements), be executed in writing or in non-rewritable, non-erasable electronic form, and be retained for at least ten years after termination. It further requires timely two-way trade confirmation of material terms (including novations and subsequent amendments) and agreement with counterparties on valuation processes. Binds SAMA-licensed banks dealing in non-centrally cleared OTC derivatives with financial and non-financial counterparties.

Appendix A Table 1 of the SAMA OTC derivatives reporting requirements, specifying the counterparty-identification fields a reporting bank must populate when submitting reportable transactions to the SAMA-authorised trade repository (reporting and other counterparty IDs, country of counterparty, broker and clearing member IDs). It sits within the reporting regime that obliges banks to report directly (no agents or outsourcing), to sign a reporting service agreement including a data-consent clause, and to pass user testing before live reporting. Binds SAMA-licensed reporting banks.

Appendix A Table 2 of the SAMA OTC derivatives reporting requirements, covering the common/transaction-level data fields (e.g. internal unique trade ID, notional, early termination date, action type) used for reporting reportable transactions and their subsequent business events to the SAMA-authorised trade repository. It is applied through a life-cycle approach with a T+1 reporting deadline (Fridays, Saturdays and KSA holidays excluded) and record-keeping sufficient to demonstrate compliance. Binds SAMA-licensed reporting banks.

Defines the identification standard used across the SAMA OTC derivatives reporting templates: parties, brokers and clearing members are identified by a 20-character ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier, with prescribed client-code fallbacks for natural persons (national ID or country code plus national ID) and for KSA corporates without an LEI (country code plus commercial registration number). Country of the other counterparty is reported using ISO 3166 two-character codes. Binds reporting banks completing trade repository submissions.

Sets out the trade identifier convention for SAMA trade repository reporting: pending a global UTI, an internal unique trade identifier must be generated (prefix plus the generating entity's LEI plus a unique code), unique to each OTC derivative contract and unchangeable once reported. Where the other counterparty is international, or where a CCP, clearing member or electronic confirmation platform is agreed as generating entity, that entity generates the UTI and must communicate it in time for the reporting counterparty to meet its deadline. Binds reporting banks and shapes their arrangements with foreign counterparties and clearing infrastructure.

Explains the action-type codes and life-cycle reporting scenarios for OTC derivative transactions reported to the SAMA-authorised trade repository: new trades (N), modifications (M) including late population of a UTI and notional increases/decreases, terminations/early terminations (C), and error reports (E) to eliminate erroneous submissions, each keyed to a previously reported internal unique trade ID. It also frames the scope of reportable transactions, including novations for central clearing and booking transfers into a KSA branch, while excluding spot FX, interbranch and intrabranch transactions. Binds SAMA-licensed reporting banks.
lookup_terms: action type N M C E

data.summary: A data-field specification (Table 3, "Evolutive Field – Common Data") within SAMA's trade repository reporting and risk mitigation requirements for OTC derivative contracts, setting out the collateral-related attributes a reporting bank must populate. It covers the collateralisation status of the contract (uncollateralised, partially, one-way or fully collateralised), portfolio collateralisation and portfolio code, initial and variation margin posted/received, excess collateral, and the ISO currency codes and character/decimal formats for each. It binds banks subject to the OTC derivatives reporting obligation when submitting trade data to the SAMA-authorised trade repository operator.

The operative reporting rules for OTC derivative contracts, covering the manner, timing, correction and record-keeping of submissions to the SAMA-authorised trade repository (TR). Key obligations: banks must report directly (no agents or outsourcing to third-party service providers), must sign a reporting service agreement containing counterparty-consent wording, must complete system linkage and user testing before acceptance, must report all template fields, must apply a life-cycle approach to business events (including re-reporting novated trades as early termination with a Linked UTI), and must report by 23:59:59 on T+1 (excluding Fridays, Saturdays and KSA public holidays). It binds reporting banks; limited relief exists where a trade is cancelled or fully terminated within the T+1 window, except where cancellation is for central clearing.

SAMA's recalibrated standardised interest rate shock scenarios for interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB), prescribing six shocks for economic value of equity (EVE) — parallel up/down, steepener, flattener, short-rate up/down — and two for net interest income (NII). It specifies currency-specific absolute shock sizes in basis points (including SAR 275/375/250 parallel/short/long), the parameterisation formulas and decay scalar (x = 4) for short, long and rotational shocks, a zero floor on post-shock rates, and worked examples. It binds banks with material IRRBB positions in each relevant currency, applied per currency.
lookup_terms: parallel steepener flattener short rate shock

data.summary: A concept node marking the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision framework as the source standard underlying SAMA's recalibrated IRRBB shock scenarios. It is not itself a SAMA instrument but signals that the prescribed six-scenario EVE / two-scenario NII approach, currency-specific shock magnitudes and shaping formulas follow the Basel IRRBB standard as adopted and adjusted by SAMA. Relevant to banks reconciling SAMA requirements with international prudential standards.
lookup_terms: interest rate risk in the banking book

data.summary: A SAMA circular (1447) requiring financial institutions under SAMA supervision to supply the customer's approved National Address (as registered with Saudi Post – SPL) to postal service providers when requesting delivery of documents relating to financial products and services. It follows a General Transport Authority decision obliging postal operators to refuse shipments not addressed by National Address from 1 January 2026, and confirms that the National Address is the primary and fundamental reference for identifying customer addresses. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA and applies alongside related SAMA instructions on residence and work address data.
lookup_terms: postal service providers delivery of documents

data.summary: A SAMA circular directing all financing entities to share individuals' residential real estate finance data with the Saudi Credit Bureau (SIMAH), in line with guidance and templates to be issued by SAMA. It is grounded in the SAMA Law, the Credit Information Law, the Banking Control Law and the Finance Companies Control Law, and is aimed at credit-sector data integration, transparency and credit-risk assessment. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom, real estate finance companies and credit information companies, and must be applied consistently with SAMA and other regulators' instructions and the Personal Data Protection Law; effective from its date.
lookup_terms: residential real estate finance data sharing

data.summary: First edition of SAMA's General Rules for Hosting and Sponsoring Events, setting minimum requirements a supervised Financial Institution must meet when hosting or sponsoring conferences, forums, seminars and similar gatherings inside or outside the Kingdom. It covers board-approved event policy, documentation and annual board reporting, conduct obligations of representatives (confidentiality, avoidance of political/sensitive topics, no binding commitments without express authority), and due diligence on event content, participants, sponsors and speakers. Binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision; it excludes temporary offices opened for marketing/product display, which fall under separate SAMA instructions, and has been superseded by the second edition.
lookup_terms: General Rules for Hosting and Sponsoring Events

data.summary: Second edition (2025) of SAMA's event rules, renamed General Rules for Participation in Events, updating and replacing the first edition. It broadens the defined term "Participation in an Event" to cover full or partial hosting, sponsorship, and presence via a "temporary booth/stand" for institutional promotion and marketing, and exempts such temporary-stand presence from the SAMA no-objection requirement; it applies to participation in any event for any purpose, inside or outside the Kingdom, directly or through a third party. Retains board-approved policy, file documentation and annual board reporting, conduct duties of representatives, and risk assessment/due diligence obligations. Binds all SAMA-licensed and supervised financial institutions.
lookup_terms: General Rules for Participation in Events

data.summary: SAMA's Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules (first edition, 2025), issuing minimum mandatory obligations for implementing UNSC-based TFS regimes on terrorism/terrorist financing and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and its financing. It defines Financial Institution, targeted financial sanctions, sanctions lists, designated persons and funds/assets, and structures obligations across governance, screening, list management, alert escalation, freezing and unfreezing, recordkeeping, and training. Binds all financial institutions subject to SAMA supervision, requires board-level presentation and allocation of responsibilities, and replaces the earlier SAMA circulars on UNSC implementation mechanisms.
lookup_terms: UN Security Council resolutions قرارات مجلس الأمن

data.summary: Chapter Three of the Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules, covering screening procedures and controls that financial institutions must apply against sanctions lists. It sits within the mandatory TFS framework alongside governance, list management, alert escalation and freezing chapters, and determines when and against what populations screening obligations arise. Binds all financial institutions under SAMA regulation and supervision.
lookup_terms: قواعد العقوبات المالية المستهدفة الفصل الثالث

data.summary: Chapter Four of the Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules, addressing management of the sanctions lists issued under the UNSC terrorism-financing and proliferation-financing implementation mechanisms. It governs how financial institutions must obtain, update and maintain list data used for screening and freezing decisions. Binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA.
lookup_terms: sanctions lists management إدارة قوائم العقوبات

data.summary: Chapter Five of the Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules, governing how screening alerts and potential matches are handled, reviewed and escalated internally, and flagged to SAMA. It links to the freezing/unfreezing chapter, since confirmed matches trigger immediate asset-freezing and notification duties. Binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision.
lookup_terms: immediate reporting to SAMA الإبلاغ الفوري

data.summary: This node covers the freezing and unfreezing chapter of SAMA's Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS) Rules, which set the minimum obligations financial institutions must meet when a match to a designated person or entity is identified. It governs the without-delay freezing of funds and other assets, the prohibition on making funds or assets available directly or indirectly to listed persons, and the procedural route for lifting a freeze (including de-listing and false-positive resolution) under the UN Security Council mechanisms adopted in the Kingdom. It binds all financial institutions regulated and supervised by SAMA, with board and senior management accountability expressly required.

Concept node for the Saudi Anti-Money Laundering Law, the statutory foundation cross-referenced by multiple SAMA instructions (TFS rules, AML/CTF guidance and related circulars). It establishes the ML offence, the obligations of financial institutions on customer due diligence, record keeping, suspicious transaction reporting and internal AML programmes, and the supervisory/penalty framework. It binds financial institutions and DNFBPs, with SAMA acting as supervisor for the entities under its remit.

Concept node for FATF Recommendations 6 and 7, the international standards on targeted financial sanctions for terrorism/terrorist financing (R.6) and for proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and its financing (R.7). They require countries and their financial institutions to implement UN Security Council designations without delay through asset freezing and prohibitions on providing funds or services to listed persons. They are not directly binding in themselves; they are given domestic force through the Kingdom's UNSCR implementation mechanisms and SAMA's TFS Rules.

Duplicate publication of SAMA's Targeted Financial Sanctions Rules (First Edition), setting the minimum requirements for implementing UN Security Council sanctions on counter-terrorism/terrorist financing and on preventing WMD proliferation and its financing. The Rules cover definitions, governance and institutional responsibilities, screening controls, sanctions list management, alert handling and escalation, freezing/unfreezing, record keeping, and training. They apply mandatorily to all SAMA-supervised financial institutions and supersede the earlier SAMA circulars on UNSCR implementation guidance.

This is SAMA's Financial Institutions Service Fee Guide (First Edition), which sets the tariff framework financial institutions must observe when charging for services and products, including fees for basic retail services (e.g. certificates of relationship, debt/liability confirmations, account statements, clearance letters) and criteria for setting product and service fees. It overrides conflicting provisions in earlier instructions, including the previously updated banking tariff. It binds all persons, natural or legal, subject to SAMA's supervision, in their dealings with customers.

This node covers the administrative-fee amendments issued alongside the Service Fee Guide, which revise Article 9 of the Consumer Finance Controls, the relevant conduct rule in the Principles and Rules of Financial Consumer Protection, and the administrative-fee clause of the standard-form individual consumer finance contract. The effect is that banks and finance companies must charge administrative fees only in line with SAMA's fee instructions, may not deduct them before contract signature (with a carve-out for real estate valuation costs after preliminary approval), and remain subject to a ceiling expressed as the lower of a fixed riyal amount or a percentage of the finance amount, excluding taxes. It binds financiers (banks and finance companies) dealing with individual consumers.
lookup_terms: Principles and Rules for Financial Consumer Protection

data.summary: Despite the label, this node is SAMA's covering circular and Financial Institutions Service Fee Guide (first issue, Rajab 1447H), setting the tariff framework financial institutions must observe when charging for services and products, plus amendments to three administrative-fee provisions: Article 9 of the Consumer Finance Regulations, Specific Conduct Rule 1 of the Principles and Rules for Financial Consumer Protection, and Article 11.1 of the standard individual consumer finance contract. It defines Financial Institution, Customer, documented channels, and standard documents (identification certificate, debt/no-liability letters, account statement), and caps combined administrative fees and costs at the lower of SAR 5,000 or 1% of the finance amount, excluding taxes. It binds all entities supervised and regulated by SAMA, with effect within a stated period from publication on SAMA's website, and overrides conflicting provisions.
lookup_terms: Principles and Rules for Financial Consumer Protection

data.summary: Duplicate instance of the Financial Institutions Service Fee Guide circular: the guide itself (general provisions, tariff for basic services to individual customers, criteria for setting fees, final provisions) together with the amended administrative-fee texts in the Consumer Finance Regulations, the Financial Consumer Protection conduct rules, and the standard individual consumer finance contract. Key operative content is the requirement to follow SAMA's administrative fee instructions, the bar on deducting administrative fees before contract signature (with a real estate appraisal exception after preliminary approval), and the fee ceiling of the lower of SAR 5,000 or 1% of the finance amount. Binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions, including banks and finance companies.

SAMA circular and the amended Implementing (Executive) Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law (Rajab 1447H / December 2025), issued under the Law promulgated by Royal Decree M/51. It sets the definitional and supervisory framework for the finance sector — defining finance activities, finance contract, instalment, term cost, total cost of financing, finance amount, annual percentage rate, board and senior management, exposure and large exposure, and influential shareholding — and confirms SAMA's mandate to regulate and supervise finance companies. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom, SAMA-licensed digital brokerage companies, and licensed debt collection entities.
lookup_terms: اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مراقبة شركات التمويل

data.summary: Licensing-focused view of the amended Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law. It frames the single-activity licence categories — micro consumer finance company, Buy Now Pay Later (deferred payment) company, debt crowdfunding company and micro finance company — each licensed to conduct only that finance activity, and ties permitted activities to those listed in Article 10 of the Law or otherwise approved by SAMA. Relevant to any entity seeking or holding a SAMA finance licence, including BNPL providers whose activity is defined as financing a beneficiary's purchase of goods or services from merchants with no term cost charged to the beneficiary.

Node covering the repeal and absorption of the standalone micro finance and micro consumer finance regimes: the circular cancels the Rules for Practising Micro Finance Activity and the Rules Regulating Micro Consumer Finance Companies, folding both into the amended Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law. Micro finance and micro consumer finance are now defined activities within the Regulation, subject to the controls in its Article 9. Finance companies were granted a transition period (stated in the circular) to align their positions.
lookup_terms: قواعد ممارسة نشاط التمويل متناهي الصغر

data.summary: Another instance of the amended Executive Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law with its issuing circular, covering definitions and general provisions (Part One) and SAMA's regulatory and supervisory role over the finance sector. It carries the key economic and governance definitions used across finance regulation — instalment, term cost, total cost of financing, total amount payable by the beneficiary, APR, senior management, exposure thresholds and influential ownership — and repeals the separate micro finance and micro consumer finance rule sets. Addressed to finance companies, licensed digital brokerage companies and licensed debt collection entities.
lookup_terms: Executive Regulation Finance Companies Control Law

data.summary: This is the amended Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law, issued by SAMA under the Law and circulated in Rajab 1447 (Dec 2025), together with the covering circular that repeals the Microfinance Activity Rules and the Micro Consumer Finance Companies Rules and gives finance companies a transition period to regularise their position. It sets the definitional architecture (finance laws, BNPL company, micro consumer finance company, debt-based crowdfunding company, microfinance company, finance contract, instalment, term cost, total cost of finance, APR, board and senior management, exposure, large exposure, influential holding) and the prudential, licensing, governance and conduct provisions applying to finance activity. It binds finance companies licensed in the Kingdom, and the distribution list also reaches SAMA-licensed digital brokerage companies and licensed debt collection entities.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law
اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مراقبة شركات التمويل

data.summary: Amended SAMA Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities, issued under the SAMA Law and the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation. They define "finance support activities" (support, complement or enable finance activity, expressly including digital brokerage for finance entities but excluding debt collection for finance entities), and set licensing application requirements, minimum capital (SAR 2 million for digital brokerage), fit-and-proper/management conditions, conduct-of-activity obligations, supervision and compliance. They bind any person licensed by SAMA to carry on a finance support activity, notably licensed digital brokerage companies.
lookup_terms: Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities
قواعد الترخيص للنشاطات المساندة لنشاط التمويل

data.summary: Governor's decision and covering circular approving amendments to the Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities, attaching the amended rules text (definitions, licensing conditions, capital, management requirements, conduct of activity, supervision and compliance). Substantively it carries the same rule set as the amended Licensing Rules node and is the instrument evidencing the amendment and its effective date. Addressed to SAMA-licensed digital brokerage companies.
lookup_terms: amendment to Finance Support Activities licensing rules

data.summary: SAMA circular prohibiting finance entities from requesting promissory notes or any commercial paper from individual (retail) customers when offering credit card finance products, issued in response to observed market practice and read alongside the existing instructions on finance entities' dealings with promissory notes and the Responsible Lending Principles for Individuals. It requires internal policies, procedures and controls to be updated, applies from 1 February 2026, and obliges firms to submit a remediation plan to SAMA's Consumer Protection Supervision Department within 30 days covering return or cancellation of previously obtained instruments, executed within six months. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular revising the framework for outsourcing collection of bank and finance company debts. It cancels the earlier circulars that had confined such outsourcing to debt collection entities licensed by SAMA and the related transitional deadlines, and instead permits contracting with entities meeting the requirements set out in the applicable laws, regulations and instructions, subject to obtaining SAMA's no-objection letter and without prejudice to the outsourcing rules and other relevant instructions. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom and SAMA-licensed debt collection entities.

SAMA circular raising the cap in Article 22(1) of the Rules for Regulating BNPL Companies on total outstanding finance per individual customer from SAR 5,000 to SAR 10,000, exercising the express power in that provision to increase or decrease the amount. The circular confirms that all other provisions and requirements continue to apply, including the debt-burden ratios under the Responsible Lending Principles for Individuals. It binds banks, finance companies and BNPL companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: buy now pay later limit increase

data.summary: This node covers SAMA's adoption of the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMIs) as the substantive benchmark in its Oversight Framework for Payment Systems and their Operators. It explains that SAMA supervises on a principles-based approach, applying both the regulatory framework and the PFMIs (April 2012 and later amendments), supported by the CPSS-IOSCO Disclosure Framework and SAMA's guidance manual on payment system compliance with the PFMIs. It binds licensed payment system operators (PSOs) of both systemically important payment systems (SIPS) and non-classified systems operating in or across the borders of the Kingdom.

The Law of Payments and Payment Services (Royal Decree M/16) and its Implementing Regulation are the statutory basis making SAMA the competent authority for regulating, supervising and overseeing payment systems, payment service providers and their operators in the Kingdom. It underpins licensing of payment institutions and e-money institutions, classification of payment systems, and SAMA's power to issue supervisory frameworks and standards. It binds any person operating a payment system or providing payment services in Saudi Arabia.
lookup_terms: Law of Payments and Payment Services

data.summary: "Self-Assessment" is a defined term in SAMA's Oversight Framework for Payment Systems and their Operators: an assessment carried out by the payment system operator itself to determine its degree of compliance with the PFMIs. It is one of the supervisory tools set out in the framework's supervisory methodology, alongside supervisory assessment. It applies to operators of payment systems licensed by SAMA.

"Supervisory Assessment" is a defined term in SAMA's Oversight Framework for Payment Systems and their Operators: an independent assessment conducted by SAMA to measure a payment system's compliance with the applicable regulatory frameworks and relevant international principles. It is the regulator-side counterpart to the operator's self-assessment within the framework's supervisory methodology. It applies to payment systems and their operators subject to SAMA oversight.

SAMA's Guidelines to Apply for a Payment Service Providers License set out the regulatory procedures, documentation and conduct expected of applicants seeking authorisation to provide payment services. They describe the two-stage process (in-principle approval, then final licensing) and the four available licence categories: Micro and Major Electronic Money Institution (e-wallet) and Micro and Major Payment Institution. They bind prospective PSP applicants and are read together with the Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services.

The Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services is the subordinate instrument containing the licensing articles and the substantive requirements for engaging in payment activities and providing payment services, including the Article 8 regulatory requirements referenced for in-principle approval. It defines the licence categories (Micro/Major EMI and Micro/Major PI) and the conditions for commencing activity after licensing. It binds applicants for, and holders of, SAMA payment services licences.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services

data.summary: SAMA circular and attached rules (first edition, Sha'ban 1444H / March 2023) setting the minimum standards and procedures financial institutions must observe when advertising any product or service. It defines key terms (Financial Institution, Customer, Consumer, Products and Services, Advertisement, Medium) and requires due care over advertising content, alongside compliance with sectoral laws (banking control, insurance, finance companies, real estate finance, leasing, payments) and media-content rules. It binds all entities supervised by SAMA, effective from the circular date.

Rules on outsourcing for finance companies, approved by Governor's decision and circulated in 1440H (Dec 2018), issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation. They define outsourcing, external service provider and material functions, and impose board-approved outsourcing policy, annually updated, risk assessment at contracting and renewal, due diligence on the provider's licensing and capability, non-delegable responsibility for provider compliance, record retention, protection/retrieval or destruction of beneficiary data, and SAMA/external auditor access rights. They bind finance companies licensed by SAMA.

Third edition (Dhu al-Qi'dah 1442H / June 2021) of SAMA's Key Principles of Governance for financial institutions under its supervision, replacing the earlier bank governance principles and mandatory from 01/01/2022. It sets definitions (Financial Institution, Board, Senior/Executive Management, executive, non-executive and independent member, relatives, major shareholders, related parties) and seven principles covering board qualifications, composition and appointment, board and executive management responsibilities, board committees, shareholder rights, and disclosure and transparency, with an annex on money exchange sector governance. It binds local banks, finance/real estate refinance/leasing-registration and finance-support companies, money exchangers, payment and fintech companies and credit bureaus — insurance and reinsurance companies are excluded.

Principle 1 of SAMA's Key Principles of Governance, addressing the qualifications required of board members of supervised financial institutions. It operates alongside the definitional chapter's independence tests (shareholding of 5% or more, family ties, recent employment or dealings, remuneration thresholds, competing business, more than nine years' tenure, credit exposure above one million riyals). Relevant to fit-and-proper assessment of directors in banks, finance companies, money exchangers, payment/fintech firms and credit bureaus (insurance excluded).

Principle 3 of SAMA's Key Principles of Governance, setting out the responsibilities of the board of directors of financial institutions supervised by SAMA, read together with Principle 4 on executive management and Principle 5 on board committees. Used to identify where accountability for strategy, internal control, risk and compliance oversight sits at board level. Binds boards of supervised institutions other than insurance and reinsurance companies.

Concept node on the audit committee as a board committee of SAMA-supervised financial institutions, drawing on the Key Principles of Governance (Principle 5 on board committees) and a related SAMA instrument on audit committees. Relevant to committee formation, membership and independence, and its mandate over internal audit, external auditor relations and financial reporting oversight. Applies to boards of institutions supervised by SAMA, excluding insurance and reinsurance.

SAMA circular (ref. 472039028, dated 08/07/1447H) announcing the Central Bank's decision to abolish the licensing requirement for carrying out debt collection activity on behalf of finance entities, issued under the SAMA Law and the Finance Companies Control Law following approved amendments to the Implementing Regulation and to the licensing rules for finance support activities. It directs entities that already hold a SAMA licence or initial approval for this activity to comply with the applicable rules on updating their activity in the commercial register. Addressed to banks, finance companies operating in the Kingdom, and SAMA-licensed debt collection entities.
lookup_terms: Finance Companies Control Law Implementing Regulation

data.summary: SAMA circular (ref. 472039139, dated 09/07/1447H) extending mandatory application of the Key Principles of Governance for financial institutions supervised by SAMA (originally issued by earlier circular) to all finance companies and payment service providers.
