It prescribes a compliance pathway: a current-state governance gap assessment, a board/managers-approved roadmap, submission of both to the designated SAMA compliance mailbox within the stated deadline, and full compliance within one year of the circular or at the end of the sitting board's term, whichever is earlier, with SAMA able to extend on justified grounds.

SAMA guide (with covering circular) on assessing business risks related to money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing, issued under the SAMA Law, the AML Law and the Law on Combating Terrorism Crimes and its Financing. It sets the minimum factors, criteria and controls a financial institution must consider when conducting its enterprise-wide business risk assessment, covers definitions, governance and institutional responsibility, and the stages of the assessment, while expressly not imposing a single mandatory methodology nor limiting other AML/CFT/CPF obligations. Binding on all financial institutions subject to SAMA regulation and supervision from the date of publication on SAMA's website.
lookup_terms: customer, product delivery channel and geographic risk

data.summary: Duplicate version of the SAMA business risk assessment guide for money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks, with the same covering circular and content. It defines key risk terms, allocates governance responsibility to the financial institution, and sets out the stages and minimum factors of the enterprise-wide business risk assessment without prescribing one standard methodology. Binding on all financial institutions supervised by SAMA; consult alongside the parallel node to confirm which version is authoritative.

Extract from SAMA's supervisory/oversight framework for payment systems and their operators, stating that SAMA is the competent authority for regulating, supervising and overseeing payment systems and operators in the Kingdom under the relevant law and its implementing regulation. It frames oversight as monitoring and assessing existing and planned systems against safety and efficiency objectives and setting controls and standards aligned with the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures. Relevant to operators of payment systems and financial market infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
lookup_terms: safety and efficiency of payment systems

data.summary: SAMA circular issued under Article 14(b) of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business, requiring exchange centres in Makkah, Madinah, King Abdulaziz International Airport and the Hajj city in Jeddah to raise their operational readiness for the Ramadan and Hajj seasons. Annex 1 sets minimum service standards, including sufficient cash and currency availability, extended working days and hours over the seasons and Eid holidays, crowd and queue management, staff identification and shift rosters, prominent and system-linked exchange-rate display, customer-rights signage, card/electronic payment acceptance, functioning CCTV, adequate security staffing, counterfeit-detection equipment and handling, mapped and bilingually named premises, and notification to SAMA.
lookup_terms: Rules Governing Money Exchange Business Article 14

data.summary: A SAMA circular (Financial Conduct Deputy Governorship) directing supervised financial institutions to establish technical linkage with the Ministry of Commerce's "Watheq" service to verify the identity of beneficial owners of companies using updated official data. It also requires notifying the Ministry of Commerce through the platform where a company has not disclosed a beneficial owner or where discrepancies appear in beneficial ownership information, based on the outcome of the institution's own customer due diligence, without prejudice to suspicious transaction reporting duties or personal data protection requirements; implementation difficulties are to be reported to SAMA's Financial Integrity General Department. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision and takes effect from publication.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Commerce beneficial ownership rules

data.summary: A SAMA circular to banks operating in the Kingdom exempting cheque proceeds payable to families of martyrs from attachment under judicial enforcement orders, building on the Enforcement Law provision listing assets not subject to seizure and SAMA's earlier circular on the updated list of amounts exempt from judicial seizure. It sets the exempt proportion of such cheque amounts that must be released to the customer and conditions availability on a notary-issued declaration, using the attached form. Effective from its date; binds banks handling attachment orders on customer accounts.

A SAMA circular reminding all supervised financial institutions to comply with the Ministry of Interior / Civil Defense regulation on the responsibilities and duties of the fire safety, prevention and protection officer. It highlights appointing or designating a qualified safety officer meeting the prescribed conditions, maintaining and testing fire safety systems, periodic inspection and maintenance, preparing and updating evacuation and emergency plans with drills, and documenting and retaining safety records. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision as an operational safety compliance obligation.

A SAMA circular confirming obligations of finance entities conducting vehicle finance leasing for individuals when determining total economic loss of a leased vehicle. Determinations must rely on reports issued by appraisal firms licensed by the Saudi Authority for Accredited Valuers, applying the total-loss provision of the Finance Lease Law together with the comprehensive insurance controls for individually finance-leased vehicles and the standard vehicle finance lease contract form; on notice of damage to the leased asset, the finance entity must exercise due care with all relevant parties to preserve the lessee's continued use before treating the vehicle as a total economic loss. Binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

Concept node for the Finance Lease Law and its Implementing Regulation, cited as the statutory basis for SAMA's instructions on finance-leased vehicles. The circular invokes the Law's article governing destruction/total loss of the leased asset as the provision to be applied when a finance entity determines total economic loss for an individual's finance-leased vehicle. It governs the rights and obligations of lessors (banks and finance companies) and lessees in finance lease arrangements supervised by SAMA.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulation of the Finance Lease Law
total loss of leased asset article

data.summary: A SAMA circular requiring non-bank financial institutions to notify SAMA in advance of any investment round, within the minimum business-day notice period stated, and to submit all related information — including timetable, purpose, value, impact on ownership structure and financial position, and the type and structure of the investment instrument (equity, convertibles, debt and similar) — plus any supporting or further documents SAMA requests. The notification duty is additional to and does not displace existing obligations, notably obtaining SAMA's prior no-objection where required. It binds finance companies, payment service providers, exchange centres and SAMA-licensed finance support activity firms, effective from its date.

SAMA circular and annexed Responsible Lending Principles for Individuals, issued under SAMA's supervisory powers and read alongside the Banking Control Law, Finance Companies Control Law, Real Estate Finance Law, Finance Lease Law and the consumer/finance customer protection principles. It defines core terms (Financer, Customer as a natural person, amount of finance, term cost, total amount payable, gross salary, total monthly income, monthly credit obligations) and sets creditworthiness-assessment and affordability duties before granting individual finance. It binds banks and finance companies licensed and supervised by SAMA that lend to natural persons.
lookup_terms: gross salary and total monthly income

data.summary: Concept node for the debt burden (deduction) ratios within the Responsible Lending Principles, built on the defined inputs of monthly credit obligations, gross salary and total monthly income drawn from licensed credit bureau reports and the customer's own disclosure. It governs the maximum share of a natural-person customer's income that may be committed to finance repayments. It binds banks and finance companies granting individual finance; note the separate SAMA exemption for BNPL exposures below the stated threshold.

SAMA circular approving the Instructions for Practising Digital Brokerage Activity, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and complementing the Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities. It sets minimum technical, organisational, disclosure, conflict-of-interest, record-keeping and contractual requirements for the licensed entity acting as a digital platform between customers and financing entities, including electronic identification and verification of the customer and validation of financing offers. It binds entities licensed by SAMA to carry out digital brokerage; related instructions (information security, business continuity, customer protection principles) continue to apply.

SAMA circular approving the Rules for Regulating Real Estate Refinance Companies, issued under the Real Estate Finance Law. The rules define the refinance company, real estate financiers, primary and secondary markets and refinance activity, and set requirements on capital adequacy and liquidity, governance, permitted activities, internal organisation, outsourcing, risk management, compliance, internal audit, supervision and secondary-market operations. They bind joint-stock companies licensed by SAMA to conduct real estate refinance activity, which must direct services to real estate financiers unless SAMA issues a no-objection.

Node for the Real Estate Finance Law (Royal Decree M/50, 1433H) and its implementing regulation, the statutory basis for licensing and supervising real estate finance and refinance in the Kingdom. It underpins SAMA's rules on real estate refinance companies and is one of the instruments to be read together with the Responsible Lending Principles. It binds banks and finance companies engaged in real estate finance and the beneficiaries (natural persons) who obtain it.

SAMA circular approving the Rules for Regulating Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) Companies, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law, covering licensing procedures and minimum conduct and operational standards for the activity of financing a customer's purchase of goods or services from merchants with no term cost to the customer. The covering circular also exempts BNPL companies and other finance companies performing BNPL from the debt burden ratios for aggregate finance below the stated threshold, without displacing the remaining Responsible Lending obligations. The rules bind joint-stock companies licensed by SAMA for BNPL activity; other SAMA instruments (leadership appointments, information security, business continuity, customer protection, individual collection rules) continue to apply.

A SAMA circular that eases two conditions on residential real estate finance portfolios sold to the Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company: it permits purchase after a minimum holding period measured from either the financing grant date or receipt of the borrower's first instalment (whichever is earlier) and shortens the recourse period against the originating financier, and it exempts such sales from the prior no-objection requirement under the rules on disposal of finance assets or rights arising from them. The exemption is conditional: financiers remain bound by all statutory periods applicable to the transferred contracts and must notify SAMA of the transaction details within five business days of signing the final sale contract. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom and SRC.
lookup_terms: الشركة السعودية لإعادة التمويل العقاري / SRC

data.summary: Concept node for the Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company, the SAMA-supervised secondary-market entity that purchases residential real estate finance portfolios from banks and finance companies. Related instruments set the conditions for such purchases, including minimum seasoning before sale, the length of the originator's recourse obligation, and relief from the prior no-objection requirement for disposals of finance assets (subject to post-transaction notification to SAMA).

SAMA instructions establishing unified technical fitness-sorting standards for the sixth issue of Saudi banknotes, covering counting and sorting controls, counterfeit detection, material and quality defects, fitness rejection levels, density measurement, quality control, machine sensors and monitoring. They apply to financial institutions as defined for this purpose — banks, cash centres and exchange centres supervised by SAMA — with staggered compliance dates by denomination and a requirement to coordinate with SAMA to obtain specimen notes for machine programming.
lookup_terms: آلات العد والفرز / counting and sorting machines

data.summary: A SAMA circular informing supervised financial institutions of a National Center for Non-Profit Sector service allowing them to query beneficial ownership information for associations and non-profit foundations via the Center's portal. SAMA stresses that the service must be used to complete customer due diligence on non-profit customers; where an undisclosed beneficial owner or discrepancies in beneficial ownership data are found, the institution must apply its CDD measures and the suspicious transaction reporting requirements in the AML/CTF framework, consistent with the Personal Data Protection Law and SAMA instructions, and notify the Center.
lookup_terms: المركز الوطني لتنمية القطاع غير الربحي / NCNP
الإبلاغ عن العمليات المشتبه بها / STR

data.summary: Updated SAMA rules on disclosure of pricing for financing and savings products, replacing the earlier circulars on the same subject. They require standardised disclosure of APR/AER and related terms (finance amount, maturity, monthly instalment, credit card purchase rate and minimum payment, LTV, early repayment charges, deposit amount) using prescribed disclosure tables for individuals and for small and micro enterprises, to enable price comparison. They bind all banks and finance companies licensed and supervised by SAMA, with a short implementation window and a confirmation-of-compliance obligation.
lookup_terms: قواعد الإفصاح عن أسعار المنتجات التمويلية والادخارية
المنشآت الصغيرة ومتناهية الصغر / SMEs and micro enterprises
رسوم السداد المبكر / early repayment charge

data.summary: Defined-term node for the Annual Percentage Rate: the discount rate at which the present value of all instalments and other amounts payable by the beneficiary (the total amount repayable) equals the present value of the finance amounts made available, measured from the date the finance or its first drawdown is available, aligned with the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law. It is the core comparability metric that banks and finance companies must disclose for financing products, and it sits alongside AER for savings and investment products.
lookup_terms: اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مراقبة شركات التمويل

data.summary: Concept node for the board-level Risk Committee as a standing committee required under SAMA's Key Principles of Governance for financial institutions (Principle on board committees), read together with the related governance instrument. It covers the committee's mandate to oversee the risk strategy, appetite and risk management framework, its composition and independence expectations, and its reporting line to the board. Binds boards of SAMA-supervised financial institutions (banks, finance and refinance companies, exchange businesses, payment and fintech companies, credit bureaus), excluding insurers/reinsurers under the governance definition of financial institution.

Concept node for the Nomination and Remuneration Committee as a board committee under SAMA's Key Principles of Governance for financial institutions, supplemented by related SAMA governance/remuneration instruments. It concerns nomination of board and executive candidates, fit-and-proper and independence assessment, board composition and succession, and the design and review of remuneration policy. Binds the boards of SAMA-supervised financial institutions within the governance framework's scope (excluding insurance and reinsurance companies).

Annex to SAMA's Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions (3rd edition, Dhul-Qi'dah 1442H / June 2021) setting sector-specific governance controls for the money exchange sector. It adapts the general board, committee and disclosure principles to exchange companies and establishments, which typically have simpler structures than banks. Binds licensed exchange companies and establishments operating in the Kingdom; the main body of the Principles applies to the wider set of SAMA-supervised financial institutions.
lookup_terms: Key Principles of Governance third edition

data.summary: SAMA instructions (Ramadan 1443H / April 2022, effective 05/09/2022) on how finance entities may deal with and enforce promissory notes taken as security for financing. It sets minimum requirements including a board-approved promissory note policy, steps and authority levels before initiating enforcement, documentation required at execution (financing contract, due note, proof of default and of documented communication with the customer), and responsibilities where enforcement is outsourced to a third party. Binds banks and finance companies supervised by SAMA in their dealings with customers (natural or legal persons) holding a financing product; it does not displace related SAMA instructions on collection, outsourcing, blank promissory notes and standard financing contracts.

SAMA circular and instructions (January 2020) on services provided to persons with disabilities by financial institutions, aimed at financial inclusion, equal access and removal of physical and behavioural barriers so that such customers can manage their finances independently and privately. Requirements cover establishing a dedicated organisational unit, accessible premises and branches, accessible self-service devices and electronic channels, transparency and fairness in dealings, and financial education. Binds all SAMA-supervised financial institutions, including banks, finance companies, insurers/reinsurers, credit bureaus, exchange businesses and payment companies, with a compliance plan required to SAMA.

SAMA principles on conduct and work ethics in financial institutions (August 2019), setting the minimum code-of-conduct standards that each institution's board must adopt in its own policy and cascade to all personnel. Topics include professional conduct, dealings with stakeholders, combating financial and administrative corruption (money laundering, terrorist financing and suspicious transactions; bribery), gifts and hospitality, conflicts of interest, confidentiality and disclosure, misuse of inside information and market manipulation, whistleblowing on actual or potential violations, remuneration and incentives, and consequences of non-compliance. Binds board and committee members, executives, employees (permanent and contracted), consultants and third-party staff of banks, finance and leasing-registration companies, insurers/reinsurers and credit bureaus supervised by SAMA.

Node covering the "Unit" (compliance function/department) as defined and regulated under SAMA's Compliance Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation. It defines the compliance function as reporting directly to the Audit Committee, together with the Compliance Officer and Unit staff, and sets the minimum requirements, key attributes, duties and responsibilities enabling the Unit to operate competently and effectively. It binds SAMA-licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies operating in the Kingdom, without prejudice to other applicable laws (AML, CTF, BNPL, real estate finance, consumer protection, governance).

Node for the Board's duties and responsibilities toward compliance under SAMA's Compliance Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies (Principle One). It addresses the Board's accountability for approving and overseeing compliance policy, embedding a compliance culture across the whole company rather than only the compliance Unit, and allocating responsibilities among Board, Audit Committee, senior management and staff. It binds boards of SAMA-licensed finance and real estate refinance companies.

Node for the Audit Committee's duties and responsibilities toward compliance (Principle Two) under SAMA's Compliance Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies. It matters because the compliance Unit reports directly to the Audit Committee, making the Committee the oversight body for the effectiveness, independence and resourcing of the compliance function. It binds audit committees of SAMA-licensed finance and real estate refinance companies.

Node for the internal audit department's responsibilities toward compliance (Principle Seven) under SAMA's Compliance Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies. It addresses how internal audit provides independent assurance over the compliance function and the company's adherence to laws and SAMA instructions, delineating third-line assurance from the second-line compliance Unit. It binds internal audit departments of SAMA-licensed finance and real estate refinance companies.

The Internal Audit Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies, issued by SAMA under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation and effective after publication on SAMA's website. It defines the internal audit function, the Department, its head and internal auditors, plus independence, objectivity and conflict of interest, and sets principles on the audit charter, policy, annual plan, reporting, external quality assessment, record retention and the relationship with first- and second-line units. It binds SAMA-licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies operating in the Kingdom.

Node for the Board's duties and responsibilities toward the internal audit function (Principle One) under SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies. It covers the Board's role in approving the internal audit charter and safeguarding the function's independence, resourcing and standing relative to the Audit Committee and executive management. It binds boards of SAMA-licensed finance and real estate refinance companies.
lookup_terms: مهام ومسؤوليات المجلس تجاه وظيفة المراجعة الداخلية

data.summary: Technical specification tables from SAMA's branch/facility physical security requirements covering the network video recorder (NVR) server and PTZ IP cameras used in CCTV installations. It sets minimum retention (continuous recorded footage over a defined day range at stated frame rate and resolution), RAID/storage, redundancy, compression, platform and integration (PSIM, ONVIF, open API) parameters, plus PTZ optical/digital zoom, pan-tilt, illumination and environmental tolerances. It binds supervised entities operating branches/facilities in KSA as a physical-security control baseline for their premises surveillance estate.

The camera products section of SAMA's CCTV/physical security requirements, specifying that surveillance cameras be Full HD IP-based, PoE-powered, ONVIF-compliant and supported by an open published API, with detailed design criteria for fixed megapixel cameras and general encoding, streaming, security and time-synchronisation requirements. It also addresses installation conditions: protective/vandal-proof enclosures, outdoor ingress protection ratings, siting for lighting conditions, and lockable racks in secure rooms aligned to branch security zoning. It binds supervised entities (and their contractors) deploying branch surveillance systems in KSA.

SAMA's Financial Sector Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Principles, structured into domains covering core CTI lifecycle principles and strategic CTI, expressed as numbered Principles addressed to Member Organizations. It sets expectations for building an in-house CTI capability (roles, dedicated team, resources, budget, internal and external communication channels) and for identifying an organisation-specific cyber threat landscape including threat actors, vulnerable assets, risks and trends. It applies to SAMA-supervised Member Organizations in the KSA financial sector, with outputs directed at executive management such as the CISO.

Domain 1 of the SAMA CTI Principles, establishing the baseline for planning, collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of threat intelligence around the intelligence lifecycle, plus continuous improvement of CTI capability and performance. Principle 1 requires Member Organizations to define internal CTI roles and responsibilities, stand up a dedicated production and dissemination team with skilled resources, tools and budget, and set communication channels with internal stakeholders and external organisations. It binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.

Domain 2 of the SAMA CTI Principles, covering strategic cyber threat intelligence focused on the objectives, motivations and intent of threat actors, attribution, links between cyber events and the financial sector ecosystem. Principle 12 requires Member Organizations to identify the cyber threat landscape relevant to their organisation and operations, including vulnerable assets, threats, risks, threat actors, observed trends and events that can shift the sector's threat landscape. Strategic output is directed to executive management (e.g. the CISO) for onward relay to IT management and business leaders.

A node indexing the operational cyber threat intelligence portion of the SAMA Financial Sector CTI Principles, sitting alongside the core CTI lifecycle domain and the strategic CTI domain. The supplied context reproduces only Domain 1 (core lifecycle principles, roles and responsibilities) and Domain 2 (strategic CTI and threat landscape identification), so the operational-level principles themselves should be verified in the source document. Like the rest of the instrument, it is addressed to SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.

This is the anti-financial-crime strand of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics for Financial Institutions (circular, August 2019), sitting under the heading on combating financial and administrative corruption crimes alongside anti-bribery. It sets conduct-level expectations that staff avoid, detect and escalate money laundering, terrorist financing and suspicious transactions, complementing (not replacing) the AML/CTF Law and SAMA's AML/CTF rules. It binds all persons associated with a supervised financial institution — board and committee members, executives, permanent and contract employees, consultants and third-party-supplied staff — in banks, insurance/reinsurance and free-zone insurance firms, finance and finance-lease registration companies, and credit information companies, with the board required to adopt a conforming internal code.
lookup_terms: Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics

data.summary: This node covers the confidentiality and information-disclosure strand of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics for Financial Institutions, including the duty to preserve confidentiality, the permitted channels for disclosing information, and the related prohibition on using or leaking inside information to manipulate the market. It operates as a minimum conduct standard, with the institution's board required to adopt a consistent internal policy and managers responsible for staff acknowledgement. It applies to all persons associated with SAMA-supervised banks, insurers, finance companies, finance-lease registration companies and credit information companies.

This node covers the conflict-of-interest strand of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics for Financial Institutions, read together with the adjacent provisions on gifts and hospitality, compliance with laws and internal policies, reporting actual or potential violations, and remuneration and incentives. It states minimum conduct rules rather than detailed procedures, leaving each institution's board to adopt a conforming policy and managers to issue more detailed departmental instructions where needed. It binds all persons associated with SAMA-supervised financial institutions, with non-compliance carrying consequences addressed in the document's final section.

Second edition (November 2021) of SAMA's Controls on the Standing Payment Order in Favour of a Financing Entity, replacing the earlier real-estate-finance-specific controls; it now covers all financing products and extends the definition of Financing Entity to government financiers including National Development Fund banks and funds. It defines the service (periodic transfers from a customer's account to the financing entity to repay financing) and sets minimum obligations on banks — verifying stable monthly income, taking the customer's acknowledgement, notification of set-up and of non-execution, execution timing, and requiring the beneficiary financier's consent or a release letter before amendment or cancellation — plus obligations on the beneficiary financing entity regarding rescheduling and issuing release letters within set deadlines. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom and applies without prejudice to responsible retail finance principles and retail collection rules.

SAMA's CCTV Specifications for the financial sector (v1.0, July 2019), setting minimum physical-security surveillance requirements for supervised financial institutions' premises. It covers operational deployment (restricted and logged access to the CCTV/control room, camera siting and relocation approvals, daily system checks, reporting of overwritten or missing footage, cooperation with law enforcement through bank procedures) and references international standards for security surveillance systems. It binds banks and other financial organisations in respect of head offices, branches, cash centres and ATMs, and carries footage-retention duties that matter for customer complaints and disputed claims.

This node is the technical core of SAMA's CCTV Specifications: the surveillance objectives framework (identification, recognition, detection) with required pixel density, face width and camera resolution, mapped to specific branch and facility areas such as entrances, cash counters, reception and waiting areas, locker/safe rooms, IT rooms and data centres, ATMs and CCDMs. It also fixes recording retention: a 90-day minimum for all bank facilities, one year for footage relating to a customer claim or complaint from receipt, and five years where a claim or complaint is rejected. These retention rules are the provisions most often relied on in customer dispute and complaint-handling matters.

A node within SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies (issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation), covering the second principle: the audit committee's duties toward the internal audit function. It addresses the committee's oversight role — including matters such as approving/recommending audit policy, plan and reporting lines, and safeguarding the department's independence and objectivity. Binds SAMA-licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies at board/committee level.

Covers the third principle of SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for Finance Companies and Real Estate Refinance Companies: the duties of Executive Management (defined as those running day-to-day business and proposing/implementing strategy, i.e. senior management) toward the internal audit function. Relevant to how management must cooperate with, resource, and respond to internal audit without compromising its independence. Binds licensed finance and real estate refinance companies.

Defines and regulates the Internal Audit Department in a finance or real estate refinance company — its key attributes, the head of department's and the department's duties, external quality assessment, record retention, and its relationship with first- and second-line units. Also anchors the defined terms independence, objectivity, conflict of interest and the internal audit function as an independent assurance and advisory activity over internal control, governance and risk management. Binds SAMA-licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies.

Refers to the seventh principle of SAMA's Internal Audit Principles: the internal audit policy, a formal document prepared by the head of internal audit and approved by the board, whose required content is set by that principle. It is the constitutive charter-type document establishing the department's mandate, authority and scope. Applies to SAMA-licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies.

Refers to the eighth principle of SAMA's Internal Audit Principles, on the internal audit plan (with related provisions on department reports and working policies/procedures). It governs how audit coverage is planned, approved and reported for a finance or real estate refinance company. Binds licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies, with approval/oversight sitting at board and audit committee level.

Concept node on the three-lines model as reflected in SAMA guidance: first-line business units that own and manage the risks of their activities within tolerances, second-line control/compliance and risk units, and internal audit as the independent third line. The thirteenth principle of the Internal Audit Principles governs the audit department's relationship with first- and second-line units, preserving audit independence from operational and control functions. Relevant to finance companies, real estate refinance companies and, via the second cited instrument, broader supervised entities.

A domain/concept node within SAMA's Financial Sector Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles, which organise CTI into core lifecycle principles plus strategic, operational and technical/tactical layers. The technical and tactical layer concerns machine- and analyst-level threat data (e.g. indicators of compromise, attacker tools and techniques) feeding detection and defensive action, as distinct from strategic intelligence aimed at executive management. It applies to Member Organizations, i.e. entities licensed and supervised by SAMA, as expected supervisory practice rather than a stand-alone law.

Cross-cutting reference to SAMA's Cyber Security Framework, the baseline cybersecurity governance and control regime for entities supervised by SAMA. It is the parent framework that the Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles and the ethical red teaming circular build on, with SAMA expecting Member Organizations to test and develop their systems against CSF requirements. Binds all SAMA-regulated Member Organizations (banks, insurers, payment and finance companies).

Glossary/concept node for MITRE ATT&CK as used in SAMA's Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles: an open-source framework taxonomising the tactics, techniques and procedures used by threat actors. It is cited as an example of the structured attack taxonomy Member Organizations are expected to use when defining attack phases and identifying relevant TTPs under the operational CTI domain. Relevant to SAMA-supervised Member Organizations; the framework itself is a third-party standard, not a SAMA rule.

Glossary/concept node for the kill chain as referenced in SAMA's Cyber Threat Intelligence Principles: a military-derived model (developed by Lockheed Martin) breaking a cyber attack into sequential phases from reconnaissance through actions on objectives. The Principles expect Member Organizations to define and taxonomise attack phases using such recognised frameworks, including unified kill chain variants. Applies to SAMA-supervised Member Organizations as supervisory expectation.

SAMA circular adopting the Financial Entities Ethical Red Teaming (FEER) framework, a regulatory framework for simulating realistic cyber attack scenarios to test the resilience of financial institutions' core systems. SAMA states it will run periodic FEER-based tests on financial institutions and expects them to conduct independent, periodic testing and remediation in line with the Cyber Security Framework. Addressed to banks operating in the Kingdom, Saudi Payments and licensed payment companies, and insurance/reinsurance entities; the framework itself is circulated separately to compliance departments.

SAMA-issued Compliance Principles for finance companies and real estate refinance companies, adopted under the Finance Companies Control Law and its implementing regulation by Governor's decision and effective a set period after publication on SAMA's website. They allocate compliance responsibilities across the board, audit committee, executive management, the compliance unit and its officer, company staff and internal audit, and set minimum requirements for the unit's independence, mandate and effectiveness, together with a compliance-risk definition covering legal sanctions, financial loss and reputational harm. They bind SAMA-licensed finance companies and real estate refinance companies and are stated to be without prejudice to other applicable regimes (including AML and counter-terrorism financing laws, BNPL rules, fraud-prevention rules, governance principles, conduct rules and consumer protection principles).

SAMA's Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulations and effective from the date stated in the covering circular. It sets a minimum standard for Shariah governance practice, covering preliminary provisions and definitions (Committee, Committee members, independent member, Shariah supervision), board and senior management duties, Shariah supervision, rules governing the Shariah Committee's work, independence and confidentiality. It binds licensed finance companies carrying on real estate finance, production asset finance, SME finance, finance lease, credit card finance and consumer finance; for other licensed finance activities it is guidance only unless other rules make provisions mandatory, and SAMA may extend it at any time.

The board-of-directors limb of SAMA's Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies (Chapter Two, on responsibilities of the board and senior management). It allocates ultimate accountability for the finance company's Shariah governance arrangements, including approving policies and procedures regulating the Shariah Committee's work (a copy of which must be filed with SAMA) and maintaining a reasonable understanding of Shariah principles and their application in Islamic finance. It binds the board of a licensed finance company within the instructions' scope.

The senior-management limb of Chapter Two of SAMA's Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies. It sets executive-level duties for implementing board-approved Shariah governance arrangements, supporting the Shariah Committee, and ensuring finance business is conducted consistently with Shariah rulings and principles, with an expectation of reasonable Shariah literacy at management level. It binds the senior management of finance companies within the instructions' scope.

The Shariah supervision/compliance element of SAMA's Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies (Chapter Three), read with the broader compliance-function expectations. "Shariah supervision" is defined as monitoring and verifying the extent to which the finance company's business complies with Islamic Shariah rulings and principles, operating alongside the Shariah Committee's decisions. It binds licensed finance companies in scope and shapes how their compliance function interacts with Shariah rulings.

The Shariah audit element within SAMA's Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies, forming part of the Shariah supervision/control architecture alongside the Shariah Committee and compliance duties. It concerns independent review and assurance that the finance company's financing activities and products conform to Shariah rulings and Committee decisions, and reporting of findings within the governance chain. It binds licensed finance companies within the instructions' scope.

SAMA's Information Technology Governance Framework, structured into domains and subdomains (IT governance and leadership, IT risk management, IT operations management, system change management), each stating a principle plus numbered mandatory control requirements. It also sets the compliance mechanics: periodic self-assessment by Member Organizations via questionnaire, SAMA review and audit, a six-level IT governance maturity model, and a formal waiver/compensating-controls route where a control cannot be met. It binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA.

A glossary/role node from SAMA's IT Governance Framework materials identifying the Chief Information Officer and related IT roles (asset owner, database administrator, enterprise/application architect, COO) used across the framework's control requirements. It clarifies defined terminology and accountability for IT strategy, operations, compliance monitoring and incident oversight within Member Organizations. Relevant to any SAMA-regulated Member Organization allocating IT governance responsibilities.

Sets out the internal audit function's IT-specific duties under the SAMA IT Governance Framework — identifying auditable IT areas, performing IT risk assessment during audit planning, and conducting IT audits — alongside adjacent obligations on IT regulatory compliance and service level agreement management. It binds Member Organizations' internal audit and IT functions, and extends to third-party/outsourcing arrangements via SLA and risk-assessment requirements.

Node for the SAMA Cyber Security Framework as cross-referenced by the IT Governance Framework and related circulars, notably where change management must apply cyber security requirements before moving changes to production. It is the reference instrument for cyber security control requirements and maturity assessment across SAMA Member Organizations, sitting alongside but distinct from IT governance controls.

Node referencing the SAMA Business Continuity Management Framework in the context of IT risk management, disaster recovery and change/configuration/patch management controls in the IT Governance Framework. It concerns continuity and recovery of critical business functions following IT or cyber disruption, binding SAMA Member Organizations.

SAMA Rules on Liquidity Risk Management for finance companies, covering liquidity risk governance, board and senior management responsibilities, risk tolerance, strategies and policies, contingency funding plans and stress testing. Binds finance companies licensed under the Finance Companies Control Law, with reporting expectations toward the Board and SAMA.

Concept node on the Board of Directors' ultimate responsibility for liquidity risk in a finance company: setting risk tolerance, approving the liquidity strategy and policies (including contingency funding plan and stress testing framework) at least annually, monitoring the liquidity profile, and ensuring senior management operationalises them. Directed at boards and senior management of SAMA-licensed finance companies, with an ALCO recommended for oversight.

The IT Governance Maturity Model is the six-level scale (0 Non-existent through 5) that SAMA uses to grade Member Organizations' IT control maturity under the Information Technology Governance Framework. It underpins the periodic self-assessment questionnaire that Member Organizations complete and that SAMA reviews and audits to determine compliance and maturity level, with higher levels requiring all criteria of the preceding levels. It binds all SAMA-regulated Member Organizations and is the reference point for waiver requests, compensating controls and internal risk acceptance where a control cannot be met.

This is Domain 3.1 of SAMA's IT Governance Framework, covering IT governance structure and leadership: board accountability, the IT Steering Committee, the CIO role, IT strategy, enterprise architecture, IT policy and procedures, and roles and responsibilities. Each subdomain sets a Principle plus numbered Control Requirements that Member Organizations are expected to implement. It binds the boards and senior management of all SAMA-regulated Member Organizations.

Domain 3.2 of the IT Governance Framework sets requirements for a defined, approved and communicated IT risk management process aligned to the Member Organization's enterprise risk management, covering risk identification and analysis, treatment, reporting, monitoring and profiling. It requires a centralized IT risk register, inherent and residual risk analysis, key risk indicators, treatment within board/ITSC-approved risk appetite, and coverage of processes, applications, infrastructure, people and third-party relationships. It binds SAMA Member Organizations, with accountability at senior management and ITSC level.

Domain 3.3 of the IT Governance Framework addresses day-to-day IT operations for Member Organizations, including service level agreement management, availability and capacity, data centre management, backup, interdependency management, and controls over virtualized environments and system-level objects. It states principles with mandated control requirements for operational resilience and monitoring of IT services. It applies to all SAMA-regulated Member Organizations.

Domain 3.4 of the IT Governance Framework governs changes to information assets (applications, software, devices, data), requiring an approved change management policy and process covering requirement definition and approval, severity and priority, risk and impact assessment, development, testing, release, and configuration monitoring. It mandates Change Advisory Board endorsement before production deployment, prior cyber security function review (cross-referencing the SAMA Cyber Security Framework), and post-implementation review, documentation and root cause analysis for emergency changes. It binds SAMA Member Organizations and their IT, cyber security and audit functions.

This node covers the IT Steering Committee (ITSC), the board-mandated body to which a Member Organization's board may delegate IT governance, responsible for defining IT governance and setting IT strategy. Requirements include a board-approved ITSC charter (objectives, roles, quorum, at least quarterly meetings, minutes retention), representation by senior managers (CRO, CISO, compliance officer, business heads) and the CIO with internal audit as observer, plus appointment of a full-time, qualified Saudi-national CIO subject to SAMA non-objection. It binds boards and senior management of SAMA Member Organizations.

Node covering the recommended asset and liability committee within SAMA's liquidity risk management rules for finance companies. It describes ALCO composition (CEO, risk management, treasury, financial control and other business areas affecting the liquidity profile), the Board's duty to define its mandate for planning, directing and managing liquidity risk, and the committee's role in ensuring the liquidity risk framework measures exposure and produces timely reporting to senior management, the Board and SAMA (e.g. quarterly risk reports on cash flow mismatches, maturity gaps, funding concentration and collateral availability). Binds finance companies licensed under the Finance Companies Control Law; ALCO establishment is recommended rather than mandatory, but reporting expectations sit alongside it.
lookup_terms: quarterly liquidity risk reporting to SAMA

data.summary: Node on liquidity risk tolerance and Board governance duties under SAMA's liquidity risk rules for finance companies. It sets out that the Board is ultimately responsible for liquidity risk, must establish a risk tolerance aligned with business strategy, approve the liquidity risk strategy and policies (including the contingency funding plan and stress testing framework) at least annually, monitor the liquidity profile through regular and immediate material-change reporting, and ensure senior management identifies, measures, monitors, controls and reports liquidity risk. Tolerance must be reviewed at least annually and may be expressed through quantitative measures such as liquid asset holdings, maturity mismatches, funding concentration and contingent liquidity obligations.

Node on the liquidity stress testing and scenario analysis obligation for finance companies. It requires a comprehensive stress testing programme covering multiple scenarios of varying severity and time horizons, run regularly for company-specific and market-wide stresses individually and in combination, supplemented by sensitivity analysis, with documented assumptions on cash flow behaviour of assets, liabilities and off-balance sheet items; results are used to confirm exposures remain within the Board-set liquidity risk tolerance. Related material covers collateral management, exclusion of pledged assets from the liquid asset stock, and SAMA's power to impose specific liquidity limits.

Node on the Contingency Funding Plan required of finance companies to handle liquidity crises and cash flow shortfalls under stress. It specifies the CFP's minimum content: a quantitative and qualitative definition of a liquidity crisis event, early warning indicators with assigned monitoring responsibility and frequency, options for different time horizons, designated roles and activation authority, escalation procedures, plans to modify balance sheet composition and maturities, a prioritised list of alternative funding sources, and periodic testing and updating. Binds finance companies; the CFP is subject to Board approval as part of the liquidity risk policy set.

Node on the requirement for finance companies to hold a cushion of unencumbered high quality liquid assets as a readily available funding source to absorb unexpected net cash outflows and survive a liquidity stress event. It explains the qualifying characteristics (easy and immediate conversion to cash at little or no loss of value, ease and certainty of valuation, low price volatility, liquidity-generating capacity retained under market stress) and links sizing of the buffer to the company's funding strategy, diversification of funding sources and tenor, and liquid assets ratio monitoring. Pledged assets are excluded from the available liquid asset stock.

Node on senior management's internal control and audit duties for liquidity risk in finance companies. It requires management to manage liquidity in an integrated manner with processes and controls limiting and monitoring material liquidity risk sources, to understand how credit, market and operational risk affect the liquidity strategy and position, and to implement adequate internal controls and audit mechanisms safeguarding the integrity of the liquidity risk management process. It sits within the Board-led governance structure that must define roles and responsibilities across senior management and functional/business units.

SAMA's Rules Governing Credit Risk Exposure Classification and Provisioning, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law (Art. 13) and its Implementing Regulation (Art. 62), setting minimum requirements for classifying credit exposures and setting provisions. It aligns regulatory classification with IFRS 9 expected credit loss concepts (PD, EAD, LGD, stages) and defines the supporting terminology. It binds licensed finance companies, which must maintain a credit risk management framework proportionate to their size and complexity as a precondition to compliance.
lookup_terms: credit risk exposure classification and provisioning
probability of default exposure at default loss given default

data.summary: Concept node for IFRS 9 as adopted by SAMA as the accounting reference for credit risk measurement by finance companies, supplying the definitions of financial asset, ECL (12-month and lifetime), PD, EAD, LGD, past due and default. The Rules map IFRS 9 stages onto SAMA regulatory categories (Regular, Special Monitoring, Substandard, Doubtful, Loss), with sub-tiers (Stage 2A/2B, 3A/3B) used for regulatory reporting only, not accounting. It matters to finance companies determining staging, default at 90 days past due, and the superseded definitions in the earlier Provisions Guidelines circular.

Concept node on Expected Credit Loss under the SAMA provisioning Rules: the IFRS 9 estimate of losses from credit events, measured as 12-month or lifetime ECL depending on staging. The Rules place responsibility on the board of directors of a finance company to keep ECL provisions adequate and to oversee credit risk practices, policies, model validation and data integrity. It prescribes minimum content for the ECL framework, including defined terms (default, SICR), roles and responsibilities, portfolio grouping, methodology choice and documentation of inputs and assumptions.

Concept node on the three-stage classification of credit exposures required of finance companies: Stage 1 (Regular, no significant increase in credit risk), Stage 2 (Special Monitoring/Substandard) and Stage 3 (Doubtful/Loss), assessed individually or collectively against credit risk at origination. It sets cure-period and re-staging conditions for moving exposures from Stage 2 back to Stage 1 (90 days generally, 60 days for retail moving from Stage 2B) and requires bifurcated Stage 2 reporting in quarterly prudential returns. It binds finance companies in both classification and regulatory reporting.

Concept node on the credit risk governance expectations embedded in the SAMA provisioning Rules: finance companies must operate an effective credit risk management framework of policies, procedures and controls to identify, measure, monitor, control and report credit risk, proportionate to the nature, size and complexity of exposures. Compliance with the classification and provisioning requirements is treated as unattainable without that framework, and the Rules require self-assessment of the existing framework. Obligations sit with the finance company and its board.
lookup_terms: classification of exposures individual or collective

data.summary: Concept node distinguishing the two permitted forms of restructuring of a credit exposure by a finance company: forbearance (a concession granted because the borrower is in financial difficulty) and renegotiation/refinancing/rescheduling (a borrower-convenience change with no financial deterioration and no reduction in present value). Forborne exposures are identified at individual exposure level and may only be reported in Stage 2B, 3A or 3B, with specified events (partial write-off, collateral repossession pending disposal, further forbearance) that cannot restore performing status. It binds finance companies in classification, ECL model inputs and regulatory reporting of restructured exposures.

Defines "default" and the related IFRS 9 credit-risk measurement terms (PD, EAD, LGD, financial asset, 12-month and lifetime ECL, Stage 1/2 exposures) used in SAMA's rules on credit risk exposure classification and provisioning for finance companies. Default is established by either a qualitative "unlikeliness to pay" trigger (e.g. Stage 3B classification, charge-off or specific provision, sale at material credit loss, concessionary modification, bankruptcy filing, referral to the Enforcement Court) or the quantitative 90-days-past-due test on any material credit obligation. It binds SAMA-licensed finance companies, which must adopt the regulatory default definition consistently for regulatory and financial reporting or document justified departures.

Sets SAMA's expectations on when finance companies must write off credit exposures: only after collection and recovery options are reasonably exhausted and subject to Internal Auditor review, and within fixed maximum periods from Stage 3 classification (360 days unsecured, 720 days secured, 1,080 days for mortgages and corporate exposures) unless a more conservative internal policy applies. It confirms that write-off is accounting de-recognition only and does not extinguish recovery rights against the borrower or collateral, and that multiple exposures to one counterparty are treated at counterparty level. It also lists situations (including partial write-off of a forborne exposure) that do not allow re-categorisation of a forborne exposure as performing.

Sets the governance framework finance companies must put in place over ECL estimation and reporting, placing ultimate responsibility on the board of directors for maintaining adequate provisions and appropriate credit risk practices. It requires documented policies on key definitions (default, SICR), roles, methodologies, data and assumptions, collateral effects, restructuring, write-offs, model validation and disclosures, plus ECL-related KPIs. Internal Audit must review, evaluate and report annually on ECL adequacy as third line of defence, with an independent third party permitted where Internal Audit cannot perform the review.

SAMA instructions (Nov 2021, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law) regulating the buyout of individual consumer finance debts between finance companies. They set obligations on the purchasing company (consumer finance licence required; no separate SAMA approval per transaction; disclosure of new financing terms and costs with documented customer consent; a standard buyout application form; settlement of the existing debt through SARIE with prescribed payment data; no transfer fees beyond early-settlement or administrative fees; no release of residual funds to the customer before a clearance letter and required security are obtained) and on the selling company (issuing liability statements and debt-proof letters, facilitating transfer, and notifying the customer, each within one business day). Binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA instructions fixing the maximum processing times financiers must observe when a natural-person customer requests a clearance letter, an account transfer or a debt transfer: one business day for a clearance letter (seven business days where a credit or charge card is involved), one business day for account transfer and for consumer finance debt-transfer forms, and three/five business days for real estate finance debt transfer steps. They supersede the timeframes set in several earlier SAMA circulars while leaving the substance of those instructions intact, and exclude cases subject to judicial rulings or pending before competent authorities. Binds banks and finance companies supervised by SAMA, effective within thirty business days.

SAMA controls and procedures (Jan 2021, under the Finance Lease Law and its Implementing Regulation) for requesting and issuing executive deed extracts for registered finance lease contracts, which constitute enforceable instruments under the Enforcement Law. They cover three extract types — repossession of movable assets, delivery of a fixed asset (real estate), and a financial enforcement certificate — and require all parties to use electronic channels; lessors may repossess movable assets only through Ministry of Justice licensed specialised companies. Binds lessors (banks and finance companies) and SAMA-licensed finance lease contract registration companies, and replaces the earlier movable-asset repossession controls.

A SAMA circular (Treasury and Issue Department) transmitting updated controls on the reproduction, photographing, printing or design of Saudi and foreign currency in circulation in the Kingdom, issued under the Penal Law for Counterfeiting and Imitation of Currency (Royal Decree M/12) and the Anti-Forgery Law. It sets a licensing requirement for reproducing currency images in printed or electronic media, plus conditions such as size limits relative to the original note, mandatory 'specimen' marking, no distortion of the King's image, prohibition of use as plaques/objects, and destruction of all materials and digital files used. It binds any natural or legal person reproducing currency in KSA and supersedes earlier circulars on the subject.

A SAMA/Saudi Payments requirements document (Nov 2021) for the ATM Receipts initiative, aimed at reducing reliance on paper receipts for the four most common ATM transactions by standardising ATM home-page and screen workflows across on-us and off-us ATMs. It states that paper receipts must still be available on cardholder request, and separates requirements into a cash-withdrawal stream and a non-cash stream (balance enquiry, mini statement, cash deposit). It binds mada Members (issuers and acquirers); it does not cover certification procedures or scheme terms and conditions.

SAMA Rules Governing the Calculation of the Annual Percentage Rate (APR), setting definitions (APR, total amount payable, total cost of finance, amount of finance), scope, the net present value calculation method, and mandatory use of SAMA's Excel-based APR Calculator. Finance providers must align policies, internal controls and audit mechanisms, validate any automated calculator against SAMA's version, and keep customer-facing website calculators updated. They bind banks and finance companies licensed for retail lending, and apply to advertising, offer stage, contracts, periodic statements and any other APR disclosure; they are read with the Finance Companies Control Law, consumer finance regulations and related circulars.

A SAMA circular and Governor's decision (agreed with the Minister of Justice) issuing the controls on registration procedures in the finance lease contracts register, the data required for registration, and the rules and procedures for third-party access to the register, under the Finance Lease Law (M/48) and Article 30 of its Implementing Regulation. It covers definitions, registration duties (including the lessor's obligation to register a contract and its amendments within a set period via the register's electronic channel), registration documents, access to register data, and enforcement-related extracts. It binds banks, finance companies and licensed finance lease contract registration companies operating in the Kingdom, whose registers remain SAMA-supervised.

SAMA's Deposit Taking Finance Companies (DTFC) Regulations 2020, setting the regulatory approach, corporate governance and prudential requirements for finance companies authorised to take savings and time deposits from non-individual customers and to lend from those deposits. It covers permitted deposit activities, depositor record-keeping and retention duties, liquidity and other prudential ratios, and detailed account-opening rules for general and term deposit accounts (linkage, naming, rollover, one deal per account). It binds all DTFCs in KSA, in addition to the Finance Companies Control Law and general finance company regulations.

A SAMA circular issuing a guide organising the operating procedures of money exchange businesses, grounded in the Rules Regulating the Practice of Exchange Business (Ministerial Decision 1350) and the SAMA licensing requirement. It distinguishes Category A exchangers (permitted, where previously licensed, to carry out domestic and cross-border money transfer) from Category B (purchase and sale of foreign currency, travellers' cheques and bank cheques), and requires compliance with related SAMA instructions and the AML/CTF rules. It binds all licensed Category A and B exchange houses in the Kingdom from two months after the circular date.
lookup_terms: دليل تنظيم إجراءات عمل محلات الصرافة

data.summary: A SAMA circular to banks operating in the Kingdom that amends the Bank Account Rules by inserting new account-opening categories for non-resident non-Saudi customers covered by the Non-Saudi Real Estate Ownership Law — one for natural persons and one for legal persons — so they can access banking services for the purpose of acquiring property or other real rights in the Kingdom. It sets the required documents (Kingdom-issued digital identity, passport, contact details and a Saudi mobile number linked to that identity, broker/developer agreement, foreign bank statement; for legal persons, MISA/NCNP registration with a unified number, authorised representative's ID, constitutive documents and board details) and general controls (verification through a reliable independent Kingdom source including biometric/attribute verification, no joint accounts or non-resident authorised signatories, limits on remote accounts, no payment or credit cards, property-related transactions only through approved Saudi electronic channels such as the Real Estate Registry, Ejar and SADAD, and ongoing validity checks and periodic data updates). It binds banks with immediate effect.

A SAMA circular instructing supervised financial institutions to use the General Authority for Awqaf's channels — technical integration with the Authority's systems, requests to its Data Management Office by email, the waqf certificate verification service, and the public register of endowments — when identifying and verifying beneficial owner data for awqaf (endowments). It is grounded in the AML Law and its Implementing Regulation's customer due diligence obligations, and additionally requires institutions to notify the Authority, via its designated form, of any discrepancies between Authority data and CDD findings, without prejudice to suspicious transaction reporting duties or the Personal Data Protection Law.
lookup_terms: customer due diligence reliable independent source

data.summary: Concept node for the Finance Lease Law (Royal Decree M/48) and its Implementing Regulation, which underpin SAMA's authority over finance leasing, lessors and licensed finance lease contract registration companies. In the cited source it is the legal basis for SAMA's controls and procedures on requesting and issuing extracts of the executive instrument (writ of execution) for a registered finance lease contract — covering repossession of movable assets, delivery of immovable assets, and financial execution certificates — which are treated as enforceable instruments under the Enforcement Law.

Node covering SAMA's consumer finance rulebook material, with the supplied text being the Rules Governing the Calculation of the Annual Percentage Rate (APR): definitions (finance provider, borrower, amount of finance, total amount payable, total cost of finance), scope, and the requirement to compute and disclose APR consistently in advertising, offers, contracts, periodic statements and any other APR disclosure. The Rules bind all finance providers engaged in retail lending — banks and licensed finance companies — and are to be read together with the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation, the Regulations for Consumer Financing, the microfinance rules, and the related SAMA clarification circular on APR calculation.

Concept node for the Non-Saudi Real Estate Ownership Law (Royal Decree M/181) and its Implementing Regulation issued by Council of Ministers decision, which define the categories of non-Saudi natural and legal persons permitted to own property or acquire other real rights in the Kingdom. For SAMA purposes it is the eligibility gateway: persons covered by this Law form the customer category for which the Bank Account Rules were amended to allow non-resident account opening, subject to prescribed documentation and restrictive operating controls.

Concept node for SAMA's Bank Account Rules, the standing framework governing who may open and operate bank accounts in the Kingdom, the documentation and identification requirements per customer category, and the operating controls and ongoing update duties applicable to each account type. The Rules bind banks operating in the Kingdom and are periodically amended by SAMA circular — in the cited source by adding rules for non-resident natural and legal persons covered by the Non-Saudi Real Estate Ownership Law.

Implementing Regulations to the Law of Combating Terrorist Crimes and its Financing, which flesh out the Law's definitions and operational duties — notably the list of financial activities and of commercial/professional (DNFBP) activities that bring a person within scope, and the minimum content of CTF policies, procedures and rules (risk management before completing customer verification, STR reporting, a senior-level compliance officer, employee screening and training, independent audit, and control of foreign subsidiaries). It binds financial institutions, designated non-financial businesses and professions, and non-profit organisations, with supervisory authorities empowered to add measures. Also imposes group-wide application where a host country's CTF standards are weaker.
lookup_terms: Law of Combating Terrorist Crimes and its Financing

data.summary: Implementing Regulation to the Anti-Money Laundering Law, setting out the detailed rules behind the Law's articles: definitions of supervisory and competent authorities, the acts that constitute conducting a transaction or business relationship, the written ML risk assessment duty, group-wide AML policies and intra-group information sharing, treatment of jurisdictions with weaker AML requirements, and the triggers and scope of suspicious transaction reporting. It binds financial institutions, DNFBPs and NPOs, and frames the reporting interface with the FIU and supervisors. Useful for scoping questions on who is covered and what documentation supervisors may demand.

SAMA circular transmitting the Implementation Rules for the Banking Control Law (Ministerial Resolution 3/2149), covering Article 12 (appointments to bank boards and senior positions, including SAMA prior approval and disclosure duties), Article 16 (conduct of banking business consistent with monetary and credit policy), Article 17 (periodic supervisory and statistical returns), Article 18 (SAMA inspections and staff conduct), and Article 22 (supervisory procedures and penalties). It binds all banks operating in the Kingdom and their directors, managers and employees.

Defined-term node for "Financial Institution" as used in the Saudi Central Bank Law: any natural or legal person subject to SAMA's supervision, oversight and regulation. The definition is the gateway to SAMA's powers — licensing, prudential policy, consumer protection directives, fintech platform rules, professional testing, and crime-prevention measures all attach to entities falling within it. Note the term is defined differently in other regimes (e.g. AML/CTF activity-based lists), so check which instrument's definition applies.

Concept node for the Capital Market Law and the Capital Market Authority regime as cross-referenced in SAMA instruments — for example, securities and securities-related trading activities that fall in AML/CTF scope, and, in the finance lease context shown here, issuance of securities against a lessor's rights under CMA rules while SAMA disclosure and supervisory obligations continue to apply. Relevant mainly for regulatory-perimeter and dual-supervision questions between SAMA and the CMA.

The Banking Control Law (Royal Decree M/5) — the primary statute governing the licensing, governance, supervision and prudential control of banks in Saudi Arabia, together with its Implementation Rules and the SAMA circulars issued under it. Key provisions addressed in the linked material include board and senior appointments, conduct of banking business, periodic reporting to SAMA, inspections, and contraventions and penalties. It binds all banks operating in the Kingdom and underpins much of SAMA's supervisory authority over them.

Sets out the CDD obligations under the AML Law's Implementing Regulation (Article 7 provisions), covering identification and verification of customers and beneficial owners, timing of verification, risk-based deferral where ML risk is low, and enhanced measures. It also addresses life/investment insurance beneficiaries, the duty to refuse or terminate a relationship where CDD cannot be completed (with consideration of an STR), the tipping-off exception, and reliance on a third-party financial institution or DNFBP subject to conditions. Binds financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses and professions in the Kingdom.

Covers the Law of Payments and Payment Services definitions and core scope: payment system, payment services, payment order, member, client, and SAMA's powers over licensing, capital and solvency, product approval, outsourcing, and designation of systemically important payment systems (SIPS). Establishes that no person may operate a payment system or provide payment services in the Kingdom without a SAMA licence, with aims of infrastructure integrity, user protection, and innovation/competition. Binds payment system operators, payment service providers, and applicants seeking to enter the market.
lookup_terms: Law of Payments and Payment Services

data.summary: Part of the Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services (issued 1446H, replacing the 2020 Rules Regulating Payment Service Providers), specifically the chapter on agents and e-money distributors. It governs when and how a licensee may appoint agents to act on its behalf, and the licensee's continuing responsibility for agent conduct. Binds SAMA-licensed payment service providers and payment system operators, with a transitional remediation plan expected within six months of entry into force.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services

data.summary: Part of the Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services dealing with e-money distributors alongside agents, and connected to the chapters on issuance and redemption of e-money and safeguarding of protected funds. It sets the conditions under which licensees may use distributors to distribute or redeem e-money and the licensee's accountability for them. Binds SAMA-licensed e-money issuers and other payment service providers.

The chapter of the Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services addressing outsourcing, internal audit and risk management obligations of licensees. It frames when functions may be outsourced, the licensee's retained responsibility, and the governance/control expectations SAMA imposes. Binds SAMA-licensed payment service providers and payment system operators.

The licensing-requirements chapter of the Implementing Regulation of the Law of Payments and Payment Services, covering capital and financial-soundness conditions for payment service providers and related licensing criteria (including controller and holding-company definitions relevant to ownership approval). Determines entry and ongoing prudential thresholds for licensees. Binds applicants for and holders of a SAMA payment licence.

This node covers SAMA's mandated Excel-based Annual Percentage Rate (APR) calculator and the accompanying Rules that standardise APR computation for retail lending, including the net present value formula and the points at which APR must be disclosed (advertising, offer stage, contract, periodic statements and any other disclosure). It binds all finance providers engaging in retail lending, requiring them to use SAMA's calculator, update internal policies, maintain controls over the calculator's integrity, reconcile any automated tool against SAMA's version, and keep customer-facing website calculators aligned. It is read together with the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation, the Rules Regulating Consumer Microfinance Companies, the interest-rate disclosure rules and the Regulations for Consumer Financing.

Second edition of SAMA's General Rules for Participation in Events (Arabic), issued by circular as an update to the earlier rules on holding and sponsoring events. It sets minimum conduct, governance and risk requirements for participation in conferences, forums, seminars and similar gatherings — inside or outside the Kingdom, directly or through third parties — including a board-approved participation policy, documentation and annual reporting to the board, careful selection and professional conduct of representatives, confidentiality, and event risk assessment. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA and notably extends scope to presence via "temporary booths" for institutional promotion, which are exempted from the SAMA no-objection requirement.

An Arabic SAMA circular on enhancing operational resilience against quantum computing risks, issued under the Saudi Central Bank Law. It requires supervised institutions to conduct an enterprise-wide quantum risk assessment (covering operational, legal, regulatory, strategic and workforce risks) with remediation plans by end of Q1 2027, to complete inventory and classification of cryptographic assets by end of Q4 2026 including third-party dependencies, to plan for cryptographic agility or alternative solutions for priority assets, and to make quantum risk a standing monitoring item for the information security committee and the board risk committee. It binds banks, credit information companies, finance companies, payment service providers and SAMA-licensed finance support entities.

The Implementing Regulation of the Payments and Payment Services Law (Royal Decree M/26), issued in Arabic by SAMA circular; it replaces the Rules Regulating Payment Service Providers from its issuance date, with a corrective-action plan required within six months. It sets definitions (including control, holding company, complaint, licence), licensing and scope requirements for payment service providers, rules on agents and e-money distributors, outsourcing/audit/risk management obligations, customer protection and financial inclusion, contract and information disclosure duties, e-money issuance and redemption, safeguarding of protected funds, account information and payment initiation services, designation and oversight of payment systems under the PFMI, settlement finality and insolvency, supervision and enforcement, and complaints and disputes. It binds licensed payment service providers and payment system operators subject to the Law.
lookup_terms: payment initiation and account information services

data.summary: The Implementing Regulation of the Finance Lease Law, setting definitions (Lessor, Lessee, Leased Asset, Contracts Register, Contracts Registration Company, Securitization) and the conditions under which finance leasing is treated as a professional activity requiring licensing.
