Covers the eligibility conditions for CVA hedges and their capital treatment: eligible external hedges are removed from market risk capital calculations, ineligible external hedges are capitalised as trading book instruments, and internal hedges only qualify where the trading desk offsets its position externally in defined cases. It also notes materiality-based alternative treatments under which CVA hedges are not recognised at all. It binds banks calculating CVA capital under BA-CVA or SA-CVA, including where SAMA approval limits SA-CVA scope.

A node on exposure at default (EAD) estimation, covering both the advanced IRB own-estimate requirements (long-run default-weighted averages, margin of conservatism, treatment of off-balance sheet items and additional drawings) and the standardised counterparty credit risk (SA-CCR) route for derivative exposures. It sets expectations on reference data quality, non-capping of EAD data, and avoidance of instability in undrawn limit factor CCF approaches. It binds banks using internal ratings-based or SA-CCR approaches under SAMA's credit risk capital rules.

Defines the aggregate add-on component of the potential future exposure (PFE) calculation under SA-CCR, combined with a multiplier that recognises excess collateral or negative mark-to-market within a netting set, alongside the replacement cost formula using threshold, minimum transfer amount and net independent collateral amount. It explains why the calculation is floored at zero and how over-collateralisation reduces counterparty credit risk capital. It binds banks computing counterparty credit risk exposures under SAMA's SA-CCR rules.

A framework-level node on the leverage ratio as a non-risk-based capital constraint, including the leverage ratio buffer and its role as a trigger for capital distribution constraints, and its mandatory appearance in Pillar 3 key metrics and reconciliation templates. It covers disclosure frequency, format and narrative expectations as well as the ratio's interaction with risk-based buffers. It binds all banks subject to SAMA's capital adequacy and Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Sets out the composition of the leverage ratio exposure measure — on-balance sheet assets, derivative replacement cost and PFE add-ons with the alpha factor, client-cleared and QCCP-related adjustments, and deductions mirroring Tier 1 regulatory adjustments — and its reconciliation to published accounting total assets. It covers permitted exclusions such as fiduciary assets, securitised exposures meeting risk transfer, and any temporary central bank reserve exemption. It binds all banks reporting the leverage ratio and completing the related mandatory disclosure templates.

Node for SAMA's market risk minimum capital requirements (SMAR) as referenced within the Basel-aligned Pillar 3 disclosure and capital framework documentation. It sits alongside the capital adequacy rules that determine risk-weighted assets and regulatory capital deductions, and is cross-referenced in disclosure templates covering RWA by risk type and capital distribution constraints. It binds SAMA-licensed banks calculating and disclosing Pillar 1 capital requirements.

Node for SAMA's operational risk minimum capital requirements (SOPE) within the Basel-aligned capital and Pillar 3 disclosure framework. It is the operational risk limb of the Pillar 1 capital calculation feeding RWA totals, capital ratios and the disclosure templates on capital adequacy and distribution constraints. Applies to banks supervised by SAMA.

SACAP is SAMA's capital definition and reforms guidance, setting out the composition of CET1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital, regulatory adjustments and deductions (goodwill, intangibles, DTAs, cash flow hedge reserve, shortfall of provisions, own-share and reciprocal holdings) and the 10%/5% threshold treatment for investments in financial-sector entities and TLAC liabilities. It is the reference standard cited throughout the Pillar 3 capital composition templates. Binding on SAMA-licensed banks at solo and consolidated levels.

Pillar 3 disclosure template KM2 setting out key metrics on total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) available and TLAC requirements measured at resolution group level, under single point of entry and multiple point of entry resolution approaches. It specifies quarterly, fixed-format quantitative disclosure of TLAC ratios against RWA and leverage exposure, with narrative explanation of material changes. Mandatory only for resolution groups of G-SIBs.

Pillar 3 template CMS1 requiring comparison of risk-weighted assets calculated under SAMA-approved internal/modelled approaches against RWA that would result from the corresponding standardised approaches, presented at the level of each risk category. It defines which exposures fall in each row (credit risk, counterparty credit risk, CVA, securitisation, equities, settlement risk) and how the standardised comparison is computed. Applies to banks using modelled approaches with SAMA approval.

Pillar 3 template CMS2 requiring the modelled-versus-standardised RWA comparison to be broken down by credit risk asset class, using the same definitions of standardised and IRB/supervisory slotting approaches as the risk-level comparison. It supports market assessment of the effect of internal model use on credit risk capital. Applies to banks with SAMA approval to use IRB approaches for credit risk.
lookup_terms: credit risk asset class RWA comparison

data.summary: A concept node within SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework covering the Tier 1 capital measure and its role in regulatory capital composition and disclosure templates (including capital distribution constraint triggers and the CC1-style line-by-line explanations of Tier 1/Tier 2 items and deductions). It anchors how CET1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 elements, regulatory adjustments, threshold deductions and TLAC-related holdings are reported. It binds banks licensed in KSA subject to SAMA's Basel III capital and disclosure rules, with cross-references to SACAP.

Concept node for SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk (SCRE), covering how risk-weighted assets and Pillar 1 capital requirements (normally RWA × 8%) are computed under the standardised approach, F-IRB/A-IRB and supervisory slotting, and how they are broken out in Pillar 3 overview templates separately from counterparty credit risk, CVA, equity, settlement and securitisation exposures. It binds banks calculating regulatory capital under SAMA's adoption of the Basel III post-crisis reforms.

Reference node for the Basel III post-crisis final reforms (BCBS, December 2017) as adopted by SAMA, identifying the family of SAMA frameworks derived from it — SCRE (credit risk), SCCR (CCR/CVA), SMAR (market risk), SOPE (operational risk), SLEV (leverage ratio), SLCR (LCR) and SNSF (NSFR) — plus the legacy SACAP guidance. Useful mainly as a glossary/orientation point for the abbreviations used across SAMA prudential and Pillar 3 texts; it binds banks through the individual adopting frameworks rather than directly.

SAMA's Output Floor Requirements, issued under the Central Bank Law (M/36) and the Banking Control Law, cap the benefit of internal models by floor-setting RWAs at a percentage of the standardised-approach outcome, to limit RWA variability and improve comparability of capital ratios. Effective 1 January 2023 with transitional phase-in, and paired with quarterly reporting to SAMA within 30 days of quarter-end. Applies to all domestic banks on consolidated and standalone bases; branches of foreign banks in KSA are out of scope and follow home-regulator capital rules.

SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework sets the guiding principles for market disclosure (clarity, comprehensiveness, meaningfulness, consistency over time, comparability across banks), requires a formal board-approved disclosure policy and internal assurance over Pillar 3 data, and governs use of signposting to other documents, reporting location, frequency (quarterly/semi-annual/annual) and publication timing alongside the financial report. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Basel III disclosure regime, with responsibilities at board and senior management level.

Concept node on credit conversion factors used to convert off-balance sheet items into credit exposure equivalents under SAMA's credit risk standard, including the 10% CCF for unconditionally cancellable commitments, SAMA's discretion to impose higher CCFs, and the rule to apply the lower of two CCFs where a commitment to provide a commitment exists. Also touches adjacent treatments for exposures giving rise to counterparty credit risk and for written/purchased credit derivatives (first-, second- and nth-to-default). Binds banks computing RWA under SAMA's Basel III frameworks.

This node covers SAMA's Output Floor Requirements and the mechanics of computing the floor, which caps the capital relief banks can obtain from internal models by referencing capital requirements derived under standardised approaches. It sets out the instrument's legal basis (Central Bank Law and Banking Control Law), scope, effective date of 1 January 2023 with transitional phase-in, quarterly reporting to SAMA within 30 days of quarter-end, and the row-by-row composition of risk categories feeding the floor calculation. It binds all domestic banks on both a consolidated and standalone basis, and expressly excludes branches of foreign banks operating in the Kingdom, which follow their home regulator's capital rules.

This node concerns the credit risk component of risk-weighted assets for output floor and Pillar 3 reporting purposes, distinguishing exposures measured under the standardised approach from those measured under foundation/advanced IRB and supervisory slotting approaches. It specifies scope boundaries, excluding counterparty credit risk, credit valuation adjustment, equity positions, settlement risk, securitisation exposures and amounts below deduction thresholds, each reported elsewhere, and addresses the phase-out of the IRB approach for equity exposures. It is relevant to banks calculating and disclosing credit risk RWA, including those with SAMA approval to use modelled approaches.

This node addresses the market risk element of risk-weighted assets within the output floor and capital reporting framework, sitting alongside credit, counterparty credit, CVA, settlement, securitisation and operational risk components. Its function is to identify which market risk RWA and capital requirements are computed under modelled versus standardised approaches when deriving the floor comparison. It applies to banks subject to SAMA's minimum risk-based capital and output floor requirements.

This node covers the operational risk component of risk-weighted assets as reported in SAMA's capital and output floor templates, forming part of the total RWA against which the Pillar 1 minimum (normally 8%) is applied. Because operational risk under the finalised Basel framework is computed on a single standardised basis, it feeds identically into both the modelled and standardised legs of the floor comparison. It applies to banks within scope of SAMA's minimum risk-based capital requirements.

SCRE is the SAMA-adopted credit risk standard of the Basel framework, referenced throughout the capital and output floor reporting rules as the source for standardised approach risk weights (SCRE5–SCRE9), IRB approaches (SCRE10–SCRE16), supervisory slotting (SCRE13), equity treatment and related provisions. It functions as the definitional anchor for which exposures and approaches populate each credit risk reporting row. It binds banks calculating regulatory capital for credit risk in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: minimum capital requirements for credit risk

data.summary: SCCR is the SAMA-adopted standard covering minimum capital requirements for counterparty credit risk (SCCR3–SCCR10) and the credit valuation adjustment risk charge (SCCR11), referenced in capital and output floor reporting to identify which RWA and capital charges belong in the CCR and CVA rows rather than the general credit risk rows. It defines the perimeter between counterparty exposure treatment and ordinary credit risk treatment. It binds banks computing regulatory capital for derivatives and securities financing exposures.

Pillar 3 disclosure template setting out the line-by-line composition of a bank's regulatory capital (CET1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2), including regulatory adjustments and deductions cross-referenced to the SAMA capital rules (SACAP). It is a fixed-format quantitative disclosure that must tie back, via the three-step approach and Template CC2, to the published balance sheet. Binds banks licensed and supervised by SAMA that are subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure framework.

Pillar 3 template reconciling the balance sheet in a bank's published financial statements (accounting consolidation) with the balance sheet under the regulatory scope of consolidation, and expanding items that feed the regulatory capital components in Template CC1. It is the first step of the required link between accounting figures and disclosed capital numbers. Applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.
lookup_terms: reconciliation of regulatory capital to balance sheet

data.summary: Pillar 3 table requiring disclosure of the main features of each regulatory capital instrument (and, where relevant, TLAC-eligible instrument) issued by the bank, such as issuer, governing law, regulatory treatment, maturity, call and loss-absorption terms. It supports market assessment of the quality and terms of instruments counted toward CET1, AT1 and Tier 2. Mandatory for banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.
lookup_terms: main features of regulatory capital instruments

data.summary: Pillar 3 template disclosing the composition of total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) at resolution group level, including eligible instruments, deductions, adjusted RWA, leverage exposure measure, TLAC ratios and buffer requirements. Completed once for single point of entry groups and per resolution group under the multiple point of entry approach. Mandatory only for banks designated as G-SIBs, effective from the TLAC conformance date.

Pillar 3 template showing, on a legal entity basis, the creditor hierarchy of each material subgroup entity that has issued internal TLAC to a G-SIB resolution entity, with nominal amounts of excluded liabilities, TLAC-eligible liabilities and their residual maturity bands. Its purpose is to let creditors assess their ranking relative to internal TLAC. Mandatory for G-SIBs, semiannually, from the TLAC conformance date.

Pillar 3 template disclosing the creditor hierarchy at legal entity level for each G-SIB resolution entity, mirroring Template TLAC2 but without reporting exposures to the resolution entity itself. It reports nominal capital and liabilities, excluded liabilities, potentially TLAC-eligible amounts and residual maturity buckets, including perpetual securities. Mandatory for G-SIBs on a semiannual basis from the TLAC conformance date.

Pillar 3 disclosure template CR2 within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, requiring banks to present a flow reconciliation of defaulted loans and debt securities from opening to closing stock (new defaults, returns to non-default status, write-offs, other changes). It fixes the reporting definitions, notably that defaulted exposures are reported net of write-offs and gross of allowances, and for standardised-approach banks correspond to exposures past due more than 90 days. Mandatory for all banks, semiannual, fixed format, with narrative explanation of significant movements and whether off-balance sheet items are included.
lookup_terms: changes in stock of defaulted loans

data.summary: Template CR3 is the credit risk mitigation overview disclosure sitting in the credit risk section of SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, alongside Table CRC (qualitative CRM disclosure). It shows the extent to which exposures are secured by collateral, financial guarantees and credit derivatives. It binds banks subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure regime, with the surrounding section defining the overall credit risk disclosure suite (CRA, CR1–CR5) and its exclusions for securitisation and counterparty credit risk.

Template CR4 is the standardised-approach disclosure showing credit risk exposures before and after credit conversion factors and credit risk mitigation, with resulting RWA and RWA density. The surrounding instructions define the standardised approach for these purposes (simple or comprehensive CRM approach with standard supervisory haircuts, inclusion of failed trades and non-DvP transactions) and the split between modelled and standardised portfolios. Applies to banks using the standardised approach under the Pillar 3 disclosure framework.

Template CR5 requires banks on the standardised approach to break down credit risk exposures (post-CCF and post-CRM) by asset class and risk weight band (0%, 20%, 50%, 100%, 150%, other). Mandatory for standardised-approach banks, semiannual and fixed format; banks phasing in IRB may use it for residual asset classes, and may omit it only where exposures are negligible, subject to explanation and SAMA's immateriality approval. Narrative must explain significant period-on-period changes and the sequence in which CCFs, provisioning and CRM are applied.
lookup_terms: exposures by asset classes and risk weights

data.summary: Template CR6 is the IRB disclosure presenting credit risk exposures broken down by portfolio and PD range, including key model parameters and resulting RWA. It sits with the IRB-related Pillar 3 disclosures, which banks complete only where SAMA has approved use of the internal ratings-based approach (F-IRB, A-IRB or supervisory slotting). The accompanying instructions distinguish modelled from standardised portfolios and exclude securitisation and counterparty credit risk positions.

Template CR7 requires IRB banks to disclose the effect of credit derivatives used as a credit risk mitigation technique, comparing hypothetical pre-credit derivatives RWA with actual RWA across IRB portfolios (sovereign, banks, corporate, specialised lending, retail sub-classes, equity, purchased receivables). Mandatory for banks using A-IRB and/or F-IRB for some or all exposures; semiannual, fixed format, with narrative explaining the RWA impact.
lookup_terms: effect on RWA of credit derivatives

data.summary: Template CDC is a mandatory Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring banks to publish the capital ratio thresholds at which capital distribution constraints are triggered, covering risk-based CET1 (including buffers, G-SIB surcharge, countercyclical buffer and Pillar 2 add-ons), TLAC-related requirements, and the leverage ratio inclusive of its buffer. It is annual, fixed-format, and requires narrative description of any constraints actually imposed plus a link to SAMA's published buffer/stacking framework. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

This node covers the Pillar 3 linkage disclosures reconciling accounting and regulatory consolidation, principally Template LI1 (mapping financial-statement carrying values to regulatory risk categories) alongside the related CC1/CC2 capital composition and reconciliation templates and the G-SIB TLAC1–TLAC3 templates. It sets out the three-step approach banks must follow to connect published balance sheet figures to disclosed regulatory capital. Mandatory for banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, with TLAC templates applying only to designated G-SIBs from the TLAC conformance date.

Template LI2 is a mandatory annual Pillar 3 disclosure explaining the main drivers of difference between financial-statement carrying values (on the regulatory consolidation basis) and the exposure amounts used for regulatory capital purposes — off-balance sheet amounts, valuation differences, netting rules, provisions and prudential filters. Its format is flexible so rows can be adapted to a bank's most meaningful drivers, with narrative support via Table LIA. The context also references Table CRB-A on prudential treatment of problem assets, including a bank's definitions of non-performing and forborne exposures relative to SAMA's Rules on Management of Problem Loans. Binds all banks.
lookup_terms: regulatory exposure amount vs carrying value

data.summary: Template PV1 requires an annual, fixed-format breakdown of prudent valuation adjustments (close-out uncertainty, model risk, operational risk, investing and funding costs and other adjustments) across equity, interest rate, FX, credit and commodity exposures, split between trading and banking book. It applies to all banks that record PVAs, and is anchored to the Basel prudent valuation guidance together with SAMA's circular on assessing banks' financial instrument fair value practices. Narrative explanation of significant changes and of unlisted "other adjustments" is expected.

Template ENC is a mandatory semiannual, fixed-format Pillar 3 disclosure of encumbered versus unencumbered on-balance sheet assets at carrying amount, on the regulatory scope of consolidation including securitization exposures. It uses a template-specific definition of encumbered assets (restricted from liquidation, sale, transfer or assignment by legal, regulatory, contractual or other limitations) that deliberately differs from the LCR definition by excluding the monetization aspect, and that definition does not carry over to other parts of the Basel framework. Binds all banks, with narrative explanation of material changes.

Template CR1 is a mandatory semiannual, fixed-format disclosure of the credit quality of a bank's on- and off-balance sheet assets — gross carrying values of defaulted and non-defaulted loans, debt securities and off-balance sheet exposures, allowances/impairments and net values — with ECL-provision columns applicable only to banks using an ECL accounting model. Banks must disclose their definition of default in the accompanying narrative. It sits within the Pillar 3 credit risk section (Tables CRA/CRB/CRB-A/CRC/CRD and Templates CR2–CR5), which excludes securitization and counterparty credit risk positions; IRB templates apply only where SAMA has approved IRB use.

Table SECA is the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure requirement on securitisation, requiring banks to describe their objectives, risk management policies and the main features of securitisation and re-securitisation activity, including the extent of credit risk transfer, risks assumed versus retained, sponsored special purpose entities and affiliated entities that invest in or manage securitisations. Where positions sit in both the regulatory banking book and trading book, the description must be given separately for each book. It is mandatory for all banks with securitisation exposures, disclosed annually in a flexible format.
lookup_terms: banking book vs trading book securitisation

data.summary: Template SEC1 is the quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of securitisation exposures held in the banking book, covering all such exposures regardless of whether risk transfer recognition criteria are met, split by the bank's role as originator, sponsor or investor. Because it is not limited to exposures treated under the securitisation capital framework, it can overlap with exposures reported elsewhere in the Pillar 3 report and is intended to give a comprehensive picture of securitisation activity. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Template SEC2 is the quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of securitisation exposures held in the trading book, again covering all such exposures by the bank's role (originator, sponsor, investor) irrespective of whether the securitisation framework applies for capital purposes. Capital charges for trading book securitisation positions are reported under the market risk disclosures rather than in this template. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Template SEC3 discloses banking book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as originator or sponsor, together with the associated capital requirements, broken down by risk weight bands and regulatory approach. It is limited to exposures actually treated under the securitisation capital framework, which for originators presupposes that the significant risk transfer recognition criteria are satisfied. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Template SEC4 discloses banking book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as investor, with the related risk-weighted assets and capital requirements by risk weight band and regulatory approach. Like SEC3, it captures only exposures treated under the securitisation capital framework, so there is no double counting with the broader SEC1/SEC2 templates. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Table MRA is the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on market risk, requiring banks to explain their market risk strategy, governance and risk management processes, including the structure and organisation of the market risk function, the scope and nature of risk reporting and measurement systems, and the definition and policies for allocating positions between the trading book and banking book. In this framework all banks, D-SIB and non-D-SIB, compute market risk capital under the standardised approach, and internal risk transfers between books are recognised only where the stated conditions are met. It binds banks subject to SAMA's market risk and Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework requiring banks to present a flow statement explaining period-on-period movements in credit risk risk-weighted assets calculated under the internal ratings-based approaches. It sits alongside the wider credit risk suite, with the IRB scope excluding counterparty credit risk, CVA and banking book securitisation exposures, which are disclosed in separate templates. It binds SAMA-licensed banks that have supervisory approval to use F-IRB, A-IRB or supervisory slotting approaches.

Disclosure content keyed to the FSB Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Term Sheet, setting out how a resolution entity reports TLAC-eligible regulatory capital and non-capital instruments, deductions, adjusted RWA, leverage exposure, TLAC ratios and buffer requirements. It reflects Term Sheet conditions on subordination, funding-vehicle instruments, ex ante recapitalisation commitments and the 2.5%/3.5% caps, with separate reporting for single-point-of-entry and multiple-point-of-entry G-SIB resolution groups. Relevant to G-SIB resolution groups and to banks disclosing TLAC-related holdings under the SAMA disclosure framework.

A Pillar 3 template requiring annual backtesting disclosure comparing probabilities of default used in IRB capital calculations against realised obligor default rates per regulatory portfolio, using at least a five-year average annual default rate. Banks must cover key group-wide models approved by SAMA, explain how model scope was determined, state the share of RWA covered, and supplement the flexible-format template with narrative commentary. Mandatory for banks using A-IRB and/or F-IRB, with separate portfolio breakdowns where both approaches are used.

A Pillar 3 template covering exposures risk-weighted under the supervisory slotting criteria within the IRB framework (specialised lending and equity-type treatments), disclosed separately from modelled F-IRB/A-IRB and standardised credit risk exposures. It forms part of the credit risk disclosure suite in SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. Binds banks whose SAMA-approved credit risk approach includes supervisory slotting.

The qualitative disclosure table for counterparty credit risk in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, opening the CCR section that covers all banking book and trading book exposures subject to a CCR charge, including exposures to central counterparties. It is the narrative companion to the quantitative CCR templates (CCR1 and CCR3 to CCR8). Mandatory for banks subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure framework.
lookup_terms: CCR exposures banking and trading book

data.summary: A Pillar 3 template requiring banks to analyse counterparty credit risk exposures by the method used to determine exposure at default, showing replacement cost, potential future exposure, EAD post-CRM and resulting RWA across the CCR approaches. It is the lead quantitative template of the CCR disclosure section, which also covers standardised and IRB portfolio breakdowns, collateral, credit derivatives, IMM flow statements and CCP exposures. Applies to banks with exposures subject to a counterparty credit risk charge under the SAMA disclosure framework.

This node sits within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework and covers the standardised-approach counterparty credit risk disclosure template (CCR3), which presents CCR exposures broken down by regulatory portfolio and risk weight. The accompanying definitions explain the standardised approach per risk type (credit, market, operational), the split between RWA from SAMA-approved modelled approaches and RWA from standardised approaches, and the residual/total rows used for comparison purposes. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime, as a periodic public disclosure obligation.
lookup_terms: CCR exposures by regulatory portfolio and risk weights

data.summary: Template CCR4 is a Pillar 3 disclosure requiring banks that use F-IRB or A-IRB approaches for counterparty credit risk to disclose CCR exposures and model parameters (EAD post-CRM, average PD, obligor numbers, average maturity, RWA) by portfolio and PD band. Separate templates must be produced where both F-IRB and A-IRB are used, with narrative on model scope and RWA coverage; CVA charges and CCP-cleared exposures are excluded. Mandatory semiannually for IRB banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

Template CCR5 requires disclosure of the composition of collateral posted and received in support of counterparty credit risk exposures arising from derivatives and securities financing transactions, including CCP-cleared trades, split by collateral type and segregated/unsegregated status. Fair values of both legs of a transaction must be reported. Mandatory for all banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, on a semiannual basis with narrative explanation of material changes.

This node is the credit derivatives exposures disclosure (Template CCR6) within the counterparty credit risk section of SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, covering protection bought and sold through credit derivatives. The extracted context here mainly reproduces adjacent credit risk templates (CR1 credit quality of assets and CR3 credit risk mitigation illustrations, including allocation of exposures secured by collateral, guarantees and credit derivatives), so verify the template content in the source. Applies to banks subject to SAMA Pillar 3 reporting.
lookup_terms: Template CR1 credit quality of assets

data.summary: Template CCR7 is the Pillar 3 RWA flow statement for counterparty credit risk exposures calculated under the internal models method (IMM), showing period-on-period movements in RWA and their drivers. The surrounding context sets out the OV1-style mapping of RWA and minimum capital requirements across credit risk, CCR, CVA, equity and other approaches, and the standardised/modelled RWA split definitions. It binds banks with SAMA approval to use IMM for CCR under the Pillar 3 framework.

Template CCR8 requires banks to disclose all exposures to central counterparties — trade exposures, initial margin (segregated and non-segregated) and pre-funded/unfunded default fund contributions — with EAD post-CRM and RWA, split between qualifying CCPs and non-qualifying CCPs. It is mandatory for all banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, semiannual, fixed format, with narrative on material changes. The extracted context also includes Table CRB-A on prudential treatment of problem assets (non-performing and forborne exposure definitions).

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework covering market risk capital requirements computed under the standardised approach, reported alongside the wider RWA breakdown (credit risk, counterparty credit risk, CVA, securitisation, settlement risk) and the minimum capital requirement measure. It fixes the rows, definitions and instructions banks must follow when publishing these figures. It binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to the Pillar 3 regime.

A qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table for banks permitted to use the internal models approach (IMA) for market risk, requiring narrative explanation of risk quantification and model governance; the surrounding framework text sets out estimation standards for PD, LGD and EAD and related model requirements. It supports interpretation of modelled capital numbers rather than setting the calculation itself. It binds SAMA-supervised banks with model approval.

A Pillar 3 template disclosing market risk capital under the internal models approach broken down by component — unconstrained and constrained expected shortfall, non-modellable risk factors, default risk charge, amber-desk surcharge and standardised amounts for IMA-ineligible desks. Accompanying text addresses internal risk transfers between banking and trading books and their regulatory capital recognition. It binds banks with SAMA approval to use the IMA.

A Pillar 3 template for banks applying the simplified standardised approach to market risk, presented within the same instruction set governing RWA and minimum capital requirement reporting across risk categories. It prescribes the fixed reporting rows and their definitional scope. It binds SAMA-supervised banks that qualify for and apply the simplified approach.

The general qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table on credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk, sitting at the head of the CVA disclosure suite (CVA1–CVA4, CVAB) and triggered by the materiality threshold in SAMA's revised CCR capital framework. It frames CVA risk as loss from changes in CVA values driven by counterparty credit spreads and market factors, and covers scope of covered transactions and the BA-CVA/SA-CVA split. It binds banks with covered derivative and SFT exposures.

A mandatory semiannual Pillar 3 template reporting the components of RWA under the reduced basic approach for CVA risk — the systematic and idiosyncratic aggregations and the total — with a required narrative on hedge types used even where not recognised under the reduced approach. It links to the overall RWA overview template. It binds banks measuring any part of their CVA RWA under the reduced BA-CVA.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring banks to publish the Business Indicator (BI) and its interest/lease/dividend, services and financial subcomponents, together with the resulting Business Indicator Component used in the standardised operational risk capital calculation. It is mandatory for all banks, fixed-format and annual, with full prior-period disclosure required from the implementation date (the usual retrospective-disclosure relief does not apply). Narrative commentary on significant changes is expected, and additional narrative is required where SAMA has approved exclusion of divested activities from the BI.

A Pillar 3 template in the operational risk disclosure series presenting the bank's minimum required operational risk capital (and related loss/RWA inputs feeding the Pillar 1 requirement). It sits alongside OR1/OR2 in the same SAMA Pillar 3 framework and binds banks subject to the disclosure requirements. Useful when tracing how operational risk RWA and capital requirements reconcile to the overview template OV1.

A qualitative (with some quantitative) Pillar 3 table requiring banks to describe their interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB) definition, management and mitigation strategies, measurement frequency and metrics, shock and stress scenarios, and any divergence between internal measurement system assumptions and those prescribed for Template IRRBB1. Mandatory annually, flexible format, for banks within the Basel IRRBB scope of application. It binds banks and frames the narrative context for the quantitative IRRBB1 disclosures.
lookup_terms: interest rate risk in the banking book

data.summary: The quantitative Pillar 3 template for IRRBB, requiring disclosure of measured changes in economic value of equity (ΔEVE) and net interest income (ΔNII) under the prescribed supervisory interest rate shock scenarios, computed using the bank's own internal measurement system. It pairs with Table IRRBBA and cross-refers to the Basel supervisory review process IRRBB standard and SAMA's IRRBB circular. It binds banks within the IRRBB scope of application.

A Pillar 3 template requiring disclosure of at least the twelve indicators used in the Basel methodology for assessing global systemic importance, with accompanying narrative on reference dates, estimates, structural changes and bucket allocation. Scope is limited: it applies to banks previously classified as G-SIBs, those with a leverage ratio exposure measure above EUR 200 billion, or those included in the assessment sample by supervisory judgment, and SAMA states it need not be completed unless SAMA identifies the bank as a G-SIB. Annual, flexible format.

A Pillar 3 template setting out the geographical distribution of a bank's private sector credit exposures (and related RWA) used to compute the bank-specific countercyclical capital buffer, including the buffer rate applicable in each jurisdiction and the resulting buffer amount. It specifies that pre-announced but not-yet-applicable buffer rates are excluded and that the bank-specific rate is a weighted average calculated under the SAMA capital adequacy rules. Binds banks subject to the Pillar 3 macroprudential disclosures.

A fixed-format Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework covering risk-weighted assets for credit valuation adjustment risk computed under the full version of the basic approach (BA-CVA), broken into the reduced component, the hedged component and the total. It is mandatory, on a semiannual basis, for banks whose CVA RWA is measured in whole or part under the full BA-CVA, populated only with amounts from netting sets under that approach, and it cross-references the counterparty credit risk capital rules and the overall RWA template. Binds SAMA-supervised banks that meet the CVA materiality threshold set in the revised CCR capital framework.

A qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table for banks that have obtained SAMA approval to use the standardised approach for CVA risk (SA-CVA), sitting alongside the quantitative SA-CVA templates CVA3 and CVA4. It supports the CVA risk disclosure block that applies once the materiality threshold in the revised counterparty credit risk capital framework is met, and it reflects the rule that BA-CVA is the default unless SAMA grants SA-CVA approval. Binds SAMA-supervised banks with covered derivative and securities financing transaction exposures using SA-CVA.

The quantitative Pillar 3 template for disclosing RWA and components of the CVA risk capital requirement calculated under the standardised approach (SA-CVA), part of the CVA disclosure set that also includes the BA-CVA templates and the SA-CVA qualitative table. It applies only where the bank has SAMA approval to use SA-CVA and where the CVA materiality threshold in the revised CCR framework is satisfied. Binds SAMA-supervised banks calculating CVA capital for derivatives and fair-valued SFTs in both banking and trading books.

A Pillar 3 flow-statement template showing period-on-period movements in RWA for CVA risk exposures measured under the standardised approach (SA-CVA), completing the CVA disclosure suite with the CVA1–CVA3 templates and tables CVAA/CVAB. It is relevant only to banks approved for SA-CVA and meeting the CVA materiality threshold, and it links to the overall RWA overview reporting. Binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to the CVA capital charge.

The general qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table on a bank's operational risk management framework, sitting within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework alongside the quantitative operational risk templates such as historical losses and business indicator data. It governs narrative disclosure of how operational risk is identified, measured, governed and capitalised under the standardised operational risk capital regime. Binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to Pillar 3 reporting.

A fixed-format annual Pillar 3 template requiring disclosure of aggregate operational risk losses net of recoveries over the past ten years, including excluded losses, at loss-event thresholds of SAR 44,600 and SAR 446,000, plus details of whether losses feed the internal loss multiplier. It is mandatory for banks in the second and third business indicator buckets and for first-bucket banks with SAMA approval to use internal loss data, with narrative commentary expected on new loss exclusions. Binds SAMA-supervised banks calculating operational risk capital; retrospective disclosure of prior periods is required unless SAMA permits fewer years transitionally.

Pillar 3 disclosure template node covering LR1, the reconciliation between a bank's published accounting total assets and the leverage ratio exposure measure. It sits within SAMA's adopted Basel disclosure framework, alongside key-metrics (KM1) and capital distribution constraint (CDC) templates, and specifies purpose, scope, content, frequency and format of the disclosure. Binding on banks supervised by SAMA that are subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Pillar 3 node for template LR2, the common disclosure of leverage ratio components — on-balance sheet exposures, derivative and securities financing transaction exposures, off-balance sheet items, Tier 1 capital and the resulting ratio. It forms part of SAMA's adopted Basel Pillar 3 template set, which also links the leverage ratio to capital distribution constraints and key metrics. Applies to banks under SAMA prudential supervision subject to Pillar 3 disclosure.

Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure node for Table LIQA, covering a bank's liquidity risk management framework: governance, funding strategy, liquidity risk tolerance, stress testing and contingency funding planning. It is the liquidity counterpart to the general risk management table (OVA) within SAMA's disclosure framework, and is narrative/flexible in format. Binding on banks subject to SAMA Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Pillar 3 node for template LIQ1, the quantitative disclosure of the Liquidity Coverage Ratio, including high-quality liquid assets, net cash outflows and the resulting ratio, generally reported as simple averages of daily or monthly observations. It complements the LCR figures summarised in the key metrics template (KM1). Applies to banks under SAMA prudential supervision subject to the LCR standard and Pillar 3 disclosure.

Pillar 3 node for template LIQ2, the quantitative disclosure of the Net Stable Funding Ratio, breaking out available stable funding and required stable funding by category and residual maturity. It is the structural-funding counterpart to LIQ1 and feeds the liquidity metrics summarised in KM1. Binding on banks subject to SAMA's NSFR standard and Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Pillar 3 node for template OV1, the overview of risk-weighted assets by risk type (credit, counterparty credit, securitisation, market, operational and residual RWA), distinguishing modelled approaches approved by SAMA from standardised approaches and showing RWA as if the full standardised approach applied. It includes the definitions and row-by-row instructions that determine how each RWA component is allocated, including output-floor comparison figures. Applies to banks under SAMA prudential supervision subject to Pillar 3 disclosure.

Node covering Template KM1 (Key Metrics) within SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements, part of the overview section on risk management, key prudential metrics and RWA. It sets the fixed content of a time-series disclosure of available capital and ratios (including buffers), RWA (pre- and post-capital-floor), the Basel III leverage ratio exposure measure, LCR and NSFR, plus fully loaded ECL variants where a bank applies the ECL transitional arrangement, and specifies cross-template linkages to CC1 and OV1. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime at the consolidated level.

Node covering Template CMS1, the Pillar 3 disclosure comparing RWA produced by internal/modelled approaches that SAMA has approved against RWA that would result from applying the full standardised approach. It defines, risk category by risk category (credit risk, counterparty credit risk, securitisation in the banking book, market risk, operational risk and residual RWA), which approach counts as "standardised" and how actual versus fully standardised RWA are to be allocated. It binds banks with SAMA model approvals that are subject to the Pillar 3 framework.
lookup_terms: comparison of modelled and standardised RWA

data.summary: Node for Template CR6, the Pillar 3 disclosure of credit risk exposures and IRB parameter estimates broken down by portfolio and PD scale. It sits in the credit risk disclosure set alongside CR1 (credit quality of assets) and CR3 (CRM techniques), and the surrounding material defines the IRB/standardised boundary, EAD post-CRM, PD, LGD and maturity inputs used for RWA. It binds banks permitted to use foundation or advanced IRB approaches for credit risk under SAMA supervision.
lookup_terms: IRB exposures by portfolio and PD scale

data.summary: Node for Template CR3, the Pillar 3 overview of credit risk mitigation techniques, disclosing carrying amounts of unsecured exposures versus exposures secured by collateral, financial guarantees or credit derivatives. It defines how multi-secured and over- or under-collateralised exposures are allocated across the columns and includes worked allocation scenarios; surrounding context also covers related credit risk templates (CR1, CCR4). It is mandatory for banks within the SAMA Pillar 3 disclosure scope.

Concept node for the internal ratings-based (IRB) approach to credit risk in SAMA's credit risk capital framework, covering asset class definitions (corporate, sovereign, bank, retail, equity, purchased receivables), foundation versus advanced approaches, risk-weight functions, risk components (PD/LGD/EAD/M), supervisory slotting for specialised lending, RWA for purchased receivables including dilution risk, treatment of expected loss and provisions, and the minimum requirements for IRB use. It applies to banks seeking or holding SAMA permission to use IRB approaches for regulatory capital.

Concept node for the External Credit Risk Assessment Approach (ECRA), under which banks risk-weight rated exposures (notably bank exposures) by reference to external ratings from ECAIs recognised by SAMA, with mandatory due diligence that can only push a risk weight to a higher bucket, never lower. The surrounding context contrasts ECRA with the Standardised Credit Risk Assessment Approach (SCRA) for unrated bank exposures and sets out operational criteria for using external credit assessments, including in the securitisation framework. It binds banks applying the standardised approach to credit risk under SAMA rules.
lookup_terms: external rating risk weight bank exposures

data.summary: Object finance is one of three specialized lending subcategories within the corporate exposure class under SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk (standardized approach). It covers funding for the acquisition of equipment (ships, aircraft, satellites, railcars, fleets) where repayment depends on cash flows from the financed asset pledged or assigned to the lender; where no issue-specific external rating is available, such exposures are risk-weighted at 100%. It binds banks licensed and supervised by SAMA when calculating credit risk RWAs.

Commodities finance is a specialized lending subcategory under the corporate exposure class in SAMA's credit risk capital framework, covering short-term lending against reserves, inventories or receivables of exchange-traded commodities where repayment comes from sale proceeds and the borrower has no independent repayment capacity. Absent an issue-specific external rating, these exposures carry a 100% risk weight; issuer ratings may not be substituted. Applies to SAMA-licensed banks computing credit risk RWAs.

This node concerns the corporate MSME exposure subcategory within the corporate exposure class of SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk. It marks the boundary between MSME exposures that meet the regulatory retail criteria (treated as retail) and those that do not (treated as corporate MSMEs), and sits within the broader corporate class covering incorporated entities, partnerships, trusts, funds, insurers, securities firms and other financial institutions, but not individuals. It binds SAMA-supervised banks in classifying counterparties and assigning risk weights.

This node sets out how equity exposures are defined and risk-weighted under SAMA's credit risk capital framework, based on the economic substance of the instrument rather than its legal form, covering direct and indirect, voting and non-voting ownership interests and instruments structured to convey equity economics. Speculative unlisted equity (short-term resale, venture capital-type holdings) attracts a 400% risk weight; all other equity holdings 250%. It binds SAMA-licensed banks and, in specified cases, requires SAMA's agreement before an instrument is treated as debt or risks decomposed.

This node covers the treatment of subordinated debt, equity and other regulatory capital instruments issued by corporates or banks under SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk. It applies only where such instruments are not deducted from regulatory capital, not already risk-weighted at 250% under the SAMA Basel III regulatory capital framework, not risk-weighted at 1250%, and excludes equity investments in funds. It binds SAMA-supervised banks and interacts with the regulatory capital rules for deductions.
lookup_terms: Basel III regulatory capital framework SAMA

data.summary: This node defines the retail exposure class under SAMA's credit risk standardized approach, comprising exposures to individuals and to MSMEs meeting the "regulatory retail" criteria (product type, an aggregate exposure cap of SAR 4.46 million per counterparty, and a 0.2% granularity limit), while excluding real estate exposures. It distinguishes regulatory retail exposures to "transactors" (45% risk weight) from other regulatory retail (75%) and "other retail" (100%). It binds SAMA-licensed banks in classifying and risk-weighting retail credit.
lookup_terms: credit cards and overdrafts risk weight

data.summary: This node covers the Standardized Credit Risk Assessment Approach within SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk, applied by banks to bank counterparty exposures that lack an eligible external rating. It requires classification of such exposures into Grades A, B or C with corresponding base and short-term risk weights, subject to conditions (including CET1 and Tier 1 leverage thresholds for a preferential unrated treatment) and to due diligence that may only push risk weights higher, never lower. It binds SAMA-supervised banks calculating credit risk RWAs under the standardized approach.
lookup_terms: Grade A Grade B Grade C
risk weight table for bank exposures

data.summary: An Arabic-language SAMA circular (from the Deputy Governor for Supervision) confirming that registration fees charged by the contracts registration company fall within the fees, commissions and administrative service costs capped by Article 83 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law. It confirms such fees cannot be passed to the customer outside that cap (the lower of 1% of the finance amount or SAR 5,000), reinforcing an earlier circular that the cap covers all unavoidable charges beyond the finance amount and term cost. It binds banks and finance companies operating in KSA (and is copied to the Saudi Finance Lease Contract Registration Company).
lookup_terms: Article 83 Implementing Regulation Finance Companies Control Law
fees commissions and administrative service costs cap

data.summary: This node is the corporate exposure class definition in SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk (standardized approach), covering loans, bonds and receivables to incorporated entities, associations, partnerships, proprietorships, trusts and funds not falling in another exposure class. It absorbs securities firms and other financial institutions, and insurance/other financial corporates that are not bank exposures, while excluding exposures to individuals, and splits into general corporate and specialized lending subcategories. It binds banks classifying exposures for credit risk RWA purposes.
lookup_terms: securities firms and other financial institutions

data.summary: This node isolates the general corporate exposures subcategory of the corporate exposure class under SAMA's standardized approach for credit risk, i.e. corporate exposures other than specialized lending. It is the residual bucket for entities that do not qualify as bank, sovereign, PSE, retail or real estate exposures and do not meet the specialized lending criteria. It binds banks assigning risk weights to corporate counterparties.

This node covers specialized lending (SL) as a subcategory of corporate exposures in SAMA's credit risk capital framework, comprising project finance, object finance, commodities finance, income-producing real estate and high-volatility commercial real estate. It is characterised by the borrower being an entity with little independent repayment capacity, with repayment driven by the financed asset's income and the lender holding substantial control over the asset. It is relevant to banks under both the standardized approach (including fixed risk weights where no issue-specific rating exists) and the IRB supervisory slotting approach.
lookup_terms: project finance object finance commodities finance

data.summary: This node defines project finance (PF) as a specialized lending sub-class where the lender looks primarily to revenues of a single project for repayment and security, typically with an SPV borrower confined to developing, owning and operating the installation. It sets out the standardized-approach risk weights where no issue-specific rating is available (higher in the pre-operational phase, lower in the operational phase, with a reduced weight for high-quality operational exposures) and the conditions for the high-quality classification, including creditor protections, reserve funding and availability-based or rate-of-return revenues. It binds banks risk-weighting project finance exposures.

Defines the "regulatory retail" sub-class within the retail exposure class under SAMA's standardised approach to credit risk capital, listing the product, low-value (SAR 4.46 million aggregate per counterparty) and 0.2% granularity criteria, and distinguishing it from "other retail". It drives the applicable risk weights (75% for non-transactor regulatory retail, 45% for transactors, 100% for other retail) and covers both individuals and qualifying MSMEs, with MSMEs failing the criteria pushed to corporate treatment. Binds banks in the Kingdom calculating minimum capital requirements for credit risk.

Defines "transactors" for standardised credit risk purposes: obligors on credit card/charge card facilities repaid in full at every scheduled repayment date over the previous 12 months, and overdraft obligors with no drawdown over that period. The classification is consequential because regulatory retail exposures to transactors attract a 45% risk weight instead of 75%. Applies to banks assigning risk weights to retail exposures.

Sets out the real estate exposure class in the standardised approach: what counts as real estate (immovable property), and the split into regulatory real estate, other real estate, and land acquisition, development and construction (ADC) exposures. It further splits regulatory real estate into residential/commercial and materially-dependent/non-dependent on property cash flows, and gives risk weights for commercial materially-dependent exposures (70/90/110% by LTV band) and for other real estate (counterparty risk weight, or 150% where materially cash-flow dependent). Binds banks computing credit risk RWAs.
lookup_terms: materially dependent on cash flows generated by the property

data.summary: Defines "regulatory real estate" and its four sub-categories, including what makes an exposure "regulatory residential" (secured by a lawful dwelling) versus "regulatory commercial" (the residual), and when an exposure is "materially dependent on cash flows generated by the property" (loan servicing and recovery depend on lease, rental or sale proceeds rather than borrower capacity). Notes the material-dependence test typically bites on corporate, MSME and SPV lending. Relevant to banks classifying mortgage and property-secured exposures for capital purposes.

Specifies how the loan-to-value ratio is calculated and maintained for real estate exposures: loan amount (including undrawn committed amounts, gross of provisions, with limited netting for pledged deposits) over an independently and conservatively appraised property value, generally frozen at origination subject to downward revision, permanent-impairment adjustment, or value-enhancing modifications. It also requires mortgage underwriting policies assessing repayment ability and confirms that LTV bucket and risk weight are set before applying credit risk mitigation. Binds banks originating and risk-weighting mortgage lending.

Node for the "whole loan approach" — the method of assigning a single LTV-based risk weight to the entire real estate exposure amount (as used in the commercial real estate tables) rather than splitting the loan. The supplied context for this node is largely document contents listing and IRB roll-out provisions rather than the whole loan approach text itself, so verify against the real estate chapter before relying on it. Concerns banks calculating credit risk RWAs on property-secured exposures.
lookup_terms: regulatory real estate risk weight table

data.summary: A node within SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk (Version 2.1, December 2022) addressing the loan-splitting method for determining risk weights, used in the real estate exposure class where an exposure is divided into a portion secured by property value and a residual portion weighted on the counterparty. Binds banks subject to SAMA's capital adequacy framework when computing risk-weighted assets. Note that the context extracted here concerns the phased rollout of the IRB approach across asset classes and business units (implementation plan agreed with SAMA, no capital relief for intra-group transactions), so confirm the exact paragraph before relying on it.

Defines "land acquisition, development and construction" (ADC) exposures as one of the three components of the real estate exposure class under the standardized approach in SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk, alongside regulatory real estate and other real estate exposures. Real estate is defined as immovable property (land, including agricultural and forest land, and attached structures such as buildings). Binds banks applying the standardized approach to credit risk under SAMA supervision.
lookup_terms: materially dependent on cash flows generated by the property

data.summary: A node covering the risk weight multiplier applied to certain unhedged exposures where the borrower's income currency differs from the currency of the loan, within the standardized approach chapter of SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk. Binds banks calculating standardized-approach RWAs. The extracted context here instead covers short-term versus long-term external ratings and the treatment of credit risk mitigants for dilution risk, so verify the operative paragraph before citing.

Addresses the capital treatment of off-balance sheet items, including the application of credit conversion factors (CCFs) under the standardized approach and the estimation of exposure at default (EAD) for such items under the advanced IRB approach. Sets out that EAD must be estimated as the expected gross exposure at obligor default with a margin of conservatism, and specifies when own estimates versus foundation CCFs apply. Binds banks subject to SAMA's credit risk capital framework.

Covers the capital treatment of credit derivatives under SAMA's credit risk framework, both where a bank sells protection (first-to-default, second-to-default and nth-to-default derivatives, with risk weights aggregated up to a 1250% cap) and where it buys protection as credit risk mitigation. Only credit default swaps and total return swaps providing guarantee-equivalent protection are eligible mitigants; nth-to-default derivatives give no capital relief to the protection buyer. Binds banks calculating RWAs under SAMA's capital rules.

Section of the standardized approach in SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk setting the risk weight treatment for defaulted exposures. Related definitional context excludes defaulted retail exposures from the regulatory retail portfolio when testing the granularity criterion (no aggregated counterparty exposure above 0.2% of the portfolio, absolute threshold SAR 4.46 million). Binds banks applying the standardized approach to credit risk.

A component of SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk dealing with the use of external (or inferred) credit ratings to set risk weights, including the securitization external-ratings-based approach (SEC-ERBA) where risk weights turn on rating grade, seniority, tranche maturity and, for non-senior tranches, tranche thickness. It sets operational criteria that must be met before external or inferred ratings may be relied upon for capital purposes. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Basel-aligned credit risk capital framework.

Defines External Credit Assessment Institutions and the eligibility criteria SAMA applies before an ECAI's ratings may be used for regulatory capital, covering resources, credibility, independence, disclosure of conflicts of interest and compensation arrangements, and cooperation with SAMA. It also underpins bank internal assessment processes (e.g. SEC-IAA) that must map to ECAI standards and use the most conservative ECAI stress factors where ratings differ. It binds banks using external ratings and sets expectations on recognised ECAIs.

Covers how SAMA assigns eligible ECAI rating grades to the risk weights available under the standardized risk weighting framework, together with the mapping table banks may apply and SAMA's right to review and revise that mapping. It sits alongside the ECAI eligibility and disclosure requirements. It binds banks calculating standardized-approach credit risk-weighted assets using external ratings.

Sets out the simple approach to credit risk mitigation, under which the counterparty's risk weight is substituted by the risk weight of the collateral instrument for the collateralized portion of an exposure. It imposes recognition conditions, notably that collateral be pledged for at least the life of the exposure and be marked to market and revalued at least every six months, within the wider collateral management and custodian-segregation requirements. It binds banks applying the standardized approach to credit risk.

Concerns the comprehensive approach to collateralised transactions, the alternative to the simple approach, under which exposure and collateral values are adjusted for volatility rather than substituting risk weights. The surrounding material addresses collateral reuse risks, custodian segregation, capital on both sides of repo and securities lending transactions, agent-arranged transactions with guarantees, and how F-IRB LGD interacts with recognised and non-recognised collateral. It binds banks recognising financial collateral for capital relief.

Defines the collateral that may be recognised for capital purposes, distinguishing eligible financial collateral under the standardized approach from the broader eligible IRB collateral (receivables, commercial and residential real estate, other physical collateral) recognised under the foundation IRB approach. It sets the definition of eligible financial receivables and the legal certainty conditions: enforceability, perfected first-priority claim, binding documentation and sufficient legal review in all relevant jurisdictions. It binds banks claiming collateral-based capital relief.

This node covers the supervisory haircut mechanics within the comprehensive approach to credit risk mitigation under SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk framework, including how exposure and collateral values are volatility-adjusted and how haircut size varies with the prescribed holding period, instrument type, transaction type, residual maturity and remargining/mark-to-market frequency. Adjacent material covers rating-assignment criteria under the IRB supervisory slotting approach and mapping internal grades to the five supervisory categories. It binds SAMA-supervised banks calculating regulatory capital for credit risk.

This node addresses eligibility and capital treatment of guarantees and credit derivatives as credit protection, including the exclusion of nth-to-default derivatives, conditions for total return swaps, substitution of the protection provider's risk weight for the protected portion, and the 1250% treatment of materiality thresholds. It also covers recognition of guarantees and tranched/pro rata credit protection in the securitization framework, including the exclusion of SPEs as eligible guarantors. It binds banks computing regulatory capital under SAMA's credit risk rules.

This node sets out when a maturity mismatch between credit protection and the underlying exposure may still be recognized (original maturity of at least one year, residual maturity of at least three months), the partial-recognition adjustment formula, and the conservative definitions of hedge and exposure maturity. It also covers how maturity mismatches are handled for securitization exposures and synthetic securitizations. It binds banks applying credit risk mitigation for regulatory capital purposes.

This node concerns the internal ratings-based treatment of corporate exposures, including the categorization of banking-book exposures into asset classes and the definitions used for securitization pool classification (IRB pool, mixed pool, SA pool) that depend on IRB approval and data sufficiency. It signposts the IRB chapters on risk-weight functions, risk components, purchased receivables, expected loss and minimum requirements. It binds banks with, or seeking, SAMA approval to use IRB approaches.

This node identifies the five specialized lending sub-classes within the IRB corporate asset class and their defining characteristics, together with the supervisory slotting approach used to assign risk weights (PF, OF, CF, IPRE and HVCRE) and to compute expected loss for SL exposures. It binds banks classifying banking-book exposures and calculating IRB capital, subject to demonstrating to SAMA that their classification methodology is appropriate and consistent.

This node defines income-producing real estate lending as funding where repayment and recovery depend primarily on cash flows generated by the property, distinguishing it from other corporate exposures merely collateralized by real estate, and contrasts it with high-volatility commercial real estate (including ADC financing). It also connects to the standardized approach real estate exposure class and the "materially dependent on cash flows" distinction. It binds banks classifying and risk-weighting real estate exposures under SAMA's credit risk capital rules.

This node covers the retail exposure class within SAMA's minimum capital requirements for credit risk, setting out how retail exposures are defined and segmented into regulatory retail (transactor and non-transactor) and other retail. It fixes the qualifying criteria — product type, an absolute aggregated exposure ceiling per counterparty, and a granularity limit relative to the overall regulatory retail portfolio — and the corresponding risk weights; real estate exposures sit outside the class and non-qualifying MSME exposures fall back to corporate treatment. It binds SAMA-supervised banks calculating risk-weighted assets for credit risk.

This node concerns equity exposures under the IRB framework and their interaction with the securitisation capital rules, including how IRB pools, mixed pools and standardised-approach pools are classified for risk-based capital. It also addresses implicit support to a securitisation, the resulting capital consequence, non-recognition of gain on sale, and the look-through risk-weight caps for senior securitisation exposures. It binds banks supervised by SAMA in determining credit risk capital, with several determinations reserved to SAMA approval or prohibition.

This node describes the foundation internal ratings-based approach, under which banks supply their own probability of default estimates and use supervisory values for the remaining risk components, always applying the prescribed risk-weight functions. It also sets out the three elements of the IRB framework (risk components, risk-weight functions, minimum requirements), the exclusions from A-IRB and from IRB generally (notably equities), and the conditions for phased rollout across asset classes and business units. It binds banks seeking or operating IRB permission, with the rollout plan requiring SAMA agreement.

This node covers the advanced internal ratings-based approach, where banks estimate PD, LGD and EAD and calculate maturity themselves subject to minimum standards, while still using the prescribed risk-weight functions. It identifies exposures for which A-IRB is not available — including large general corporates above a consolidated revenue threshold and bank/financial institution exposures — and equities for which IRB is not permitted, and it frames the phased migration from foundation to advanced. It binds SAMA-supervised banks using or applying for IRB permission.
lookup_terms: own estimates of LGD and EAD

data.summary: This node points to the supervisory slotting approach for specialised lending within the IRB chapter structure, covering risk weights for project, object, commodities finance and income-producing real estate, the separate treatment of high-volatility commercial real estate, expected loss for slotted exposures, and the qualitative slotting criteria. The context is largely the framework's chapter map, so the operative detail sits in the referenced slotting chapter. It binds banks on IRB that cannot meet the requirements for own PD estimates on specialised lending exposures.
lookup_terms: project finance object finance commodities finance

data.summary: This node relates to the IRB risk-weight functions that convert risk components into risk-weighted assets, including treatment of defaulted exposures and of corporate, sovereign and bank exposures, alongside the purchased receivables chapter's rules on recognising credit risk mitigants. It explains how guarantees and collateral covering default risk, dilution risk or both are substituted or apportioned, including where mitigants provide first-loss protection interacting with the securitisation IRB approach. It binds SAMA-supervised banks computing IRB credit risk capital.

Concept node covering the four IRB risk components — probability of default (PD), loss given default (LGD), exposure at default (EAD) and effective maturity (M) — as used in SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk to drive the IRB risk-weight functions. It distinguishes foundation IRB (supervisory parameter values) from advanced IRB (own estimates) across corporate, sovereign, bank, retail, equity and purchased receivable asset classes, and covers how credit risk mitigants such as guarantees and collateral feed into the parameters. It binds SAMA-supervised banks that have adopted, or seek approval for, an internal ratings-based approach.

Concept node on expected loss (EL) under the IRB approach: how banks calculate EL amounts, compare them with eligible provisions, and treat any shortfall or excess in regulatory capital. It also covers the treatment of defaulted assets, where the bank must form a best estimate of expected loss and hold capital for the excess of LGD over that estimate, with supervisory scrutiny where the estimate falls below specific provisions and partial charge-offs. Applies to SAMA-supervised banks using IRB for credit risk.

Concept node for the supervisory slotting criteria applied to object finance (OF), a sub-class of specialized lending, where banks unable to estimate PD map internal grades to five supervisory categories (strong, good, satisfactory, weak, default) with prescribed risk weights and expected loss amounts. The linked minimum requirements govern rating structure, use of current and material information, and demonstrating that the internal-to-supervisory mapping is consistent. Binds SAMA-supervised banks using IRB for specialized lending exposures.
lookup_terms: slotting categories strong good satisfactory weak

data.summary: Concept node for the supervisory slotting criteria applied to commodities finance (CF), a specialized lending sub-class, setting the assessment factors and characteristics used to assign exposures to the five supervisory categories and their associated risk weights and expected loss amounts. It connects to the IRB minimum requirements on rating structure, information quality and the mapping of internal grades to supervisory categories. Binds SAMA-supervised banks applying the slotting approach to specialized lending.

Concept node on calculating risk-weighted assets for default risk on purchased receivables under the IRB approach, including use of top-down pool estimates and the interaction with credit risk mitigants. It sets out how guarantees covering default risk (alone or together with dilution risk) allow substitution of the guarantor's risk weight, and how uncovered portions are treated under proportional or tranched coverage rules. Applies to SAMA-supervised banks using IRB for purchased receivable exposures.

Concept node on the separate capital charge for dilution risk on purchased receivables — the risk that receivable amounts are reduced by credits or offsets to the obligor — and how its RWA is calculated and added to default risk RWA under the IRB approach. It covers recognition of collateral and guarantees that cover dilution losses, including first-loss protection interacting with the securitization framework and SEC-IRBA exposure-weighted LGD. Binds SAMA-supervised banks using IRB for purchased receivables.

This node covers the foundation variant of the internal ratings-based approach within SAMA's minimum capital requirements for credit risk, where a bank uses its own probability of default estimates but supervisory values for other risk components such as loss given default and exposure at default. It sits alongside the rules on asset class definitions, adoption of IRB per asset class, phased roll-out and the implementation plan that must be agreed with SAMA. It binds banks that have obtained SAMA approval to use IRB for regulatory capital purposes.

This node concerns the advanced IRB treatment, under which a bank uses own estimates of loss given default and exposure at default in addition to probability of default, where SAMA permits such use. It is framed by the roll-out provisions allowing a staged move from the foundation to the advanced approach across asset classes and business units, subject to an implementation plan agreed with SAMA and a prohibition on cherry-picking to minimise capital. It applies to SAMA-approved IRB banks and their banking groups.
lookup_terms: own estimates of LGD and EAD

data.summary: This node addresses the capital charge for dilution risk on purchased receivables under the IRB framework, including how dilution PD, LGD and maturity inputs feed the risk weight calculation and how dilution risk is recognised when applying the securitisation internal ratings-based approach. It also relates to the worked examples distinguishing common and non-common loss waterfalls for default and dilution losses. It binds IRB banks holding purchased receivables or securitisation exposures to such pools.

This node sets out how credit risk mitigants are recognised for purchased receivables under the IRB approach, in particular the substitution treatment for guarantees from the seller or a third party depending on whether cover extends to default risk, dilution risk or both, and the treatment of partial or tranched cover. It also notes when collateral or partial guarantees providing first-loss protection fall to be treated under the securitisation chapters. It binds IRB banks calculating capital on receivables pools.

This node covers the IRB chapter on expected losses and provisions, explaining that risk-weight functions capitalise unexpected loss while expected loss is addressed separately through comparison with eligible provisions. It links the calculation of expected losses, the calculation of provisions, and the capital consequences of any shortfall or excess. It binds banks approved by SAMA to use the IRB approach for credit risk.

This node defines total eligible provisions for IRB purposes as the aggregate of specific provisions, partial write-offs and portfolio-specific general provisions attributed to IRB exposures, plus permitted discounts on defaulted assets, while excluding provisions held against securitisation exposures. It also sets out how banks using both standardised and IRB approaches allocate general provisions between the two treatments, including pro rata attribution and SAMA discretion to accept internal allocation methods. It binds banks using IRB for all or part of their credit risk exposures.

Node covering the expected loss (EL) amount concept in SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Credit Risk (Basel III credit risk framework): EL multiplied by exposure at default, aggregated across all IRB exposures to give a total EL amount that is then compared with eligible provisions for capital purposes. It sets how EL is derived (PD x LGD for non-defaulted corporate, sovereign, bank and retail exposures; best-estimate expected loss or supervisory LGD for defaulted exposures; slotting-based EL for specialised lending), and excludes securitisation exposures. Binds SAMA-licensed banks that have been permitted to use the internal ratings-based approach.
