It covers development approach, secure coding standards, testing types, version control, quality control, data migration, documentation and end-user training, plus approved low-level system design documents and secure code review (or an independent assurance statement where source code is unavailable). Applies to Member Organizations, including for externally developed applications.

Testing controls within the system change management section of the SAMA IT Governance Framework. It requires documented test cases with defined attributes, minimum testing types (unit, system integration, stress where applicable, security and user acceptance testing), testing in a separate test environment, formal business-user acceptance, positive and negative scenarios, retention of UAT results, and use of sanitised rather than production data. It also flags third-party testing certification where applicable. Binds Member Organizations.

Short sub-section of the SAMA IT Governance Framework requiring cyber security requirements to be defined and fully tested in a test environment for all changes to information systems, so vulnerabilities are identified and mitigated before production release. It expressly ties the change management process back to the SAMA Cyber Security Framework for defining, testing and implementing those security requirements. Applies to Member Organizations.

A control area within the System Change Management chapter of SAMA's IT governance/IT controls framework, addressing how approved and tested changes are released into production, including use of agreed change windows and a separate approval route for exceptions. It sits alongside adjacent requirements on change governance, change testing (unit, SIT, stress, security and UAT, using sanitized rather than production data) and change security requirements aligned to the SAMA Cyber Security Framework. It binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA, which must define, approve, implement, communicate and periodically evaluate the process.

Control requirements obliging Member Organizations to define, approve, implement and communicate a configuration management process that keeps reliable and accurate records of configuration items (CIs) for their information assets. It covers roles and responsibilities, identification and criticality of CIs against supporting business processes, interrelationships between CIs, periodic verification, and maintenance of a configuration management database (CMDB). The process must also be monitored and periodically evaluated.

Requires Member Organizations to define, approve, implement and communicate a patch management process so that applicable functional and non-functional patches are installed in a timely manner, reducing technical failures and security breaches arising from unremediated vulnerabilities. Effectiveness of the process must be measured and periodically evaluated. It forms part of the System Change Management chapter and interacts with IT risk management and configuration management controls.

Sets out the formal IT project management requirements for Member Organizations: an approved framework, policy and procedure covering the project lifecycle from initiation to closure, detailed project plans (scope, milestones, deliverables, roles, risks), and mandatory documentation such as the project charter, requirements and information-flow analysis, feasibility and cost-benefit analysis. It also requires an IT project steering committee with business and technical representation, and risk assessment, mitigation and monitoring throughout the project lifecycle, with process effectiveness monitored and periodically evaluated.

Requires Member Organizations to establish an approved, communicated quality assurance process that independently verifies that changes or developments to information assets meet business/user and applicable regulatory requirements before release to production. It prescribes clear QA roles, minimum quality requirements, and handling of quality records, and requires the QA function to be independent in existence and reporting so it can give objective evaluation and report results to stakeholders with improvement recommendations.

Node for the SAMA organisational unit referenced in connection with this IT governance/IT controls framework; the surrounding text concerns the IT risk management chapter (risk identification and analysis, risk register content, risk treatment options of accept/avoid/transfer/mitigate, and risk reporting, monitoring and profiling). It is useful for locating the supervisory owner of the framework and the IT risk governance expectations imposed on Member Organizations, including reporting to business owners, senior management, the risk committee and the ITSC. Substantive obligations in the surrounding context bind Member Organizations rather than the department itself.
lookup_terms: General Department of Cyber Risk Control

data.summary: A subdomain of SAMA's Cyber Security Framework requiring Member Organizations to define, approve, implement and monitor cyber security controls within a cloud computing policy and process, with periodic measurement of effectiveness. It is expressly scoped to hybrid and public cloud services and does not apply to private (internal) cloud, and it sits alongside the adjacent outsourcing subdomain, which requires prior SAMA approval for material outsourcing and compliance with the SAMA outsourcing circular. Compliance is assessed against the framework's six-level cyber security maturity model through self-assessment and SAMA review.

Part of SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Operational Risk, setting the criteria banks must follow to build and maintain the internal operational loss data set used in the standardized approach. It fixes definitions of gross loss, net loss and recoveries, mandatory inclusions (direct P&L charges, consequential costs, provisions, pending and timing losses) and exclusions (general maintenance, post-event business enhancements, insurance premiums), plus use of the date of accounting and allocation of related losses across years. It binds domestic banks on both a consolidated and standalone basis and makes exclusion of loss events subject to SAMA approval.

The framing and scope provisions of SAMA's operational risk capital framework implementing the Basel III post-crisis reforms (December 2017), adopting the revised standardized approach as the sole method for calculating operational risk capital. It defines operational risk, sets the ORC = BIC × ILM calculation with the Business Indicator thresholds, quarterly Q17 reporting within 30 days of quarter-end, and loss-data disclosure duties. It applies to domestic banks consolidated and standalone, excludes foreign bank branches, and supersedes conflicting prior Basel II guidance.

Covers how operational loss events are identified, classified and treated for inclusion in the standardized approach loss data set under SAMA's operational risk capital framework. It addresses grouping of losses arising from a common or related operational risk events, allocation across accounting years, the accounting-date reference for legal loss events, and the required policies and procedures for classification. Binding on domestic banks; removal of events from the loss component requires strong justification and SAMA approval.

The structural and governance-leadership portion of SAMA's IT Governance Framework, explaining how the framework is organised into domains and subdomains, each with a principle and mandated Control Requirements, and covering IT governance and leadership topics such as IT strategy, enterprise architecture, IT policies and procedures, and roles and responsibilities. It also sets the compliance mechanics: periodic self-assessment by Member Organizations, SAMA review and audit, a six-level IT governance maturity model, and a formal waiver route where controls cannot be met. It binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA.

The IT Risk Management domain of SAMA's IT Governance Framework, requiring Member Organizations to define, approve, implement and communicate an IT risk management process aligned with enterprise risk management, covering risk identification, analysis and classification, treatment, reporting, monitoring and profiling. It prescribes a centralised IT risk register, analysis attributes (asset classification, threats, impact and likelihood, existing controls, risk and control owners, inherent and residual risk), key risk indicators, and treatment within the risk appetite approved by the ITSC. Scope extends to business processes and data, applications, infrastructure, people and third-party relationships.

A methodology section of SAMA's Rules on Stress Testing describing scenario analysis as the measurement of portfolio value changes arising from simultaneous moves in multiple risk factors, alongside sensitivity analysis. It sets expectations for scenario design: scenarios must reflect the bank's own business environment and risk profile, may be historical or hypothetical (each with stated limitations), must capture all material risk factors and both on- and off-balance sheet exposures, and must include at least one viability-threatening (reverse) scenario. It binds banks licensed and supervised by SAMA, which are expected to select methods proportionate to their nature, size, complexity and risk profile.

This node covers the reverse stress testing requirement in SAMA's Rules on Stress Testing, together with the adjacent guidance on use of financial/statistical models. Banks must stress test their business plan to the point of failure — where loss of market confidence makes the business unviable — identify the adverse circumstances that would produce that outcome, assess their likelihood, and take remedial measures where the resulting failure risk is inconsistent with the bank's risk appetite or tolerance. It also reflects SAMA's supervisory review of stress testing programs through ICAAP discussions and on-site examinations.

Sets out how banks must stress test credit exposures under SAMA's Rules on Stress Testing, covering both on- and off-balance sheet exposures and estimating impacts on asset quality, profitability and capital. Banks may use the Standardised or IRB approach and risk parameters such as EAD, PD, LGD and maturity, and are expected to design their own scenarios (e.g. oil price declines, economic downturn, parameter shifts) rather than rely on SAMA-supplied standard scenarios. Accompanying FAQ material confirms that banks cannot limit testing to major portfolio segments and must reflect portfolio nature, size and mix, including retail and consumer books.

Addresses market risk stress testing under SAMA's Rules on Stress Testing: banks must test the resilience of on- and off-balance sheet positions exposed to adverse movements in interest rates, FX rates, equity prices, credit spreads and commodity prices. It breaks market risk into component factors, notably interest rate risk (re-pricing, basis, yield curve and options risk), with duration GAP or equivalent models as possible techniques. FAQ material clarifies that SAMA will not supply a covariance matrix or common multifactor methodology; banks choose techniques suited to their own risk profile, and stress effects are applied as at the reporting date.
lookup_terms: foreign exchange and equity price risk

data.summary: This node sits within SAMA's Rules on Stress Testing and is framed by the implementation and monitoring provisions, under which SAMA assesses the adequacy of banks' stress scenarios, methodologies, assumptions, frequency and board/senior management involvement through supervisory review, ICAAP meetings and on-site examinations. The associated FAQ material confirms banks must identify their own risk factors and apply stress effects as at the reporting date, while SAMA may mandate ad-hoc tests using standard scenarios. Binding on SAMA-supervised banks; open the source for the specific liquidity risk scenarios and parameters.

Covers operational risk stress testing under SAMA's Rules on Stress Testing: banks must build scenarios from their own past operational loss event data plus professional judgement, using assumptions distinct from those applied to credit and market risk, and must feed any resulting additional capital need into capital planning. Plausible scenarios include major business disruption or system/telecommunication failures assessed for their effect on earnings and capital. The node also reflects the residual "other risks" expectation that banks identify and stress further material risks, and SAMA's supervisory monitoring of program effectiveness and compliance.

A concept node covering the role of the Member Organization's IT steering committee within SAMA's IT Governance Framework, principally as a mandatory internal approval gate before any request to amend the Framework or to obtain a waiver from a control requirement is escalated to SAMA through the CEO or managing director. It sits alongside the CIO sign-off, business-owner accountability and risk-committee endorsement of IT risk assessment results and residual risk acceptance. It binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations, not SAMA itself; the Framework continues to apply in full while any update or waiver request is pending.
lookup_terms: General Department of Cyber Risk Control

data.summary: An orientation node for the structure and assessment mechanics of SAMA's IT Governance Framework: how it is organised into domains and subdomains, each with a principle and numbered control requirements, and how compliance is measured. It also covers the periodic self-assessment questionnaire reviewed and audited by SAMA, the six-level IT governance maturity model (0-5, cumulative), and the option of compensating controls plus internal risk acceptance and a formal SAMA waiver where a control cannot be met. Relevant to all Member Organizations subject to the Framework.

An Arabic-language SAMA circular addressed to credit information companies, issued under the Credit Information Law and its Implementing Regulations. It requires those companies to obtain SAMA's prior no-objection before supplying any data or statistics to governmental or non-governmental entities, carving out only what is already covered by member agreements concluded under that Law and its Regulations. It binds licensed credit bureaus and constrains their data-sharing and disclosure practices.

SAMA's Rules on Stress Testing for banks, setting out mandatory requirements for stress testing as part of a bank's risk management and ICAAP, including types and frequency of tests, board and senior management responsibilities, framework design, methodologies, scenario selection and periodic reporting to SAMA. The document also includes SAMA's supervisory review approach and an FAQ clarifying that banks choose their own methodologies and risk factors, with SAMA able to impose standard scenarios. Binds banks supervised by SAMA.

A concept node on the Basel Committee's 2009 Principles for Sound Stress Testing Practices and Supervision as incorporated into SAMA's stress testing regime: SAMA circulated the Principles to banks in 2009 and requires banks to take them into account, in addition to the Rules, when designing and implementing stress testing programmes. Where the Rules and the BCBS Principles conflict, banks must seek SAMA guidance rather than resolve the inconsistency themselves. Also relevant for the Rules' effective date and the deadline for having a compliant framework in place.
lookup_terms: BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing Practices

data.summary: A definitional node within SAMA's stress testing Rules describing sensitivity analysis as a stress testing technique: measuring the change in portfolio value from shocks of varying degrees to a single risk factor or a small set of closely related factors, without evaluating the relationships between risk factors, with capital typically the dependent variable. It sits alongside scenario analysis, financial models and reverse stress testing among the methodologies banks may combine, chosen according to the nature, size, complexity and risk profile of the bank.

A section of SAMA's Rules on Stress Testing describing supervisory (top-down/macro) stress testing, distinct from banks' own bottom-up tests. It sets out SAMA's three-component approach: using banks' submitted bottom-up results, directing banks to run SAMA-specified sensitivity or scenario tests and report the outcomes, and SAMA running its own system-wide tests on macroeconomic and collected banking data. The reporting obligations bind banks; the accompanying Q&A confirms SAMA will not formally release its top-down results, though high-level findings may be shared in bilateral supervisory meetings.

Material within SAMA's Stress Testing Rules linking stress testing outputs to the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Plan and to remedial action requirements. It identifies the impact parameters to be assessed (asset quality, profitability, capital adequacy/CAR, liquidity), requires results and their assumptions, methodologies and limitations to be communicated to the board, senior management and SAMA, and requires realistic, time-bound remedial plans including capital buffer adequacy assessment. ICAAP submission is annual and does not apply to branches of foreign banks; ICAAP reporting is separate from and additional to stress testing reporting.

Sets out the board of directors' duties under SAMA's Stress Testing Rules: overall responsibility and oversight of the stress testing framework, approval of the stress testing policy and revisions, ensuring adequate resources and infrastructure, reviewing major findings and ensuring remedial action, and requiring periodic reporting or independent evaluation by internal audit or a third party. Related implementation material confirms SAMA assesses board and senior management involvement during supervisory review, ICAAP meetings and on-site examinations. Binds boards of banks within scope of the Rules.

Specifies senior management's obligations under SAMA's Stress Testing Rules: designing, developing and implementing the stress testing framework, establishing organisational structure, resources, processes and supporting infrastructure, overseeing scenario definition and methodology selection, ensuring clear compilation and communication of results to the board, committees, business areas and SAMA, preparing action plans, and periodically reassessing the framework with board approval for changes. Read together with the board's oversight role in the same section.
lookup_terms: reporting results to board and SAMA

data.summary: Refers to the reporting format annexed to SAMA's Stress Testing Rules, under which banks submit stress testing results and top-down data to SAMA on a half-yearly basis. The accompanying Q&A clarifies that the data template under Para 10(i) largely follows the existing semi-annual template, that SAMA may request additional data over time and will communicate revisions in advance, and that stress effects are applied to financial statements as at the reporting cut-off date. Methodology choice remains with the bank, though SAMA may prescribe standard scenarios.

Glossary and template material from SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework identifying the SAMA-issued Basel III component standards (SACAP, SCRE, SCCR, SMAR, SOPE, SLEV, SLCR, SNSF) that underpin disclosure obligations. It includes Template KM1 on key prudential metrics, mandatory for all banks, requiring quarterly fixed-format disclosure of risk-based capital, leverage and liquidity metrics with narrative explanation of significant changes. Binds banks subject to SAMA's capital and disclosure framework.

Fixed-format Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring banks to publish a five-quarter time series of key prudential metrics at consolidated level: available capital (CET1, Tier 1, total), RWA (including pre-floor RWA), risk-based ratios, buffer requirements, Basel III leverage ratio, LCR and NSFR. It also requires banks applying the ECL transitional arrangement to show 'fully loaded' ECL comparatives so users can see the transitional impact on capital and leverage ratios. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework, with prescribed row instructions and cross-template linkages to CC1 and OV1.

Fixed-format quarterly Pillar 3 template disclosing total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) available, TLAC ratios against RWA and leverage exposure, and related buffer requirements, reported at resolution group level for single point of entry and multiple point of entry structures. It is mandatory only for resolution groups of global systemically important banks and takes effect from the TLAC conformance date; SAMA's framework states TLAC disclosures need not be completed unless SAMA specifies otherwise. Requires a narrative explaining material period-on-period changes.
lookup_terms: single point of entry SPE MPE

data.summary: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table in which a bank describes its risk management approach — its risk strategy, risk appetite, governance, and how the board and senior management identify, assess and manage risks. It provides the narrative context for the quantitative RWA and capital metrics disclosed in OV1 and KM1. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements at consolidated level.
lookup_terms: board and senior management risk oversight

data.summary: Pillar 3 template giving an overview of total risk-weighted assets — the denominator of the risk-based capital ratios — broken down by risk type and calculation approach, with corresponding minimum capital requirements (normally RWA × 8%). Rows cover credit risk (standardised, F-IRB/A-IRB, supervisory slotting), counterparty credit risk, CVA, equity positions, equity investments in funds, settlement risk, securitisation, market risk, operational risk, trading/banking book switches and amounts below deduction thresholds. Binds banks making SAMA Pillar 3 disclosures; linked to KM1 row 4.

Pillar 3 'capital floor / comparison of modelled and standardised' template requiring banks to disclose, by risk category, RWA arising from internally modelled approaches that SAMA has approved, RWA from standardised approaches, total actual RWA, and the RWA that would result if the full standardised approach were applied to all exposures. It covers credit risk, counterparty credit risk, securitisation, market risk, operational risk and residual RWA. Relevant to banks using IRB or other model-based approaches under SAMA approval and subject to the output/capital floor.

Companion Pillar 3 template presenting credit risk RWA split by asset class, comparing amounts produced under modelled (IRB/slotting) approaches with those that would arise under the standardised approach for credit risk. It supports assessment of the capital floor impact and of variability between internal models and the standardised framework. Applies to banks using SAMA-approved internal approaches for credit risk when making Pillar 3 disclosures.
lookup_terms: credit risk RWA by asset class

data.summary: Pillar 3 disclosure template LI2 under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, requiring banks to explain the main drivers of difference between accounting carrying values (under the regulatory scope of consolidation) and the exposure amounts used for regulatory capital purposes, broken down by credit risk, counterparty credit risk, securitisation and market risk frameworks. Differences arising purely from scope of consolidation belong in Template LI1; LI2 covers off-balance sheet amounts, valuation and netting differences, provisions and prudential filters. Mandatory for all banks, annual, flexible format, with accompanying narrative in Table LIA. Context also carries Table CRB-A on prudential treatment of problem assets (non-performing and forborne exposure definitions).

Table REMA is the qualitative Pillar 3 remuneration policy disclosure in SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, describing governance bodies overseeing remuneration, design of remuneration processes, risk adjustment, and identification of senior managers and material risk-takers. It is mandatory for all banks, annual, flexible format, and anchors the employee categories used in Templates REM1–REM3. Disclosure must be published annually and, if not concurrent with the annual report, as soon as possible thereafter.

Template REM1 is the quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of fixed and variable remuneration awarded during the financial year to senior management and other material risk-takers, under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. It sits alongside Table REMA (policy) and Templates REM2 (special payments) and REM3 (deferred remuneration), and is an annual requirement for banks. The surrounding context also covers transitional timing rules for first disclosure periods by fiscal-year calendar.

Template REM2 is the quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of special payments made during the financial year — guaranteed bonuses, sign-on awards and severance payments — split by number of employees and total amount for senior management and other material risk-takers. Employee categories must match those described in Table REMA. Mandatory for all banks, annual, flexible format, with optional narrative on significant movements.

Template REM3 is the Pillar 3 disclosure of a bank's total outstanding deferred and retained remuneration, completing the remuneration set with Table REMA and Templates REM1 and REM2 under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. It applies annually to banks, using the senior management and material risk-taker categories defined in Table REMA, and must be published annually (as soon as possible after the annual report if not simultaneous).

Table CRA is the general qualitative credit risk disclosure in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, requiring banks to describe their credit risk profile and business model linkage, credit risk policy and limit-setting, the structure of the credit risk management and control function, its interaction with risk control, compliance and internal audit, and credit risk reporting to executive management and the board. Mandatory for all banks, annual, flexible format. It heads section 19 on credit risk, which excludes securitisation positions (section 21) and counterparty credit risk (section 20), and sets out the full suite of CR/CRB/CRC/CRD templates, with IRB disclosures required only where SAMA has approved IRB use.

Pillar 3 disclosure template specifications for total loss-absorbing capacity at resolution group level, covering the KM2 key-metrics template (quarterly, fixed format, five reporting periods) and the TLAC1 composition template that breaks down regulatory capital and eligible TLAC instruments, deductions, adjusted RWA, leverage exposure, resulting TLAC ratios and buffer requirements. It applies only to G-SIBs and is reproduced per resolution group under an MPE approach; SPE groups may align certain rows with Template CC1. Binding on banks designated as G-SIBs subject to SAMA's adoption of the Basel Pillar 3 framework.
lookup_terms: single point of entry / multiple point of entry

data.summary: Disclosure template requiring G-SIBs to set out, on a legal entity basis, the creditor hierarchy of each material subgroup entity that has issued internal TLAC to a resolution entity, showing total capital and liabilities, excluded liabilities, TLAC-eligible amounts and residual maturity bands. Reported semiannually in fixed format, grouped by resolution group so exposures to each resolution entity are identifiable, with narrative on jurisdiction-specific credit hierarchies. It binds G-SIBs and serves creditors assessing their ranking in resolution.

Reference points into SAMA's capital framework (SACAP) used by the Pillar 3 composition-of-capital disclosures: the regulatory adjustments and deductions applied to CET1 (prudent valuation, goodwill and intangibles, DTAs, cash flow hedge reserve, provision shortfall, securitisation gain on sale, own credit risk, pension assets, own shares, reciprocal cross-holdings, threshold deductions) and the parallel Tier 2 deductions covering capital instruments and other TLAC liabilities. Includes the 10% and 5% threshold treatments, with distinct conditions for G-SIBs versus non-G-SIBs. Binds banks calculating regulatory capital and completing Template CC1.

Cross-references to SAMA's credit risk capital standard (SCRE) as used in the Pillar 3 overview of RWA: which exposures fall under the standardised approach, foundation and advanced IRB, and supervisory slotting, and which are carved out to counterparty credit risk, CVA, equity, settlement, securitisation and threshold-deduction rows. Also covers Template CDC on capital ratio levels triggering capital distribution constraints (risk-based buffers, G-SIB surcharge, countercyclical buffer, Pillar 2 and leverage buffer). Binds banks calculating credit risk RWA and making Pillar 3 disclosures.

Disclosure template for the creditor hierarchy of each G-SIB resolution entity at legal entity level, mirroring TLAC2 but omitting the resolution-entity-as-creditor column, so only one column per hierarchy layer. Requires nominal values for total capital and liabilities, excluded liabilities, potentially TLAC-eligible amounts and residual maturity buckets including perpetual securities, semiannually in fixed format. Binds G-SIBs and informs external creditors of their standing in resolution.

Covers the Pillar 3 linkage disclosures explaining gaps between accounting and regulatory figures: Template LI2 on the main sources of difference between financial statement carrying values (under the regulatory scope of consolidation) and regulatory exposure amounts across credit, counterparty credit, securitisation and market risk frameworks, with Table LIA providing the qualitative explanation. Also includes Table CRB-A requiring banks to state their definitions of non-performing and forborne exposures and whether they follow SAMA's Rules on Management of Problem Assets. Mandatory for banks, annual, flexible format.
lookup_terms: Rules on Management of Problem Assets

data.summary: Template CR2 is a fixed-format Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework requiring banks to show the semiannual movement in their stock of defaulted loans and debt securities: opening balance, new defaults, cures back to non-defaulted status, write-offs and other changes. Defaulted exposures are reported net of write-offs and gross of allowances/impairments, with standardised-approach banks aligning default to the past-due-more-than-90-days concept. It is mandatory for all banks and must be accompanied by narrative explaining significant flows and whether off-balance sheet items are included.
lookup_terms: changes in stock of defaulted loans

data.summary: Table CRB is the additional qualitative and quantitative disclosure on the credit quality of assets, sitting in the general credit risk block of SAMA's Pillar 3 framework alongside Table CRA, Templates CR1 and CR2 and Table CRB-A. It supplements the quantitative default and impairment templates with the bank's definitions and breakdowns underpinning reported credit quality. It binds banks subject to the Pillar 3 disclosure framework; the section scope excludes securitisation positions and counterparty credit risk, which are disclosed elsewhere.

Table CRB-A is a mandatory annual, flexible-format Pillar 3 disclosure supplementing the quantitative credit-quality templates with information on non-performing and forborne exposures. Banks must state their own definitions of non-performing and forborne exposures, say whether they follow SAMA's Rules on Management of Problem Assets (No. 41033343, January 2020), and explain materiality thresholds for past due, exit criteria and probation periods, including any corporate/retail differences. It binds all banks reporting under the framework, using carrying values on the regulatory scope of consolidation.
lookup_terms: Rules on Management of Problem Assets 41033343

data.summary: Table CRC is the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on credit risk mitigation techniques, forming the CRM block of the credit risk section together with Template CR3. It requires narrative explanation of how the bank uses collateral, guarantees and credit derivatives to reduce credit risk and capital requirements, complementing the quantitative CRM figures. It applies to banks disclosing under the SAMA Pillar 3 framework; related instructions distinguish the simple and comprehensive approaches to CRM under the standardised approach.
lookup_terms: credit risk mitigation techniques qualitative disclosure

data.summary: Template CR3 is a mandatory, fixed-format semiannual Pillar 3 template giving an overview of the extent to which banks use credit risk mitigation, splitting carrying values of loans and debt securities into unsecured exposures and exposures secured by collateral, financial guarantees or credit derivatives, including a defaulted sub-line. All CRM techniques used to reduce capital requirements and all secured exposures must be captured, regardless of whether the standardised or IRB approach is used. It binds all banks, with narrative commentary required on significant period-on-period changes and disclosure of the allocation method for multi-secured exposures.

Table CRD is an annual, flexible-format qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on the use of external credit ratings under the standardised (or simplified standardised) approach for credit risk. Banks must name the ECAIs used, the asset classes each is used for, the issuer-to-issue rating transfer process for banking book assets, and the mapping of each agency's rating scale to risk buckets per SAMA circular No. B.C.S 242 (11 April 2007). It binds banks that both use the standardised approach and rely on external ratings; disclosure may be omitted only where amounts are negligible and the bank explains why, describing the portfolios and aggregate RWA concerned.

A fixed-format Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, showing credit risk exposures before and after credit conversion factors and credit risk mitigation, together with resulting RWA and RWA density, by asset class under the standardised approach. It applies the standardised credit risk rules (including simple or comprehensive CRM with supervisory haircuts, failed trades and non-DvP transactions) and excludes counterparty credit risk, CVA and banking book securitisation. It binds SAMA-supervised banks disclosing at the regulatory consolidation level.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring banks to break down standardised approach credit risk exposures (post-CCF and post-CRM) across regulatory asset classes and the applicable risk weight buckets. It supports comparison of risk weight distribution and sits alongside CR4 in the standardised credit risk disclosure set, excluding counterparty credit risk, CVA and banking book securitisation exposures. It binds banks supervised by SAMA that use the standardised approach for some or all exposures.
lookup_terms: exposures by asset class and risk weight

data.summary: A mandatory annual qualitative Pillar 3 table for banks using foundation or advanced IRB approaches, describing the main characteristics of internal credit risk models used at group level. It covers model development, approval and change governance, independence of model review from model development, internal reporting on credit risk models, the scope of SAMA's model approval by entity/portfolio/exposure class, and the share of EAD covered by standardised, F-IRB and A-IRB approaches. It binds SAMA-supervised banks with IRB permission.

A Pillar 3 template requiring semiannual disclosure of IRB credit risk exposures broken down by regulatory portfolio and PD scale, with the key parameters driving RWA (EAD post-CRM, average PD, number of obligors, average LGD, average maturity, RWA and expected loss). Portfolio rows reflect the exposure categories set by SAMA for local IRB implementation; a parallel structure applies to counterparty credit risk under CCR4. It binds banks approved to use F-IRB or A-IRB approaches.
lookup_terms: IRB exposures by portfolio and PD scale

data.summary: A mandatory semiannual Pillar 3 template showing, for each IRB portfolio, RWA calculated without recognising credit derivatives as a credit risk mitigant against actual RWA reflecting that mitigation, so users can gauge the capital impact of credit derivative CRM. Rows split sovereign, bank, corporate, specialised lending, retail sub-classes, equity and purchased receivables between F-IRB and A-IRB. It binds SAMA-supervised banks using A-IRB and/or F-IRB for some or all exposures, with narrative commentary expected.

A Pillar 3 flow statement template reconciling movements in IRB credit risk RWA between reporting periods, attributing changes to drivers such as asset size, asset quality, model updates, methodology and policy, acquisitions and disposals, and foreign exchange movements. It covers credit risk RWA under IRB approaches, excluding counterparty credit risk, CVA, equity positions, settlement risk and securitisation, which are reported elsewhere. It binds SAMA-supervised banks using IRB approaches.

Pillar 3 disclosure template CR9 within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, requiring banks to backtest modelled probability of default against realised obligor default rates for each regulatory portfolio, using at least a five-year average annual default rate. It is mandatory only for banks with SAMA approval to use the F-IRB and/or A-IRB approaches, with separate template sets where both approaches are used. Disclosure is annual, flexible in format, and must be accompanied by narrative explaining model scope and the share of RWA covered.

Pillar 3 disclosure template CR10 in SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, covering specialised lending (and equity, where relevant) exposures risk-weighted under the supervisory slotting approach rather than full F-IRB/A-IRB modelling. It binds banks that use IRB-family approaches and apply supervisory slotting categories, sitting alongside the standardised-approach and IRB credit risk templates. Relevant when identifying which credit exposures fall outside modelled PD/LGD disclosure.

Table CCRA is the qualitative disclosure requirement heading SAMA's counterparty credit risk (CCR) section of the Pillar 3 framework, which covers all banking book and trading book exposures attracting a CCR charge, including exposures to central counterparties. It introduces the full CCR template set (CCR1, CCR3–CCR8) and binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure regime. Useful as the entry point for locating which CCR disclosures apply and their scope boundaries against credit risk and securitisation sections.

Template CCR1 requires banks to disclose counterparty credit risk exposures broken down by the method used to determine exposure at default (e.g. standardised and internal models approaches), with associated EAD and RWA. It applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework holding derivative, SFT or other CCR-bearing positions in the banking or trading book. It is the summary-level CCR template that the more granular CCR3–CCR8 templates decompose.
lookup_terms: analysis of CCR exposures by approach

data.summary: Template CCR3 requires banks using the standardised approach for credit risk to disclose counterparty credit risk exposures (post-CRM, post-CCF) broken down by regulatory portfolio and risk weight band. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 framework whose CCR exposures are risk-weighted under the standardised approach, and is the standardised counterpart to the IRB template CCR4.

Template CCR4 requires disclosure of the IRB parameters used to calculate counterparty credit risk capital — EAD post-CRM, average PD, number of obligors, average LGD, average maturity and RWA — broken down by regulatory portfolio and PD scale. It is mandatory for banks using A-IRB or F-IRB for CCR exposures regardless of the EAD method, excluding CVA charges and CCP-cleared exposures, with separate templates where both IRB approaches are used. Disclosure is semiannual in fixed format (SAMA sets the portfolio breakdown) with narrative on model scope and RWA coverage.
lookup_terms: IRB CCR exposures by PD scale

data.summary: A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework (Dec 2022) covering the breakdown of collateral used in counterparty credit risk (CCR) exposures, including derivative and securities financing transaction collateral, segregated vs unsegregated and received vs posted. It sits in the CCR disclosure section alongside CCRA and CCR1–CCR8, which spans banking book and trading book exposures subject to a CCR charge, including exposures to CCPs. It binds SAMA-supervised banks subject to the Pillar 3 regime.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring banks to report credit derivative exposures (protection bought and sold) as part of the counterparty credit risk disclosure section of SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. It is one of the CCR-series templates (CCRA, CCR1, CCR3–CCR8) covering banking and trading book exposures subject to a CCR capital charge. Applies to banks supervised by SAMA under the Pillar 3 regime.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring a flow statement explaining period-on-period movements in risk-weighted assets for counterparty credit risk exposures calculated under the internal models method (IMM). It is applicable only to banks with SAMA approval to use IMM and forms part of the CCR disclosure section of the Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework. Binds SAMA-supervised banks using modelled CCR approaches.

A mandatory, semiannual, fixed-format Pillar 3 template in which banks disclose all exposures to central counterparties — trade exposures, segregated and non-segregated initial margin, and pre-funded/unfunded default fund contributions — with EAD post-CRM and RWA, split between qualifying (QCCP) and non-qualifying CCPs. Banks must add narrative commentary explaining significant period changes. Applies to all SAMA-supervised banks under the Pillar 3 framework.

The qualitative disclosure table opening the securitisation section of SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, requiring banks to describe their securitisation activities, roles (originator, sponsor, investor, servicer) and related risk management and accounting policies. It covers all securitisation exposures, not only those treated under the securitisation capital framework, and excludes trading book securitisation capital charges reported elsewhere. Binds SAMA-supervised banks with securitisation exposures.

A Pillar 3 template requiring banks to disclose securitisation exposures in the banking book, broken down by the bank's role (originator, sponsor, investor) and by traditional/synthetic structures. Together with SEC2 it captures all securitisation exposures, including those failing the risk transfer recognition criteria, whereas SEC3 and SEC4 are limited to exposures treated under the securitisation capital framework. Applies to SAMA-supervised banks subject to Pillar 3 disclosure.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework covering securitisation exposures in the trading book where the bank acts as originator, sponsor or investor. It sits in the securitisation section (alongside Table SECA and template SEC1), which captures all securitisation exposures regardless of whether risk transfer recognition criteria are met, as opposed to SEC3/SEC4 which are limited to banking book exposures treated under the securitisation framework. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime at the regulatory scope of consolidation.

A Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure template for banking book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as originator or sponsor, showing exposures, regulatory approaches applied, risk weight bands, RWA and capital requirements. Only exposures the bank treats under the securitisation framework are reported here, which for originators presupposes that the significant risk transfer recognition criteria are satisfied. It binds banks reporting under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

A Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure template for banking book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as investor, reporting exposure amounts, approaches used, risk weight bands, RWA and capital requirements. Like SEC3, it is limited to positions subject to the securitisation regulatory framework, so no double-counting arises with the broader SEC1/SEC2 templates. It applies to banks within the scope of SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure regime.

A qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table requiring banks to describe their market risk management strategy, governance, reporting and measurement arrangements under the standardised approach. It sits at the head of the market risk section, which covers trading book and banking book exposures subject to market risk capital requirements plus trading book securitisation positions, but excludes counterparty credit risk (reported separately). It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

A Pillar 3 quantitative template disclosing market risk capital requirements computed under the standardised approach, broken down by risk class (including general interest rate, equity, FX, commodity and credit spread risk) and by default risk and residual risk add-on components. It complements the qualitative Table MRA and excludes counterparty credit risk on the same exposures. Applies to banks reporting under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

A Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure table mandatory only for banks that have SAMA approval to use the internal models approach for market risk, requiring description of trading desk structure, model scope, expected shortfall methodology, default risk capital requirement and treatment of non-modellable risk factors. Disclosure must be at group-wide regulatory consolidation level and indicate the share of capital requirements covered by the described models. It binds IMA-approved banks annually.

Pillar 3 disclosure template MR2 under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework, setting out the fixed-format quarterly breakdown of market risk capital requirements for banks using the internal models approach (IMA). It covers unconstrained and constrained expected shortfall by regulatory risk class, IMCC, the capital charge for non-modellable risk factors (SES), the default risk capital requirement, and the surcharge for 'amber zone' trading desks, plus backtesting exception data and narrative on outliers. Mandatory for banks with SAMA approval to use the IMA for part or all of their market risk, at the group-wide regulatory consolidation level.

Pillar 3 disclosure template MR3 requiring semiannual, fixed-format reporting of market risk capital requirements computed under the simplified standardised approach (SSA), broken down by interest rate, equity, commodity and FX risk for outright products plus option risk under the simplified, delta-plus and scenario methods, and securitisation. It binds banks that use the SSA to determine their market risk capital requirements under SAMA's adoption of the Basel market risk framework.

Node covering SAMA's Pillar 3 section on credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk disclosures, including Table CVAA, the general qualitative disclosure on a bank's CVA risk exposures and how they are managed. The section applies only where the materiality threshold in SAMA's revised risk-based capital charge for counterparty credit risk is met, and it maps the full CVA disclosure set (CVA1, CVA2 under BA-CVA; CVAB, CVA3, CVA4 under SA-CVA).

Pillar 3 template CVA1 setting out the components of risk-weighted assets computed under the reduced basic approach for CVA risk: the aggregated systematic component (perfect correlation assumption), the aggregated idiosyncratic component (zero correlation assumption), and the total (K-reduced scaled by 12.5). Mandatory semiannually, in fixed format, for banks measuring part or all of their CVA RWA under the reduced BA-CVA, with narrative on hedges used even where not recognised; it reconciles to the overview template OV1.

Pillar 3 template CVA2 covering disclosure of RWA components under the full basic approach for CVA risk, i.e. the variant of BA-CVA that recognises eligible CVA hedges. It sits alongside CVA1 in SAMA's CVA disclosure set and binds banks measuring part or all of their CVA RWA under the full BA-CVA, subject to the counterparty credit risk materiality threshold.

Table CVAB requires annual, flexible-format qualitative disclosure of a bank's CVA risk management framework, including senior management involvement and governance arrangements such as documentation, an independent control unit, independent review and independence of data acquisition from business lines. Mandatory for all banks using the standardised approach for CVA (SA-CVA) to calculate CVA risk RWA.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework covering the standardised approach for credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk, with accompanying definitions and completion instructions for rows/columns and the treatment of standardised versus SAMA-approved modelled approaches. It is a reporting/disclosure obligation rather than a substantive capital rule, and sits alongside related comparison disclosures of actual RWA versus RWA under full standardised approaches. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime, at the frequency and format fixed for the template.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template requiring an RWA flow statement for CVA risk calculated under the standardised approach (SA-CVA), showing movements in RWA and the associated minimum capital requirement between reporting dates. The surrounding instructions explain how CVA RWA and capital charges relate to credit risk, counterparty credit risk and other RWA categories reported elsewhere in the framework. It binds banks required to disclose under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

Table ORA is the qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on a bank's operational risk management framework, requiring description of policies and governance structure, the operational risk measurement system, internal and board reporting, and risk mitigation/transfer (including insurance and outsourcing policy). It is mandatory for all banks, annual, and flexible in format. It binds banks under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework and links operational risk governance to disclosed capital outcomes.

Template OR1 requires annual disclosure of aggregate operational risk losses over the past ten years, net of recoveries and of excluded losses, at loss event thresholds of SAR 44,600 and SAR 446,000, plus information on whether losses feed the internal loss multiplier (ILM). Scope is mandatory for banks in the second or third business indicator (BI) bucket and for first-bucket banks with SAMA approval to use internal loss data. Narrative commentary on new loss exclusions and other material information is expected; the general retrospective-disclosure carve-out does not apply.

Template OR2 requires annual disclosure of the business indicator (BI) and its subcomponents — the interest, lease and dividend component, services component and financial component — together with the resulting business indicator component (BIC) used in the operational risk capital calculation. It is mandatory for all banks, fixed format, with narrative explanation of significant changes and of any SAMA-approved exclusion of divested activities. It binds banks disclosing under SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework.

Template OR3 is the Pillar 3 disclosure of the minimum required operational risk capital and associated RWA, drawing together the business indicator component and, where applicable, the internal loss multiplier. It sits within the operational risk disclosure set (ORA, OR1, OR2) of SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework and feeds the operational risk line of the overall RWA overview. It binds banks subject to that disclosure framework.

A qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure table within SAMA's Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements Framework requiring banks to describe their objectives, policies, governance, measurement and mitigation approach for interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB), including shock and stress scenarios, modelling assumptions and how IRRBB is defined for control purposes. It is the qualitative companion to Template IRRBB1 and binds all banks within the IRRBB scope of application, with annual, flexible-format disclosure. Banks are directed to use their own internal measurement system, referencing the SAMA IRRBB circular and the Basel supervisory review process standard.
lookup_terms: interest rate risk in the banking book
IRRBB risk management objectives and policies

data.summary: A quantitative Pillar 3 template under SAMA's disclosure framework requiring banks to report IRRBB exposure values — changes in economic value of equity (ΔEVE) and net interest income (ΔNII) — under the prescribed Basel interest rate shock scenarios. It binds banks in scope of the IRRBB standard and is paired with the qualitative Table IRRBBA. Values are computed using the bank's own internal measurement system, with reference to the relevant SAMA IRRBB circular.
lookup_terms: banking book interest rate risk template

data.summary: A Pillar 3 template setting out the twelve indicators feeding the Basel methodology for assessing global systemic importance. Under SAMA's framework it is mandatory only for banks previously classified as G-SIBs, those exceeding the EUR 200 billion leverage ratio exposure threshold, or those in the assessment sample by supervisory judgment; SAMA states it need not be completed unless SAMA identifies the bank as a G-SIB. Disclosure is annual, flexible in format, in the bank's own currency, with accompanying narrative and links to prior assessment disclosures.

A Pillar 3 template requiring disclosure of the geographical distribution of private sector credit exposures used to compute the bank-specific countercyclical capital buffer rate. It binds banks subject to a countercyclical buffer requirement, but only where they have exposures in jurisdictions with a buffer rate above zero; disclosure is semiannual with a flexible format adaptable to domestic implementation. Banks should allocate exposures on an ultimate risk basis where possible and explain the geographical allocation methodology used.

A fixed-format Pillar 3 template reconciling total assets in published financial statements with the leverage ratio exposure measure, listing the prescribed adjustments (scope of regulatory consolidation, securitisation risk transfer, temporary central bank reserve exemption, fiduciary assets, regular-way purchases and others). It is mandatory for all banks on a quarterly basis, normally quarter-end, with more frequent averaging only subject to SAMA approval or requirement. Banks must state the calculation basis used and explain material differences.

The common disclosure template for the leverage ratio within SAMA's Pillar 3 framework, presenting the components of Tier 1 capital and the leverage ratio exposure measure and the resulting ratio. It sits alongside Template LR1 (reconciliation) and feeds the leverage metrics reported in Template KM1, binding banks on a quarterly, fixed-format basis.

Table LIQA is a mandatory annual Pillar 3 disclosure table on liquidity risk management, requiring qualitative and quantitative narrative on liquidity governance, risk tolerance, funding strategy and diversification, mitigation techniques, stress testing, contingency funding plans, concentration limits and entity-level liquidity exposures. Format is flexible, so banks select content proportionate to their business model and liquidity risk profile. It binds all banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure framework and sits alongside the risk-management overview table (OVA) in the same instrument.

Template LIQ1 is the fixed Pillar 3 disclosure of the Liquidity Coverage Ratio, reported as averages of daily observations over the most recent three months, with HQLA shown after haircuts but before Level 2/2B caps, and inflows/outflows shown unweighted and weighted, then adjusted for applicable caps. It explains why reported components may not sum exactly to the disclosed LCR where the inflow cap binds. It applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 regime and is read with the KM1 key metrics template.

Template LIQ2 is the Pillar 3 disclosure of the Net Stable Funding Ratio, presenting available and required stable funding components. In the source instrument it appears with the quarterly KM1 key prudential metrics template and the CDC capital distribution constraints template, which together frame a bank's capital, leverage and liquidity disclosure set. It binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Template OV1 is the Pillar 3 overview of risk-weighted assets, breaking RWA down by risk type (credit risk, counterparty credit risk, CVA, securitisation, market risk, operational risk) and by whether modelled or standardised approaches are used. It carries the row definitions and instructions that also drive the comparison template CMS1, including treatment of equity investments in funds, settlement risk, trading/banking book switches and amounts below deduction thresholds. It applies to banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.

Template CMS1 requires banks to compare actual RWA (including portfolios where SAMA has approved modelled approaches) against RWA that would result from applying the full standardised approach across credit, counterparty credit, securitisation, market and operational risk, plus residual RWA. The instructions define each row's standardised-approach baseline, including credit risk mitigation treatment and the phase-in for equity exposures under IRB. It binds banks using internal models under SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

This is the line-by-line NSFR disclosure template with its instructions, mapping each funding source to an ASF factor (regulatory capital, stable and less stable retail and small business deposits, operational deposits, other wholesale funding, derivative liabilities, interdependent liabilities) and each asset to an RSF factor (HQLA, performing loans, residential mortgages, non-HQLA securities, traded commodities, initial margin and default fund contributions, derivative assets). It cross-references the SAMA NSFR and LCR rulebook sections for each factor. It binds banks subject to the NSFR standard and Pillar 3 disclosure.

Specification for Pillar 3 Template CR9, the annual disclosure backtesting internal probability-of-default estimates against realised obligor default rates for each regulatory portfolio, using at least a five-year average annual default rate. It is mandatory for banks on the foundation and/or advanced IRB approaches, requiring separate portfolio breakdowns where both approaches are used, coverage of key SAMA-approved group-wide PD models, and narrative explaining model scope and the share of RWA covered. Binds SAMA-licensed banks using IRB for credit risk capital.

Specification for Pillar 3 Template CR7, a fixed-format semiannual disclosure comparing hypothetical pre-credit-derivative RWA with actual RWA to show the mitigation effect of credit derivatives under the IRB approach, broken down by regulatory portfolio. Mandatory for banks using A-IRB and/or F-IRB for any exposures, with narrative commentary on the RWA impact. The surrounding context also illustrates completion of Template CR3 on credit risk mitigation coverage.

Sets out the scope of the Pillar 3 securitisation disclosure chapter and Template SEC1 on carrying values of securitisation exposures. All securitisation exposures, including those failing significant risk transfer recognition, are reported in SEC1/SEC2 and Table SECA, while SEC3/SEC4 are confined to exposures capitalised under the securitisation framework; trading book securitisation capital charges are excluded. Binds banks preparing Pillar 3 reports, with related guidance on reconciliation to Template LI1/LI2.

Specification for Pillar 3 Template CCR8, a fixed-format semiannual disclosure of exposures at default (post-CRM) and RWA arising from dealings with central counterparties, split between qualifying and non-qualifying CCPs and by trade type, initial margin and default fund contributions. Mandatory for all banks, with narrative on period-on-period changes. The context also carries Table CRB-A on the prudential treatment of problem assets, requiring banks to disclose their non-performing and forborne exposure definitions.

Covers the guiding disclosure principles (meaningfulness, consistency over time, comparability across banks), Pillar 3 assurance expectations including a board-approved disclosure policy, and the conditions under which banks may signpost fixed-format disclosures to another document. Also introduces the frequency and timing rules requiring the Pillar 3 report to be published alongside the corresponding financial report. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 framework.

Addresses how often and when Pillar 3 disclosures must be made: quarterly, semiannual or annual depending on the template, as summarised in Annexure 2, with the Pillar 3 report published concurrently with the corresponding financial report. Read together with the disclosure principles, assurance requirements and the signposting conditions for fixed-format templates. Binds banks preparing Pillar 3 reports under SAMA's framework.

A Pillar 3 disclosure template within SAMA's market disclosure framework requiring banks to present an overview of exposures covered by credit risk mitigation, split between unsecured carrying amounts and amounts secured by collateral, financial guarantees and credit derivatives. It sits in the credit risk section alongside the qualitative CRM table (CRC) and is supported by worked allocation examples for multi-secured and over/under-collateralised exposures. Binds banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure requirements; scope excludes securitisation and counterparty credit risk positions, which are disclosed elsewhere.

A mandatory Pillar 3 template requiring banks to disclose the composition of collateral supporting counterparty credit risk, broken down by collateral type and by whether it is posted or received, segregated or unsegregated, and used in derivatives or securities financing transactions (SFTs), including CCP-cleared trades. Disclosure is semiannual, with fixed columns, flexible rows and a narrative explaining material period-on-period changes. Applies to all banks within SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure scope.
lookup_terms: composition of collateral for CCR exposure

data.summary: A Pillar 3 market risk template covering capital requirements determined under the internal models approach (IMA), sitting within SAMA's suite of quantitative disclosure templates for banks. The surrounding framework material addresses related capital-composition and distribution-constraint disclosures (e.g. CET1 triggers, buffers, Tier 2 deductions), indicating the template's placement in the capital adequacy disclosure chain. Relevant to banks with SAMA approval to use internal models for market risk.

A Pillar 3 template presenting the flow statement of risk-weighted assets for counterparty credit risk exposures calculated under the internal model method (IMM), explaining movements over the reporting period. It forms part of the counterparty credit risk disclosure set, which is separated from general credit risk, credit valuation adjustment and securitisation RWA reporting. Applies to banks permitted by SAMA to use internal model approaches for counterparty credit risk.

A Pillar 3 linkage template requiring banks to reconcile the carrying values in published financial statements with the balance sheet under the regulatory scope of consolidation, and to map those amounts to the credit risk, counterparty credit risk, securitisation and market risk frameworks. It is the first step in the disclosure chain connecting accounting figures to regulatory capital (with CC2 and CC1) and to exposure-level differences shown in LI2. Mandatory for banks subject to SAMA's Pillar 3 requirements.

A mandatory Pillar 3 template setting out the main sources of difference between financial statement carrying values (on the regulatory consolidation basis) and the exposure amounts used for regulatory capital purposes, covering off-balance sheet amounts, valuation and netting differences, provisions and prudential filters. It complements LI1 (which handles scope-of-consolidation differences) and is explained narratively in Table LIA. Applies annually to all banks within SAMA's Pillar 3 disclosure scope.
lookup_terms: regulatory exposure amounts vs carrying values

data.summary: This node covers the CVA risk capital component of SAMA's Minimum Capital Requirements for Counterparty Credit Risk and Credit Valuation Adjustment framework, setting out the scope of covered transactions (derivatives other than those with a QCCP, plus fair-valued SFTs where CVA loss exposure is material), the definition of CVA risk, and the standalone CVA portfolio. It fixes the choice of calculation method — BA-CVA by default, SA-CVA only with SAMA approval — and the treatment of eligible versus ineligible internal and external CVA hedges relative to the market risk framework. It binds banks supervised by SAMA that hold covered transactions in either the banking or trading book, and includes a supervisory notification/justification duty where a bank deems SFT CVA exposures immaterial.

This node sets the scope and positioning of the Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR) — applying to OTC derivatives, exchange-traded derivatives and long settlement transactions — and the routing of calculated CCR exposures (EAD) into the standardized or IRB credit risk approaches, or the CCP exposure rules. It also carries the IRB maturity adjustment cap, the IMM current-versus-stressed RWA floor, exemptions where no CCR charge applies (certain purchased credit protection and banking book sold CDS), and the cross-reference to minimum haircut floors for non-centrally cleared SFTs. It binds banks that lack SAMA approval for the Internal Model Method, which must use SA-CCR.
lookup_terms: sold credit default swap banking book

data.summary: This node defines the potential future exposure (PFE) add-on used in SA-CCR, comprising an aggregate add-on component and a multiplier recognising excess collateral or negative mark-to-market within a netting set. It sits alongside the replacement cost formula (including threshold, minimum transfer amount and net independent collateral amount, floored at zero) and is illustrated by worked hedging-set aggregation examples such as the commodity asset class. It applies to banks calculating counterparty credit risk exposure under SA-CCR.

This node defines hedging sets for SA-CCR add-on aggregation: one per currency for interest rate derivatives, one per currency pair for FX, single sets for credit and for equity, and four broad commodity sets (energy, metals, agricultural, other). It also carves out basis transactions and volatility transactions into separate hedging sets, with the supervisory factor halved for basis hedging sets, and shows the step-by-step effective notional and add-on calculation. It binds banks applying SA-CCR to derivative exposures.

This node explains the PFE multiplier in SA-CCR — a function of net market value (V), collateral (C) and the aggregate add-on — which reduces the PFE component to recognise over-collateralisation or a negative mark-to-market position in a netting set. It sits within the EAD formula (alpha of 1.4 times replacement cost plus PFE) and the distinction between margined and unmargined netting sets, including the cap of margined EAD at the unmargined amount. It applies to banks computing counterparty credit risk exposure under SA-CCR.

This node describes the supervisory factor (SF) in SA-CCR — the supervisory-specified change in the underlying risk factor, calibrated to its volatility — used with aggregation formulas to convert effective notionals into hedging-set add-ons, with the values tabulated in the framework. It is presented together with the other effective notional inputs (adjusted notional, maturity factor, supervisory delta) and the rule halving the supervisory factor for basis-transaction hedging sets. It binds banks applying SA-CCR.

Defines the maturity factor (MF) used in SA-CCR to scale the effective notional of a derivative trade for the time horizon over which potential future exposure is measured. It sets a separate calculation for unmargined netting sets (based on remaining maturity capped at one year and floored at ten business days) and for margined netting sets (based on the margin period of risk subject to prescribed floors, including for centrally cleared trades). It binds SAMA-supervised banks computing counterparty credit risk capital.

Defines central counterparty (CCP), clearing member and client for counterparty credit risk purposes, including the treatment of a linked second CCP as a clearing member of the first. It also sets the Pillar 2 expectation that a bank remains responsible for holding adequate capital against CCP exposures regardless of QCCP status, and must stress test and report CCP exposures to senior management and the board. Applies to banks dealing with CCPs as clearing members or clients.

Sets out the qualifying CCP (QCCP) concept: a CCP licensed and supervised under rules consistent with the PFMI, with SAMA able to determine QCCP status where the home regulator does not apply the Principles, and subject to the default fund calculation conditions being met. QCCP status determines the preferential capital treatment available to clearing member banks and their clients, but does not remove the bank's Pillar 2 responsibility.

Governs the capital treatment of clearing member banks' prefunded default fund contributions to a QCCP, using a risk-sensitive two-step formula based on the CCP's hypothetical capital requirement (KCCP) and the member's share of the default waterfall, with a floor. It also imposes data and calculation duties: KCCP must be computed at least quarterly (more often if SAMA requires) and sufficient information shared so each clearing member can compute its requirement and SAMA can verify it.

Covers the counterparty credit risk treatment of securities financing transactions and repo-style transactions, including eligible collateral and haircuts in the trading book, and the separate regime of minimum haircut floors for certain non-centrally cleared SFTs. It specifies scope and exemptions (central bank SFTs, qualifying cash-collateralised securities lending, collateral upgrade transactions where re-use is precluded) and sets the haircut floor percentages. Binds banks entering SFTs with in-scope counterparties.

Explains KCMi, the clearing member bank's risk-sensitive capital requirement for its default fund contribution to a QCCP, derived in two steps from the CCP's hypothetical capital requirement and the member's contribution share. Related provisions address how clearing members capitalise exposures to clients as bilateral trades (with a reduced five-day margin period of risk) and how client-posted collateral passed to the CCP may be recognised on both legs. Applies to banks acting as clearing members, including in multi-level client structures.

This node covers the hypothetical capital requirement of a central counterparty (KCCP) used as the first step in determining a clearing member bank's risk-sensitive capital charge for its default fund contributions to a qualifying CCP. It sits within SAMA's counterparty credit risk framework and explains that KCCP is a notional, consistently computed figure for capitalizing default fund contributions only, not the CCP's own regulatory capital. It binds SAMA-supervised banks acting as clearing members, and also frames Pillar 2 expectations to hold capital beyond the minimum where CCP dealings are riskier or QCCP status is unclear.

This node addresses the CVA risk capital requirement, including the treatment of eligible and ineligible internal and external CVA hedges and their interaction with the market risk framework. It sets out the scope of covered transactions (derivatives other than those with a QCCP, and fair-valued SFTs where CVA loss exposure is material), the standalone CVA portfolio concept, and the choice between BA-CVA (default) and SA-CVA (requires SAMA approval). It binds all SAMA-supervised banks with covered transactions in either the banking or trading book.

This node defines regulatory CVA and the principles for calculating it at counterparty level for CVA capital purposes, notably excluding the bank's own default risk and imposing constraints on accounting-CVA practice. It also sets the minimum eligibility criteria a bank must meet for SAMA to permit use of SA-CVA, including monthly CVA and sensitivity computation and a dedicated CVA desk. It binds banks with covered derivative and SFT positions and requires demonstration of compliance to SAMA.

This node sets out how SA-CVA capital is built up as the sum of delta and vega risk charges across prescribed risk classes (six for delta, five for vega, with no vega charge for counterparty credit spread risk). It covers the CVA multiplier, the requirement to allocate an eligible credit spread hedge wholly to one risk class, and the calculation of CVA and hedge sensitivities including index hedges. It binds banks approved by SAMA to use the SA-CVA.

This node concerns supervisory risk weights used in the CVA capital calculations alongside the SA-CVA delta/vega risk-class structure and the CVA multiplier that SAMA may raise where model risk warrants. The surrounding material also covers IMM model validation, independent review, board and senior management involvement in counterparty credit risk control, and integration of the exposure model into day-to-day risk management. It binds SAMA-supervised banks calculating CVA and counterparty credit risk capital, particularly those using internal models.

This node sets out the treatment of derivative exposures in the Leverage Ratio exposure measure, comprising replacement cost and potential future exposure, with special rules for eligible bilateral netting and for written credit derivatives (including when a purchased credit derivative on the same reference name may offset, subject to same-or-more-conservative material terms). It also covers conditions under which cash pooling arrangements may be treated on a combined rather than account-by-account basis. It binds SAMA-supervised banks computing the leverage ratio.

Part of SAMA's leverage ratio framework, setting how securities financing transaction (SFT) exposures enter the leverage ratio exposure measure. It covers the bank-as-principal general treatment (gross SFT assets with no accounting netting, exclusion of securities recognised as assets, and the cumulative conditions for netting cash payables/receivables with the same counterparty), novated trades cleared through QCCPs, and the agency model — including the requirement that a bank indemnifying or guaranteeing both the securities lender and borrower compute the measure separately for each party. Binds SAMA-licensed banks calculating the leverage ratio.

Addresses on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet items within SAMA's leverage ratio exposure measure, including fiduciary assets, trade/settlement date accounting and delivery-versus-payment, cash pooling arrangements, and the conversion of commitments, direct credit substitutes, acceptances and letters of credit via credit conversion factors. It also flags SAMA's supervisory concern with structures designed to minimise the exposure measure (agency-model arbitrage, collateral swaps, off-balance sheet transfers) and confirms that central bank reserves are included absent a temporary SAMA exemption. Binds SAMA-licensed banks.

Defines and scopes "written credit derivatives" for leverage ratio purposes — any instrument or option through which the bank effectively provides credit protection, not only CDS and total return swaps — and sets the conditions for offsetting the effective notional amount against purchased credit protection. Key tests are identical reference names (same legal entity), same or more conservative material terms (subordination, optionality, credit events, strike price), and economic equivalence where protection is bought on a pool rather than individual names. Binds SAMA-licensed banks computing derivative exposures in the leverage ratio.
lookup_terms: credit default swap total return swap

data.summary: An Arabic-language SAMA circular (supplementing an earlier circular on executing judicial judgments without delay) requiring all supervised entities to respond promptly to judicial authorities, reply to their requests within the prescribed statutory periods, receive judgments and decisions, and implement them expeditiously. SAMA warns that delay or procrastination will attract regulatory action against both institutions and staff. Addressed to banks, finance companies, money exchangers and credit information companies.

SAMA rules (first issue, Arabic) on the electronic issuance and verification of bank documents, defining "bank documents" as certificates or statements issued at a customer's request and requiring banks to process all such requests through technical systems, issue electronically in Arabic (English on request), and provide an electronic verification channel for every document issued, whether electronic or paper. It sets a minimum list of documents that must be available electronically (bank certificate, proof of indebtedness, account statement, clearance letter, IBAN certificate), alignment with the Personal Data Protection Law, Electronic Transactions Law and SAMA's information security and business continuity frameworks, issuance-date inclusion, customer awareness and adherence to SAMA's prescribed issuance timeframes. Mandatory for banks licensed under the Banking Control Law from the stated effective date.

A SAMA circular directing supervised financial institutions to align with the Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree M/19) and with the data governance policies, controls and rules issued by SDAIA/NDMO, noting that the compliance scope of some of these instruments extends to SAMA-supervised entities. It requires institutions to review and amend internal policies and procedures within the statutory compliance window, perform a regulatory gap analysis against the Law and the SDAIA rules, and submit a remediation timeline to the board for approval, with correspondence routed to SAMA's designated compliance mailbox.

SAMA circular directing banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom to respond promptly to requests from the General Secretariat of the Committees for Banking and Finance Disputes and Violations when it prepares cases for hearing.
