It binds addressees to the response deadlines set out in an annexed schedule (generally three, seven, ten or fifteen business days by document type, e.g. contracts, statements, transfer and SWIFT records, POS and card-dispute evidence, CCTV, call recordings, guarantees, pledges), and requires immediate notification with a justification and a substitute date not exceeding thirty days where a deadline cannot be met. Non-compliance exposes the institution to supervisory action.

SAMA circular requiring banks and finance companies to take into account loans granted to individual customers by development funds and banks affiliated with the National Development Fund when assessing affordability. It builds on the Responsible Lending Principles requirement to count government-provided loans within the customer's monthly obligations, and directs lenders to rely on reports from licensed credit bureaus and to include the development-fund deduction in the customer's monthly debt-burden ratio before granting new financing.

SAMA circular addressing fraudulent misuse of the preauthorization and subsequent capture/purchase advice functions on POS terminals using cards on international payment networks. It obliges banks and payment service providers offering acquiring services to apply the relevant international scheme rules, restrict these transaction types to eligible merchant segments, monitor and investigate suspicious and high-risk preauthorization/capture activity by customer segment and amount, and enhance fraud monitoring and detection arrangements consistent with SAMA's Counter-Fraud Manual.

SAMA circular strengthening KYC by requiring financial institutions to verify that the mobile number linked to a customer account or membership belongs to the same identity holder, matched against the national trusted source (the "Tahaqaq" verification service). Addressed to banks, finance companies, payment service providers and category (A) exchange centres, it requires assessment of existing non-matching accounts, submission of results and a remediation plan to SAMA, adoption of the verified mobile number in onboarding for new accounts/memberships (in-person and remote), implementation within 45 days, and continued compliance with the Rules for Bank Account Opening.

SAMA circular on the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development "remote work" initiative, addressed to all financial institutions supervised by SAMA. It requires that remote customer-service staff be recorded in official registers and either enrolled in social insurance or have their contracts documented on the Ministry's designated portal, including where the worker is engaged directly or supplied through an intermediary, contractor or outsourcing provider.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development

data.summary: SAMA circular unifying the minimum content of transaction notification messages sent to customers of financial institutions, extending earlier requirements for mada card notifications. Addressed to banks, payment service providers and category (A) exchange companies, it requires notifications for all financial transactions containing at least the data elements listed in the annexed tables (by transaction type: domestic/international purchases, ATM withdrawals, deposits, cheques, domestic and cross-border transfers, internet purchases, bill payments, financing drawdowns and instalments, fees, refunds/reversals, mobile-app and e-wallet transactions), along with a standardised Arabic/English terminology list, implementation within 15 days and submission of an implementation plan within two weeks.

First edition of SAMA's Internal Audit Principles for local banks, issued under the SAMA Law and the Banking Control Law and effective from the stated implementation date. It sets out the board's, audit committee's and senior management's duties toward internal audit, and the independence, objectivity, professional competence, ethics, charter/policy, organisation, reporting lines, risk-based audit planning, quality assurance and documentation requirements for the internal audit unit as third line of defence, including SAMA no-objection for appointing or changing the head of the unit and coverage of subsidiaries. It binds locally licensed banks operating in the Kingdom and their governance bodies.

SAMA circular reaffirming compliance with remote-work requirements for customer service roles, supplementing an earlier circular requiring remote workers to be recorded in the institution's official records and GOSI registers and their contracts documented on the designated portal. It attaches the MHRSD ministerial decision restricting remote customer service occupations to Saudi nationals (direct or outsourced), with its procedural guide and penalty regime. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA, effective from the circular's date.

Short SAMA circular on customer communication channels requiring financial institutions to replace the 920 unified customer service number with the toll-free unified 800 number, reaffirming an earlier circular on making contact channels available. It obliges institutions to make the free unified number accessible to all customer segments. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision.

Fourth edition of SAMA's instructions on the banding/bundling card templates used for the sixth issue of banknotes, replacing the third edition and adding a template for the SAR 200 denomination following its circulation. It prescribes mandatory card designs, colour codes per denomination, and required content (bank name and logo, note count and denomination, issue reference, two staff names and signatures) for notes delivered to SAMA branches. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom and cash centres, with a three-month implementation period.

Urgent SAMA circular adopting the requirement that lawyers hold the national unified entity number beginning with 7, obtained through the legal-practice entity register, following the Ministry of Justice/Saudi Bar Association correspondence and a Council of Ministers decision. It builds on earlier SAMA instructions substituting the unified national number for commercial registration and licence numbers for non-government entities. It binds all financial institutions supervised by SAMA and credit information companies, and is relevant to identifying legal-person/professional customers (KYB) and to credit data records.

SAMA circular reinforcing earlier security instructions by requiring banks and exchange centres to strengthen banknote inspection procedures and exercise maximum care in verifying the authenticity of currency circulating in the Kingdom. Staff must immediately notify the security authorities on suspicion of any counterfeit note and inform SAMA. It binds banks and money exchange centres operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular transmitting the Instructions on Services Provided to Persons with Disabilities in Financial Institutions, aimed at fairness, financial inclusion and removal of physical and behavioural barriers to accessing financial services. It defines "person with disability", "disability", "financial institution" and "accessibility", and imposes requirements such as establishing a dedicated administrative unit, accessible built environment, self-service/electronic channels, transparency and fair treatment, and financial education. It binds all SAMA-supervised entities — banks and foreign bank branches, insurance/reinsurance firms, finance and finance-lease registration companies, credit information companies, exchange houses, and payment companies — with compliance due within three months and a compliance plan within one month.

SAMA circular requiring banks and payment service providers to be operationally ready to receive and process requests from retail-sector merchants for electronic payment acceptance, following the national decision mandating all retail activities to offer electronic payment from the stated date. Obligations cover readiness to open merchant accounts and e-wallets, to install SAMA-authorised payment means (mada POS, e-wallets) through all customer channels, accurate assignment of Merchant Category Codes, and internal communication to branches and customer service. It binds banks, PSPs and Saudi Payments.

SAMA circular on real estate appraisal fees in retail real estate finance contracts. Financiers may not deduct appraisal fees from the customer before the customer has received preliminary financing approval, and must inform the customer — and obtain an acknowledgement — before contracting that the fee is non-refundable if the financing is not completed for reasons attributable to the customer. It binds banks and real estate finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

Short SAMA circular extending the scope of the Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions (issued under the earlier referenced circular) to exchange companies and establishments. It confirms that money changers fall within the "financial institution" definition for those principles, which address discipline, integrity, transparency, objectivity, competence and loyalty of staff. It binds exchange companies and establishments operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular imposing settlement fees on banks in connection with mada claims. Banks must refund customers for erroneous or incomplete transactions across ATM, POS and e-commerce services within two business days, and banks failing to do so incur per-claim settlement fees under a stated tariff, effective from the specified date. It binds banks, payment service providers and Saudi Payments, and rests on SAMA's statutory authority over payment and settlement systems.

SAMA circular requiring banks and payment service providers to be ready to receive requests for electronic payment means from merchants in personal services activities, following the mandate obliging that sector to accept electronic payment from the stated date. Requirements include readiness to open bank accounts and e-wallets for such merchants, to provide SAMA-authorised payment means (POS devices or QR code) through branches, website and call centre, to apply the Merchant Category Codes designated for the sector, and to circulate the decision internally. It binds banks, PSPs and Saudi Payments.

SAMA circular (General Department for Supervision of Finance Companies) on finance companies issuing debt instruments through special purpose entities (SPVs). It confirms that, consistent with Article 14 of the Finance Companies Control Law and Article 66 of its Implementing Regulation, a finance company must apply to the Capital Market Authority to establish an SPV under the CMA's SPV rules, notify SAMA of that application, and obtain SAMA's prior no-objection before any debt instrument is issued through the SPV. It binds all finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular to all banks operating in the Kingdom reinforcing earlier circulars on customer awareness when dealing in cash. Following reports of thefts from customers carrying large cash sums, banks must activate the prior circulars, educate customers on the risks of carrying large amounts of cash, encourage use of electronic payment channels, and inform them of licensed cash and precious metals transport companies as a safe alternative.

SAMA circular issued under Article 15(c) of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business requiring Saudization of all jobs in money exchange establishments and companies (category A/B). Licensees must restrict all activity positions to Saudi nationals, train and qualify Saudi staff, submit a full Saudization plan to SAMA within two weeks, and complete Saudization within one year, with enforcement action against non-compliant exchangers.

A bilingual FAQ document supporting applicants to SAMA's Regulatory Sandbox, explaining its purpose, benefits, eligibility and the nature of exemptions granted. It clarifies that the Sandbox is reserved for new business models or concepts for which no regulatory framework or licensing path already exists, that testing occurs live within pre-defined limits (customer numbers, transaction volume and value), and that exemptions are assessed case by case per the published Sandbox Framework. It is guidance for prospective applicants rather than a binding rulebook.

SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions (v1.0, August 2019) sets the minimum controls financial institutions must adopt for receiving and handling violation reports. It covers general obligations, the unit handling reports, reportable cases, obligations of whistle blowers and of institutions, protection of whistle blowers from retaliation and against disclosure of identity (except to investigative or judicial authorities), report processing and approval arrangements, and reporting/performance indicators. It binds SAMA-supervised financial institutions and shapes duties of their employees and stakeholders.

SAMA circular from the General Department for Supervision of Finance Companies requiring finance companies to obtain SAMA's no-objection before providing governmental or non-governmental bodies with the periodic supervisory data submitted to SAMA or with unpublished statistical data. It reflects SAMA's control over the integrity and publication of sector data and binds all finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA circular and annexed instructions requiring supervised entities to substitute the Unified Number (issued by the National Information Center, beginning with "7") for the Commercial Registration number and licence numbers as the digital identifier of non-governmental entities, while retaining the existing CR field and linking the two so a search on either returns both. It extends the migration deadline, replaces all earlier circulars on the subject, and requires entities to inventory affected customers, licensed non-CR entities (e.g. lawyers, non-profit associations) and business partners, and to assess risk impacts on credit, blocks/freezes, dormant accounts, local and UN lists, KYC generally and beneficial-owner verification. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision and all credit information companies.
lookup_terms: KYC beneficial owner verification unified number

data.summary: SAMA's Compliance Principles for banks and commercial banks operating in the Kingdom, issued under the SAMA Law and the Banking Control Law to replace the earlier Compliance Manual (2008). It defines the compliance function, compliance policy, compliance unit, head of compliance, compliance officers/staff and compliance risk, and sets board and senior management responsibilities, reporting, sanctions, outsourcing of compliance tasks and cross-border/foreign-operations issues. It binds local banks and licensed branches of foreign banks (with the branch's senior officer standing in for the board), initially on a guidance basis and later as a mandatory requirement.

SAMA instructions setting the minimum requirements financiers must meet when offering retail (individual) real estate finance products, reissued to amend paragraph 3 so that the financing offer may be delivered electronically at the customer's choice; they supersede the earlier instructions. Requirements include affordability/credit-capacity assessment before any offer, a documented plain-language explanation of terms and risks, an offer valid at least fifteen working days containing the finance contract, the disclosure form and (for variable-rate products) a credit-risk acknowledgment, plus a mandatory session with an independent qualified credit advisor. It binds banks and real estate finance companies supervised by SAMA.

SAMA circular transmitting instructions (originally sent by email, effective from that notification) on readiness to provide electronic payment acceptance to the groceries and foodstuff retail sector, following the joint decision with the anti-commercial-concealment programme and other ministries mandating such outlets to accept electronic payment. It requires banks and payment service providers to be ready to open merchant bank accounts and e-wallets, to receive and process requests for SAMA-authorised acceptance means (POS terminals, QR codes) across all channels under the applicable regulatory and operational rules, to use merchant category code 5411, and to brief staff internally. It binds banks and payment service providers.

Short SAMA circular reaffirming the existing advertising and marketing instructions, which require promotional material for products and services to be clear and free of wording that directly or indirectly misleads customers. Issued after SAMA observed non-compliant promotional advertisements, it directs financial institutions to review all promotional advertising for conformity and warns that statutory action will be taken against violators. It binds banks, finance companies and payment companies operating in the Kingdom, effective from its date.

SAMA circular mandating use of a unified response template for complaints received through the "SAMA Cares" system, annexed in three forms: requesting missing documents, informing the customer of the outcome and corrective action taken, and responding to complaints escalated to SAMA with supporting documents and reference to the instruction, contract or terms relied on. It builds on the earlier service level agreement instructions for complaint handling and also requires firms to strengthen the customer care function, maintain and measure an internal SLA ensuring complaints are resolved within prescribed timeframes. It binds all financial institutions under SAMA supervision, effective from its date.

SAMA circular (issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation) requiring finance and refinance companies to disclose SAMA enforcement actions taken against them in their annual board of directors' reports, under a dedicated heading for SAMA enforcement decisions. Disclosure must cover the current and prior financial year and state the subject of the violation, the number of enforcement decisions (monetary and non-monetary) and total fines in SAR, broken down into supervisory/regulatory breaches, consumer protection breaches, and AML/CTF customer due diligence breaches. SAMA will reconcile these disclosures against its own records, publish violations on its website, and act against non-compliant companies; effective from the FY2017 board report.
lookup_terms: Finance Companies Control Law implementing regulation

data.summary: SAMA circular to licensed money exchangers (categories A and B) attaching the minimum requirements for exchange centre premises, issued under the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business, with a one-year period to bring existing premises into compliance. It sets conditions on location (main commercial street, mall, airport/border crossing), minimum floor areas and counter setbacks for head offices and branches (with special thresholds for the Central Area of the Two Holy Mosques), 3D engineering designs consistent with the financial-sector security and safety manual, fit-out and signage, insurance of premises, complaint handling, and technical requirements including an automated accounting/reporting system supporting AML obligations and screening against international prohibition lists in Arabic and English, off-site data backup and restrictions on third-party access to data. SAMA no-objection is required before leasing premises and before executing designs.
lookup_terms: money exchangers category A and B

data.summary: SAMA circular to exchange centres operating in the Kingdom (categories A and B) clarifying an earlier circular that restricted all jobs in the exchange sector to Saudis. It confirms that categories treated as Saudis for labour purposes — including the child of a Saudi mother — count toward Saudization ratios in line with decisions of the Ministry of Labour and Social Development, and that this must be disclosed in data submitted to SAMA. Exchange centres must continue to track and comply with whatever the Ministry issues on the matter.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Labour and Social Development

data.summary: SAMA circular, following a communication from the Minister of Communications and Information Technology on class (B) licence terms, requiring all financial institutions operating in the Kingdom to contract only with SMS service providers licensed by the Communications and Information Technology Commission (CITC), with licence status verifiable on the CITC website. It binds banks, finance companies, insurance-sector companies, payment companies and exchange centres (categories A and B), effective from its date.

SAMA circular to exchange centres (categories A and B) supplementing the February 2010 manual on exchange business procedures regarding customer acceptance and identity verification. Based on approval from the Minister of Interior, customers of airport branches who are travelling outside the Kingdom only are exempted from presenting the national ID for executing transactions; a passport and boarding pass, matched against the customer's name, suffice. Effective from its date.

Arabic SAMA circular with heavily degraded OCR; the legible elements cite the Finance Lease Law, Real Estate Finance Law, Finance Companies Control Law and related finance/payment legislation and concern how supervised financial institutions deal with customers, including making documents, contracts and disclosures available to customers through approved electronic channels. The distribution list covers banks, finance companies, insurance companies and other SAMA-supervised institutions. Because the text is only partially recoverable, the precise obligations should be confirmed against the original PDF before relying on this node.

A SAMA circular prohibiting supervised entities from placing the SAMA logo on their own printed materials and publications except where expressly permitted, after SAMA observed unauthorised use without prior approval. It is aimed at preventing reputational harm to SAMA, commercial exploitation of its emblem and misleading of customers. It binds all SAMA-supervised entities — banks, insurance and reinsurance companies, finance companies, credit bureaus, insurance-related professional firms and exchange houses — and their branches, with enforcement action against breaches.

A SAMA circular requiring finance companies to obtain the signature of natural-person customers on every page of contracts and agreements to which they are a party, grounded in the Finance Companies Control Law and the finance customer protection principles on disclosure, transparency and customer awareness. Application to legal persons is left to the finance company's discretion, but the company bears the risk arising from unsigned pages in corporate contracts. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: natural person vs legal person customer

data.summary: A SAMA circular instructing finance companies to accept electronically notarised formation contracts of limited liability companies that carry only the Ministry of Commerce and Investment seal and no notary public seal, following the Ministry's move to electronic notarisation for LLCs owned by Saudi partners (non-minors), a Saudi individual or a registered resident. Companies must still verify the contract data through the existing verification service used by banks and financial institutions or the Ministry's business record portal. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom and is relevant to corporate customer documentation and identification/KYB practice.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Commerce seal notary public

data.summary: A SAMA circular making compliance with specified articles of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law optional for finance companies when dealing with small, medium and large enterprises, issued under SAMA's mandate to regulate and supervise the finance sector. It defines the relevant enterprise sizes by reference to an earlier SAMA circular adopting the SME Authority's size-classification decision. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom and functions as a scope limitation on retail-style conduct obligations for business customers.
lookup_terms: Implementing Regulation Finance Companies Control Law articles

data.summary: A SAMA circular requiring equal treatment of all segments of society in access to financing products and in insurance coverage under finance lease contracts, invoking the fair-treatment and non-discrimination principles in the banking and finance customer protection principles. It cross-refers to SAMA's instruction to insurers prohibiting refusal of compulsory or comprehensive motor cover based on the age of the actual user of a leased vehicle, and correspondingly bars discrimination against finance customers on that ground. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA circular notifying finance companies that, following a Ministry of Justice decision adding a provision to the Implementing Regulation of the Code of Law Practice, employees of in-house legal departments of private legal persons are treated as statutory representatives once licensed by the Ministry's General Department of Advocacy. Accordingly, finance company legal department staff may litigate for the company before the competent judicial bodies in no more than three cases at a time, subject to listed licensing conditions and documents (including a valid power of attorney and employment contract). It is addressed to finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: Code of Law Practice in-house counsel licensing
General Department of Advocacy Ministry of Justice

data.summary: SAMA circular (Finance Companies Control General Department) setting out the activities licensed finance companies may conduct with persons authorised by the Capital Market Authority, issued under the Finance Companies Control Law and coordinated with the CMA. It permits sale of finance portfolios to investment funds, loan participation agreements with funds for co-financing, and fund investment arrangements provided the credit-granting decision remains with the finance company. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom and does not override the Finance Companies Control Law or its Implementing Regulation.

SAMA circular amending the maximum loan-to-value ratio under Article 12 of the Implementing Regulation of the Real Estate Finance Law, raising the cap for citizens acquiring a first home to 90% of the dwelling value. Banks remain at 70% and real estate finance companies at 85% for second and subsequent homes for all beneficiaries. It binds SAMA-licensed banks and real estate finance companies, and reiterates risk-policy review, credit concentration monitoring and affordability/repayment-capacity verification before granting finance.

Short SAMA Banking Supervision circular to all money exchange businesses in the Kingdom, grounded in the requirement (Article 18 of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business) to appoint a SAMA-accepted licensed external auditor for annual audit. It directs each exchanger to obtain and report to SAMA the accounting standards its external auditor applies when auditing the financial statements. It binds licensed money exchange companies and establishments.

SAMA Banking Supervision circular reminding all money exchange companies and establishments of their obligation to comply with the rules on physical cash movement/transport and the security safety guide, referencing earlier circulars and the Law on Transport of Money and Precious Metals. It warns that transporting cash unlawfully, or receiving cash unlawfully transported from other exchangers, exposes the party to statutory penalties under the Banking Control Law. It binds licensed money exchange companies and establishments.
lookup_terms: transport of money and precious metals

data.summary: SAMA circular confirming that repossession of movable assets from a lessee, where the contract gives the lessor a repossession right, may occur only through the competent authorities, based on Article 25(3) of the Finance Lease Law and Ministry of Interior instructions on vehicle repossession. Until the Ministry of Justice licenses specialised enforcement companies, financiers must follow the Ministry of Interior instructions; staff who repossess without recourse to the competent authorities face legal liability. It binds banks and finance companies licensed for finance leasing activity.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Justice licensed repossession companies

data.summary: SAMA circular fixing official holiday periods for finance companies under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation: four days for Eid al-Fitr beginning after 29 Ramadan (Umm al-Qura calendar), four days for Eid al-Adha beginning on the Day of Arafah, and National Day with defined weekend substitution rules. Any change to Eid holiday dates will be circulated separately by SAMA. It binds all finance companies operating in the Kingdom and their branches.

SAMA circular clarifying the fee cap in Article 83 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law and Article 9 of the Consumer Finance Regulations (the lower of 1% of the finance amount or SAR 5,000). It confirms that the cap covers every amount the beneficiary must pay other than the finance amount and the term cost — i.e. all unavoidable fees such as application study, property valuation, property inspection and registration fees — and that the financier alone must deal with and pay third parties (valuers, registration bodies) rather than instructing the customer to do so; all such fees must be reflected in the APR. Binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom, effective from the circular date.
lookup_terms: fees and administrative service costs cap
Article 83 Implementing Regulation Finance Companies Control Law
real estate valuation and registration fees

data.summary: Urgent SAMA circular confirming, in response to industry queries, that financing of land for individuals falls under Article 12 of the Implementing Regulation of the Real Estate Finance Law. It relies on SAMA's powers under the Real Estate Finance Law and the Finance Companies Control Law. Binds all real estate financiers — banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: Article 12 Implementing Regulation Real Estate Finance Law
banks and finance companies land purchase finance

data.summary: A SAMA circular whose source PDF is a scanned Arabic image that did not convert to readable text; the extracted content is largely unusable OCR noise. Subject matter, legal basis and addressees cannot be reliably determined from the available extract, though the document sits among SAMA supervisory circulars of the same series. The original PDF must be opened to establish its scope and any obligations.

SAMA circular setting the timetable for finance companies to begin applying international accounting standards under Article 71 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law. Applicants licensed as joint stock companies start from the beginning of 2015 and submit IFRS-based quarterly statements from Q1 2015; applicants licensed as limited liability companies start from the date of the Minister of Commerce and Industry's decision converting them into a joint stock company, with quarterly statements from the first quarter of their first financial year as a JSC or Q1 2015, whichever is later, in line with Article 72. Binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: Article 71 Implementing Regulation Finance Companies Control Law
conversion from LLC to joint stock company

data.summary: SAMA circular requiring banks and finance companies to document real estate mortgages according to the true nature of the contract and to stop procedures that transfer ownership of the property instead of registering a mortgage over it. It also requires rectification of properties currently registered in the name of the bank or finance company within a stated period, customer awareness of that process, and reporting to SAMA of cases where notaries refuse to register a mortgage in the financier's favour. Issued under the SAMA Law, Banking Control Law, Finance Companies Control Law and the Registered Real Estate Mortgage Law; effective immediately.
lookup_terms: registering mortgages per reality of the contract
transfer of property ownership instead of mortgage
rectification of properties registered in financier's name

data.summary: SAMA circular to money exchange centres setting out reporting obligations under Articles 15(c), 17 and 19 of the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business: quarterly financial position within 15 days of the following quarter plus externally reviewed quarterly statements within 30 days, and audited annual balance sheet within one month with audited annual financial statements within two months of financial year-end. It also caps the external auditor's appointment at five years, requires an annual external auditor assessment of internal control systems submitted separately from the financial statements within two months of year-end, and prescribes submission channels. Binds licensed money exchange centres from financial year 2014, with SAMA reserving enforcement action for breaches.
lookup_terms: Rules Governing Money Exchange Business Articles 17 and 19

data.summary: A SAMA circular issued by the General Department for Supervision of Finance Companies directing banks and licensed finance companies to register land plots subject to the White Land Fees Law within the prescribed registration window, so that beneficial/real owners are not exposed to financial penalties. It is an operational compliance instruction tied to the White Land Fees Law and its Implementing Regulation rather than a substantive prudential rule. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A Banking Policies Department circular confirming that deeds and documents issued by notaries licensed by the Ministry of Justice (including powers of attorney and their revocation, company contracts and amendments) are to be accepted within the notaries' scope of competence and treated as enforceable instruments under the Enforcement Law. It also notes that the validity of a notary's licence can be verified through the Ministry of Justice notaries portal. It binds banks, insurance and reinsurance companies, finance companies, credit information companies and money exchange businesses.

A SAMA circular standardising the definition of "commercial real estate finance" as credit granted to a natural or legal person to purchase, develop or build real estate, where at least one of four criteria is met: the beneficiary is a legal person; the financed property has five or more residential units; the property is mainly used for non-residential purposes; or the property is income-generating. Entities must align policies, procedures and regulatory reporting with this definition from the stated reporting period. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A Banking Policies Department circular adopting the unified definition of micro, small, medium and large enterprises based on the decision of the Small and Medium Enterprises General Authority (Monsha'at), using revenue bands as the primary classification criterion and full-time headcount where revenue data is unavailable (e.g. new entities). It provides the common classification used for SME-related reporting and credit categorisation. It binds banks, finance companies operating in the Kingdom and the licensed credit information companies (SIMAH and Bayan).

A SAMA circular prohibiting licensed finance companies from requiring the official stamp of establishments and companies on documents and papers submitted in financing transactions, following Ministry of Commerce and Investment decisions and a Royal Order aimed at improving the investment environment. The prohibition applies where no statutory requirement for a stamp exists and is expressly without prejudice to Know Your Customer requirements. It binds licensed finance companies with effect from the circular's date.
lookup_terms: ease of doing business finance companies

data.summary: A SAMA circular, grounded in the requirement under the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law that finance companies follow international accounting standards, directing all licensed finance companies to begin immediate preparation for adopting IFRS 9 (Financial Instruments) covering classification and measurement, impairment (expected/forward-looking loss recognition) and hedge accounting. Firms must submit quarterly progress reports to SAMA starting from the end of the first quarter of the stated year and acknowledge receipt within one week. It binds finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

A SAMA circular (dated 07/08/1438H, ref. 361000107381) addressed to supervised institutions concerning the periodic submission of financial/statistical returns to SAMA, including submission in the prescribed electronic (Excel) format within stated deadlines. It requires the returns to be accompanied by a Certification Statement signed at senior level (Chief Accountant, CFO and CEO or Managing Director). The scanned source is heavily degraded in Arabic OCR, so the precise scope and deadlines should be verified against the original before relying on it.

SAMA circular (1434H) on Saudization/employment of nationals and on requirements for contracting with recruitment and outsourcing service providers, addressed to banks operating in the Kingdom and Class (A) money exchange companies. It requires localisation of all job grades including senior leadership, restricts branch, remittance-centre and cash-centre posts to Saudis (with a narrow exception for one non-Saudi customer-service assistant with no system access or account-opening authority), and reserves cash-handling, funds transfer, information security and AML/CTF roles for Saudis only. It also bans dealing with marketers acting in the Kingdom for foreign banks or financial institutions, mandates Saudization plans and timelines, and assigns HR ownership with Compliance oversight and quarterly progress reporting.

SAMA's Licensing Disclosure Instructions (July 2019), circulated with a three-month implementation period, require financial institutions to disclose in the footers of their correspondence, printed material, email, websites, mobile apps, advertising and social media that they are licensed and subject to SAMA supervision, together with entity name as licensed, type, head office, commercial registration and licence number. Defined terms include "Financial Institution", "Correspondence", "Footers", "Advertising" and "Customers". It binds banks, finance companies, insurance/reinsurance and free-profession insurance firms, credit bureaus, money exchangers, payment and payment-systems companies and cash centres; foreign branches of Saudi institutions may add the disclosure subject to host-country law, and commercial-paper banking transactions are excluded.

SAMA circular (29/03/1439H) issuing Instructions on Publication of Banking Penalties, requiring banks to disclose in their annual reports, under a dedicated heading for SAMA penal decisions, the violations for which penal decisions were issued — showing the violation subject, number of decisions and total fines in SAR for the current and prior financial year (current year only in the first year of application). Violation subjects must be stated using the attached classification guide, which maps specific penal-decision grounds to published categories such as breach of supervisory instructions, consumer protection instructions, due diligence, AML/CTF due diligence, and ATM/POS performance standards. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom; SAMA will republish the disclosed data on its website.

SAMA circular (04/12/1440H) issuing the Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions (August 2019), with a three-month implementation period. The Principles set a minimum standard of behaviour covering professional conduct, dealing with stakeholders, combating financial and administrative corruption (including AML/CTF and bribery), gifts and hospitality, compliance with laws and internal policies, conflicts of interest, confidentiality and disclosure, misuse of inside information, whistleblowing on actual or potential violations, remuneration and incentives, and consequences of non-compliance. They bind all personnel of a Financial Institution — board and committee members, executives, permanent and contract staff, consultants and third-party staff — and the board must adopt a conforming code, with managers responsible for staff acknowledgement and awareness.
lookup_terms: Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics

data.summary: The AML/CTF component of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions, placed within the section on combating financial and administrative corruption alongside anti-bribery. It obliges personnel of a Financial Institution to observe conduct standards on anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing and suspicious transactions as part of the institution's board-approved code of conduct, and interacts with the separate, substantive AML/CTF Law and Rules and with the whistleblowing and confidentiality principles in the same document. It binds board members, executives, employees, contractors, consultants and third-party staff of banks, insurers, finance and finance-lease registration companies and credit bureaus supervised by SAMA.

A SAMA circular (Banking Policies Department) setting binding controls for how banks and exchange companies handle "banking procedure" transactions received from SAMA on behalf of authorities legally empowered to act on customer accounts — e.g. judicial enforcement, seizure/garnishment, lifting of holds, disclosure of account information and documents. It fixes maximum turnaround times by category (judicial, civil/general, security), requires an immediate nil reply where no relationship exists, and mandates dedicated, independent and adequately resourced units with full authority to execute, plus business-continuity planning and strict confidentiality on the data involved, with a limited carve-out for the customer or their special agent enquiring about execution on their own accounts. Banks and exchange companies bear responsibility toward the requesting authorities, SAMA and the customer for breach, and SAMA may shorten the deadlines and take enforcement action.
lookup_terms: turnaround time for court and security requests
banking secrecy exception for customer or agent

data.summary: Annex 1 to SAMA's Consumer Financing (Finance Consumer Protection) rules, setting the mathematical basis and assumptions for calculating the Annual Percentage Rate, together with the defining terms used (APR, Total Amount Payable by the Borrower, Amount of Financing, Consumer Financing, Borrower, Business/Calendar Day, Change in Circumstance, Authenticated Communication). It requires a 12-equal-month year, inclusion of all unavoidable costs and fees but exclusion of default/breach charges, assumes the contract runs to term with both parties performing, freezes unquantifiable variable charges at their initial level, and requires expression to at least two basis points with rounding. It binds Creditors (banks and finance companies) disclosing APR on consumer finance to natural-person Borrowers acting outside trade or profession.
lookup_terms: Total Amount Payable by the Borrower

data.summary: Article 23 (Section Seven) of SAMA's consumer financing rules defines "account statement error/dispute" and sets the Creditor's handling duties: investigate and apply the disclosed dispute procedures within 60 calendar days and in no case beyond 90, correct confirmed errors and refund the disputed amount with related Term Cost and charges, and notify the Borrower by Guaranteed Communication. Pending satisfactory resolution the Borrower need not pay the disputed portion and the Creditor may not pursue collection, nor make or threaten an improper credit-standing report or delinquency report based on non-payment of the disputed amount. Binds Creditors (banks/finance companies) toward individual Borrowers under Consumer Financing.
lookup_terms: refund of Term Cost and charges

data.summary: Article 22 (Section Six) of SAMA's consumer financing rules requires Creditors to give each Borrower at least a quarterly Consumer Financing account statement (written or, if pre-agreed, electronic) disclosing statement period dates, opening/closing balances, each draw-down, Term Cost debited and when, and all fees and charges. It also requires at least 60 calendar days' advance notice by Guaranteed Communication of changes to account charges or payment method, and places on the Borrower a duty to keep contact details current, failing which the Creditor is released from the related notification liability. Context includes Article 14 (33.33% salary deduction cap, 25% for pensioners, mandatory credit bureau check and registration with Borrower consent) and the 5-year maximum term for deferral/skip-payment offers.

A SAMA Currency Department circular setting the agreed mechanism with Customs for the inbound and outbound movement of Saudi and foreign banknotes through King Fahd Causeway customs. It covers electronic financial declaration forms, sealing and faxing of consignment details to SAMA's Dammam branch, deposit matching and counting, mandatory reporting of discrepancies (declared vs delivered amounts, condition, non-arrival, delay) and of counterfeit notes, and conditions for GCC cash-in-transit vehicles entering Saudi territory (armoured specification compliance and a licensed armed escort). Binds all banks and exchange companies operating in the Kingdom, with SAMA's Dammam branch and Customs as counterparts.
lookup_terms: cash in transit / armoured vehicle GCC

data.summary: A SAMA circular addressed to banks, finance (including real estate finance) companies and insurance companies in their capacity as clients of real estate valuation, requiring them to deal only with valuers holding Taqeem (Saudi Authority for Accredited Valuers) fellow membership and to govern the valuation process. It mandates a written valuer-selection policy and separation between financing/underwriting staff and the valuation process, and prohibits influencing valuation outcomes by coercion, inducement, fee withholding, blacklisting threats, supplying target values, prescribing valuation methods, setting inadequate timeframes, demanding disproportionate bank guarantees, or linking fees to volume of work. It also requires supplying sufficient asset information and setting acceptance criteria for financeable properties.
lookup_terms: valuer independence and conflict of interest
Accredited Valuers Law real estate branch
separation of credit and valuation functions
valuation fees and bank guarantee limits

data.summary: A section of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics for Financial Institutions dealing with safeguarding confidentiality of information and the permitted channels/mechanisms for disclosure, sitting alongside related sections on misuse or leakage of inside information, market manipulation and whistleblowing. The principles set a minimum conduct floor that each institution's board must translate into its own approved code of conduct policy. They bind all personnel of SAMA-supervised financial institutions — board and committee members, executives, permanent and contract staff, consultants and third-party-supplied staff — across banks, foreign bank branches, insurance/reinsurance and free-zone insurers, finance and finance-lease registration companies, and credit information companies.
lookup_terms: code of conduct and work ethics

data.summary: SAMA's Money Exchange Business Procedures Guide (First Edition, February 2015), issued as a complement to the Ministry of Finance Rules Governing Money Exchange Business and to SAMA's AML/CTF rules for banks and money exchangers. It structures the operational and compliance framework for licensed exchange houses: customer categories (membership customers vs. walk-in/transient customers), customer acceptance policies, KYC and CDD, permitted exchange activities, inbound/outbound domestic and cross-border remittances, bank cheques, cross-border transport of cash and bearer negotiable instruments, correspondent banking relationships, physical security systems, staffing and training, plus monthly reporting annexes on FX sales/purchases and Category (A) remittance flows. It binds Category (A) and Category (B) money exchangers licensed by SAMA; deposit-taking and banking business remain prohibited to them.
lookup_terms: دليل تنظيم إجراءات عمل محلات الصرافة
monthly FX sales and purchases return

data.summary: The Know Your Customer principle within SAMA's Money Exchange Business Procedures Guide. It requires an exchange house to form a reliable picture of each customer's true identity and the types of business and transactions the customer is likely to conduct, including identifying and verifying beneficial owners from reliable and independent sources, risk-rating customer types and applying enhanced identification where warranted, keeping identification data updated, tracking changes in customer and beneficial-owner identity, and making identification records available to the AML/CTF compliance officer and relevant officers. It binds licensed money exchangers in relation to both membership customers and transient customers, and is applied together with the transaction-threshold rules for currency exchange.

The Customer Due Diligence section of SAMA's Money Exchange Business Procedures Guide, defining CDD for exchange houses as ongoing monitoring and understanding of customers' and beneficial owners' financial transactions, verification of the business they conduct, and satisfaction that the data underlying the membership relationship is reliable and clear. It operates with the KYC principle and with tiered identification/record-keeping duties by transaction size and customer type (foreign nationals, citizens and GCC nationals, high-income customers via membership only, and legal persons subject to enhanced due diligence). It binds licensed money exchangers and drives when a membership relationship, rather than a walk-in transaction, is required.

The correspondent banking section of SAMA's Money Exchange Business Procedures Guide, covering the relationships Category (A) exchange houses maintain with correspondents for issuing and receiving remittances, within the broader chapter on exchange business activities. It sits alongside the guide's KYC/CDD, remittance and cross-border cash rules and is read with SAMA's AML/CTF rules for banks and money exchangers. It binds SAMA-licensed money exchangers; only Category (A) houses may issue or accept remittances through correspondents.

A SAMA circular updating the standard-form current account opening agreement for individuals and legal persons issued under the earlier standard-form circular. It adds a clause under the parties' rights and obligations permitting, for activation of and subscription to additional services in the instant payments system, confidential sharing of specified account information — customer name, account number, mobile number, ID/commercial registration/unified number and email — with Saudi Payments as national system operator, and stresses that banks must always use the versions published on SAMA's website. It binds banks operating in the Kingdom, within the implementation timeframe set in the referenced circular.
lookup_terms: الصيغ النموذجية لاتفاقية فتح حساب بنكي جارٍ

data.summary: A SAMA circular (issued under the SAMA Law, the Banking Control Law, the Finance Companies Control Law and the Registered Real Estate Mortgage Law) imposing uniform procedural requirements for documenting and registering real estate mortgages before notaries, together with Ministry of Justice-aligned registration forms and an incident-recording form. It sets conditions such as attendance of the mortgagor and a duly authorised representative of the financier, the financier holding a valid real estate finance licence, ownership/eligibility of the mortgaged property, Shariah committee product approval evidence, and completion of transfer and mortgage in a single procedure. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom, which must also report to SAMA cases where notaries refuse to act.

A SAMA circular issued under the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business updating operational requirements for exchange houses and exchange companies. It requires minimum one-year retention of CCTV footage, provision of account statements to membership holders on request, safekeeping of all customer transaction documents (originals or copies) with electronic archiving for at least ten years, recording of residential or national address at relationship establishment, a prohibition on deleting any transaction or membership record, and business continuity/disaster recovery plans tested periodically. It binds all exchange institutions and companies, with a four-month compliance window and the prospect of supervisory action for non-compliance.

SAMA guidelines explaining how to apply for a licence to practise finance or refinance activities under the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulations. They set out submission channel and format, the unmodifiable application form, required attachments (draft Articles of Association, organisational structure, fit and proper forms for founders, 5%+ owners of corporate founders and candidate board/committee members, feasibility study and business plan, draft third-party and related-party agreements), and an irrevocable bank guarantee equal to 20% of the minimum required capital. They bind applicants (founders/shareholders seeking SAMA approval), who are warned that false or omitted material information is a violation of the Law and may cause rejection or cancellation of the licence.

A SAMA circular concerning acceptance of the Saudi Premium Residency (both limited-term and permanent categories) as issued by the Premium Residency Center. The supplied content is limited to the Premium Residency Center material rather than operative circular text, so the specific obligations (typically acceptance of the premium residency card as valid identification in customer onboarding and identity verification) must be confirmed from the underlying document. Relevant to financial institutions supervised by SAMA that verify customer identity documents.

A SAMA circular transmitting controls and procedures for compensating Saudi banknotes stained by security ink as a result of technical or human error, supplementing earlier instructions mandating use of secure cash containers in cash transport. It prohibits circulation of ink-stained notes, requires their direct presentation to a SAMA branch with a compensation request form and declaration, requires counting/sorting/deposit and self-service machines to detect and reject such notes, requires staff training, and makes banks liable for operational compensation costs where negligence is shown and for failures by their cash-transport contractor; stained notes found in bank deposits attract a penalty under Article 23 of the Banking Control Law. It binds banks, exchange institutions and companies, and licensed cash-transport companies.

SAMA guidance accompanying updated supervisory data templates and returns for exchange centres, submitted through the Central Bank's regulatory reporting (RMS) portal. The content is largely procedural: use of the template shared by the Central Bank, uploading the completed return file, validation of errors, submission for regulator approval, and resubmission requests after final submission. It binds exchange institutions and companies subject to periodic supervisory reporting (e.g. monthly returns covering sales and purchases and currency export/import).

This is the standard-form current account opening agreement for natural persons issued under SAMA's model-forms circular, together with the update adding a clause to the parties' rights and obligations section permitting confidential sharing of specified account data (customer name, account number, mobile number, ID/CR/unified number, email) with Saudi Payments as national operator for activation of additional Instant Payments System services. It sets the mandatory contractual template, the customer data-capture fields (identity, national address, income, expected account activity, purpose of account, PEP and PEP-relative declarations, disability and marketing-consent options) and the general terms and definitions of the two parties. It binds banks and banking institutions operating in the Kingdom, which must use the version published on SAMA's website and implement the update within the circular's timeframe.

This node covers the standard-form current account opening agreement for legal persons (juristic entities) under the same SAMA model-forms circular, updated to insert a clause in the rights and obligations section allowing confidential disclosure of account data (including commercial registration or unified number, contact details and account number) to Saudi Payments for subscription to additional Instant Payments System services. The extracted context reproduces mainly the parties, identification and general terms sections of the model agreement. It binds all banks operating in the Kingdom, which must adopt the website-published version and complete compliance steps within the stated period.
lookup_terms: rights and obligations of the parties

data.summary: A SAMA circular transmitting the security committee recommendations on cash, precious metals and valuables transportation, addressed to banks and licensed cash-in-transit companies. It requires banks to strengthen oversight of contracted CIT firms inside cash centres and enforce receipt/delivery procedures, mandates separation of cash transport duties from ATM replenishment (three-member armoured vehicle crew with two armed, plus a separate two-member replenishment team in a civilian escort vehicle), dual-control sealing of ATM cassettes under CCTV, independent reconciliation of returned cash, upgraded tracking/self-destruct containers, use of SIMAH credit records in vetting CIT job applicants, and reporting of monitoring procedures to SAMA. It also signals future licensing of company-operated cash processing units.

A SAMA circular issuing the Finance Contract Summary Form, grounded in Article 79 of the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law and Article 5(1) of the updated Consumer Finance Regulations. It requires the summary form to appear at the front of every finance contract subject to that Law and those Regulations, disclosing beneficiary identity, total cost of finance, term cost, administrative and real-estate valuation fees, number and amount of instalments, first and last instalment dates, total amount payable, and cross-references to key contract clauses (including collateral shortfall handling and termination rights), with a note that the summary does not substitute for reading the contract. It binds banks and finance companies operating in the Kingdom.
lookup_terms: Finance Companies Control Law Implementing Regulation Article 79
total cost of finance / term cost

data.summary: A SAMA circular to licensed exchange businesses (categories A and B) requiring monthly reporting, on the attached template, of inbound and outbound physical cash movements across the Kingdom's land, air and sea border crossings. It relies on the Rules Governing Money Changing Business (Article 15(a) and (c) on supplying SAMA with requested data and issuing supervisory instructions, and Article 17 on accounting records and additional data requests). It binds licensed money changers only, not banks.
lookup_terms: licensed exchanger category A and B
Rules Governing Money Changing Business Article 15

data.summary: SAMA instructions governing when banks, banking institutions and licensed exchange businesses may release customer account documents, information and data to governmental and non-governmental bodies, framed around banking secrecy and the prior no-objection requirement. It sets out categories where direct disclosure is prohibited and requests must be routed through SAMA — criminal matters (via the Public Prosecution under the Law of Criminal Procedure implementing regulation), civil matters (via judicial authorities under the Enforcement Law and Law of Civil Procedure), and statutory information powers of certain other government agencies, which SAMA assesses against reasoned objective grounds — and identifies limited exceptions where direct disclosure is permitted without SAMA's no-objection. Non-compliant direct requests must be declined in writing citing these instructions.

Arabic SAMA circular amending Annex (1) of the second edition of the Requirements for Appointment to Leading Positions in SAMA-supervised financial institutions, adding a further senior role (customer-facing/customer care management) to the list of posts needing SAMA's prior written no-objection. The annex enumerates board and senior-management positions (chair, board members, committee heads, CEO, CFO, CRO, internal audit, compliance, AML/CTF, anti-fraud, anti-financial-crime, credit, operations, legal, governance/board secretary, information security/cyber, IT, HR, retail and corporate banking, treasury ALM/SAIBOR setter, financial enforcement unit head, and any executive reporting directly to the CEO). It binds banks operating in the Kingdom and applies to appointments made from the circular's date.

Operational guidelines (March 2019) for Bank Primary Dealers (Bank-PDs) in the Saudi government securities market, setting eligibility conditions (capital adequacy under ICAAP, trading and risk-management capability, infrastructure, SAMA no-objection) and conduct obligations. It requires a Primary Dealers' Committee and code of conduct, a board-approved investment policy covering PD dealing, underwriting and market-making, application of held-for-trading classification and valuation rules, inclusion of PD holdings in SAMA liquidity ratios, separate books with audit trails, and reporting to SAMA of breaches of the Debt Management Office undertaking agreement.

Arabic SAMA circular directing exchange centres to comply with the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business by conducting an independent test at least annually to assess the centre's operations, automated systems and adherence to internal policies and procedures, to be completed no later than end of July each calendar year. It also requires the external auditor's internal control systems report to include, as a minimum, any findings on the centre's compliance with those Rules. Binding on exchange centres operating in the Kingdom, with acknowledgement of receipt within one week and enforcement action for non-compliance.

Arabic SAMA circular instructing all real estate finance companies to accept the ownership document issued by the Economic Cities Authority for property or land inside economic cities as an official, approved title document equivalent to a title deed (sakk) used outside economic cities. Grounded in the Finance Companies Control Law and the Finance Lease Law implementing regulation, together with the Economic Cities Authority statute. Binds real estate finance companies operating in the Kingdom.

Arabic SAMA circular inviting supervised financial institutions to support the Kingdom's Social Responsibility Day (23 March annually, per Council of Ministers resolution) by launching development initiatives or awareness campaigns and reporting their publication contribution to SAMA. It is a participation/awareness request rather than a prudential requirement, addressed to all institutions supervised by SAMA.
lookup_terms: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development

data.summary: Arabic SAMA circular requiring all exchange centres and companies in the Kingdom to provide and activate point-of-sale (POS) service for customers with immediate effect, following SAMA's development of a unified pricing model for POS transactions made with mada cards at exchange centres. Issued under the Rules Governing Money Exchange Business; non-compliance exposes the entity to regulatory penalties.

Node within the SAMA Cyber Security Framework covering cyber security awareness and training expectations, situated alongside the framework's maturity model, cyber security policy content requirements and the allocation of cyber security roles and responsibilities. It requires that relevant stakeholders be made aware of cyber security expectations and expected behaviour through a defined awareness programme, with the Board holding ultimate responsibility (including budget and approvals). It binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA, and is assessed against maturity levels (target levels require formalised, documented and demonstrable controls).

Covers the cyber security risk management and compliance domain of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework, requiring a defined, approved and implemented cyber risk management process aligned with the Member Organization's enterprise risk management. Its objective is protection of confidentiality, integrity and availability of information assets, with compliance subject to periodic review and audit. Applies to Member Organizations under SAMA supervision and is graded against the six-level maturity model.

Sub-node of the framework's risk management cycle dealing with identification of cyber security risks as the first step before analysis, response and monitoring. It sits within the control set that requires documented risk treatment options and alignment with the organisation's risk appetite and SAMA regulations. Binds Member Organizations and is measured under the cyber security maturity model.

Sub-node addressing cyber security risk analysis — determining the likelihood of identified cyber risks materialising and their resulting impact — as the second stage of the framework's risk cycle. It feeds the risk response step, where treatment options and risk acceptance limits are assessed against risk appetite. Applies to Member Organizations and is scored against maturity levels.

Sets out how Member Organizations must respond to identified and analysed cyber risks: documenting treatment options of accepting, avoiding, transferring/sharing or mitigating through controls. Risk acceptance requires predefined limits, business owner sign-off, reporting to the cyber security committee, and must not conflict with SAMA regulations; mitigation requires evaluation, costing, feasibility and compliance review before control selection. Binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA.

Covers the final stage of the framework's cyber risk cycle: monitoring risk treatment and reviewing the effectiveness of cyber security controls on an ongoing basis, with compliance subject to periodic review and audit. Links risk acceptance and treatment decisions back to reporting lines such as the cyber security committee. Applies to Member Organizations and is evaluated through the maturity model.
lookup_terms: cyber security risk monitoring and review

data.summary: This node covers SAMA's mandatory model contract for individual real estate financing structured as Ijarah (lease-to-own), issued under a circular updating the earlier standard forms. It fixes the contract architecture — financing summary page, parties, definitions, term, promise to transfer ownership, ownership and delivery of the leased asset, rental periods, fixed and variable rental instalments and how variable amounts are recalculated, late payment, early repayment/early ownership transfer, maintenance, total/partial loss, assignment, breach and termination, customer withdrawal, death or incapacity — plus annexes for rental schedules and acceptance/ownership-transfer certificates. It binds banks and real estate finance companies operating in the Kingdom, which must use the attached form (per their approved policies) from the stated compliance date and may not conclude or amend non-conforming contracts thereafter.
lookup_terms: model Ijarah real estate financing contract
الصيغة النموذجية لعقد التمويل العقاري بصيغة الإجارة

data.summary: This node covers SAMA's mandatory model contract for individual real estate financing on a Murabaha basis, issued in the same circular that updated both the Murabaha and Ijarah standard forms. It standardises disclosure and contractual terms for retail mortgage financing — the financing summary (amount, term cost, APR, instalments, administrative fees), definitions, payment terms, late payment consequences, early repayment, withdrawal rights, security arrangements, breach and termination, and notices. It binds banks and real estate finance companies in the Kingdom, which must adopt the attached form by the deadline set in the circular and may not issue or amend contracts departing from it.
lookup_terms: model Murabaha real estate financing contract
الصيغة النموذجية لعقد التمويل العقاري بصيغة المرابحة

data.summary: This node is the leadership and governance domain of SAMA's cyber security framework, setting principles, objectives and control considerations for cyber security policy content and for the allocation of cyber security roles and responsibilities across a Member Organization. It places ultimate accountability on the Board of Directors (including budget allocation and approval of key cyber security documents) and requires a policy addressing scope, information classification and ownership, risk assessment, awareness, regulatory and contractual compliance, breach reporting and business continuity. Compliance is assessed against the framework's six-level cyber security maturity model, with formal definition, approval and demonstrable implementation required from level 3.
lookup_terms: Board of Directors cyber security responsibility

data.summary: This node sets the requirement that cyber security be embedded in project management and project governance within a Member Organization. Controls include integrating cyber security into the project methodology, including cyber security objectives in project objectives, involving the cyber security function across all project phases, performing a risk assessment at project start, registering and tracking cyber security risks in the project risk register, allocating responsibilities, and obtaining an independent internal or external cyber security review. It is assessed against the framework's maturity model and binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.
lookup_terms: cyber security risk assessment at project start

data.summary: This node covers the cyber security awareness requirement in SAMA's cyber security framework: a defined and approved awareness program must be conducted for staff, third parties and customers of the Member Organization. Its objective is a risk-aware culture in which those groups make effective risk-based decisions protecting the organization's information; the related policy provisions require that relevant stakeholders be made aware of cyber security and expected behaviour. Maturity of this control is measured on the framework's 0–5 scale.
lookup_terms: staff third party and customer awareness

data.summary: This node concerns the Rules Governing Exchange Business (issued by Ministerial Decision) as invoked by a SAMA circular updating the supervisory return templates for money exchange centres. It relies on the Rules' powers requiring an exchange centre to supply SAMA with any data or reports it requests at the times it specifies, and allowing SAMA to issue instructions necessary to apply supervisory requirements to exchange business. The circular binds licensed exchange centres in the Kingdom to submit monthly (sales/purchases), quarterly (currencies, largest customers, counterfeit currency, staff data, financial statement comparison) and annual returns through SAMA's Returns Management System within set deadlines, on pain of enforcement action.
lookup_terms: largest customers and counterfeit currency return

data.summary: Sub-domain 3.2.2 of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework, requiring each Member Organization to maintain a defined process to identify, communicate and comply with the cyber security implications of applicable regulation. The process must run periodically and on entry into force of new requirements, involve key business areas, and feed changes back into cyber security policy, standards and procedures. It binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations (banks, insurers and financing companies) and sits alongside industry-standards compliance, cyber security review and audit provisions.

Sub-domain 3.2.3 of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework, obliging Member Organizations to comply with mandatory national and international industry standards, naming PCI-DSS, the EMV technical standard and the SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework (March 2017 version). It is the hinge between the Framework and card/payment-scheme and messaging-network rulebooks. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations, with obvious relevance to card issuers, acquirers and institutions on SWIFT.

Sub-domain 3.2.4 of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework, requiring periodic cyber security reviews of the Member Organization's information assets to confirm that controls are securely designed, implemented and monitored for effectiveness. Reviews focus on critical information assets and customer/internet-facing services. Results feed the Framework's maturity model, under which level 3 and above require demonstrable, formalized and reviewed controls.

Sub-domain 3.2.5 of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework, covering independent cyber security auditing of the Member Organization's controls as a third line of assurance, distinct from management-led cyber security reviews. It connects to board-level accountability for cyber security and to the maturity model used by SAMA to assess and compare Member Organizations. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations and their internal audit function and Board.

Sub-domain 3.3.1 of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework (Operations and Technology domain), requiring cyber security requirements to be embedded in HR processes across the employment lifecycle. Covers security responsibilities and non-disclosure clauses in staff agreements, awareness training at onboarding and during employment, disciplinary triggers, screening and background checks, and post-employment steps such as revoking access and returning assets. Binds Member Organizations in respect of their staff.

Sub-domain 3.3.2 of the SAMA Cyber Security Framework (Operations and Technology domain), addressing physical protection of information assets and facilities as a component of the overall cyber security control set. Like other sub-domains, its controls must be defined, approved, implemented, monitored and periodically evaluated, and are scored against the six-level maturity model. Binds SAMA-supervised Member Organizations.

Procedural guidance issued by SAMA for submitting an application to obtain a licence to practise finance support activities, supplementing the Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities. It sets out who may apply (founders or an authorised representative), the duty to provide accurate and complete information, the channel for submission, and the checklist of documents required, including fit and proper forms for founders, 5%+ owners of corporate founders and board candidates, a feasibility study and three-year business plan, and an irrevocable bank guarantee equal to 20% of the minimum capital. It binds applicants seeking SAMA authorisation to incorporate and operate a finance support company.
lookup_terms: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities

data.summary: A SAMA circular updating the mandatory model (standard-form) contracts for individual real estate financing under Murabaha and Ijarah, attached to the circular. It requires all real estate financiers to adopt the updated model forms within the stated deadline and prohibits concluding or amending contracts that depart from them; the annexed Ijarah template covers the contract summary, rental periods and payment schedule, variable-rate calculation, late payment, early repayment/early ownership, default and termination, withdrawal, and transfer of title. It binds banks and real estate finance companies operating in the Kingdom dealing with individual (retail) customers.

SAMA's Cyber Security Framework, setting principles, objectives and control considerations for cyber security governance and defining a six-level maturity model (0–5) used to measure and benchmark compliance. It specifies the required content of a cyber security policy, board-level ultimate responsibility including budget and approvals, and the allocation of cyber security roles and responsibilities across the organisation. It binds Member Organizations supervised by SAMA.

The eligibility criteria and operating conditions for banks wishing to act as Primary Dealers (Bank-PDs) in Saudi Government dated securities, requiring the ICAAP-set minimum capital adequacy ratio, adequate trading and risk management capability, infrastructure and skilled staff, and SAMA's no-objection. It also imposes ongoing obligations: a board-approved investment policy covering PD activity, prudential exposure limits, held-for-trading valuation treatment, liquidity ratio counting, and reporting of undertaking-agreement violations. It binds banks licensed in the Kingdom that undertake or seek to undertake PD business.

Identifies the Debt Management Office as the counterparty that appoints Primary Dealers and signs the undertaking agreement with Bank-PDs, and as a recipient of regulatory returns alongside SAMA. Under these Rules, Bank-PDs must report to SAMA any breach of the DMO undertaking agreement, subject PD transactions and DMO/SAMA returns to concurrent annual audit, and note that the SAMA no-objection requirement does not apply to banks already appointed by the DMO before the effective date. Relevant to banks engaged in primary dealership of Saudi Government securities.

Describes the Returns Management System, SAMA's digital portal through which supervised entities submit defined supervisory and prudential return templates and through which SAMA supervisors review, accept or return them; it includes a user guidance manual and the accompanying circular updating supervisory return forms for money exchange centres. It sets submission mechanics and deadlines (monthly sales/purchases returns within a set period after month-end; quarterly currency, largest-customer, counterfeit-currency and staff data within the stated days after quarter-end), completion and validation duties, and resubmission where SAMA raises observations. It binds entities supervised by SAMA required to file returns, notably money exchange centres under the Exchange Business Rules.

A control domain within SAMA's Cyber Security Framework (section 3.3.3) requiring Member Organizations to define, approve, implement, communicate and monitor an asset management process supported by an accurate, unified information asset register.
