The lessor data circular attaches data-accuracy/reporting responsibility to the financier, linking pricing disclosure to credit information and consumer protection duties.
Hierarchy runs from rules/regulations down to the standard contract template and then to clarifying circulars.
start_here: Rules for Disclosure of Financing and Savings Product Prices

data.theme: Institutional governance architecture for SAMA-supervised entities: board composition and duties, mandated board committees, the compliance and internal audit functions, conduct/ethics obligations, disclosure, and remuneration design including risk-adjustment mechanisms.
how_members_connect: The core governance principles act as the parent instrument; board qualification, board responsibility, committee and sector-annex items are subordinate provisions citing back to it.
An obligation chain runs board → audit/risk/nomination-and-remuneration committees → compliance unit and internal audit, allocating oversight, reporting lines and independence requirements.
The code of conduct links governance to substantive regimes — AML/CTF, confidentiality and conflict of interest — showing conduct duties as the delivery mechanism for those regimes at firm level.

Remuneration rules depend on governance definitions (independent member, nomination and remuneration committee) and add risk-sensitive controls such as malus, clawback, misconduct-risk adjustment and compliance reporting.
Sector-specific overlays (exchange sector annex; finance and real estate refinance compliance principles) apply the general principles proportionately to particular licence types.
start_here: Corporate Governance Principles for Financial Institutions
Compliance Principles for Finance and Real Estate Refinance Companies

data.theme: SAMA's conduct expectations for supervised entities' involvement in conferences, exhibitions and similar events — both as host/sponsor and as participant — covering prior notification/approval, branding and sponsorship limits.
how_members_connect: Two sibling rule sets in the same instrument family, split by role: hosting/sponsoring versus participating.
The participation rules cross-refer to the hosting and sponsoring rules, so scope carve-outs and approval pathways must be read together to avoid double-counting obligations.
Versioning matters: V1 and V2 are distinct issuances, so the effective requirement depends on which activity and which version governs.
start_here: General Rules for Hosting and Sponsoring Events (V1)
General Rules for Participation in Events (V2)

data.theme: The targeted financial sanctions (TFS) regime: obligations on financial institutions to screen against designation lists, handle alerts, and execute freezing/unfreezing without delay, aligned to FATF Recommendations 6 and 7.
how_members_connect: The TFS Rules are the parent instrument; screening, list management, alert handling and freezing/unfreezing are its component obligation chains, each cross-referenced from the Rules.
A sequential obligation chain runs list ingestion → screening → alert triage/escalation → freeze and reporting, so a defect at any upstream step is a breach of the downstream duty.
FATF Recommendations 6 and 7 are cited as the international standard the Rules implement, relevant to interpreting 'without delay' and designation scope.
Note the duplicate node: treat it as the same instrument, not a separate legal source, when citing.

data.theme: Limits and disclosure duties on fees and charges imposed on finance consumers — service fees, administrative fees on consumer finance, and how these interact with consumer protection principles and finance company licensing.
how_members_connect: The service fee guide sits downstream of the consumer protection principles (fairness, transparency, disclosure) and operationalises permissible fee types and caps.

Administrative fee controls on consumer finance are conceptually anchored in the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law, which supplies the licensing perimeter and product definitions.
Micro finance / micro consumer finance rules and licensing requirements inherit from the same Implementing Regulation, so fee ceilings must be read against the specific licence category and product.
Beware the 'Consumer' definition: fee protections attach to consumers, not all customers, which narrows scope relative to AML-style 'customer' duties.

data.theme: Licensing and ongoing conduct of finance companies and finance support activities under the Finance Companies Control Law, including debt collection, BNPL limits, credit card security instruments, governance and AML/CFT/CPF risk assessment.
how_members_connect: The Executive Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law is the hub: licensing rules, circulars and product-limit decisions all reference it as their legal basis.

A clear hierarchy law → executive regulation → licensing rules → amending circulars; the debt collection circulars form a chronological chain where the later cancellation of the licence requirement supersedes earlier outsourcing conditions.

Product-specific interventions (BNPL per-customer limit, prohibition on promissory notes for credit card financing) modify permitted conduct without altering the licence category, so both must be read alongside the Regulation.

Governance principles and the AML/CFT/CPF business risk assessment guide attach as cross-regime obligations on licensed finance companies; note BNPL 'Consumer' does not map one-to-one to the AML 'Customer'.
Duplicate nodes for the Regulation and the risk assessment guide are the same instruments, not independent authorities.
start_here: Executive Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law
Licensing Rules for Finance Support Activities
Cancellation of License Requirement for Debt Collection Activity

data.theme: Registration of finance lease contracts in the statutory contract registry and the downstream right to obtain executive (enforceable) deed extracts, which determine when a lessor can enforce without a fresh court judgment.
how_members_connect: Both control sets derive their authority from the Finance Lease Law (Royal Decree M/48) and its registry mandate — a law-to-implementing-controls hierarchy.
Registry entry is the condition precedent: only a validly registered contract can generate an executive deed extract, so the two control sets form a sequential obligation chain.
Shared defined terms (finance lease contract, registry, lessor/lessee, executive deed) must be read consistently across both instruments.
Scope limit: these controls govern registration and enforceability mechanics, not the prudential licensing of the lessor.
start_here: Controls for Contract Registry Entry Procedures

data.theme: Restrictions on reproducing, imitating or depicting Saudi currency (images, advertising, souvenirs, digital renderings) to protect currency integrity and prevent counterfeiting confusion.
how_members_connect: Standalone control set: obligations attach to any person or entity reproducing currency, not only SAMA-supervised institutions.
Operates alongside criminal counterfeiting law; the controls set permission and format conditions rather than penalties.
No internal cross-references in this cluster — assess it as a discrete compliance duty for marketing and communications activity.

data.theme: Consumer-protection style requirements on the content, availability and retention of ATM transaction receipts issued to customers.
how_members_connect: Standalone initiative-based requirement directed at banks/ATM operators as part of disclosure and transaction-evidence duties.
Reads across to consumer protection and payments regimes on transaction records and dispute evidence, though not cross-referenced here.
Obligation is operational and customer-facing: what must be printed/offered, and when.

data.theme: The prudential and governance regime for finance companies licensed to take deposits, covering authorization, capital adequacy, liquidity and board-level governance and risk management.
how_members_connect: The 2020 DTFC Regulations act as the parent instrument; the other members are its constituent obligation pillars referenced from it.
Authorization is the gateway condition — capital, liquidity and governance requirements are ongoing licence conditions whose breach affects continued authorization.
Shared defined term 'Deposit Taking Finance Company' delimits scope: these duties sit above the ordinary finance company regime but below the banking law regime.
Governance and risk management provisions interact with SAMA's wider corporate governance, internal control and AML/CTF expectations for supervised entities.

data.theme: Insolvency and corporate-existence law as it bears on account handling: how a licensed institution treats accounts of entities in liquidation or financial restructuring, and the statutory basis for those procedures.
how_members_connect: The accounts instruction is the operative SAMA-level obligation; the Bankruptcy Law and Companies Law supply the underlying procedures and defined statuses (liquidation, restructuring) it cross-references.

Legal hierarchy runs law -> SAMA instruction: the two statutes define when an entity enters a procedure and who has authority to act; the accounts rules determine account status, signatory authority and operating restrictions.
Shared reliance on court/trustee appointments and corporate dissolution concepts, which also condition KYC/mandate verification for the affected customer.

data.theme: Prudential reserve requirement imposed on money exchange centres — the amount and maintenance of statutory reserve balances held with SAMA.
how_members_connect: Standalone circular; its linkage is to the money-exchange licensing regime rather than to other nodes in this graph.
Relevant as a prudential/supervisory condition of licence, distinct from AML/CTF obligations that also bind exchange centres.
start_here: SAMA Circular on Statutory Reserve for Money Exchange Centers

data.theme: Supervisory circulars addressed to finance companies covering conduct and prudential expectations across the credit lifecycle: granting policies, outsourced debt collection, real estate secondary-market duties, and SME financial awareness.
how_members_connect: Common addressee and scope: entities licensed under the finance companies regime, so each circular layers onto the same licensing and consumer-protection base.
Obligation chain follows the credit lifecycle — origination and credit-granting policy, ongoing servicing and disclosure, then collection and transfer/assignment in the secondary market.
Outsourced collection engages third-party/outsourcing accountability: the financier remains responsible for the service provider's conduct toward the borrower.
Circulars are the lowest tier — they refine, not replace, the underlying finance regulations; read them as supplemental obligations.
start_here: SAMA Circular on Updating Credit Granting Policies for Finance Companies
SAMA Circular on Debt Collection Controls via External Service Providers

data.theme: The core AML/CTF customer due diligence regime: risk assessment, identification and verification of customers and beneficial owners, calibrated CDD intensity, and the record-keeping and governance obligations that support them.
how_members_connect: All members hang off the risk-based approach: ML/TF risk assessment determines whether standard, enhanced or simplified due diligence applies, so the three CDD tiers are variants of one obligation rather than separate regimes.

Defined terms propagate — Beneficial Owner and PEP status are inputs that trigger EDD; correspondent relationships and wire transfers are named higher-risk contexts with their own additional measures.
Accountability chain: the Board carries responsibility for the AML/CTF programme and the risk assessment, while reliance on a third party shifts execution but not ultimate responsibility for CDD.

Hierarchy runs from the statutory base (terrorism crimes and financing law) and FATF standards down to the SAMA guide, which operationalises them; record keeping is the evidentiary backbone making all other duties supervisable.

data.theme: Cyber and IT risk governance for SAMA-supervised entities: the Cyber Security Framework as the umbrella obligation set, extended into third-party/cloud arrangements, change and project controls, and alignment with external technical standards.
how_members_connect: The Cyber Security Framework sits at the top of the hierarchy and is the instrument that incorporates or aligns with external standards (NIST, PCI DSS, SWIFT CSCF), so compliance with those standards is read as evidence of framework compliance rather than as freestanding KSA obligations.

Domain nodes (third-party cyber security, cloud computing controls, IT risk management, change management, system development, project management, quality assurance) are subordinate control areas that cite back to the framework for their mandatory baseline.

Outsourcing/cloud linkage creates an obligation chain: the supervised entity remains accountable for cyber controls exercised by service providers, connecting this cluster to outsourcing and operational-risk regimes.
The General Department of Cyber Risk Control is the supervisory counterpart, relevant to notification, approval and examination touchpoints.
start_here: Cyber Security Risk Management and Compliance

data.theme: Prudential liquidity risk management obligations for banks: the governance, control, stress-testing and contingency-planning requirements that an institution must have in place and evidence to SAMA.
how_members_connect: The Rules on Liquidity Risk Management are the parent instrument; governance, internal controls, stress testing and the contingency funding plan are mandated components cross-referenced from it.

Stress testing and the contingency funding plan form an obligation chain: scenario results must feed the triggers and actions in the plan, so a deficient stress-testing programme undermines plan adequacy.
Internal controls (general and liquidity-specific) provide the assurance layer, linking this cluster to board/senior-management accountability and internal audit duties.

data.theme: Combined prudential regime for liquidity adequacy and credit risk classification/provisioning: board-level liquidity governance, ILAAP and stress-testing on one side, and IFRS 9-based staging, forbearance, default, write-off and collateral rules on the other.
how_members_connect: Two obligation chains meet at governance: board and ALCO oversight sets liquidity risk tolerance, which drives stress testing, LCR/NSFR monitoring, ILAAP and the contingency funding plan.

The Rules Governing Credit Risk Exposure Classification and Provisioning are the parent instrument for the credit-side members, importing IFRS 9 as the accounting basis while imposing SAMA-specific staging, default, forbearance and write-off requirements — where they diverge, the prudential rule governs.

Restructuring taxonomy (short/long-term measures, forgiveness, loan splitting, debt-to-equity or asset swaps, NPV analysis) operates as defined forbearance treatments that trigger staging and provisioning consequences rather than as commercial options.
Internal audit review of ECL adequacy and collateral valuation rules are the assurance and measurement anchors linking classification outcomes back to capital and provisioning adequacy.
start_here: Rules Governing Credit Risk Exposure Classification and Provisioning

data.theme: Consumer finance conduct regime: cost-of-credit transparency (APR), contract documentation, borrower treatment and dispute handling, plus debt buyout/transfer between finance companies and adjacent mortgage and licensing requirements.
how_members_connect: The Regulations for Consumer Financing are the anchor instrument; the APR rules, annex methodology and SAMA calculator prescribe the single mandatory disclosure metric, and fee/administrative-cost circulars clarify what must be included in it.

Circulars (signing all contract pages, equality in financing products and insurance coverage, fee clarification) operate as supervisory refinements layered on the regulation — they narrow discretion rather than create a separate regime.

Debt buyout instructions and clearance-letter/transfer timeframes form a procedural obligation chain with deadlines running between the transferring and acquiring finance companies, with consumer-protection effect if breached.

Borrower-dealing and dispute-resolution articles, the finance contract summary form, mortgage documentation and valuation-client obligations attach to the same Consumer/borrower defined term, while licensing guidelines set who may undertake the activity at all.
start_here: Rules Governing Calculation of Annual Percentage Rate (APR)
Consumer Finance Debt Buyout Instructions Between Finance Companies

data.theme: Third-line assurance architecture for SAMA-supervised entities: the mandate, independence and reporting lines of internal audit, and the parallel Shariah compliance and Shariah audit functions required of banks, Islamic windows and finance companies.
how_members_connect: Obligation chain by organ: board and audit committee set and approve the internal audit charter/policy and risk-based plan; executive management must enable access and remediation; the internal audit department executes — each node cross-references the others.

Shariah governance mirrors this hierarchy: the Shariah Committee issues resolutions, a Shariah compliance function monitors first/second-line adherence, and internal Shariah audit provides independent assurance, typically housed within or reporting alongside internal audit.

Sectoral split of the same concept: the Shariah Governance Framework for Local Banks and the Shariah Governance Instructions for Finance Companies impose analogous duties on different licence types; product development and Islamic window operations are the in-scope activities.
The Three Lines of Defense model is the shared conceptual spine linking internal audit, compliance principles for banks and conduct/ethics rules for exchange centres.
start_here: Internal Audit Principles for Local Banks
Shariah Governance Framework for Local Banks

data.theme: Basel III prudential quantification in the KSA context — liquidity (LCR/NSFR), capital scope and credit risk approaches, plus D-SIB add-ons — together with the Shariah-specific adaptations (HQLA alternatives, profit-sharing investment accounts) that SAMA layers on top.
how_members_connect: Definitional dependency: LCR is built from HQLA stock over total net cash outflows, which in turn is decomposed into retail, unsecured wholesale, operational-deposit and secured-funding run-off categories.
Hierarchy law→standard→guidance: SAMA circulars and guidance documents transpose and amend the BCBS Basel III LCR and NSFR texts, so BCBS documents are cited rather than directly binding.

Shariah bridge: the Treatment for Shariah Compliant Banks and Alternative Liquidity Approaches connect the liquidity regime to Mudarabah/Wakalah/Musharakah-based funding, PSIA rules, PER/IRR and Investment Account Holders, with Shari'ah Committee and board/senior-management governance duties attached.

Capital-side branch: scope of application of the Basel framework, standardized vs IRB credit risk, ECRA/SCRA and D-SIB assessment with higher loss absorbency sit alongside liquidity as the other pillar of the same prudential package.
Banks' investment rules (governance, risk monitoring, approval controls) feed the asset side that drives RSF/HQLA classification.

data.theme: SAMA's IT Governance Framework: the mandatory domain structure and governance roles that supervised entities must implement to direct, resource and control technology, including change management and operational resilience linkages.
how_members_connect: Single parent instrument: the IT Governance Framework is the anchor, with each domain (governance and leadership, IT risk, IT operations, system change management) a referenced sub-obligation.
Role allocation within the leadership domain: the IT Steering Committee, CIO and an independent internal IT audit function form the accountability chain.
Cross-regime link: IT operations management refers out to the SAMA Business Continuity Management Framework, so continuity obligations are read together with IT governance rather than in isolation.
Overlapping labels (domain vs. topic nodes) reflect the same requirement expressed at framework and detail level.

data.theme: Cyber security governance obligations under the SAMA Cyber Security Framework — board-level ownership, the CISO role and committee structure, and the maturity model used to assess compliance.
how_members_connect: The Cyber Security Framework is the parent instrument; the leadership and governance domain and the maturity model are its referenced components, with maturity levels functioning as the assessment benchmark for whether obligations are met.
Role obligations converge on the CISO and the Cyber Security Committee as the required governance structures.
A SAMA circular on leadership position appointments adds fit-and-proper/appointment conditions layered onto the CISO role defined in the framework.
The IT Governance Maturity Model is the structural analogue of the cyber maturity model, so findings under one are read consistently with the other.

data.theme: The internal AML/CTF control architecture of a supervised institution: who must monitor transactions, who escalates, and how suspicion converts into a mandatory external report. It links ongoing monitoring duties to the STR obligation owed to the Financial Intelligence Unit and to accountability at senior management level.
how_members_connect: Obligation chain: ongoing monitoring of transactions and activities generates the trigger for suspicion, which activates the reporting duty; reporting is not discretionary once the threshold is met.

Shared institutional actor: the AML/CTF compliance function is the designated owner of both monitoring outputs and the reporting channel to SAFIU, making it the addressee of most duties in this cluster.

Hierarchy of responsibility: senior management responsibilities sit above the compliance function — resourcing, independence and approval of the AML programme — so failures in monitoring or reporting escalate as governance breaches.
External reference point: SAFIU is the statutory recipient, which also engages tipping-off restrictions and confidentiality constraints around any filed report.

data.theme: The requirement for an independent audit function to test the adequacy and effectiveness of the AML/CTF programme, separate from the compliance function that operates it.
how_members_connect: Standalone node: its legal significance is as the third line of defence — independence from the function being tested is the operative requirement, not the audit methodology.
Cross-regime linkage: findings feed governance/risk reporting lines and, in practice, the senior management and compliance-function duties in the AML compliance cluster.

data.theme: The obligation to provide AML/CTF training to staff, calibrated to role and risk exposure, as a component of the required AML programme rather than an optional control.
how_members_connect: Standalone node that operates as a programme element: inadequate training is typically assessed as a deficiency in the overall AML/CTF programme owned by the compliance function.
Relevant to any function performing CDD or monitoring, including outsourced or agent-performed activity where the institution retains responsibility.

data.theme: The agent banking regime: a bank may deliver defined services through third-party agents but remains the regulated and accountable entity, including for customer due diligence, KYC and AML/CFT performed at the agent's counter. The cluster sets eligibility, vetting, permitted/prohibited scope and registration conditions for that arrangement.
how_members_connect: Instrument hierarchy: the Regulation of Agent Banking is the parent instrument, and the article-level nodes (eligibility, fit & proper, agent due diligence, bank obligations, permissible/prohibited activities, registry) are its operative provisions.

Two distinct diligence layers that must not be conflated: diligence on the agent itself (eligibility plus fit & proper assessment of the agent/its principals) versus customer due diligence performed through the agent on the bank's customers.
Non-delegable accountability: board responsibility and the bank's obligations article mean outsourcing delivery does not transfer AML/CFT or KYC liability; the bank answers for agent conduct.

Scope boundary: permissible and prohibited activities define the outer limit of what may be agent-delivered, and the registry provision conditions lawful operation on notification/registration with the supervisor.

data.theme: Licensing and conduct-of-business requirements for exchange (money changing) activity in KSA, covering how exchange houses must organise operations, controls and customer dealings.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a SAMA guide that consolidates procedural requirements for the exchange sector rather than cross-referencing other instruments in this graph.
Sits below the primary banking/AML legislative layer as guidance interpreting licensing and operational duties for a distinct licensee class.
Practical intersection with AML/CTF CDD and remittance obligations even though those instruments are clustered elsewhere.
start_here: Guide for Organizing Exchange Business Procedures

data.theme: Bank account access for non-residents in the context of the new non-Saudi real estate ownership regime — i.e., when and on what basis a non-resident may hold an account tied to property acquisition.
how_members_connect: Clear hierarchy: a royal-decree level ownership law drives a SAMA update, which in turn amends the Bank Account Rules.
The update operates as an amendment instrument; its meaning is only complete when read into the parent Bank Account Rules provisions on non-resident eligibility.
Shared defined scope around 'non-resident' status and the permitted account purpose, which limits the exemption to real-estate-related dealings.
Downstream consequence for CDD: eligibility widening does not relax identification/verification duties under the AML regime.
start_here: Update to Bank Account Rules for Non-Resident Real Estate Ownership
Non-Saudi Real Estate Ownership Law (Royal Decree M/181)

data.theme: Discrete SAMA circulars addressing narrow supervisory expectations — treatment of real property contributed in kind and arrangements around fintech membership agreements.
how_members_connect: Same instrument type and issuing authority (SAMA circulars), linked conceptually rather than by textual cross-reference.
Both act as supervisory overlays that qualify how licensed entities document and register specific asset or contractual arrangements.
Each must be read against the underlying licensing/prudential framework it modifies; neither is self-standing authority.
start_here: SAMA Circular 1607 - Real Property In-Kind Registration

data.theme: The core Saudi bank account regime: who may open an account, on what documentation, how accounts are operated, frozen, disclosed, dormant-managed and closed — with AML/CTF customer due diligence as the gating condition throughout.
how_members_connect: Strong hub-and-spoke hierarchy: the Rules for Bank Accounts 1644 is the parent instrument and nearly every other member is a chapter or annex elaborating one account category or lifecycle stage.

Two definitional branches — natural persons (residents, expatriates) and juristic persons — with the juristic branch further subdividing into resident companies, non-profit/endowment, Hajj and Umrah, multilateral and non-resident/foreign-investor categories, each inheriting the general documentation baseline and adding sector-specific evidence.

AML/CTF and KYC obligations operate as a cross-cutting condition on opening, remote onboarding, operation and freezing, linking this cluster to the sanctions/TFS and AML regimes; identity anchors such as the MOI computer number feed the verification chain.

Lifecycle and enforcement obligations (freezing, disclosure and enforcement on accounts, inoperative accounts, closure) attach post-onboarding and involve third-party authority requests, a distinct legal basis from customer consent.

Special-purpose account rules (escrow for real estate development, collection accounts for payment companies, debt crowdfunding risk reporting) bridge into the payments/PSP and finance-company regimes, where account segregation duties sit alongside the banking rules.
start_here: Rules for Opening Bank Accounts for Juristic Persons

data.theme: Standardised documentation and pricing mechanics for vehicle finance leases, covering the mandatory contract form, treatment of cooperative insurance cost changes (VAT), and subsequent amendments to the Finance Lease Implementing Regulations.
how_members_connect: All three rest on the Finance Lease Law and its Implementing Regulations; the standard vehicle contract is the operative instrument through which those regulation-level obligations bind lessors.

The VAT/cooperative insurance instruction modifies a cost component embedded in the standard contract, so it functions as an overlay on existing executed and future leases rather than a free-standing rule.
Amendments to the Implementing Regulations sit above the standard contract in the hierarchy (law → regulation → standard form → circular), so contract terms must be read as updated by them.
Shared defined terms — lessor, lessee, finance lease, cooperative insurance — carry consumer-protection consequences on disclosure and unilateral variation of charges.
start_here: Standard Vehicle Finance Lease Contract Compliance
Amendments to Finance Lease Implementing Regulations

data.theme: Certification/approval of finance products in digital form, addressing how finance companies evidence that a product and its documentation have been cleared for offering to customers.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: an instruction directed at licensed finance entities, operating as a compliance condition on product offering rather than a substantive product rule.
Interacts with finance-sector consumer protection and disclosure obligations, since certification status affects what may lawfully be marketed.

data.theme: Obligations on finance companies to keep public-facing channels — websites and social media — accurate and current, chiefly as a consumer disclosure and fair-dealing requirement.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster; the duty derives from consumer protection principles applied to finance companies' advertising and product information.
Cross-reads with product disclosure and certification requirements: published terms must match approved product documentation.
start_here: Update Finance Company Websites and Social Media

data.theme: Regional card acceptance at point of sale through the GCC-NET switch, covering the payments regime for cross-border GCC transactions processed at KSA POS terminals.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster within the payments/PSP regime; touches acquirer and merchant obligations and the operating rules of the national switch.
Relevant to AML/CTF and sanctions screening of cross-border card flows, and to consumer protection on fees and transaction disclosure.

data.theme: Segregation and handling of participant money in debt-based crowdfunding, where platform operators hold subscription and repayment funds that are not their own assets.
how_members_connect: The circular sets the operating condition for pooled client-money accounts, and the finance-value management account is the defined vehicle through which those balances are held and reconciled.
Linkage is definitional and operational: the account construct gives effect to the circular's segregation/no-commingling obligation owed to beneficiaries and lenders.
Both sit downstream of the crowdfunding licensing regime, so scope depends on being a licensed debt-based crowdfunding company.
start_here: Pooled Accounts for Debt-Based Crowdfunding Circular

data.theme: Prudential concentration-risk control for banks: hard limits on exposures to single counterparties and connected groups, plus the measurement inputs (exposure value, eligible capital, CRM, margin for non-cleared derivatives) that make those limits operative.
how_members_connect: A single hierarchy: SAMA's LEX Rules transpose the BCBS April 2014 large exposures framework and sit alongside the Basel risk-based capital framework, which supplies the eligible capital base denominator.

Obligation chain: identify the group of connected counterparties, compute exposure value (including trading book positions and SA-CCR for derivatives), apply recognised credit risk mitigation, then test against maximum exposure limits and report.
Carve-outs and special treatments (central counterparties, covered bonds) and tighter treatment for G-SIB/D-SIB counterparties qualify the general limit.

The non-cleared derivatives margin rules (initial/variation margin, eligible collateral, re-hypothecation limits) reduce and reshape counterparty exposure and share the collateral-eligibility logic used in CRM; CR3 is the disclosure counterpart.

data.theme: The regulatory boundary between banking book and trading book, and the classification and capital consequences that follow for instruments, fund exposures and internal risk transfers.
how_members_connect: Shared defined terms (trading book, banking book, trading desk) drive assignment, with the trading book policy statement and desk definition as the governance evidence for classification.

Classification determines which capital regime applies: market risk minimum capital requirements versus SAMA's minimum capital requirements for credit risk, with CVA attaching to derivative counterparty exposures.
Fund and securitisation exposures are routed through a tiered measurement hierarchy — look-through, then fall-back — depending on data availability.
Internal risk transfer rules are the anti-arbitrage hinge preventing free movement of positions across the boundary.
start_here: Boundary Between Banking Book and Trading Book

data.theme: Licensing and ongoing conduct obligations for debt-based crowdfunding companies, with outsourcing governance as the principal operational-risk control applied to them and to other supervised entities.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy runs from the licensing guidelines into the substantive crowdfunding rules, which define the crowdfunding company and platform and impose risk management and creditworthiness assessment duties.
Outsourcing compliance for crowdfunding entities is an express cross-reference into SAMA's general Rules on Outsourcing rather than a standalone regime.
The outsourcing rules branch by scenario — material outsourcing, foreign bank branches, overseas service providers — each with distinct notification/approval and accountability consequences.
Responsibility is non-delegable: outsourcing does not transfer the licensee's obligations toward beneficiaries or SAMA.
start_here: Rules for Engaging in Debt-Based Crowdfunding
Guidelines for Applying for Debt-Based Crowdfunding Licensing

data.theme: AML/CTF and operational controls governing bank-operated remittance centres and money transfer services, covering customer identification, transfer execution and suspicious activity reporting for cross-border and domestic flows.
how_members_connect: The Guide sits at the top of the hierarchy and pulls in the CDD/KYC obligation set as the entry condition for executing any outbound or inbound remittance.
CDD measures are anchored to FATF standards, so the domestic rules inherit the international risk-based expectations and their interpretation.

The remittance execution chain links settlement infrastructure (SARIE) on the operational side with SAFIU reporting on the AML side — the same transaction triggers both a processing and a reporting obligation.
'Money Transfer Services Providers' scopes who the rules bind; note the distinction between a bank's own remittance centre and a licensed standalone provider when applying the obligations.
start_here: Guide to Rules Governing Banks' Remittance Centers

data.theme: Entry-to-market authorisation for banks in KSA: the minimum criteria an applicant must satisfy to be licensed, plus the incremental conditions imposed on digital-only banking models.
how_members_connect: The core Licensing Guidelines act as the base instrument; capital adequacy, corporate governance and compliance/AML-CTF capability are each cited as mandatory assessment criteria rather than optional considerations.
The guidelines are expressly aligned to the Basel Core Principles, which supplies the supervisory rationale behind the criteria.
The Digital-Only Bank guidelines are additive — they do not displace the general criteria but layer further requirements keyed to the 'Digital-only Bank' definition.
Technology/cybersecurity risk assessment and a credible Exit Plan are the distinguishing digital-only conditions, reflecting heightened operational-resilience and orderly-wind-down concerns.
start_here: Additional Licensing Guidelines for Digital-Only Banks

data.theme: Governance of outsourcing arrangements by finance companies, principally the boundary between functions that may be delegated and those requiring heightened control and SAMA visibility.
how_members_connect: The Rules are the single governing instrument; the other members are its defined terms and required artefacts.
'Material Functions' is the classification trigger — it determines the intensity of the approval, oversight and contractual obligations that attach to an arrangement.
'External Service Provider' fixes the counterparty scope, including whether intra-group and cross-border providers fall in.
A board-approved Outsourcing Policy is the standing compliance obligation that must exist before individual arrangements are entered into.
start_here: Rules on Outsourcing for Finance Companies

data.theme: Operational and cyber resilience expectations for SAMA-supervised entities: running security operations, detecting events, escalating incidents, and managing third-party and cloud dependencies.
how_members_connect: Cyber Security Operations and Technology is the parent domain; SOC capability, event management, incident management and threat management are its component control areas.
There is a clear escalation chain: monitoring/detection (SIEM, SOC) feeds event management, which feeds incident management, which in turn triggers notification obligations to SAMA.
IT Incident Management and Cyber Security Incident Management overlap substantially but are distinct control tracks — do not assume one satisfies the other's requirements.
Outsourcing and Cloud Computing connect the internal control set to external dependencies, where the regulated entity retains accountability toward SAMA regardless of delegation.

data.theme: Saudi instant payment rail infrastructure (Sarie) as a designated payment system, relevant to settlement finality, participant obligations and payment-service scope.
how_members_connect: Single-node cluster: the system itself is the anchor entity rather than a rule family, so linkage runs outward to PSP licensing, operational/fraud controls and consumer protection for instant transfers.
Its regulatory weight derives from the payments regime (system operator/participant duties) rather than from internal cross-references.

data.theme: Consumer protection governance inside supervised entities: the mandated customer care function, complaint handling, quality monitoring and financial awareness, plus the staff competence/certification and Saudization conditions attached to customer-facing roles.
how_members_connect: The Customer Care Department Rules act as the parent instrument and constitute the three sub-units (complaints, quality/performance analysis, awareness and education) as required organisational functions.
The rules are anchored in the High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection, giving a principles-to-rules hierarchy for interpreting ambiguous complaint-handling duties.
Professional certification requirements bind to the same customer-facing roles (credit advisory, retail banking), converting consumer-protection outcomes into individual staff eligibility conditions.
Dual employment restrictions and localisation at exchange centres sit alongside certification as fit-and-proper style workforce controls.
start_here: High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection

data.theme: The baseline duty of supervised entities to track, acknowledge and comply with SAMA circulars as binding instruments, and the official channel through which those circulars are issued.
how_members_connect: A compliance obligation paired with its authoritative source-of-truth channel: the portal fixes what counts as validly issued guidance for compliance purposes.
Cross-cuts every other regime, since circulars amend or supplement regulations across AML, payments, finance companies and consumer protection.

data.theme: Identity verification and authentication controls for remote customer onboarding and ongoing access to digital financial channels, sitting at the intersection of AML/CTF customer identification, cybersecurity/fraud controls and personal data protection.
how_members_connect: Minimum Verification Controls is the hub obligation, referencing channel-specific overlays for e-wallets and lending applications and specifying authentication strength (MFA, OTP).
Remote onboarding via biometric verification is tied to the national digital identity mechanism (Nafath), linking KYC adequacy to a specified trusted identity source.
Processing of biometric and identity attributes triggers personal data protection duties, so verification design choices carry a parallel data-protection consequence.
Registration/onboarding controls chain into OTP requirements, forming an onboarding-then-authentication obligation sequence.

data.theme: Changes to the international accounting standards that SAMA-supervised entities must apply in preparing regulatory and statutory financial statements. The compliance issue is the timing and scope of adoption of amended standards.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the amendment instrument sits at the top of an accounting-reporting obligation chain, feeding prudential returns and audited statements.
Links outward rather than internally — its consequence is felt through reporting, disclosure and supervisory return requirements imposed on licensed entities.
Effective-date and transitional provisions determine which reporting period first triggers the obligation.

data.theme: SAMA's intelligence-led ethical red teaming regime for financial entities: mandated adversarial testing of live production systems, the roles of the parties involved, and the reporting and remediation duties that follow a test.
how_members_connect: The F.E.E.R. framework is the parent instrument; it defines each team role (Red, Blue, White, Green) and the qualification conditions for an external Red Teaming Provider.

Obligation chain runs test → findings → reports: the Red Teaming Provider issues the Red Team Evaluation Report and the defending Blue Team issues the Blue Team Report, both of which feed a mandatory Remediation Plan owned by the White Team.
Shared defined terms (Threat Intelligence, Cyber Kill Chain Methodology) fix the required methodology and scope of the exercise.
Penetration Testing is distinguished from red teaming in scope and intrusiveness — a scope boundary that matters for whether an entity has met the framework's requirement.
start_here: Financial Entities Ethical Red Teaming Framework (F.E.E.R.)

data.theme: Governing principles for cyber threat intelligence capability within supervised financial entities — how intelligence is produced, classified and shared, and at what level it must inform governance decisions.
how_members_connect: Core CTI Principles act as the baseline requirement; Strategic CTI Principles layer board- and risk-governance-level expectations on top of that baseline.
The Intelligence Lifecycle supplies the process definition against which the Core Principles are assessed.
The Traffic Light Protocol is the referenced handling/classification convention, constraining onward disclosure of shared intelligence and interacting with confidentiality duties.

data.theme: The operational tier of the cyber threat intelligence expectations — technical and tactical intelligence requirements applicable to supervised entities' security functions.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster that completes the CTI tiering alongside the core and strategic principle sets; read together with the CTI principles community.
Its requirements are operational in nature but derive their enforceability from the parent cyber threat intelligence framework.
Outputs at this tier feed detection and defensive activity that is separately tested under the ethical red teaming regime.

data.theme: Controls governing how licensed currency exchange businesses may receive inbound money transfers, sitting at the intersection of the money exchange licensing regime and AML/CTF source-of-funds and counterparty due diligence expectations.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the control set stands alone as a conduct requirement addressed to currency exchange licensees rather than to banks or PSPs.

Obligation logic runs from the money exchange licensing/permitted-activities perimeter to specific operational limits on receiving transfers, with AML/CTF customer and counterparty verification as the implicit backstop.
Read together with the broader AML/CTF regime where the transfer originator or correspondent is treated as a customer or counterparty requiring CDD.
start_here: Controls for Receiving Money Transfers for Currency Exchange

data.theme: Disclosure and transparency obligations requiring finance companies to publish financial statements, supporting supervisory oversight and market/consumer visibility of licensee financial condition.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster addressed to finance companies as a licensee class under the finance companies regime.
The obligation chain runs from the finance law and implementing regulation's accounting and audit requirements to the specific publication duty (what, when, and in what form).
Interacts with governance and supervisory reporting duties: published statements are the public-facing element of a wider prudential reporting stack.
start_here: Publication of Finance Company Financial Statements

data.theme: Recognition of government digital credentials (Absher and Tawakkalna) as acceptable identification evidence, bearing directly on customer identification and verification under the AML/CTF and KYC regimes.
how_members_connect: The two instruments are directly cross-referenced: the family record acceptance builds on and extends the earlier acceptance of digital identity from the same platforms.

Both operate as permissions/clarifications layered onto the underlying CDD obligation to identify and verify customers and, where relevant, dependents or related persons using reliable independent source documents.
Shared defined terms: what constitutes a valid identification document, and which government-issued digital artefact is deemed equivalent to a physical original.
Consequence is cross-regime: the same acceptance standard feeds account opening, onboarding for PSPs and finance companies, and consumer-facing identity checks.
start_here: Acceptance of Digital Identity from Absher and Tawakkalna
Acceptance of Family Record from Absher and Tawakkalna

data.theme: Supervisory data and reporting requirements for the finance sector, covering how lenders classify exposures, report interest rates on assets and liabilities, and observe timelines in real estate finance debt transfer.
how_members_connect: Shared reporting taxonomy: the interest rate reporting guidelines rely on ISIC4 as the classification standard for categorising counterparties and exposures, an explicit cross-reference.
Real estate finance debt transfer timelines and rate reporting are conceptually linked through the same underlying credit exposures, which must be consistently identified and reported across returns.
Hierarchy runs from the finance regime's prudential and reporting powers down to guideline-level instructions on classification and submission content.
Practical consequence: misclassification under ISIC4 propagates into rate reporting and into the accuracy of supervisory views on real estate finance portfolios.
start_here: Interest Rates on Assets and Liabilities Reporting Guidelines

data.theme: Governance of departures from model- or rating-driven outputs in credit risk assessment, i.e. when and how a firm may override an assigned internal or external rating and what documentation and control expectations attach to that discretion.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the override concept sits inside the internal ratings-based credit risk regime and depends on the defined terms used for rating assignment and validation.
Legally it operates as a conditional permission plus an evidentiary burden - the exercise of judgement must be justified, recorded and subject to independent review.
Interacts upward with governance/risk expectations (board and risk function oversight of rating systems) and downward with capital calculation outcomes.

data.theme: Forward-looking assessment of capital sufficiency: the requirement that a bank test its capital ratios against adverse but plausible scenarios rather than relying on point-in-time adequacy.
how_members_connect: Standalone node linking the capital adequacy regime to the supervisory review / ICAAP obligation chain.
Obligation is continuous and internal-governance anchored: board and senior management must own scenario design, severity and the management actions assumed.
Outputs feed supervisory dialogue and can drive capital planning, buffer usage and distribution decisions.

data.theme: Timing rules that phase new prudential requirements in over a defined period, governing what applies to a firm at a given date and how legacy positions are treated during the run-in.
how_members_connect: Single node that functions as a temporal scope limit across otherwise separate capital and liquidity requirements.
Legal effect is to modify, not remove, the underlying obligation - compliance must be measured against the schedule applicable on the relevant reporting date.
Typically set out in the parent framework and refined by subsequent circulars, so hierarchy and effective dates must be read together.

data.theme: Capital treatment of securitisation exposures under the external ratings-based approach, including the preferential risk weights available where a transaction meets the simple, transparent and comparable criteria.
how_members_connect: Standalone node dependent on defined terms: securitisation exposure, tranche seniority, external rating and STC eligibility.
Eligibility is conditional - the concessional weights apply only where the qualifying criteria and due diligence obligations are satisfied, otherwise the general hierarchy of approaches applies.
Cross-references the broader credit risk and external credit assessment institution recognition rules.

data.theme: Accessibility obligation on supervised entities to ensure persons with disabilities can be safely evacuated from premises in an emergency, sitting at the intersection of consumer protection/fair treatment and operational safety duties.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone accessibility requirement not yet cross-linked to the broader consumer protection or business continuity nodes in the graph.
Reads as a service-accessibility duty owed to customers and visitors on the entity's premises, rather than a prudential or conduct-of-sale rule.
Practical linkage points for a researcher are the consumer protection principles (fair treatment, accessibility of banking services) and operational/BCM requirements.
start_here: Emergency Evacuation for Persons with Disabilities

data.theme: Licensing and ongoing conduct regime for money changers in KSA, covering who may carry on money changing business and the AML/CTF controls that attach to that licence.
how_members_connect: The Rules Regulating Money Changing Business act as the parent instrument, cross-referring both to the licensing conditions and to the AML/CTF obligations.
Licensing is a gateway control: authorisation conditions are the hook through which AML/CTF and supervisory requirements become enforceable on the money changer.

Cross-regime interaction: money changers are DNFBP-adjacent financial institutions, so the AML/CTF Law and Implementing Regulations apply in parallel with these sectoral rules (CDD, record keeping, STR reporting, TFS screening).

data.theme: The Basel-aligned securitisation capital framework as adopted by SAMA: how banks recognise risk transference, classify exposures, choose a capital treatment, and meet due diligence, STC and disclosure obligations.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy of instruments: the general provisions and defined terms (traditional/synthetic securitisation, SPE, resecuritisation, sponsor, ABCP conduit, clean-up call) feed the operational recognition-of-risk-transference tests, which gate any capital relief.

Obligation chain on calculation: due diligence requirements are a precondition to using the approach hierarchy (SEC-IRBA, SEC-ERBA, SEC-IAA, SEC-SA), with shared inputs (KIRB, attachment/detachment points, supervisory parameter p) and caps/floors.
External rating dependency: SEC-ERBA, inferred ratings and the IAA all rely on ECAI eligibility and mapping, linking this cluster to the standardized credit risk cluster.

Special regimes branch off the core: STC term and short-term (ABCP) criteria give preferential treatment, while non-performing loan securitisations and dilution risk carry bespoke rules; Pillar 3 templates SEC1 and SEC3 close the loop as disclosure obligations.

data.theme: Standardized approach mechanics for credit risk: how banks may use external ratings to risk-weight exposures (notably corporates) and the conditions for recognising credit risk mitigation such as on-balance sheet netting.
how_members_connect: Shared gatekeeping definition: eligible ECAIs and the supervisory mapping of their assessments to risk weights condition every rating-based determination in the cluster.

Rule chain on rating use: eligibility feeds the multiple-ratings rule, the issue-specific vs issuer rating rule, and the short-term/long-term rating interaction, which then drive the corporate exposure risk weights.

CRM provisions cross-refer to the same rating rules when determining the treatment of collateral, guarantees and protection providers, and set operational conditions (legal enforceability, netting agreements) for capital recognition.
Corporate exposure nodes sit downstream as the main application case, including unrated/general corporate treatment where external ratings are unavailable.
start_here: Standardized Approach: Use of External Rating

data.theme: Market risk capital measurement under the simplified/standardised regime: how a bank computes charges for interest rate, equity, FX and commodity exposures, including the specific treatments available for option positions.
how_members_connect: A single scope gateway (the Simplified Standardised Approach) determines eligibility and then routes the bank into the four risk-class charges, which explains the hub-and-spoke reference pattern.
Shared defined terms — general market risk, delta, maturity ladder — carry across risk classes, so the ladder and delta concepts are reused rather than redefined for each exposure type.

The three option methods form a tiered obligation chain by complexity of the book: simplified for purchased-option-only profiles, delta-plus for written positions, scenario for more complex portfolios; choosing one constrains the rest of the calculation.

Hierarchy runs from the framework's scope provisions down to risk-class calculation rules and then to method-level annex detail; the SSA-prefixed members are the scoped-down variants of the general risk-class rules.

data.theme: Bucketing and correlation parameters for commodity exposures used to aggregate risk-class sensitivities into a capital charge.
how_members_connect: Isolated parameter node: it supplies the calibration inputs relied on by the commodity risk calculation rather than imposing a standalone obligation.
Meaning depends entirely on the upstream commodity risk provisions that define which exposures fall into which bucket.

data.theme: Bucketing and correlation parameters for foreign exchange exposures feeding the FX component of the market risk capital charge.
how_members_connect: Standalone calibration node whose legal effect arises only when applied through the FX risk charge provisions.
Parallel in structure and function to the commodity bucket parameters, so the two should be read as companion annex-level tables.
start_here: Foreign Exchange Risk Buckets and Correlations

data.theme: The test for whether a risk factor may be treated as modellable, which determines if it can sit inside an internal model or must be capitalised separately as non-modellable.
how_members_connect: Gatekeeping provision: it conditions the availability of internal-model treatment, so it is logically prior to model-based capital rules even though it appears unlinked here.
Currently isolated in the graph — researchers should read it against the internal models and standardised fallback provisions to see the consequence of failing the test.

data.theme: Classification and capital treatment of specialised lending — exposures whose repayment depends primarily on the income generated by a specific asset or project rather than the general capacity of a broader obligor. It sets the boundary between sub-classes and the supervisory slotting fallback where banks cannot estimate own risk components.
how_members_connect: A single defined asset class (specialised lending) is subdivided into named sub-classes — project, object, commodities, income-producing real estate and the higher-risk HVCRE category — each definition gating a different risk-weight outcome.

The slotting approach operates as the conditional alternative within the IRB hierarchy: where PD/LGD estimation requirements are not met, supervisory categories map directly to risk weights and to expected loss amounts.
HVCRE is carved out of, and treated more conservatively than, ordinary income-producing real estate, so the definitional test determines the capital consequence.
Expected loss links this cluster to the wider IRB provisioning treatment rather than being a standalone concept.

data.theme: Definition and segmentation of retail credit exposures for capital purposes, including the boundary between retail and corporate/MSME treatment and the identification of lower-risk revolving borrowers.
how_members_connect: All members hang off a single eligibility definition: whether an exposure qualifies as retail determines which risk-weight regime (standardised regulatory retail or IRB retail) applies.
Sub-categorisation chains downward — retail class into regulatory retail, qualifying revolving retail, and MSME exposures treated as corporate where thresholds are exceeded.
The transactor concept operates as a carve-out inside the revolving sub-class, reducing the applicable weighting for borrowers who settle in full.
The currency mismatch multiplier is an add-on applied to retail exposures, so it depends on the class definition being settled first.

data.theme: The core mechanics of the internal ratings-based approach to credit risk capital: the risk components banks estimate, how those feed the supervisory risk-weight functions, and the split between foundation and advanced permissions.
how_members_connect: A common input set (PD, LGD, EAD, maturity) is shared by every member; the risk-weight functions consume those inputs, so definitional changes to a component propagate through the whole capital calculation.
Foundation versus advanced IRB is a permissions hierarchy over the same components — which parameters a bank may estimate itself versus take from supervisory values.
Expected loss and provisions treatment closes the loop, linking the same parameters to the capital deduction/add-back mechanism.
Adjustments such as the MSME firm-size factor sit as modifiers on the function rather than as separate regimes; the market risk framework is referenced for exposure measurement overlap.

data.theme: The qualifying conditions a bank must satisfy before SAMA will permit use of the IRB approach — rating system design and operation, governance, data, parameter estimation, collateral recognition, validation and Pillar 3 disclosure.
how_members_connect: Everything is subordinate to a single gateway obligation: the minimum requirements that condition supervisory permission to use internal estimates for regulatory capital.
Obligation chain from definitions outward — the default and economic loss definitions anchor PD, LGD and EAD estimation, which in turn depend on data maintenance and validation duties.

Governance layer (board and senior management oversight, an independent credit risk control unit, internal and external audit, the use test) is the control counterpart to the quantification requirements.

Credit risk mitigation members (real estate, receivables, other physical collateral, leasing and residual value) qualify only where the recognition conditions are met, otherwise supervisory LGD/EAD values apply; SAMA's Basel III guidance circular sits above these as the local implementing instrument.
start_here: SAMA Guidance Document on Basel III (Circular 341000015689)

data.theme: Credit risk mitigation (CRM) for banking-book and counterparty exposures: when collateral, netting, guarantees and credit derivatives may reduce regulatory exposure, and the haircuts, eligibility and maturity conditions attached to that recognition.
how_members_connect: A single eligibility gate feeds everything: eligible financial collateral and eligible protection providers determine whether the simple or comprehensive approach, or substitution via guarantee/credit derivative, may be applied.

Collateralized transactions act as the hub node, branching to the two alternative computation routes (simple vs comprehensive with supervisory haircuts) and to the netting treatment for securities financing transactions.

Cross-cutting conditions override both routes: maturity mismatch rules and the CCR framework constrain recognition regardless of which technique is used; off-balance-sheet and credit derivative items are pulled in as exposures needing mitigation treatment.
Sovereign guarantees and counter-guarantees sit as a preferential carve-out within the general guarantee rules, so the general rule must be read before the exception.

data.theme: Basel III post-crisis measurement of counterparty credit exposure and leverage: SA-CCR and the Internal Models Method for deriving EAD on derivatives and SFTs, capital for exposures to central counterparties, and the leverage ratio exposure measure.
how_members_connect: SA-CCR is the computational spine: EAD is built from replacement cost plus the PFE add-on, which in turn depends on netting sets, hedging sets, effective notional, supervisory delta, supervisory factors, maturity factor and the PFE multiplier.
IMM is the alternative permission-based route, conditioned on model validation, stress testing, margin period of risk, alpha multiplier and wrong-way risk (including specific WWR) controls.

CCP exposure capital reuses the same EAD outputs: trade exposures and default fund exposures to a qualifying CCP are calculated from KCCP and clearing-member contributions, so SA-CCR must be settled first.

The leverage ratio framework consumes these measures as inputs — derivative exposures, SFT exposures, off-balance-sheet items with credit conversion factors, written credit derivatives and cash variation margin — against the Tier 1 capital measure; the Basel III finalisation document is the parent instrument for all of it.

data.theme: Internal Ratings-Based approach to credit risk: how exposures are classified into asset classes and how risk-weighted assets are derived under the foundation versus advanced variants, including the special case of purchased receivables.
how_members_connect: The IRB overview node is the definitional parent: corporate, sovereign and bank exposure definitions determine which risk-weight function and parameter regime applies.
Choice of F-IRB versus A-IRB governs which parameters a bank may estimate itself, and both routes feed the same default-risk RWA calculation.
Purchased receivables form a nested regime that inherits the asset-class definitions but adds a separate dilution-risk capital charge alongside default risk.
Recognition of credit risk mitigants is the cross-reference out of this cluster into the CRM/collateral rules, so eligibility conditions are resolved elsewhere.
start_here: IRB Approach: Overview and Asset Class Definitions
IRB Approach: RWA for Purchased Receivables

data.theme: Specialized lending as a distinct sub-class of corporate exposure, where repayment depends primarily on the cash flows of the financed asset or project rather than the borrower's broader capacity, and where supervisory slotting may substitute for internal estimates.
how_members_connect: Specialized lending is the parent definition; project, object, commodities finance and income-producing real estate are its enumerated sub-categories, each with its own qualifying characteristics.

The supervisory slotting criteria approach applies across all four sub-categories, mapping each to supervisory categories and prescribed risk weights where a bank cannot meet the estimation requirements of the general corporate IRB treatment.
The cluster is hierarchically subordinate to the IRB asset-class definitions: classification as specialized lending is a carve-out from the general corporate exposure class.

data.theme: Capital treatment of transactions that have not settled on the agreed date, distinguishing delivery-versus-payment (and payment-versus-payment) settlement from free-delivery exposures. The problem-space is how long a trade remains unsettled and what capital charge attaches from the contractual settlement date onward.
how_members_connect: All members turn on the same defined settlement mechanism (simultaneous exchange of delivery and payment), which is the gateway condition for the lighter unsettled-transaction treatment.
The capital-treatment provision is the parent obligation; the DvP entries supply the definitional scope it cross-references.
Duplicate DvP labels indicate the same defined term surfacing in more than one part of the framework, so scope should be read consistently across both.
Linkage is definition-to-charge: failure to meet the DvP condition shifts the exposure into a different, more punitive capital category.
start_here: Capital Treatment of Unsettled Transactions and Failed Trades

data.theme: The default-risk and residual-risk components of the standardised market risk framework: capturing jump-to-default loss in trading book positions and adding capital for risks not captured by delta, vega or curvature charges.
how_members_connect: The Standardised Approach is the hierarchical parent; the default risk capital requirement and the residual risk add-on are its mandated components alongside the sensitivities-based method.

The DRC charge decomposes by portfolio type — non-securitisations, securitisations, and the correlation trading portfolio — each applying the same jump-to-default gross/net and hedge benefit ratio mechanics with different bucketing.

Shared defined terms (jump-to-default exposure, hedge benefit ratio, securitisation exposure, correlation trading portfolio) create the cross-references; the CTP definition in particular determines which DRC sub-regime applies.
Specific risk and credit derivative offsetting rules supply the legacy/offsetting logic that constrains how hedges may reduce the default charge.

data.theme: The sensitivities-based component of the standardised market risk capital charge, which aggregates delta, vega and curvature sensitivities across prescribed risk classes using regulator-set risk weights and correlations.
how_members_connect: The sensitivities-based method is the umbrella obligation; delta, vega and curvature are the three mandatory risk measures it requires to be computed and summed.

Each risk class (general interest rate, credit spread, FX, equity) applies the same three-measure structure but with its own bucket, risk-weight and correlation tables — a parallel obligation pattern rather than a hierarchy.
Correct classification of an instrument into a risk class and bucket is the shared definitional pivot: it determines weights, correlations and therefore the charge.
Curvature and vega are linked because both attach only to instruments with optionality, narrowing their scope relative to delta.

data.theme: The internal models approach to market risk capital: the conditions on which a bank may use its own models, the expected-shortfall based capital calculation, and the ongoing model-performance tests (backtesting, P&L attribution, risk factor modellability) that determine continued eligibility.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy runs from the Basel Framework and the IMA general provisions down to detailed model requirements, then to the quantitative tests and the capital aggregation formula.

Eligibility is conditional and revocable: the risk factor eligibility test splits factors into modellable (capitalised via IMCC/expected shortfall) and non-modellable (capitalised via the stress scenario/stressed ES add-on), while backtesting zones and the PLA test can push a desk back to the standardised approach.
The P&L definitions (risk-theoretical, hypothetical, actual) and the test metrics (Spearman correlation, Kolmogorov-Smirnov) are shared defined inputs feeding both backtesting and PLA outcomes.

Several labels appear in near-duplicate form (expected shortfall, PLA test, backtesting zones, IMCC, SES), reflecting the same concepts stated in general provisions and again in the detailed calculation rules — read them as one obligation chain, not separate requirements.
Liquidity horizons and the IMA default risk model are scope parameters that determine how the expected shortfall and total IMA capital requirement are built up and aggregated.

data.theme: Pillar 1 minimum capital for operational risk under SAMA's adoption of the Basel III post-crisis reforms, i.e. how a bank must compute its operational risk capital charge and report it.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy: SAMA's operational risk capital rules implement the Basel III post-crisis reform standard, then cascade into the prescribed calculation method and reporting template.
Obligation chain within the calculation: Business Indicator feeds the Business Indicator Component, which combines with the Internal Loss Multiplier to produce Operational Risk Capital.
Scope of Application fixes which entities and consolidation levels the Standardised Approach binds; the Simplified Alternative is a carve-out/derogation from that default method.
The Q17 template is the supervisory reporting consequence of the same defined inputs, so definitions must be read consistently across calculation and reporting.
start_here: Minimum Capital Requirements for Operational Risk

data.theme: The loss-data component of the operational risk capital charge: what qualifies as an operational loss, how it must be identified, collected, classified and treated over the required observation history.
how_members_connect: The Loss Component is the quantitative output that depends on a compliant Operational Loss Data Set, creating a direct data-quality-to-capital linkage.
Loss Data Identification/Collection/Treatment sets the eligibility, thresholds and treatment rules that govern what may enter the data set.
Loss Event Type Classification and its detailed breakdown provide the shared taxonomy used for both data collection and supervisory disclosure.
Feeds upward into the Internal Loss Multiplier and therefore into Operational Risk Capital (see the operational risk capital cluster).

data.theme: Capital treatment of counterparty credit risk on derivatives and securities financing transactions, including exposure measurement, netting and collateral haircut requirements.
how_members_connect: CCR sits as a sub-regime of the credit risk capital rules, so the CCR/CVA requirements are read as an extension of and cross-reference to the credit risk framework.
Exposure measurement chain: Effective EPE modelling, its stress calibration, and cross-product netting determine the exposure amount on derivatives and SFTs.
SFTs are the shared defined term linking netting rules, minimum haircut floors and trading-book CCR treatment.
Template CCR5 is the disclosure consequence of the SFT collateral rules, tying calculation obligations to reporting obligations.
start_here: Minimum Capital Requirements for CCR and CVA

data.theme: The aggregation layer of Pillar 1: CVA capital methodologies, total RWA build-up across credit, market, operational and CCR risk, the output floor constraint on internally modelled RWA, and the Pillar 3 disclosure templates that evidence all of it.
how_members_connect: Methodology hierarchy: the CVA framework branches into BA-CVA (reduced and full versions) and SA-CVA, with stand-alone CVA capital, eligible hedges, regulatory CVA and supervisory risk weights as shared defined inputs.
RWA for credit, market and operational risk are sourced from the respective SAMA minimum capital rulebooks (SCRE, SCCR, SMAR, SOPE) and then aggregated for the output floor calculation.
The output floor operates as a binding constraint on modelled approaches, which is why the CMS templates compare modelled against standardised RWA.
The CR, CCR, MR, CVA and OV templates and CRB tables are the disclosure obligations that mirror the underlying calculation rules; defined terms must align between calculation and template.
Central clearing exposures (clearing member capital requirement, CCP hypothetical capital) attach to the same CCR/credit risk chain covered by the counterparty credit risk cluster.

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of counterparty credit risk (CCR) exposure measurement, specifically the breakdown of CCR exposures by the calculation approach used (e.g. SA-CCR, IMM) and the resulting EAD and RWA. It frames the entry point for how a bank evidences its chosen CCR methodology to SAMA and the market.
how_members_connect: Single-member community: the template functions as the summary layer from which the other CCR templates disaggregate exposures by approach, counterparty rating, collateral and CCP type.
Its scope depends on the CCR definitions and approach eligibility set in the underlying capital adequacy framework; the template imposes a disclosure obligation, not a measurement rule.
Completion obligations are periodic and formatted, so scope limits (which products and netting sets fall within CCR) must be read from the framework rather than the template itself.
start_here: Template CCR1: Analysis of CCR Exposures by Approach

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of CCR exposures under the standardised approach and of exposures to central counterparties, covering risk-weight and counterparty-type breakdowns and the qualifying/non-qualifying CCP distinction.
how_members_connect: The two templates are cross-referenced: CCP-related exposures disclosed in CCR8 are carved out of, or reconciled against, the standardised-approach exposures reported in CCR3.
Both rely on the same defined terms for exposure at default, netting set and risk weight drawn from the capital adequacy framework.
Together they form an obligation chain from measurement rules in the framework down to a fixed-format periodic disclosure to SAMA and the market.
start_here: Template CCR8: Exposures to Central Counterparties

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of CCR exposures for banks using internal ratings-based approaches, presented by PD band with associated LGD, maturity, EAD and RWA density.
how_members_connect: Single-member community whose use is conditional on SAMA approval to apply IRB; it is the IRB counterpart to the standardised-approach CCR disclosure.
Definitions of PD, LGD and EAD are inherited from the credit risk framework, so the template cannot be read independently of the IRB parameter rules.
It disaggregates the approach-level totals reported in the summary CCR exposure template.
start_here: Template CCR4: IRB CCR Exposures by PD Scale

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of collateral used to mitigate counterparty credit risk, split between collateral for derivative transactions and for securities financing transactions, and between segregated and unsegregated, received and posted.
how_members_connect: Single-member community that supports the exposure templates by evidencing the credit risk mitigation assumed in the reported EAD figures.
Relies on collateral eligibility, haircut and segregation concepts defined in the capital adequacy and CRM rules; the template only prescribes presentation.
Segregation categories interact with the CCP disclosure regime, since client collateral treatment differs for cleared exposures.
start_here: Template CCR5: Composition of Collateral for CCR

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of counterparty credit risk arising from credit derivative positions, covering protection bought and sold and the resulting exposures that must be reported to the market.
how_members_connect: Single-template cluster: the counterparty credit risk (CCR) disclosure series, sitting at the template layer beneath the Pillar 3 disclosure framework and the underlying CCR capital treatment rules.
Relies on defined terms shared across the CCR templates (notional amounts, protection bought/sold, netting) rather than on cross-references to other clusters.
Obligation chain runs from the disclosure requirement (who must publish, at what frequency and format) to the fixed template content, which banks may not vary.

data.theme: Qualitative narrative disclosure on a bank's securitisation activity - roles undertaken (originator, sponsor, investor, servicer), objectives, risk retention and accounting treatment.
how_members_connect: Acts as the qualitative anchor for the securitisation disclosure family: the narrative table that gives context to the quantitative securitisation templates.
Shares the securitisation defined-term set (originator/sponsor/investor, banking book vs trading book, resecuritisation) with the SEC quantitative templates.
Hierarchy: Pillar 3 disclosure requirements set the obligation; this table prescribes the minimum narrative content and management judgement to be explained.

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of securitisation exposures held in the trading book, broken down by bank role and exposure type.
how_members_connect: Part of the SEC quantitative template series; the trading-book counterpart to the banking-book templates, split by where the exposure is booked.
Depends on the same securitisation definitions and role classifications set out in the qualitative securitisation table.
