Content is fixed-format: the disclosure obligation is satisfied only by completing the prescribed rows and columns.
start_here: Template SEC2: Securitisation Exposures Trading Book

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of banking-book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as investor, together with the associated capital requirements.
how_members_connect: Sits in the SEC quantitative series alongside the trading-book template, distinguished by book (banking book) and by the bank's role (investor rather than originator/sponsor).
Uses the role and exposure definitions established in the qualitative securitisation table, and links exposure amounts to the securitisation capital treatment.
Hierarchy: disclosure framework obligation to the specific template; figures disclosed must reconcile with the capital requirements calculated under the securitisation rules.
start_here: Template SEC4: Securitisation Banking Book Investor

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure of a bank's market risk profile — the narrative explanation of market risk strategy, governance and measurement that must accompany the quantitative market risk templates.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a qualitative disclosure table within the market risk section of the Pillar 3 disclosure regime.
Sits in the hierarchy Basel framework as adopted by SAMA → disclosure rules → prescribed table format, so the obligation is to populate the table in the prescribed form and frequency.
Paired in obligation terms with the quantitative market risk templates (standardised and internal models), which it contextualises for users of the disclosures.
Defined terms (market risk, trading book, risk measurement approach) are inherited from the capital adequacy rules, not redefined in the table.
start_here: Table MRA: Market Risk Qualitative Disclosure

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure specific to banks permitted to use the internal models approach (IMA) for market risk capital, covering model scope, validation and supervisory approval.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a qualitative table that applies only to banks with supervisory permission to use internal models, so its scope is narrower than the general market risk disclosure.
Conditional obligation chain: model approval under the capital adequacy/market risk rules triggers the enhanced disclosure duty in this table.
Cross-references the general market risk qualitative disclosure, which it supplements rather than replaces.
Relies on defined terms for model scope and validation drawn from the market risk capital requirements.

data.theme: Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure of market risk capital requirements calculated under the simplified standardised approach, for banks not using internal models.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a fixed-format quantitative template reporting capital charges by risk class.
Scope is mutually exclusive with the internal models disclosures — applicability turns on which calculation approach the bank is permitted to use.
Figures must reconcile to the market risk capital requirement computed under the capital adequacy rules; the template does not create the calculation, only the disclosure duty.
Read alongside the market risk qualitative table, which explains the approach behind the reported numbers.
start_here: Template MR3: Market Risk Simplified Standardised Approach

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure of credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk — how a bank identifies, measures and manages counterparty credit valuation risk and which CVA approach it applies.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a qualitative table in the CVA section of the Pillar 3 disclosure framework.
Depends on CVA and counterparty credit risk definitions set in the capital adequacy rules; the table imposes a disclosure duty only.
Interacts with counterparty credit risk and market risk disclosures, since CVA capital treatment and hedging sit across both regimes.
Hierarchy: Basel standard as adopted by SAMA → disclosure requirements → prescribed table format and frequency.

data.theme: Pillar 3 market-disclosure obligations for banks in KSA: the fixed-format templates and tables through which regulatory capital, leverage, RWA, TLAC and valuation positions must be published, plus the frequency and timing rules governing them.
how_members_connect: A hierarchy runs from the Basel III framework and the FSB TLAC term sheet, through SAMA's SACAP capital-reforms guidance and the SCRE credit-risk rules, down to the Pillar 3 framework that mandates each named template.
The framework document is the hub: it cross-references every KM/CC/CCA/TLAC/LI/PV/LR/CCyB/CR/CCR/SEC template, so disclosure obligations are defined by reference rather than restated.

Templates chain to each other through shared measurement inputs - key metrics draw on the capital-composition template, TLAC and capital-distribution templates draw on the same regulatory capital definitions, and the LI/PV reconciliations link accounting balances to regulatory exposure amounts.
Counterparty concepts (CCP, qualifying CCP, default fund contributions) and the disclosure FAQ supply the defined terms and interpretive gloss applied across the credit and counterparty templates.
start_here: SACAP - Basel III Capital Reforms Guidance

data.theme: Disclosure of encumbered versus unencumbered assets, relevant to assessing how much of a bank's balance sheet is available to unsecured creditors.
how_members_connect: Single isolated template; it operates as a standalone Pillar 3 disclosure item with no internal cross-references captured here.
Read alongside the main Pillar 3 disclosure framework, which sets the mandate, format and timing for this template.

data.theme: Internal ratings-based (IRB) credit risk disclosure and the underlying IRB treatment of corporate, specialised-lending and equity exposures, including model validation evidence.
how_members_connect: The IRB approach rules sit above the exposure-class provisions (corporate, equity) and are the substantive source the CR6, CR9 and CR10 templates report against.
PD backtesting disclosure is tied to the exposure template, linking model outputs to reported risk parameters - a validation obligation chain, not just a reporting one.
Equity-exposure treatment and subordinated debt/capital-instrument treatment share definitional boundaries, which determines which template and risk-weight regime applies.
Slotting disclosure applies where IRB parameter estimation is not permitted, so template choice follows the approach-eligibility rules.
start_here: Template CR6: IRB Credit Risk Exposures
Template CR9: IRB Backtesting of PD

data.theme: Qualitative narrative disclosure on counterparty credit risk - risk management objectives, policies, limits and collateral/CVA practices - as distinct from the quantitative CCR templates.
how_members_connect: Standalone table with no internal links captured; its legal force derives from the Pillar 3 disclosure framework that mandates it.
Conceptually paired with the quantitative CCR templates and the CCP/QCCP definitions used in the capital-disclosure cluster.

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure of the standardised approach to credit valuation adjustment (SA-CVA) risk, covering how a bank explains its CVA risk governance, scope and methodology rather than numeric outcomes.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a disclosure table sitting in the market/counterparty credit risk branch of the Pillar 3 hierarchy (capital framework rules -> disclosure requirements -> prescribed table).

Its content depends on defined terms and eligibility conditions for SA-CVA use set out in the minimum capital requirements for CVA risk; the table is the reporting consequence of that approval-based regime.
Qualitative narrative is meant to be read alongside the quantitative CVA disclosures, so completeness is assessed against the underlying capital computation obligations.

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure of a bank's operational risk framework — how operational risk is defined, governed, measured and mitigated for capital purposes.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster acting as the narrative anchor for the operational risk disclosure set; the quantitative operational risk templates are the numeric counterpart.
Relies on the operational risk definitions and Business Indicator concepts established in the operational risk capital requirements, so scope limits there flow through to what must be disclosed.
Sits at the table (qualitative) level of the law -> capital rules -> disclosure requirement chain.

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 operational risk disclosures: the loss history, the Business Indicator and its components, and the resulting minimum operational risk capital requirement.
how_members_connect: Obligation chain: historical loss data (OR1) and the Business Indicator with its subcomponents (OR2) are the two inputs that feed the capital figure disclosed in OR3.
Both OR1 and OR2 are cross-referenced by OR3, making OR3 the reconciliation point where the standardised operational risk calculation is evidenced.

All three share the defined terms (Business Indicator, loss component, internal loss multiplier) fixed in the operational risk capital rules; a change in scope or bucket thresholds there changes all three templates.
Read together with the qualitative operational risk framework table, which explains the governance behind these numbers.
start_here: Template OR3: Minimum Required Operational Risk Capital
Template OR2: Business Indicator and Subcomponents

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure on interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB): how a bank identifies, measures, monitors and controls IRRBB, including modelling and behavioural assumptions.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster in the banking-book risk branch of the disclosure hierarchy; it narrates the assumptions underlying the quantitative IRRBB measures.

Depends on the IRRBB standards' defined terms (economic value of equity, net interest income, interest rate shock scenarios) and on the governance and risk-appetite obligations imposed on the board and senior management.
Cross-regime link: the disclosure duty is a transparency consequence of the underlying Pillar 2 / supervisory review expectations on interest rate risk management.

data.theme: Liquidity risk reporting under the Basel-based prudential regime: the standardised return by which banks evidence that stable funding sources cover the funding requirements of their assets and off-balance-sheet exposures.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a reporting template that operationalises the NSFR standard rather than creating substantive obligations of its own.
Legally dependent on the underlying NSFR rules (available vs required stable funding factors and category definitions), which supply the meaning of each template line.
Sits in the hierarchy as supervisory reporting instrumentation beneath the liquidity framework; breaches are assessed against the ratio rules, not the form.
start_here: Template LIQ2: Net Stable Funding Ratio

data.theme: Licensing and authorisation administration for finance companies: the fees payable to SAMA in connection with registration/licensing under the finance companies regime.
how_members_connect: Standalone circular acting as an implementing instrument under the Finance Companies Control Law and its implementing regulation.
Relevance is conditional on entity classification as a licensed finance company, so scope turns on definitions in the finance regime rather than on payments or banking rules.
Compliance consequence is administrative (fee payment as a condition of registration), distinct from prudential or conduct obligations.
start_here: SAMA Circular: Registration Fees in Finance Companies

data.theme: Credit risk capital treatment of real estate exposures under the standardised approach: how an exposure is classified as real estate, when it qualifies as regulatory real estate, and how risk weights follow from collateral value and borrower repayment source.
how_members_connect: Hierarchy of defined terms: the real estate exposure class is the parent category, with regulatory real estate, land/ADC exposures and defaulted exposures as mutually exclusive sub-classifications carrying different risk weights.
Qualification as regulatory real estate is the gateway condition for the LTV-based treatment; failing the criteria pushes the exposure into harsher buckets.
LTV is the shared measurement input feeding both the whole loan approach and the loan splitting approach, which are alternative methods for converting the same ratio into risk weights.
Default status overrides the ordinary regulatory real estate treatment, creating a cross-reference chain from classification to defaulted exposure rules.

data.theme: Specialised lending under the credit risk framework: supervisory slotting categories used to assign risk weights to object finance exposures where repayment depends on cash flows generated by the financed asset.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster providing the supervisory grade scale (strong through default) for one specialised lending sub-type.
Depends on the upstream definition of specialised lending and object finance to determine which exposures are in scope.
Functions as a mapping table between qualitative supervisory assessment and prescribed risk weights, rather than an independent obligation.

data.theme: Capital adequacy treatment of specialised lending: assigning supervisory slotting grades to commodities finance exposures where a bank cannot rely on internal PD estimates.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster sitting within the credit risk / IRB framework, where slotting criteria drive risk-weight assignment.
Depends on upstream definitions of specialised lending sub-classes and the supervisory grade scale (strong through default) used across the slotting family.

data.theme: Timing and phase-in of a regulatory regime: how existing positions, approvals or exposures are treated between the old and new rulebook.
how_members_connect: Standalone provision that qualifies the effective date of the substantive obligations it accompanies, so it must be read against the parent framework rather than alone.
Legal effect is temporal scoping — grandfathering and cut-off dates — rather than creating new substantive duties.

data.theme: SAMA-mandated use of the Qawaem program for financial statement submission/verification by supervised entities, i.e. a reporting and disclosure compliance obligation.
how_members_connect: Circular-level instrument issued under SAMA's supervisory authority; the obligation flows from regulator to the addressed institutions.
The SAMA node anchors the hierarchy (enabling law → SAMA supervisory power → circular) and identifies the recipient of the resulting submissions.
start_here: Circular on Mandatory Use of Qawaem Program

data.theme: Acceptance of ownership documentation issued by the Economic Cities Authority for property-related transactions, relevant to collateral, title verification and customer documentation.
how_members_connect: Single circular that broadens the set of legally acceptable title evidence, so it operates as an amendment to documentation requirements in lending and real estate finance practice.
Cross-reads to KYC/documentation and collateral-perfection expectations, since acceptability of the document determines whether security can be relied on.
start_here: Circular on Adopting Ownership Document from Economic Cities Authority

data.theme: Control over changes to the configuration of IT assets, addressing the governance/risk regime's requirement that system settings are authorised, documented and traceable rather than altered ad hoc.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the configuration management control stands alone but sits downstream of the IT governance framework's control objectives.
Legally relevant as an operational-risk control whose failure is evidenced in audit and incident reporting to SAMA.

data.theme: The governance body accountable for IT strategy, prioritisation and oversight within a supervised entity, and the board-delegated mandate that makes IT decisions attributable to named accountable persons.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the committee is the accountability node to which IT governance obligations (strategy approval, resource allocation, escalation) attach.
Connects upward to board responsibility and downward to individual IT control requirements in the same framework.

data.theme: Defined terminology for the IT governance regime, which fixes the scope and meaning of the obligations imposed on supervised entities.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster acting as the definitional layer: terms defined here govern how the framework's control and committee requirements are read.
Cross-regime relevance where the same terms recur in cyber-security, outsourcing and business continuity requirements; definitions should not be borrowed across regimes without checking scope.

data.theme: Sharing of credit information between entities, covering permissible disclosure, consumer consent and the limits on use of credit data under the credit information regime.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a circular-level instrument that operationalises the credit information law and its implementing regulation.
Interacts with consumer protection (consent, accuracy, correction rights) and with CDD/KYC use of credit bureau data, where reliance limits must be observed.

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB), requiring banks to publish standardised quantitative measures of economic value and earnings sensitivity under prescribed interest rate shock scenarios.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a fixed-format disclosure template rather than a rule text, so its obligation content is derivative of the IRRBB standard and the Pillar 3 disclosure requirements that mandate its publication.

Depends on definitions and measurement conventions (banking book scope, shock scenarios, economic value and net interest income metrics) set in the underlying IRRBB framework, not in the template itself.
Sits at the bottom of the hierarchy: prudential standard -> disclosure framework -> template, with frequency, scope of application and format fixed by the parent disclosure rules.
start_here: Template IRRBB1: Quantitative Information on IRRBB

data.theme: Disclosure of the indicators used to assess global systemic importance of banks, feeding the G-SIB identification and higher loss-absorbency assessment methodology.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a reporting/disclosure template whose legal force comes from the systemic-importance assessment framework and the Pillar 3 disclosure obligation that requires its publication.
Indicator definitions (size, interconnectedness, substitutability, complexity, cross-jurisdictional activity) are imported from the G-SIB methodology; the template adds no substantive definitions.
Scope limit worth flagging: applicability depends on the size/activity thresholds that trigger indicator reporting, so not all banks in the KSA sector are in scope.

data.theme: Qualitative disclosure of a bank's liquidity risk management framework - governance, funding strategy, stress testing, contingency funding planning and risk tolerance.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a narrative (table) disclosure whose content requirements are tied to the liquidity risk governance and management expectations set out in the prudential liquidity framework.
Provides the qualitative context for the quantitative liquidity metrics disclosed elsewhere, so it is read together with the LCR/NSFR templates rather than standalone.
Links governance/risk-management obligations to transparency obligations: the same internal framework the bank must maintain is what it must describe publicly.

data.theme: Standardised public disclosure of the Liquidity Coverage Ratio - high-quality liquid assets against stressed net cash outflows over a 30-day horizon.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a fixed-format template giving effect to the disclosure limb of the LCR standard; the substantive calibration, haircuts and run-off assumptions sit in the LCR rules, not here.
Uses the LCR standard's defined terms (HQLA categories, net cash outflows, weighted/unweighted values) and its averaging and observation-period conventions.
Complements the qualitative liquidity risk management disclosure, forming the quantitative half of the liquidity transparency package.

data.theme: Registration formalities for finance lease contracts, i.e. the perfection/recording step that conditions a lessor's ability to assert its rights in leased assets under the Finance Lease Law regime.
how_members_connect: Single-instrument cluster: a SAMA circular operating as subordinate guidance under the Finance Lease Law and its implementing regulation.
Linkage is to the finance-company licensing and contract-documentation chain rather than to internal cross-references.
Relevance is decisional: whether a lease is registered affects enforceability and priority against third parties.
start_here: Circular on Registration of Finance Lease Contracts

data.theme: Permission for the Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company to acquire residential real estate finance portfolios, touching secondary-market mortgage liquidity and the scope of permitted acquisitions by a SAMA-supervised entity.
how_members_connect: Isolated circular acting as a targeted authorisation/carve-out layered on the real estate finance and finance company regulatory framework.
Consequences run to assignment and transfer of consumer real estate finance contracts and the continuity of borrower protections post-transfer.
start_here: Circular Allowing SRC to Purchase Residential Real Estate Finance Portfolios

data.theme: Supervisory expectations for identifying, classifying, restructuring and resolving problem and non-performing loans, including governance of a dedicated workout function and fair treatment of distressed borrowers.
how_members_connect: The Rules on Management of Problem Loans sit at the head of the cluster and pull in the operational concepts (early warning signals, watch list, workout unit, NPL strategy, collateral management) as mandated components.

An obligation chain runs from detection (early warning signals, watch list) to triage (portfolio segmentation, initial viability assessment) to remediation (workout plan, restructuring) to post-restructuring monitoring.

Viability testing is anchored in defined quantitative metrics (LTV, loan life coverage, Debt/EBITDA) and qualitative analyses (business, cash flow, SWOT), which determine whether restructuring or exit is required.

Cross-regime link to the Credit Risk Classification and Provisioning Rules ties workout outcomes to classification and provisioning consequences; the Code of Conduct adds a consumer-protection/fair-treatment overlay on collection and restructuring conduct.
start_here: Rules on Management of Problem Loans
SAMA Rules on Credit Risk Classification and Provisioning
Code of Conduct for Problem Loans

data.theme: The credit information regime governing licensed credit bureaus, the content and handling of credit records, and the dispute/violation mechanism available to data subjects and members.
how_members_connect: The Implementing Regulation is the parent instrument under the Credit Information Law and defines the licensed Credit Information Company and the Credit Record it maintains.
Obligation chain: consent and accuracy duties of members and bureaus feed the content of the credit record, which in turn grounds the data subject's correction and objection rights.
The Committee for Violations and Credit Information Disputes is the designated adjudicatory forum, making it the escalation endpoint for record-accuracy and unlawful-disclosure complaints.
Interacts with consumer protection and data privacy expectations, and with lender affordability/credit assessment duties that rely on bureau data.
start_here: Implementing Regulation of Credit Information Law

data.theme: Contractual architecture of a corporate loan restructuring: the documents that record renegotiated terms and the continuing financial and behavioural undertakings of the borrower.
how_members_connect: The restructuring agreement is the operative instrument and expressly incorporates the commercial parameters agreed in the term sheet.
Loan covenants are carried into or reset by the restructuring agreement, so breach analysis runs from covenant text back to the restructured facility.
Hierarchy is commercial rather than regulatory: indicative term sheet gives way to binding agreement, with covenants as the ongoing compliance layer.
Relevant to creditor classification, provisioning and consumer/SME treatment questions where SAMA rules attach to modified credit terms.

data.theme: Multi-creditor workout mechanics: how banks hold off enforcement and coordinate while a restructuring is negotiated.
how_members_connect: The standstill agreement supplies the contractual moratorium within which the coordinating bank operates.
The multi-bank coordinator is the conduit for information sharing and creditor decision-making during the standstill period.
Both concepts sit upstream of the restructuring documentation cluster and shape when a modified exposure crystallises.

data.theme: Two intersecting regimes: licensing and contracting requirements for aggregation (finance support) entities, and the operational resilience obligations - business continuity, disaster recovery, crisis management and cyber resilience - that licensed entities must satisfy, including sandbox-stage participants.
how_members_connect: The aggregation instructions define the Aggregation Entity and Platform and mandate the two contractual relationships (with the consumer and with the financier), while citing the licensing rules for finance support activities as the authorising base.
The same instructions pull the Business Continuity Management Framework into the aggregation perimeter, so a resilience failure is a licensing-condition failure, not merely an operational lapse.

Within the BCM framework, governance, strategy, business impact analysis, the continuity plan, IT disaster recovery, crisis management and testing form a single obligation chain, benchmarked against ISO 22301.

Cyber resilience requirements and the Cyber Security Framework cross-reference BCM, and the resilience domain links back to the continuity plan; the sandbox framework and its FAQ determine how these duties apply to pre-licence testing.
start_here: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities

data.theme: Controlled modification of production systems: the discipline of authorising, testing and recording changes, with security patching as a governed sub-case.
how_members_connect: Patch management is treated as a change subject to the change and release management control, so patch deployment inherits change authorisation and rollback requirements.
Both are operational controls within the wider cyber security and resilience obligations, and evidence of them is what supervisory review examines.

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of how credit derivatives used as credit risk mitigation affect risk-weighted assets for exposures under the internal ratings-based approach.
how_members_connect: Single-template cluster: sits within the SAMA Pillar 3 disclosure framework for banks approved to use IRB approaches for credit risk.
Depends on upstream definitions of eligible credit risk mitigation (guarantees and credit derivatives) and of the IRB exposure classes used to scope the disclosure.
Complements the other IRB credit-risk templates by isolating the RWA effect attributable to CRM rather than the underlying exposure measurement.
start_here: Template CR7 - IRB Effect on RWA of Credit Derivatives as CRM

data.theme: Periodic disclosure explaining movements in credit risk RWA under the IRB approach between reporting dates.
how_members_connect: Single-template cluster forming part of the mandatory Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure set for IRB banks.
Obligation chain: IRB approval and capital adequacy rules generate the RWA figures that this flow statement must reconcile period-on-period.
Cross-reads with the other IRB credit-risk templates, which supply the opening and closing RWA balances whose drivers are explained here.
start_here: Template CR8 - RWA Flow Statements of Credit Risk Exposures Under IRB

data.theme: Disclosure of specialised lending exposures risk-weighted under the IRB supervisory slotting criteria rather than a bank's own parameter estimates.
how_members_connect: Single-template cluster anchored in the IRB sub-class of specialised lending and its prescribed supervisory categories.
Applies where a bank cannot meet the requirements for own estimates of IRB risk parameters, so the slotting approach substitutes supervisory risk weights.
Scope is defined by the capital adequacy framework's exposure-class taxonomy, which determines which facilities fall into this template versus the general corporate IRB templates.
start_here: Template CR10 - IRB Specialised Lending Under Slotting Approach

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on counterparty credit risk, covering the bank's objectives, policies and management approach for CCR exposures.
how_members_connect: Single-table cluster providing the narrative counterpart to the quantitative CCR disclosure templates.
Draws on defined terms from the counterparty credit risk measurement rules (exposure measurement methods, collateral and wrong-way risk concepts).
Governance linkage: the disclosure obliges the bank to describe risk management, limit-setting and collateral policies set under its board-approved risk framework.
start_here: Table CCRA - Qualitative Disclosure Related to CCR

data.theme: SAMA's stress testing regime for banks: the mandatory programme covering scope, methodologies, risk-type coverage, and the link between stress results and capital adequacy assessment under ICAAP.
how_members_connect: The Rules on Stress Testing act as the parent instrument and expressly reference each technique (sensitivity, scenario, reverse) and each risk-type exercise (credit, market, liquidity, operational, top-down/macro) as required components of a bank's programme.

Obligation chain runs outward to ICAAP: stress outcomes must feed the bank's internal capital adequacy assessment, so the same scenarios carry capital-planning consequences, not just risk-measurement ones.
International standards are incorporated by citation to the BCBS sound stress testing principles, which informs how SAMA expectations should be interpreted where the Rules are principles-based.

Annexure-I fixes the reporting format, converting the substantive testing obligations into a defined supervisory submission; Pillar 3 Table OVA sits alongside as the disclosure-side narrative on risk management approach.
start_here: Rules on Stress Testing for Banks
Annexure-I: Stress Testing Results Reporting Format

data.theme: Allocation of accountability for the stress testing programme between the board and senior management — who owns approval, oversight, and execution.
how_members_connect: Both members derive from the same governance provisions of the stress testing rules and split a single obligation set: board-level approval and oversight versus management-level design, execution and escalation.
They form a hierarchy: senior management's duties are discharged under, and reported up to, the board, so a gap at one level is a compliance failure at the other.
The pairing is the governance entry point into the wider stress testing cluster (community 20) — programme adequacy is assessed against these responsibilities.

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure of a bank's remuneration policy — the governance, design and risk-alignment features that must be described publicly.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a standalone Pillar 3 narrative table whose obligation is disclosure content rather than conduct.
Conceptually paired with the quantitative remuneration templates; the policy narrative is the interpretive frame for the figures disclosed.
Sits within the governance/risk regime, linking remuneration design to risk-taking incentives and board oversight.

data.theme: Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure of remuneration actually awarded in the financial year, by category and instrument type.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a fixed-format disclosure template, so the obligation is completeness and format fidelity rather than substantive conduct.
Reads together with the qualitative remuneration policy table, which supplies the definitions and policy context for the reported amounts.
Part of the broader Pillar 3 disclosure framework and its periodic publication timing requirements.
start_here: Template REM1 - Remuneration Awarded During Financial Year

data.theme: Pillar 3 counterparty credit risk disclosure for credit derivative positions, requiring banks to present protection bought and sold separately so supervisors and market participants can assess CCR concentration and transfer of credit risk.
how_members_connect: Single-template cluster sitting within the counterparty credit risk (CCR) disclosure series, so its linkage is hierarchical: framework requirement down to prescribed reporting template.
Relies on CCR definitions and exposure measurement concepts shared across the CCR template family rather than on internal cross-references.

data.theme: Flow-statement disclosure of movements in risk-weighted assets for counterparty credit risk exposures calculated under the Internal Model Method, aimed at explaining period-on-period RWA changes.
how_members_connect: Isolated template whose obligation depends on the bank having supervisory approval to use IMM, making scope conditional on model permission rather than on other templates.
Shares RWA definitions and reconciliation logic with the wider capital adequacy disclosure hierarchy (framework requirement to template).
start_here: Template CCR7 - RWA Flow Statements of CCR Exposures Under IMM

data.theme: Qualitative narrative disclosure on securitisation activity, covering the bank's objectives, roles (originator, sponsor, investor, servicer), risk management approach and accounting treatment.
how_members_connect: Serves as the narrative counterpart that frames and gives interpretive context to the quantitative securitisation exposure templates.
Uses the defined securitisation roles and exposure categories that drive the scope and row structure of the numeric templates.
start_here: Table SECA - Qualitative Disclosure on Securitisation Exposures

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of banking book securitisation exposures, splitting total exposure amounts from the capital requirements applicable where the bank acts as originator or sponsor.
how_members_connect: The two templates share underlying exposure data: amounts reported in the general banking book template feed the originator/sponsor capital requirement breakdown.
Both depend on the same defined roles (originator, sponsor, investor) and banking book scope boundary, so a classification decision in one drives the other.
Both sit beneath the securitisation framework's capital treatment rules, with the qualitative table supplying the explanatory context.
start_here: Template SEC1 - Securitisation Exposures in the Banking Book
Template SEC3 - Securitisation Exposures Banking Book Originator/Sponsor

data.theme: Pillar 3 remuneration disclosure covering guaranteed bonuses, sign-on awards and severance payments made during the reporting year. It addresses transparency over discretionary pay outside the standard variable-remuneration cycle, where governance and risk-alignment concerns are highest.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a prescribed SAMA disclosure template forming part of the remuneration (REM) series within the Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.
Legally dependent on the underlying rules on compensation practices and the governance framework that defines material risk takers and senior management as the population in scope.
Sits in a hierarchy: capital/disclosure framework -> Pillar 3 disclosure requirements -> prescribed template with fixed rows, columns and reporting frequency.
Read alongside the other REM templates, since scope of covered staff and definitions of fixed/variable pay are shared across them.

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of deferred and retained remuneration, including outstanding exposed and unexposed amounts and reductions applied through malus or clawback. The problem-space is ex-post risk adjustment of variable pay.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a prescribed template in the remuneration (REM) series of the Pillar 3 disclosure requirements.
Obligation chain runs from the compensation/governance rules (deferral, vesting, malus and clawback requirements) to the annual quantitative disclosure of how those mechanisms operated.
Shares defined populations and pay categories with the other REM templates, so figures must reconcile across the series.
Hierarchy: disclosure framework -> Pillar 3 requirements -> fixed-format template with specified reporting frequency.

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure on the bank's overall credit risk profile: business model drivers of credit risk, risk appetite and limits, governance and reporting structures, and the definitions used for past-due and impaired exposures.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a qualitative narrative table anchoring the quantitative credit risk templates that follow it in the Pillar 3 set.
Relies on definitions drawn from the capital adequacy framework and the credit classification/provisioning rules (default, past due, impairment).
Hierarchy: Basel-aligned capital framework adopted by SAMA -> Pillar 3 disclosure requirements -> general qualitative credit risk table.
Interacts with governance and risk-management expectations, since disclosed content must reflect the board-approved credit risk appetite and control framework.
start_here: Table CRA - General Qualitative Information About Credit Risk

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure on credit risk mitigation: use of collateral, netting, guarantees and credit derivatives, together with valuation, management and concentration considerations arising from mitigants.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a qualitative table that explains the policies behind the quantitative credit risk mitigation templates.
Depends on the eligibility criteria and recognition conditions for collateral, guarantees and netting set in the capital adequacy framework's credit risk mitigation rules.
Directly complements the general credit risk qualitative table, sharing scope, exposure definitions and governance narrative.
Hierarchy: capital adequacy framework -> Pillar 3 disclosure requirements -> credit risk mitigation qualitative table.
start_here: Table CRC - Qualitative Disclosure on Credit Risk Mitigation Techniques
Table CRA - General Qualitative Information About Credit Risk

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of counterparty credit risk (CCR) at the entry point: the summary view of CCR exposures broken down by the measurement approach used (e.g. standardised vs internal models). It frames how a bank must publicly evidence the basis on which its derivative and SFT exposures are measured.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the CCR1 template is the gateway disclosure from which the more granular CCR templates inherit their exposure measure and scope.
Obligation chain runs from the capital adequacy/Pillar 3 disclosure framework (law/regulation level) down to the prescribed template format banks must complete and publish.
Defined terms (exposure at default, replacement cost, potential future exposure, approach used) are set at this level and carry into the portfolio-level templates.
start_here: Template CCR1 - Analysis of CCR Exposures by Approach

data.theme: Granular Pillar 3 CCR disclosure where exposure is decomposed by risk weight and by counterparty type, covering both standardised-approach bank book counterparties and exposures to central counterparties (qualifying and non-qualifying CCPs).
how_members_connect: Both templates disaggregate the same aggregate CCR exposure measure disclosed at summary level, so figures must reconcile across the template set.
CCP exposures are carved out of the general standardised-approach portfolio breakdown, creating an explicit cross-reference/exclusion relationship between the two templates.
Shared defined terms: qualifying CCP, default fund contribution, trade exposure, risk-weight bucket — each drives a different capital treatment.
start_here: Template CCR3 - Standardised Approach CCR Exposures by Portfolio and Risk Weights
Template CCR8 - Exposures to Central Counterparties

data.theme: Pillar 3 CCR disclosure for banks permitted to use the internal ratings-based approach, requiring exposures to be presented by portfolio and probability-of-default band.
how_members_connect: Applies only to banks with supervisory approval to use IRB for counterparty exposures — a scope limit that distinguishes it from the standardised-approach template.
Draws its exposure measure from the summary CCR approach template while adding IRB-specific risk parameters (PD, LGD, maturity, RWA).
Sits in the same hierarchy: capital framework, then Pillar 3 disclosure requirement, then prescribed template.
start_here: Template CCR4 - IRB CCR Exposures by Portfolio and PD Scale

data.theme: Disclosure of the collateral supporting counterparty credit risk exposures, split by collateral type and by whether it is used in derivative transactions or securities financing transactions, and whether it is segregated.
how_members_connect: Functions as the credit risk mitigation counterpart to the exposure templates: collateral disclosed here underpins the net exposure figures reported elsewhere in the CCR template set.
Relies on the framework's eligible-collateral and segregation definitions, which determine recognition for capital purposes.
Same disclosure obligation chain: capital adequacy rules, then the public disclosure requirement, then the fixed template format.
start_here: Template CCR5 - Composition of Collateral for CCR Exposures

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure on how a bank uses external credit assessment institutions (ECAIs) when assigning risk weights under the standardised approach to credit risk. It addresses the mapping and consistency of nominated ratings to exposure classes, not the computation itself.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the table sits at the qualitative layer of the disclosure hierarchy (Basel/SAMA capital framework rules on ECAI recognition, then the standardised approach rules, then this disclosure obligation).
Its content is the narrative counterpart to the standardised-approach quantitative templates, explaining the rating inputs that drive the risk-weight buckets reported elsewhere.
Obligation is periodic disclosure by the bank; scope is limited to exposure types where a nominated ECAI rating is actually used.
start_here: Table CRD - Use of External Credit Ratings Under Standardised Approach

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of standardised-approach credit risk: exposure amounts before and after credit conversion factors and credit risk mitigation, and the resulting distribution across asset classes and risk weights.
how_members_connect: Both templates share the same defined perimeter (standardised-approach exposures, asset classes, CRM techniques), so definitional consistency across them is an enforceable reconciliation point.
Direct cross-reference: post-CRM, post-CCF exposure reported in CR4 is the base that CR5 disaggregates by risk weight.
They depend on the ECAI/rating disclosures for the inputs that determine the risk-weight bands.
Sit below the capital adequacy rules in the hierarchy: the rules set the measurement, these templates set the disclosure form and frequency.
start_here: Template CR4 - Standardised Approach Credit Risk Exposure and CRM Effects
Template CR5 - Standardised Approach Exposures by Asset Classes and Risk Weights

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure for banks permitted to use internal ratings-based approaches: model scope, supervisory approval status, rating system design, governance and control of the estimation process.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster acting as the narrative gateway to the IRB quantitative templates — it explains the models whose outputs those templates quantify.
Applies only to banks with supervisory permission to use IRB, so the disclosure obligation is conditional on the approval regime rather than general.
Links governance/model-risk expectations to the capital framework: the qualitative account must be consistent with the approved model perimeter.
start_here: Template CRE - Qualitative Disclosure on IRB Models

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure for IRB credit risk: exposures and risk parameters by portfolio and PD band, and back-testing of realised defaults against estimated PD to evidence model performance.
how_members_connect: Shared defined terms and segmentation — portfolio, PD range/band, obligor grade — so the two templates must be populated on a consistent basis.
Data dependency: the PD estimates and portfolio buckets disclosed in CR6 are the estimates tested against realised outcomes in CR9.
Both are conditional on IRB permission and take their model scope and governance narrative from the IRB qualitative disclosure.
Back-testing disclosure operationalises the supervisory expectation of ongoing model validation, creating a consequence chain from model underperformance to supervisory challenge.
start_here: Template CR6 - IRB Credit Risk Exposures by Portfolio and PD Range
Template CR9 - IRB Backtesting of PD Per Portfolio

data.theme: Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure obligations for banks permitted to use the internal models approach (IMA) for market risk, covering how the model is scoped, governed and validated.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a prescribed disclosure table whose content obligation is triggered only by supervisory approval to use IMA for market risk.
Sits in the disclosure layer of the market risk framework, reporting on the capital treatment applied under the substantive market risk rules rather than creating it.
Definitional dependence on trading book / market risk scoping terms used across the market risk regime; disclosure scope follows model permission scope.
Read alongside the quantitative market risk templates and the simplified/standardised disclosures, which are the alternative path where no IMA permission exists.
start_here: Table MRB - Qualitative Disclosures for Banks Using IMA

data.theme: Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure of market risk capital requirements for banks eligible to apply the simplified standardised approach.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a template whose applicability is defined by eligibility for the simplified standardised approach, an exemption-style scope limit.
Alternative branch to the IMA and full standardised disclosure tables — mutually exclusive by approach used.
Disclosure obligation derives from the market risk capital calculation rules; the table reports outcomes, it does not set the methodology.
start_here: Table MR3 - Market Risk Under Simplified Standardised Approach

data.theme: General qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure on credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk — how the bank identifies, measures, governs and hedges counterparty-credit valuation risk.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the entry-point qualitative disclosure applying to all banks subject to the CVA risk capital framework, irrespective of approach chosen.
Acts as the parent to approach-specific CVA disclosures (e.g. SA-CVA), which add obligations on top of this baseline.
Relies on defined terms from the counterparty credit risk and derivatives framework; scope follows the population of in-scope derivative and SFT exposures.
start_here: Table CVAA - General Qualitative Disclosure on CVA Risk

data.theme: Approach-specific Pillar 3 qualitative disclosure for banks using the standardised approach for CVA risk (SA-CVA), covering governance, eligible hedges and model/inputs controls.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: obligation conditional on supervisory permission to use SA-CVA rather than the basic approach.
Layered on the general CVA qualitative disclosure — the general table is the baseline, this adds approach-specific content.
Cross-refers to CVA hedging eligibility and capital calculation rules in the substantive CVA framework; disclosure scope mirrors the permission's scope.
start_here: Table CVAB - Qualitative Disclosures for Banks Using SA-CVA
Table CVAA - General Qualitative Disclosure on CVA Risk

data.theme: Pillar 3 public disclosure of the indicators used to assess global systemic importance, feeding the G-SIB identification and higher loss-absorbency regime.
how_members_connect: Single-template cluster: a fixed-format disclosure obligation sitting in the Pillar 3 framework hierarchy (Basel standard adopted via SAMA rules -> disclosure templates).
Scope is limited to banks meeting the size/indicator thresholds for the G-SIB assessment exercise; it is an indicator-reporting duty, not a capital requirement in itself.
Links outward to capital adequacy and buffer obligations, since the indicators drive any systemic-importance surcharge.
start_here: Template GSIB1 - Disclosure of G-SIB Indicators

data.theme: Qualitative disclosure of how a bank governs and manages liquidity risk, providing the narrative context for the quantitative liquidity ratios.
how_members_connect: Table-format (qualitative) Pillar 3 item, paired by design with the quantitative liquidity templates it explains.
Relies on the same defined liquidity concepts (funding strategy, stress testing, contingency funding) used in the LCR and NSFR requirements.
Sits in the governance/risk regime: obligations run to the board and senior management as owners of the liquidity risk framework.

data.theme: Standardised public disclosure of the short-term liquidity metric: stock of high-quality liquid assets against 30-day stressed net cash outflows.
how_members_connect: Quantitative Pillar 3 template giving effect to the underlying LCR minimum standard; the disclosure duty is distinct from, and dependent on, the prudential ratio rules.
Shares defined terms (HQLA, inflow/outflow rates, averaging basis) with the liquidity rules and with the qualitative liquidity table.
Complements the structural funding measure, so the two liquidity templates are read together as one disclosure set.

data.theme: Standardised public disclosure of the structural funding metric: available stable funding against required stable funding over a one-year horizon.
how_members_connect: Quantitative Pillar 3 template implementing the NSFR minimum standard; disclosure obligation layered on top of the prudential ratio requirement.
Uses the same balance-sheet categorisation and weighting definitions (ASF/RSF factors, residual maturity buckets) as the NSFR rules.
Paired with the LCR template and explained by the qualitative liquidity risk management table.
start_here: Template LIQ2 - Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR)

data.theme: Pillar 3 narrative disclosure of a bank's operational risk framework — the qualitative account of how operational risk is identified, governed, measured and mitigated, which contextualises the quantitative operational risk capital figures.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the qualitative table is the descriptive counterpart to the operational risk quantitative templates, and is read with them rather than standalone.
Sits in the disclosure hierarchy as a SAMA-adopted Pillar 3 requirement giving effect to the operational risk capital regime; obligation is periodic public disclosure in the prescribed format.
Defined terms (e.g. business indicator, loss data) are inherited from the operational risk capital rules, not redefined here.
start_here: Table ORA - General Qualitative Information on Operational Risk Framework

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of operational risk capital under the standardised approach: historical loss experience, the business indicator and its subcomponents, and the resulting minimum required operational risk capital.
how_members_connect: OR1 (loss data) and OR2 (business indicator components) are input templates whose figures feed directly into the OR3 capital calculation — an explicit computational and cross-referencing chain.
All three share the operational risk capital definitions (business indicator, business indicator component, internal loss multiplier) from the underlying capital framework.
Together they operationalise the qualitative framework described in the ORA table; inconsistency between narrative and templates is a disclosure compliance risk.
start_here: Template OR3 - Minimum Required Operational Risk Capital
Template OR2 - Business Indicator and Subcomponents

data.theme: Qualitative Pillar 3 disclosure of interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB): the bank's risk management objectives, governance, measurement assumptions and modelling choices for banking book rate exposures.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster providing the assumption set and methodology narrative needed to interpret the IRRBB quantitative template.
Depends on IRRBB definitions (economic value of equity, net interest income, prescribed interest rate shock scenarios) set in the underlying IRRBB standard rather than in the disclosure table itself.
Disclosure obligation is triggered by the bank's scope of application under SAMA's adopted Pillar 3 framework.
start_here: Table IRRBBA - IRRBB Risk Management Objectives and Policies

data.theme: Quantitative Pillar 3 disclosure of IRRBB outcomes — changes in economic value of equity and net interest income under the prescribed interest rate shock scenarios.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster that is the numerical output of the methodology and assumptions disclosed in the IRRBBA qualitative table; the two are designed to be read as a pair.
Scenario definitions and measurement conventions are imported from the IRRBB standard, so the template cannot be applied without that upstream rule.
Comparability is the regulatory purpose: deviations in assumptions must be explained in the qualitative table, not in the template.
start_here: Template IRRBB1 - Quantitative Information on IRRBB

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of securitisation positions held in the trading book, i.e. the quantitative template banks use to expose their securitisation activity and exposures on the trading side.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the SEC2 template stands alone as the trading-book leg of the securitisation disclosure suite.
Legally it sits within the Pillar 3 disclosure framework, taking its scope from the defined terms 'securitisation exposure' and 'trading book' used across the capital rules.
Read together with its banking-book counterparts (SEC1/SEC3/SEC4) to avoid double-counting or scope gaps in disclosed exposures.
start_here: Template SEC2 - Securitisation Exposures in the Trading Book

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of banking-book securitisation exposures where the bank acts as investor, including the associated capital requirements.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster covering the investor role, distinct from originator/sponsor roles disclosed elsewhere in the SEC series.
Obligation depends on correct role classification (investor vs originator/sponsor), a definitional determination made under the securitisation capital rules.
Cross-reads to the trading-book securitisation template and to the overall RWA overview for consistency of reported amounts.
start_here: Template SEC4 - Securitisation Exposures Banking Book Investor

data.theme: The qualitative narrative disclosure obligation on market risk: how a bank must describe its market risk strategy, governance and management processes rather than report numbers.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster providing the qualitative frame that contextualises the quantitative market risk templates (MR1/MR2).
Ties the disclosure duty to the bank's governance and risk-management arrangements, so content must be consistent with board-approved risk appetite statements.
Functions as the interpretive gateway for the market risk measurement approach (standardised vs internal models) disclosed quantitatively elsewhere.
start_here: Table MRA - General Qualitative Disclosure on Market Risk

data.theme: Pillar 3 quantitative disclosure of market risk and credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk capital, and their consolidation into the bank's overall risk-weighted assets picture.
how_members_connect: All templates feed into the RWA overview template, which acts as the reconciliation hub: figures disclosed in the market risk and CVA templates must tie back to the aggregate RWA statement.

The CVA templates form a tiered set reflecting the permitted approaches (reduced basic, full basic, standardised) plus an RWA flow statement, so which template applies is determined by the approach the bank is authorised to use.

Market risk disclosures split by approach: standardised versus internal models, with the internal models template cross-referring to both the standardised template and the modelled-versus-standardised comparison, supporting supervisory output-floor and benchmarking scrutiny.

Membership is governed by the same underlying capital adequacy framework definitions (trading book boundary, covered positions, eligible hedges), so a change in classification propagates across multiple templates.
start_here: Table MR1 - Market Risk Under Standardised Approach
Template CVA3 - Standardised Approach for CVA

data.theme: Compliance by supervised financial entities with the KSA Personal Data Protection Law, covering lawful processing, data subject rights and accountability for customer personal data held under SAMA-regulated activities.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the PDPL obligation set sits outside SAMA's core prudential regimes but binds the same regulated entities as a parallel legal duty.

Interacts with SAMA regimes where customer data is collected or shared — CDD/KYC records, credit information, outsourcing and complaint handling — so scope overlaps must be reconciled rather than treated as alternatives.
Hierarchy point: PDPL is primary legislation with its own supervisory authority; SAMA instructions do not displace it and should be read as cumulative.

data.theme: Conditions under which regulated entities may operate remote/work-from-home arrangements, and the requirement that customer-facing service functions remain located and staffed within the Kingdom.
how_members_connect: Direct cross-reference: the remote work permission is framed by, and expressly points to, the localization requirements for remote customer service.
Shared obligation chain — an entity relying on remote working must still satisfy in-Kingdom siting, supervision and Saudization-related conditions for customer service channels.
Operational-risk and outsourcing adjacency: remote delivery does not relax accountability for service quality, confidentiality of customer data, or SAMA access to records.

data.theme: Consumer-protection requirement that regulated entities provide customers a unified toll-free number for service and complaints, supporting accessibility of the complaint-handling channel.
how_members_connect: Standalone instruction that feeds the broader consumer protection and complaint-handling obligation chain (accessible channel → logged complaint → resolution timelines).
Relevant to the remote customer service localization cluster, since the free number is a customer-facing channel subject to in-Kingdom requirements.

data.theme: Prescribed form and content requirements for currency bundling/packaging card templates used in cash handling and distribution.
how_members_connect: Single-member operational instruction within SAMA's currency issuance and cash-handling authority, rather than a conduct or prudential regime.
Compliance consequence is conformity of banknote bundle labelling with the mandated template; deviations are supervisory findings, not consumer-protection breaches.

data.theme: Standardised public disclosure of the Net Stable Funding Ratio, breaking funding into available stable funding and required stable funding components. It sits in the liquidity-standards limb of the prudential regime, where the obligation is to disclose in a prescribed, comparable format rather than to compute a new requirement.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the template is the disclosure instrument attached to the underlying NSFR liquidity requirement, so its legal force derives from the parent liquidity/Pillar 3 rules rather than standing alone.
Depends on the defined ASF/RSF weighting categories used in the NSFR calculation rules — the template cannot be read without those definitions.
Interacts with other prudential disclosure templates (capital, market risk) as part of one periodic disclosure obligation cycle to SAMA and the public.

data.theme: Pillar 3 disclosure of market risk capital requirements calculated under the Internal Models Approach. The compliance question is scope and eligibility: only banks with SAMA permission to use internal models populate this template.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the template implements the disclosure leg of the market risk capital framework; the substantive calculation and model-approval conditions live in the parent market risk rules.
Its applicability is conditional on prior supervisory approval of the internal model — an approval-gated obligation rather than a general one.
Sits alongside the standardised-approach market risk templates in the same disclosure suite, so the correct template depends on the approach the bank is authorised to use.

data.theme: The duty of supervised financial institutions to respond promptly and completely to requests, orders and enquiries from judicial and investigative authorities. It is a cooperation/conduct obligation that cuts across banking secrecy, account freezing and law-enforcement support.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: a circular-level instruction that operationalises statutory cooperation duties owed to courts, prosecution and enforcement bodies.
Interacts with the AML/CTF and sanctions regimes, where similar duties to act on official orders (freezing, information production) arise from a different legal base.
Constrains the confidentiality/bank secrecy regime — lawful judicial requests are a recognised gateway, so the two must be read together.
Timeliness is the enforceable element: delay itself is the breach, independent of the substantive answer given.
start_here: Prompt Response to Judicial Authorities Circular

data.theme: Rules on issuing bank documents electronically and enabling reliable verification of their authenticity by recipients. The regulatory concern is document fraud, evidentiary reliability and customer convenience in dealings with third parties and government bodies.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: an operational instruction to banks on the form and verifiability of documents they issue (certificates, statements, confirmations).
Connects to consumer protection principles on accurate, accessible and timely provision of records to customers.

Touches the evidentiary/authentication dimension relied on by counterparties, courts and authorities, and so indirectly supports information-request and verification duties elsewhere in the framework.
start_here: Electronic Issuance and Verification of Bank Documents

data.theme: Migration of entity identification in KSA from commercial registration numbers to the Unified Number (including the professional/licensing equivalent for law firms), and the consequence for onboarding, KYB and record-keeping fields used by financial institutions.
how_members_connect: Both items address the same identifier reform: the Unified Number becomes the authoritative entity identifier that supersedes or sits alongside the commercial registration number.
The lawyers' item is a sectoral application of the general rule, so it should be read as a downstream extension of the replacement instruction rather than a separate regime.

Practical linkage is through customer/entity due diligence: identification and verification data captured for legal-person Customers must reflect the new identifier, and legacy records must remain reconcilable.
Explicit cross-reference exists between the two members, confirming hierarchy: general instruction first, profession-specific instruction second.
start_here: Replacing Commercial Registration with Unified Number

data.theme: Operational obligation on banks and cash-handling entities to inspect banknotes, covering authenticity checks and handling of suspect or unfit currency at the teller and cash-centre level.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster; the obligation stands alone as a supervisory instruction to cash-handling institutions.
Its practical significance is as a control feeding currency-integrity and counterfeit-reporting duties, and it interacts with AML suspicion-reporting where counterfeit or suspect cash is presented.

data.theme: Duties of supervised financial institutions to respond to requests and correspondence from the Committee for the Settlement of Banking Disputes, including timeliness and completeness of submissions.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster; the requirement is a procedural cooperation obligation owed to an adjudicatory body rather than a prudential rule.
It links conceptually to consumer protection and complaint-handling regimes, since disputes escalated by customers become matters requiring institutional response and documentary support.
start_here: Responding to Banking Disputes Committee Requests

data.theme: Treatment of government development fund loans in banks' dealings with customers, including how such financing is to be considered in credit assessment and customer accommodation.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster; the instruction is directed at lenders' credit and customer-treatment practices in relation to state-backed development financing.
It intersects with credit-granting and consumer/SME finance obligations, particularly affordability and obligation-to-income assessment where subsidised loans form part of the customer's exposure.

data.theme: Card-payment integrity and cost allocation in the domestic scheme environment: preventing misuse of preauthorization holds and controlling what fees may be charged in connection with mada claims/chargeback handling.
how_members_connect: Both sit in the payments/card-scheme regime and bind the same actors — acquirers, issuers and merchants operating under mada rules.

Shared obligation chain: proper authorization/preauthorization handling is the control that determines when a claim (dispute/chargeback) arises, and the fee rules then govern who bears the cost of that claim.
Consumer-protection overlay: both constrain charges and conduct toward the cardholder, so fraud-loss allocation cannot be passed on as an unapproved fee.
Fraud-related preauthorization misuse also engages AML/fraud reporting duties, a cross-regime link to suspicious-activity obligations.

data.theme: Identity verification of customers by reference to a trusted/reliable independent source — the core CDD building block for onboarding and ongoing due diligence.
how_members_connect: Anchors the AML/CTF defined term 'Customer' and the requirement that identification be verified against independent, reliable documents or data.
Feeds downstream obligation chains: ongoing monitoring, record-keeping, enhanced due diligence and reliance on third parties for CDD.
Cross-regime relevance: payments/PSP onboarding, BNPL 'Consumer' onboarding and merchant/KYB checks all inherit this verification standard.
start_here: Customer Identity Verification via Trusted Source

data.theme: Standardisation of the content and format of financial notifications sent to customers, so disclosures about transactions and account events are consistent, complete and comprehensible.
how_members_connect: Consumer-protection regime: converts general transparency/disclosure duties into prescribed notification elements financial institutions must include.
Links to transaction-execution and fee-disclosure obligations, since the notification is the evidentiary touchpoint for what the customer was told and when.
Supports dispute and complaint handling, as notification timing and content determine customer awareness and objection periods.

data.theme: Prudential and conduct rules for real estate finance products, covering permitted product structures and the treatment of appraisal costs within financing contracts.
how_members_connect: Both apply to banks and finance companies offering real estate finance, under the same product-approval and contract-terms framework.
Hierarchy link: product instructions set what may be offered and on what terms; the appraisal-fee rule constrains a specific charge that must appear in — and be limited by — those contract terms.
Consumer-protection chain: fee transparency and cost-recovery limits interact with disclosure and total-cost-of-financing requirements for the borrower.
Appraisal outcomes also feed collateral valuation and LTV-type prudential considerations, connecting conduct rules to credit-risk treatment.
start_here: Real Estate Appraisal Fees in Financing Contracts

data.theme: Funding-side regulation of finance companies: raising debt through special purpose vehicles, and the conditions and supervisory consent attaching to such structures.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster anchored on the finance company licensing/supervision regime, where debt issuance is a permitted funding activity subject to SAMA conditions rather than a free commercial choice.
Links outward to finance company prudential rules (leverage, capital adequacy) and to corporate governance obligations over off-balance-sheet or SPV structures.
Defined-term dependency: 'Finance Company' and the scope of licensed finance activity determine who may use the SPV route and for what underlying receivables.
start_here: Finance Companies Debt Issuance via SPVs

data.theme: Operational and conduct obligations around physical cash movement: licensed transport of cash and valuables, and the duty to warn customers of the risks of carrying cash themselves.
how_members_connect: Both circulars sit under the cash transport regulatory framework and address the same risk (loss, theft, AML exposure from untraced cash movement) from two angles: institutional compliance and customer-facing awareness.
Obligation chain: the transport regulations bind institutions to use licensed arrangements, while the awareness circular pushes a disclosure/advisory duty onto the customer relationship.
Cross-regime interaction with AML/CTF — large physical cash handling is a recognised higher-risk channel and feeds CDD and reporting expectations.
start_here: Circular: Compliance with Cash Transport Regulations
Circular: Client Awareness of Cash Carrying Risks

data.theme: Supervisory requirements imposed on exchange (money changing) companies, covering workforce nationalisation targets and periodic financial and internal control reporting to SAMA.
how_members_connect: Both circulars are addressed to the same licensed population — exchange companies — and form part of the ongoing licence-condition set rather than one-off approvals.
Shared supervisory logic: SAMA uses reporting obligations and staffing/Saudization conditions as continuing compliance measures enforceable against the licence.
The internal control report requirement links to the governance and AML/CTF control expectations applicable to exchange businesses, which are treated as higher-risk cash-intensive entities.
start_here: Circular: Providing Financial Statements and Internal Control Reports
Circular: Saudization of Exchange Company Jobs

data.theme: Governance requirement for financial institutions to maintain a whistle blowing framework enabling protected internal reporting of misconduct, fraud and regulatory breaches.
how_members_connect: Standalone policy instrument that attaches to the governance/internal control regime: board responsibility, independence of the reporting channel, and protection of the reporting person.
Feeds obligation chains in AML/CTF and fraud regimes, where internally raised concerns may trigger suspicious transaction reporting and notification to SAMA.
Interacts with confidentiality and banking secrecy duties, which must be read as not overriding the protected disclosure route.
start_here: Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions

data.theme: Sector-specific mandates to enable and accept electronic payment at points of sale across merchant categories (groceries, general retail, personal services), forming part of SAMA's cash-reduction and merchant-acceptance policy track.
how_members_connect: Each member applies the same core obligation — merchant enablement/acceptance of electronic payment instruments — to a different merchant sector, so the operative rule is common and only scope differs.
Linked by shared defined terms (merchant, point-of-sale device, electronic payment means) and by the acquirer/PSP-side duties that make merchant acceptance effective.
Cross-regime relevance: merchants onboarded for acceptance are the acquirer's customers for KYB/CDD purposes, so sector rollout obligations feed into AML/CTF onboarding duties.
Sequenced as a phased extension of the same policy instrument rather than a law→regulation hierarchy; read them as parallel scope extensions.

data.theme: Consumer-protection conduct duties governing how financial institutions market to, communicate with, and resolve complaints from customers, including accessibility obligations toward persons with disabilities.
how_members_connect: Common consumer-protection base: advertising/marketing content standards, complaint-handling standards and accessibility duties all attach to the same customer-facing conduct obligation set.
Accessibility requirements cross-reference marketing and disclosure rules, so advertising material and channels must meet disability-access standards as well as fairness/clarity standards.

The unified complaint response template operationalises complaint-handling obligations and supplies the standardised output SAMA expects, making it the procedural endpoint of breaches of marketing or accessibility duties.
Hierarchy runs from consumer-protection principles down to instructions and then to the standardised template/form level.
start_here: Compliance with Advertising and Marketing Instructions
Unified Complaint Response Template - SAMA Cares

data.theme: SAMA's framework for publicly disclosing supervisory penalties imposed on supervised entities — the transparency and reputational consequence layer of enforcement.
how_members_connect: Standalone instrument in this graph: it sits downstream of substantive obligations across all regimes, since any enforceable breach can feed into publication.
Legal significance is consequential rather than conduct-defining — it governs what SAMA publishes about a sanction, not what the entity must do operationally.
Relevant to decisions on remediation, self-reporting posture and reputational risk assessment across AML/CTF, payments, consumer protection and governance breaches.

data.theme: Licensing and operational prerequisites for the physical premises of money exchange centres, covering minimum standards a licensed exchanger's branch must satisfy.
how_members_connect: Standalone premises-standard instrument within the exchange/money-changing licensing regime; it conditions licence grant and continued authorisation.
Connects conceptually to AML/CTF and security expectations for cash-handling businesses, since premises controls support customer identification and safe handling at the point of service.
Read as a supervisory requirement layer beneath the exchange-business licensing rules rather than as an independent regime.
start_here: Minimum Requirements for Exchange Center Premises

data.theme: Workforce nationalization (Saudization) treatment of dependants — whether the children of a Saudi citizen may be counted toward a supervised entity's Saudization ratio. Sits in the HR/licensing-condition space rather than a prudential or conduct regime.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster: the rule stands alone as an interpretive position on how Saudization headcount is calculated for entities SAMA supervises.
Legal consequence attaches to licensing and ongoing-compliance conditions (nationalization targets), not to AML/CTF or consumer-protection duties.
No internal cross-references in the graph; linkage to other regimes would be indirect, via fit-and-proper/governance and staffing obligations.

data.theme: Customer notification by SMS — the terms on which supervised entities subscribe customers to SMS alert/notification services, and the consequences for consent, fees and transaction transparency.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster addressing the conduct/consumer-protection dimension of customer communications.
Obligation chain runs from the entity to the individual customer: enrolment, disclosure and continuity of alerting.
Interacts indirectly with fraud-detection and transaction-advice duties, but the rule itself is a service-terms instruction.

data.theme: A narrow identification carve-out for exchange (money-changing) centers located at airports serving travellers — a scope limit on the standard CDD identification requirement for defined low-value or transit transactions.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster, but legally dependent on the general AML/CTF customer identification baseline it derogates from; the exemption only has meaning by reference to that baseline.
Closely adjacent to the exchange-center customer conduct instructions (community 307): same licensed population, different obligation type (AML identification vs. customer dealing).
Any reliance on the exemption must respect its stated scope (location, customer type, transaction character); outside that scope full CDD revives.
start_here: Airport Exchange Center Traveler ID Exemption

data.theme: Conduct requirements governing how licensed exchange centers deal with customers — the baseline instructions on customer handling, disclosure and service delivery in the money-changing sector.
how_members_connect: Single-member cluster functioning as the sector-specific conduct layer for exchange centers.
Shares its addressee population with the airport traveller ID exemption (community 306); read together to separate conduct duties from AML identification duties.
Interpretation should preserve the exchange-center licensing perimeter — obligations bind licensed centers, not their agents or counterparties, unless stated.

data.theme: Controls on onward disclosure of supervisory information: a supervised entity must obtain SAMA's prior no-objection before sharing data or correspondence received from or generated for the supervisor with third parties.
